Donât confuse it with the Dominican Republic car, which has black stripes on the roof rack, or the CuraÃ§ao car, which has a black front. A similar car is found in Laos, so always check the surroundings before making a guess.

metas.name: Jordan - Black car meta
metas.description: While driving on the right side, yellow outer lines with white middle lines are commonly found in Jordan, Israel, and the UAE. The black back of the Google car without an antenna can help confirm youâre in Jordan 100%.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Pickup car meta
metas.description: All of the Kazakhstan coverage was taken with white pickup truck(can be sometimes fully blurred) and often it's gonna be in flat and open landscape. There is other countries covered by pickup truck so use other clues(landscape etc) to make your guess.

metas.name: Kenya - Pickup car
metas.description:
Sometimes you won't see Kenya snorkle and instead you will see gray/white pickup car with/without antenna and sometimes it might be even fully blurred.
But if you have a vibe that you are in Africa and you see pickup truck and you are driving on the left side you should be in Kenya(Or Namibia).
metas.comparison: Note:Other countries in Africa with pickup truck coverage drive on the right.

metas.name: Kenya - Unique car
metas.description: If you see a snorkel on the Google car, youâre in Kenya.
metas.comparison: However, the car is sometimes seen without it, so donât rule out Kenya if the snorkel isnât visible.

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - Unique car
metas.description: Kyrgyzstan can be recognized by the silver Google car with four visible bars. Coverage was done during winter, so trees often lack leaves, the landscape appears drab, and snow is visible in many areas.

metas.name: Laos - Unique car
metas.description: If you are in South East Asia with this roof-rack car you gonna be in one of 4 cities in Laos: Vang Vieng, Luang Prabang, Savannakhet, and Pakse.
metas.comparison: Note: You can find similar car in Guatemala so look around before making a guess.

metas.name: Mongolia - Unique car

metas.comparison: -White-Blue themed pickup truck mostly found only in Capital -Pickup truck with a tent on top

metas.name: Mongolia - Unique car
metas.description: The Street View car with a tent on top is unique to Mongolia. While Mongolia has other unique Google cars, this is the most common one.

metas.name: Namibia - Pickup truck
metas.description: Namibia is the newest African country with coverage featuring the white pickup truck.
metas.comparison: The landscape is similar to Botswanaâflat and dry. Roads typically have yellow outer lines, and driving is on the left side. Note: You may not always be on main roads with outer yellow lines. In such cases, it can resemble some parts of Kenya, which also drives on the left and sometimes features the white pickup truck.

metas.name: Northern Mariana Islands - Unique car
metas.description: The entire Google car is blurred, but an antenna at the front right can still be seen. It will feel noticeably closer to the car than in other countries with a similar car.
metas.comparison: You can confuse it with:

metas.name: Oman - Pickup car
metas.description: If you have a vibe that you are in Middle East and you see big white pickup truck with antenna in the middle you gonna be in Oman
metas.comparison: Note: Car might be sometimes fully blurred with visible antenna and sometimes  you can find similar pickup truck in UAE. Qatar pickup truck will have antenna in front left of the car.

metas.name: Qatar - Car meta
metas.description: Qatar's landscape is predominantly desert, with arid, mostly flat expanses of sand as far as the eye can see. You will often not see many trees or other greenery.
metas.comparison: The Google car will usually be blurred, with only the antenna on the left and a sliver of the car visible. Sometimes the entire white pickup truck can be visible. You might occasionally confuse it with the UAE or Oman pickup truck coverage, but in those countries, the antenna on the pickup car will be in the middle.

metas.name: Reunion - Unique car

metas.comparison: Donât confuse this with the Ghana car, which has tape on the front right bar.

metas.name: Rwanda - Unique car
metas.description: If you see a pickup truck with a red brake light on top in Africa, you're most likely in Rwanda.
metas.comparison: The car can be white, black, or brown, but it will always have this red brake light. Sometimes, the car might be fully blurred, so donât rule out Rwanda if you donât see it. Note: Similar car can be found in Ecuador so check surroundings before making a guess.

metas.name: Senegal - Pickup truck

metas.comparison:
Note:

metas.name: Turkey - Pickup car

metas.name: Australia - ACT gap reflector
metas.description: If you see gap and reflector in between outer lines you gonna be in ACT.
metas.comparison: (South Australia might have gaps in outerlines but reflector in a gap is super rare there)

metas.name: Australia - Melbourne white blue sticker
metas.description: Those white-blue stickers on poles are unique to Melbourne in Australia.

metas.name: Australia - NSW guardrail ending
metas.description: Guardrail ending, featuring a black dash on a yellow background, is almost exclusive to New South Wales and the ACT.

metas.name: Australia - NSW red no stopping sign
metas.description: New South Wales is the only state to use red âNo Stoppingâ signs.

metas.name: Australia - NSW yellow plates.
metas.description: If you see more than couple yellow plates in Australia you should be in NSW

metas.name: Australia - NT pole
metas.description: Rusty metal holey poles are unique to Northern Territory state in Australia.

metas.name: Australia - QLD black paint
metas.description: These black markings are specific to electricity poles in Queensland(from Gold Coast to Sunshine Coast). They are often accompanied by diagonal numbers.

metas.name: Australia - QLD non south-east pole marking
metas.description: If you see this grayish long thin plate with numbers, sometimes with extra blue(or other color) little circle marking you gonna be in QLD(not in south east most likely because they use different marking).

metas.name: Australia - SA flat sign posts
metas.description: You can only find flat signposts in South Australia and Western Australia (in WA they mostly will be yellow but not always). You will also find rounded sign posts in SA (so don't rule SA if you see rounded one).

metas.name: Australia - SA property markers
metas.description: You can find these white property markers on the sides of roads in South Australia.

metas.name: Australia - SA stobie pole
metas.description: The iconic Stobie pole, made of steel and concrete, is specific to South Australia.(A few thousand of these poles can be found in other states, most notably Tasmania - super rare)

metas.name: Australia - Tasmania pole metas
metas.description: Metas for Tasmiania poles:

metas.name: Australia - Vic pole top
metas.description: Victorian pole tops feature 3 circular coils; 2 on the sides, and 1 vertical one at the top.(sometimes might be missing the top one)

metas.name: Australia - Victoria hydrant bollard
metas.description: You can find these white hydrant poles that feature a blue circle and a red section on top of it in Victoria.(they have couple different designs but they all follow same color/shape +/- pattern)

metas.name: Australia - WA bollard
metas.description: Bollards with brown paint at the bottom are most commonly found in Western Australia.

metas.name: Australia - wa pole metas
metas.description: Western Australia pole metas:

metas.name: Australia - WA property marker
metas.description: You can find these dark green property markers on the sides of roads in Western Australia.

metas.name: Australia - WA stripy bollard
metas.description: Black-and-white stripy bollards are unique to Western Australia.

metas.name: Australia - WA yellow sign posts
metas.description: Yellow signposts are specific to Western Australia.

metas.name: Brazil - Acre red brick road
metas.description: Some roads in Acre are made of red brick.

metas.name: Brazil - Bahia and Pernambuco pole markings
metas.description: Markings on poles are used by the electricity companies to identify them. This pole ID is long, yellow pole paint with a black code. The ones that start with a letter are found in Bahia and Pernambuco.

metas.name: Brazil - Carnauba Palms
metas.description: CarnaÃºba palms have short but strong, fan-like leaves and a trunk that is smooth at the top and spiked at the bottom. They are common in CearÃ¡ but are also in PiauÃ­ and Rio Grande do Norte.

metas.name: Brazil - CearÃ¡ lamps
metas.description: Lamps in CearÃ¡ often have a fancy and colourful arm, whether as lampposts or attached to utility poles. It sometimes says the town on the arm.

metas.name: Brazil - Ceara pole top
metas.description: This asymmetrical concrete crossbar with no supports is exclusive to Ceara.

metas.name: Brazil - Coffee beans
metas.description: Coffee beans are by far the most common in Minas Gerais, but also can be found in EspÃ­rito Santo and northeastern SÃ£o Paulo.

metas.name: Brazil - Concrete bins
metas.description: Brazil often uses metal trash baskets outside houses. In Acre and RondÃ´nia, however, it is much more common to see them made of concrete.

metas.name: Brazil - EspÃ­rito Santo - Exposed rock
metas.description: EspÃ­rito Santo, and the surrounding areas, often have large mountains with exposed rock.

metas.name: Brazil - GoiÃ¡s pole markings
metas.description: Similar to the Bahia and Pernambuco poles, GoiÃ¡s poles also use long, yellow pole paint with a black paint code, but it always starts with a number. They also have a rarer yellow on black pole ID, which can be either paint or a plate.

metas.name: Brazil - Macaw palms
metas.description: Macaw palms have thin leaves compared to other palms, and often have a visible spear shaped top. They are very common around Mato Grosso do Sul and the surrounding states, but can be seen much further out sometimes. These palms should be used with caution, and single trees are much less of an indicator than multiple trees.

metas.name: Brazil - MaranhÃ£o wide insulators
metas.description: Poles with these wide insulators in a trident formation are common in MaranhÃ£o. The insulator itself is common across many states, but not in this configuration.

metas.name: Brazil - Mato Grosso pole
metas.description: Poles that have one insulator on top and alternating horizontal insulators can be found in Mato Grosso and southern Acre. It is also very rare in Rio Grande do Sul.

metas.name: Brazil - ParanÃ¡ pines
metas.description: These distinct trees, called ParanÃ¡ pines, have long horizontal branches with leaves only at the end. They grow mainly in the southern Brazilian states of ParanÃ¡, Santa Catarina, and Rio Grande do Sul.

metas.name: Brazil - ParanÃ¡ pole markings
metas.description: Pole IDs in ParanÃ¡ are usually made up of black paint and yellow or white painted text.

metas.name: Brazil - PiauÃ­ road
metas.description: Most roads in PiauÃ­ have red gravel on the side of the road. Some roads in Generation 4 now have tarmac and kerbs, but some gravel shoulders remain.

metas.name: Brazil - Rolling grassy hills
metas.description: Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro and EspÃ­rito Santo often have rolling grassy hills.

metas.name: Brazil - Rural Roraima
metas.description: Rural locations in Roraima are mostly open grassy plains with large, distant mountains in the background. Occasionally, you are on roads within the mountains. Furthermore, the grass in Roraima is distinctly thin, and grows in bunches.

metas.name: Brazil - Sugarcane plantations
metas.description: Sugarcane plantations are by far most common in the state of SÃ£o Paulo, and in the coastal north east states, especially Alagoas and Pernambuco.

metas.name: Brazil - Very tall grass
metas.description: Very tall grass can be often seen in the centre of the country, most notably in the Tocantins, GoiÃ¡s, Bahia, and Minas Gerais states.

metas.name: Cambodia - Unique car
metas.description: This back of the google car with white stripe on the left, and a yellow stripe on the right is unique to cambodia.

metas.name: Canada - 45Â° angle transformers
metas.description: Transformers on Prince Edward Island and Nova Scotia will be installed at a 45Â° angle relative to the road. On PEI, red numbers will usually be written on the side.

metas.name: Canada - Concrete barriers
metas.description: British Columbia predominantly uses concrete barriers instead of guardrails.

metas.name: Canada - Manitoba bollards
metas.description: Manitoba uses black and grey painted bollards. Most of the time an orange stripe will be present below the grey one.
metas.comparison: Wooden, rectangular bollards of this form are typically found further north in Manitoba NOTE: Bollards in this format with just a black top are seen in Manitoba and Saskatchewan.

metas.name: Canada - Manitoba stop signs
metas.description: You can sometimes find a green and white striped sticker on signposts in Manitoba.

metas.name: Canada - Newfoundland bins
metas.description: Bins made of wood planks can be seen on Newfoundland driveways. These are most commonly octagonal, however they can have other shapes.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Although they are most common in Newfoundland, they can also sometimes be seen in other provinces, such as New Brunswick.

metas.name: Canada - Newfoundland fire hydrant markers
metas.description: Fire hydrants in Newfoundland often have a diamond-shaped marker next to them.

metas.name: Canada - Ontario diamonds
metas.description: You can find these diamond-shaped markers on the sides of the roads in Ontario. The colours can vary.

metas.name: Canada - Ontario guard rails
metas.description: In Ontario, you will often see these types of guardrails. They consist of cylindrical wooden posts, held together by precisely three metal wires. Some posts are marked by a reflective white band.

metas.name: Canada - Ontario traffic cones
metas.description: Ontario uses distinct orange and black striped traffic cones.

metas.name: Canada - Quebec double sign post
metas.description: Double sign posts on warning sings in Canada is unique to Quebec.

metas.name: Canada - Quebec guardrail bollards
metas.description: Quebec has unique bollards that are always attached to guardrails. They are long, thin white poles with a red or green reflector at the top.

metas.name: Canada - Quebec pole stickers
metas.description: QuÃ©bec poles may sometimes have a vertical black and yellow label. There is a small âQâ in the black part.

metas.name: Canada - Quebec rectangle markers
metas.description: You can find these rectangular markers on the sides of the roads in QuÃ©bec. The colours can vary.

metas.name: Canada - Sask alt insulators
metas.description: Pole top insulators in Saskatchewan alternate. While one pole will have one insulator on the left and two on the right, the next will have two on the left and one on the right.(might sometimes rarely find it in Manitoba(i think lol))

metas.name: Canada - Sask stop sign white triangles.
metas.description: Those white triangles(can be different ammount of them) on signposts of stop signs are unique to  Saskatchewan.

metas.name: Canada - Sask white dashes between lines
metas.description: Those white dashes between yellow lines are most commonly found in Saskatchewan. You can also sometimes find them in BC but the landscape will be way different.

metas.name: Canada - Transformers facing the road
metas.description: The transformers on poles will face the road in British Columbia and New Brunswick, while in other provinces, it will be parallel with the wires.

metas.name: Canada - Wooden post pyramid top
metas.description: In Newfoundland and Labrador, most wooden posts on guardrails have this pyramid shaped top. Occasionally, you can spot them on standalone posts and signposts as well.

metas.name: Colombia - Antioquia pole paint
metas.description: These pole markings with one short black strip on the top and bottom, and a longer yellow section in the middle, are most commonly found in the Antioquia department. Sometimes, you can find them in the Cordoba department as well.

metas.name: Czechia - Arrow-shaped signs
metas.description: Czechia uses arrow-shaped directional signs with a filled in tip. Due to the shape, they are recognizable from behind.

metas.name: Ecuador - Ecuador shitcam
metas.description: If you have vibes that you are in South America and coverage was taken using "shitcam" camera you gonna be in Ecuador. There is "shitcam" in other countries but in South America you can only find "shitcam" in Ecuador.
metas.comparison: Note: Ecuador also has GEN3(and little bit of GEN4) coverage not only shitcam! So don't discard Ecuador if it's not shitcam.

metas.name: Gibraltar - Gibraltar silver tip antenna
metas.description: That long antenna with a silver tip on google car is mostly found in Gibraltar.
metas.comparison: It's British Overseas Territory so you will see a lot of English, UK license plates(back yellow, front white) but remember that Gibraltar drives on the right.

metas.name: Greece - Greece double white lines
metas.description: In Greece you will commonly see slightly faded, solid white double middle lines. This can be used to distinguish it from most other Mediterranean countries.

metas.name: India - Assam pole top
metas.description: Trident poletops with the tip of the middle bar bent at a 90Â° angle can be found in Assam.

metas.name: India - Assamese language
metas.description: Assamese, mainly found in Assam, also uses the Bengali script, with the addition of some characters, most notably à§° and à§±.

metas.name: India - Bihar pole paint
metas.description: Pole paint consisting of exactly four thicker black and yellow stripes can be found in Bihar.

metas.name: India - Bihar tree paint
metas.description: In Bihar, and less commonly Jharkhand, you may find trees with four red and white stripes painted near the bottom.

metas.name: India - Flat Guna tiles
metas.description: Flat Guna tiles is just a tiled roof full of staple-shaped tiles. It can be found around Prayagraj, south east of Uttar Pradesh state,

metas.name: India - Flat tiles
metas.description: Flat tiles seem to be the worst type of tile by their appearance. They are mainly found in Madhya Pradesh and southern Uttar pradesh.

metas.name: India - Gujarat holey poles
metas.description: Concrete holey poles are unique to Gujarat and the Union territory of Daman and Diu, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli.

metas.name: India - Guna tiles
metas.description: It has âUâ shape but there is a flatter shaped tile connecting tiles to each other.
metas.comparison: Itâs very common in southeastern Uttar Pradesh, western Bihar and rarely in northeastern Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand.

metas.name: India - Indent poles
metas.description: Poles divided in two sections, in a similar fashion to Brazilian poles, are common in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

metas.name: India - Kannada Language
metas.description: Kannada is found in Karnataka and has a script with a lot of smooth curves and small circles. Many characters also feature a distinct squiggly tail in the top right corner, which is less common in Telugu. It is very similar to the Telugu script(but that one has usually "checkmarks" on top of letters.

metas.name: India - Kerala yellow marking
metas.description: You can commonly find those small yellow pole markings in Kerala. Other states might have sometimes yellow markings like that but they are just way more rare.

metas.name: India - Madhya Pradesh pole
metas.description: Poles in Madhya Pradesh often have a metal bar shaped like an upside down A slightly below the top of the pole.

metas.name: India - Malayalam language
metas.description: The Malayalam script can be found in Kerala and mostly consists of somewhat simple-looking curvy letters, often containing upside-down U-shapes.

metas.name: India - Manipur metal trident pole top
metas.description: In Manipur you can often find trident poletops on poles made entirely out of metal. They sometimes have small bars on the top of the trident.

metas.name: India - Marathi language
metas.description: Marathi, found in Maharashtra, also uses the Devanagari script so basically looks like hindi but if you can see the letter à¤³ that means it's Marathi. Sometimes you won't see that letter so don't rule out Maharashtra.

metas.name: India - Odia language
metas.description: The Oriya script is found in Odisha and has a curvy look, with many letters having wide semi-circles covering the top. Many letters have a distinct diacritic in the shape of a wide curve above the top of the letter. A useful mnemonic is that the shape of the characters resembles ð emoji.

metas.name: India - Punjab electricity boxes
metas.description: Electricity boxes what are mint green with small window-like squares are almost exclusive to Punjab.
metas.comparison: You can rarely see them in Haryana

metas.name: India - Punjabi language
metas.description: Punjabi can be found in Punjab in northwestern India. While the script looks somewhat similar to Hindi, it can generally be differentiated by the softer shape of the letters and the horizontal bar being broken over certain letters. It also has some distinctly different features, such as the letters à¨¨, à¨² and à¨.

metas.name: India - Tamil language
metas.description: The Tamil script is found in Tamil Nadu and has a distinct combination of curves, straight lines and 90Â° angles. Some letters also have diacritics shaped like dots.

metas.name: India - Tamil Nadu paint
metas.description: Markings on poles and trees, consisting of one black stripe in-between two white ones, are common in Tamil Nadu.

metas.name: India - Telugu language
metas.description: Telugu, found in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh has script with a lot of smooth curves and circles. It looks similar to Kannada language but you can see a lot of distinct "checkmarks" on top of the letters.

metas.name: India - Trapez pole top
metas.description: A connector on the pole which looks like an upside down trapezoid is most common in Chhattisgarh and somewhat common in Meghalaya, Tripura and Maharashtra, but can rarely be found in many other states.
metas.comparison: NOTE: They can also be paired with Holey Poles in Gujarat and Ladder Poles in Andhra Pradesh, thus only use the trapezoid when no other pole meta is present.

metas.name: India - Upside down triangle pole
metas.description: Upside down triangle poletops placed below the top of the pole are commonly found in Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, and less commonly in Madhya Pradesh.

metas.name: India - Wide W tiles
metas.description: This type of tile is like a larger kind of W tile. Another way to tell it apart is the small pike in the middle of the tile.
metas.comparison: It is very common in West Bengal, eastern Jharkhand and eastern Bihar, but doesnât go further north than Purnia, Bihar.

metas.name: India - Window pole top
metas.description: Small metal poletops in the shape of a window are found in Punjab(super common) and Haryana.

metas.name: Indonesia - Bali vibes
metas.description: Architecture in Bali is unique because it was influenced by old Balinese culture and Hinduism. The most important thing to look for crown-like roof pinnacles, found everywhere in Bali. Guardian statues and slit-drum towers are common too. Andesite, a dark, volcanic rock, is a common building material in Bali. You can often see gates, walls, and other intricately carved ornaments built from this material.

metas.name: Indonesia - North Sumatra pole
metas.description: These poles are almost exclusive to North Sumatra. The bar which holds the insulators is even, but features uneven insulators with one on one side and two on the other.

metas.name: Indonesia - Nusa pole
metas.description: On the Lesser Sunda Islands (âNusasâ), you can find poles with an extra long support on the pole top. Sometimes, two supports can be present.

metas.name: Italy - Guardrail endings
metas.description: Italian guardrails commonly end in this distinct shape. The guardrail gets flatter, wider, and it bends away from the road.(San Marino can have same guardrail ending)

metas.name: Japan - Chubu Plate
metas.description: Chubu plate is super unique because of the rounded shape, you can spot it from far away.

metas.name: Japan - Chubu triangle mount
metas.description: Transformers in Chubu are often attached with large triangle and horizontal bars.

metas.name: Japan - Chugoku arrow
metas.description: You may sometimes find an orange arrow located above the top most pole plate in Chugoku.

metas.name: Japan - Chugoku cross-shaped bar
metas.description: The transformers in Chugoku, which have a cross-shaped bar attached in the middle of the pole, mounted by a full triangle, will have a long horizontal or short vertical insulator(s) at the end.

metas.name: Japan - Chugoku plate
metas.description: Chugoku plates will have usually written Energia in latin and sometimes they will include logo.

metas.name: Japan - Chugoku pole top
metas.description: This pole top is unique to Chugoku, there is similar version that are more thicc so make sure the pole top is thin like the one on the image.

metas.name: Japan - Hokkaido Plate
metas.description: Hokkaido plate can be recognized by having a lot of numbers in rows of 2.

metas.name: Japan - Hokuriku plates
metas.description: Silver horizontal plates with logo on the top right. NTT plates will be also horizontal(in Tohoku NTT plates are vertical, and only Tohoku plate is horizontal).

metas.name: Japan - Kansai 120 stepdown
metas.description: These attachments with an approximately 120-degree angle can commonly be found on poles in Kansai.

metas.name: Japan - Kansai pole top
metas.description: This tuning fork pole top, with a thin wire and horizontal bar below, is common in the Kansai region. Make sure it looks exactly the same with that little thing on the wires in the middle(idk how to call it lol)

metas.name: Japan - Kansai reflector
metas.description: Tall reflector with washed colors is exclusive to Kansai region.

metas.name: Japan - Kansai transformers
metas.description: The transformers in Kansai have either a straight or zigzag bar mounted on the bottom of a square. The transformer(s) will be mounted on the sides of that same square. (Tohoku transformers are mounted in similar way but the bar will be connected to top of the square)

metas.name: Japan - Kanto plate
metas.description:
Often silver and handwritten characters.
Horizontal characters above three vertical digits.

metas.name: Japan - Kanto tall hat insulators
metas.description: Those insulators are unique to Kanto region and are easy to spot. They have black "hat" on top of white insulator.

metas.name: Japan - Kyushu bulky insulator
metas.description: Black meteor like looking insulator, from far might be confused with Kanto tall-black hat insulator but Kyushu one appears little more bulkier even from far.

metas.name: Japan - Kyushu Plates
metas.description: Distinc logo(sometimes might be missing). Three numbers horizontally near the top, with 4 vertical characters below them on the right(1 kana and 3 numbers).

metas.name: Japan - Kyushu transformers
metas.description: Transformers mounted opposite side of the pole with a straight bar mounted on the side of the pole with 3 insulators on one side at the end.(Okinawa has T shaped bar)

metas.name: Japan - Kyushu/Okinawa guy wire
metas.description: Guy wires that look like paddle are unique to Kyushu and Okinawa.

metas.name: Japan - Kyushu/Okinawa reflector.
metas.description: Protruding bumps, sometimes darker reflector in the middle. Can also be found in Okinawa.

metas.name: Japan - Okinawa plates
metas.description: Plate with multiple numbers and lines in between them. Often will have more than 2 plates.

metas.name: Japan - Okinawa Transformers
metas.description: Transformers mounted opposite side of the pole with a T shaped bar mounted on the side of the pole.(Kyushu has straight bar). Sometimes only 1 transformer is present.

metas.name: Japan - Shikoku cross bar
metas.description: The transformers in Shikoku, which also have a cross-shaped bar attached in the middle of the pole, mounted by a half triangle, will have âhat shapedâ short horizontal insulators at the end.

metas.name: Japan - Shikoku orange band
metas.description: These orange and black bands wrapped around poles can often be found in Shikoku.

metas.name: Japan - Shikoku plate
metas.description: Distinct logo that you can remember since it has 4 dots representing 4 prefectures of Shikoku.

metas.name: Japan - Shikoku reflector
metas.description: 6 small reflectors with a little strip "connecting" them in the middle.

metas.name: Japan - Tohoku plate
metas.description: Silver horizontal plates with logo in top left. NTT plate will be vertical.(In Hokuriku all the plates will be horizontal)

metas.name: Japan - Tohoku reflectors
metas.description: Gray/White and Gray/Yellow reflectors.

metas.name: Japan - Yamaguchi guardrails
metas.description: Yellow guardrails are exclusive to Yamaguchi prefecture.

metas.name: Laos - Vientiane
metas.description: All other Laos coverage was taken with unique google car but if you have a vibe you are in Thailand but you will see yellow plates, ppl are driving on the right etc you will be in capital of Laos - Vientiane.

metas.name: Latvia - Electricity marker
metas.description: You can find these electricity markers in Latvia â they have a distinct shape with a black tip and a different color underneath.

metas.name: Latvia - Hook pole
metas.description: Wooden poles with alternating pattern of hook-shaped insulators are really common in Latvia. They might appear sometimes in other countries but if you see them with flat landscape you gonna be most likely in Latvia(If you vibe baltics). Always try using other clues to confirm it.

metas.name: Malaysia - Alam Flora bins
metas.description: Trash bins with this logo featuring a sunny landscape, saying âAlam Floraâ are found in Pahang, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya. The logo will occasionally be absent, and it will just say âAlam Floraâ.

metas.name: Malaysia - Boomerang lamp
metas.description: This lamp post with a supporting piece of sheet metal resembling a boomerang is found in Sarawak.

metas.name: Malaysia - Isolated rock formations
metas.description: These isolated rock formations, rising abruptly from an otherwise flat landscape, can be found near the Thai border in Perlis state.

metas.name: Malaysia - Johor yellow street signs
metas.description: Yellow street name signs are specific to the state of Johor.

metas.name: Malaysia - Perlis and Kedah bins
metas.description: Trash bins with a logo resembling leaves are found in Perlis and Kedah.

metas.name: Malaysia - S logo bins
metas.description: Trash bins with a logo resembling an âSâ are found in the states of Negeri Sembilan, Malacca and Johor.

metas.name: Malaysia - Sabah pole
metas.description: Thin metal poles with two parallel pole tops are exclusive to the Sabah region of Borneo.

metas.name: Malaysia - Sarawak pole
metas.description: Electricity poles on the Borneo side typically have a 2-1 insulator configuration, and a long diagonal wooden support. They are exclusive to the Sarawak region of the island.

metas.name: Mexico - Agave salmiana
metas.description: Agave salmiana, also known as pulque agaves, have wide, smooth, curling leaves, and a crown-like appearance. They are common in the central Mexican valley and further north around the city of San Luis Potosi.

metas.name: Mexico - Agave tequilana
metas.description: Vast fields of blue agave (Agave tequilana), used to produce tequila, are mostly found in Jalisco and Nayarit.

metas.name: Mexico - Blindingly white soil
metas.description: Almost blindingly white soil in the Yucatan peninsula is most common in Quintana Roo.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This is only consistent in Generation 3.

metas.name: Mexico - Blue Myrtle Cacti
metas.description: The Blue Myrtle Cacti have short arms that uniformly curve and point upwards. It is abundantly found in San Luis Potosi, but also common in Queretaro and Hidalgo.

metas.name: Mexico - Boojum trees
metas.description: Boojum trees can be recognized by their alien, tentacle-like appearance. They are almost exclusively found in the southern half of Baja California.

metas.name: Mexico - Brittlebush
metas.description: Brittlebush are small shrubs with bright silver-grey leaves that are most commonly found in Sonora, especially around Hermosillo.

metas.name: Mexico - Chihuahua cross
metas.description: A thick cross can be seen on the back of signs in Chihuahua.

metas.name: Mexico - Cobblestone pavement
metas.description: This style of cobblestone pavement, unorganised with irregular tiles, can be found in most of the central states, but is by far most commonly found in the states of Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima, and Queretaro.

metas.name: Mexico - Concrete hanging insulator pole
metas.description: These concrete poles with insulators suspended below the crossbars are unique to the Yucatan peninsula.

metas.name: Mexico - Guanajuato extremely dark fields
metas.description: Extremely dark fields are common in Guanajuato.

metas.name: Mexico - Hexagonal tiles pavement
metas.description: This pavement consisting of hexagonal tiles is found in Puebla and Tlaxcala.

metas.name: Mexico - Light coloured rock walls
metas.description: These walls made of light coloured rock are found in the Yucatan peninsula, but most common in Yucatan state.
metas.comparison: Comment from Vincent: When not in the sun, the rock walls appear darker, but it's likely the same type of rock.

metas.name: Mexico - Nayarit bollard
metas.description: Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit, apart from one exception being Federal Highway 190 on the Oaxaca-Chiapas border.

metas.name: Mexico - Oaxaca pavement
metas.description: This exact pavement design with three lines of cobblestone patterning is exclusive to Oaxaca.

metas.name: Mexico - Oil palm plantations
metas.description: Oil palm plantations are most common in Chiapas, and occasionally on the outskirts of the state in Veracruz, Tabasco, and Campeche.

metas.name: Mexico - Red agricultural fields
metas.description: Red agricultural fields are commonly seen in Zacatecas and occasionally southern Durango.

metas.name: Mexico - Saguaro Cacti
metas.description: The Saguaro Cacti can be spotted in the western half of Sonora, featuring short curving arms that stem from a main trunk.

metas.name: Mexico - Wooden hanging insulator pole
metas.description: The wooden variant of the hanging pole is found on the Baja California peninsula.

metas.name: New Zealand - Marlborough possum guard
metas.description: Most utility poles in the Marlborough region have a long square shaped olive-brown possum guard. These can appear alongside the usual shorter silver possum guards.

metas.name: New Zealand - Timaru orange sticker
metas.description: Poles near Timaru often have a tall rectangle of orange paint on them with the text âDANGER LIVE WIRESâ.

metas.name: Norway - Bamboo snow poles
metas.description: Bamboo snow poles are regional and can mostly be found in Innlandet, Akershus, Ãstfold, Buskerud and Vestfold but can also be found rarely in TrÃ¸ndelag, Vestland, Agder, Telemark and Rogaland.

metas.name: Portugal - Side walks
metas.description: Cobblestone sidewalks made of distinctly bright stones are very common in Portugal.

metas.name: Slovakia - Blue directional signs
metas.description: Slovakia uses blue directional signs, with small white arrows.
metas.comparison: This is mostly tip to differentiate it from Czechia which uses arrow-shaped signs.

metas.name: South Africa - Bird nests pole top
metas.description: Big bird nests on top of poles are commonly seen in the northern part of the Northern Cape Province.

metas.name: South Africa - Blue back of google car(GEN4)
metas.description: If you see blue back of the google car with/or without antenna you can be only in South Africa or Europe.
metas.comparison: With yellow outer lines and driving left you are gonna be only in South Africa.

metas.name: South Africa - KwaZulu trident pole top
metas.description: Trident pole tops are almost unique to KwaZulu-Natal.

metas.name: South Africa - WC pole top
metas.description: Poles with 3 bars forming the letter âAâ, with the bottom insulators being attached at the edges of a horizontal bar, can be found almost exclusively in Western Cape, and rarely in bordering provinces.

metas.name: South Korea - Jeju vulcanic rocks
metas.description: Jeju is a volcanic island that has a lot of rock walls, made of dark volcanic rocks.

metas.name: Spain - Aragon Bollards
metas.description: In AragÃ³n, it is common to see this bollard design on regional roads.
metas.comparison: It has a simple design, consisting of a short flat rectangular white stick with a grey reflector on both sides. NOTE: There are similar bollards in other regions, but they appear much less frequently than in AragÃ³n.

metas.name: Spain - Asturias snow poles
metas.description: Yellow snow poles with one or two reflectors are unique to Asturias. They are usually found in the south of the region.

metas.name: Spain - Catalan language - carrer
metas.description: If you're in Spain and see a street sign with "Carrer" instead of "Calle", you're likely in a Catalan-speaking region, such as Catalonia, Valencia, or the Balearic Islands.
metas.comparison: Andorra also uses Catalan as its official language.

metas.name: Spain - Cogersa bins
metas.description: Trash containers in Asturias frequently have the logo of COGERSA, the logoâs shape is distinct and can be recognized from afar.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Recycling bins can also feature this logo.

metas.name: Spain - Extremadura bollards
metas.description: In the region of Extremadura, it is common to see the normal Spanish bollards with green tops. This bollard variant is exclusive to this region.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Gen4 low cam
metas.description:
All the Gen4 coverage taken in Sri Lanka is low-cam(gen3 coverage in Sri Lanka is not low cam), the only two other countries with low-cam is Japan and Switzerland but they look different.
You can recognize lowcam because of wide blur of the street view car and lower vantage point compared to normal camera.

metas.name: Sweden - M letter sign
metas.description: On smaller roads, it is common to see these blue signs with a large white M.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Similar signs can be found in Norway, however the font is distinctly different. The middle point of the M extends to the bottom of the letter. There are no similar signs in Finland.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Scottish passing place signs
metas.description: These âPassing Placeâ signs are unique to Scotland.

metas.name: United States - Minnesota bridge signs
metas.description: In Minnesota, these yellow signs with vertical, black triangles are placed before bridges at most major river crossings and at the beginnings and ends of guardrail sections on large highways.

metas.name: United States - Montana/SD bollard
metas.description: The most common type of roadside bollard in South Dakota and Montana features a dark metal post with a white diamond on each side of the top.

metas.name: United States - Nevada bollard
metas.description: This bollard is found in Nevada. It consists of a reflector on a thin stick. The reflector is a vertical rectangle that consists of a white field surrounded by a black outline.

metas.name: United States - Saguaro Cactus
metas.description: In US you can find this cactus(tall,thick upward-curving arms) south of Arizona.
metas.comparison: You can find same cactus in Mexico over the border in Sonora or similar one in north of Argentina.

metas.name: United States - Square guardrail
metas.description: You can find those square guardrails mostly in state of New York and Wyoming.
metas.comparison: You can rarely see them in states close to New York state.

metas.name: United States - Washington bollard
metas.description: The state of Washington uses bollards that consist of a white or brown post with a white rectangle on the front of the bollard, and two smaller white or silver squares on the back of the bollard.

metas.name: United States - West Virginia fraction signs
metas.description: West Virginia sometimes features street signs with a symbol that resembles a fraction inside a circle.

metas.name: Vietnam - 75% holey pole
metas.description:
Concrete poles with holes running up to 75% of the height of it are found almost exclusively in northern Vietnam.
Note: there is poles that holes goes up to 50% of the height all over Vietnam.

metas.name: Vietnam - Central A-shape poletop
metas.description: Central A-shaped top is where you can see an A standing on the crossbar. It can be centered or off to the side. It is almost exclusively found in central Vietnam.

metas.name: Vietnam - Dalat green houses
metas.description: Greenhouses can be found in ÄÃ  Láº¡t valley.

metas.name: Vietnam - Dragonfruit plantations
metas.description: Dragonfruit plantations are most common in BÃ¬nh Thuáº­n, but can be found all over the south.

metas.name: Vietnam - North canals
metas.description: Low-lying, agricultural plains sometimes accompanied with canals are common around Nam Äá»nh and southern Hanoi.
metas.comparison: Note: You can also find canals max south of the country but they will have different landscape.

metas.name: Vietnam - One sided pole top
metas.description: One sided top is where the pole has the crossbar on one side with a single diagonal support beam. It can either be completely on one side or uneven to one side. Important to note that you should not confuse it with trapezoid support which has an extra horizontal segment in the support beam.
metas.comparison: It is almost exclusively found in the far south.

metas.name: Vietnam - Pepper plantations
metas.description: Pepper planations are most commonly found in Dak Nong, Dak Lak, and Gia Lai provinces.

metas.name: Vietnam - Plain concrete pole.
metas.description: Plain concrete poles without holes or pinholes are almost exclusively found in northern part of the country.

metas.name: Vietnam - Rubber trees
metas.description: Rubber tree plantations are primarily found in the provinces to the north of Ho Chi Minh City, as well as in several parts of the Central Highlands.
metas.comparison: Rubber trees can be recognized by their thin trunks. In Vietnam, it is typical for a section of the tree trunk to be wrapped in a piece of plastic. These trees tend to be neatly organized in a dense grid-like pattern.

metas.name: Vietnam - Side mounted lamp
metas.description: Lamp mounted to the side of the pole with 2 brackets is only found in the region shown on second image.

metas.name: Vietnam - South Canals
metas.description: Canals are very commonly found in the Mekong Delta. Canals can also be found in the north, but the landscape is very different.

metas.name: Vietnam - Spools pole
metas.description: Mounted spools are spools mounted directly to the pole. It is almost exclusive to the far south of the country .

metas.name: Vietnam - Traditional architecture
metas.description: Traditional architecture can mostly be found in the north, but can be seen in Äáº¯k Láº¯k and Gia Lai. The landscape will generally be flatter in those two areas, which can be a good clue for that area.

metas.name: Vietnam - triangle supports
metas.description: When two supports of the main crossbar of the pole form triangle it should put you south of the country.
metas.comparison: There is similar support that looks like trapezoid so make sure it's actually triangle. Note: I found those poles rarely north but there was always some other clue to know it's not south.

metas.name: Vietnam - tripple trapezoid pole
metas.description: Poles with 3 half trapezoid supports on a side are exclusively found in the North of the country.

metas.name: Vietnam - Ventilation electric box
metas.description: Meter Box Designs with trap door style windows plus ventilation slits on the sides are very common in the province of Khanh Hoa. It can be found everywhere in the province from rural villages to coastal areas.
metas.comparison: Note: Other regular Meter box designs can be found throughout the whole country.

metas.name: ACT gap reflector
metas.description: If you see gap and reflector in between outer lines you gonna be in ACT.
metas.comparison: (South Australia might have gaps in outerlines but reflector in a gap is super rare there)

metas.name: Melbourne white blue sticker
metas.description: Those white-blue stickers on poles are unique to Melbourne in Australia.

metas.name: NSW guardrail ending
metas.description: Guardrail ending, featuring a black dash on a yellow background, is almost exclusive to New South Wales and the ACT.

metas.name: NSW red no stopping sign
metas.description: New South Wales is the only state to use red âNo Stoppingâ signs.

metas.name: NSW yellow plates.
metas.description: If you see more than couple yellow plates in Australia you should be in NSW

metas.name: NT pole
metas.description: Rusty metal holey poles are unique to Northern Territory state in Australia.

metas.name: QLD A6 pole top
metas.description: This poletop is unique to QLD and most commonly you can find it on A6 highway.

metas.name: QLD black paint
metas.description: These black markings are specific to electricity poles in Queensland(from Gold Coast to Sunshine Coast). They are often accompanied by diagonal numbers.

metas.name: QLD non south-east pole marking
metas.description: If you see this grayish long thin plate with numbers, sometimes with extra blue(or other color) little circle marking you gonna be in QLD(not in south east most likely because they use different marking).

metas.name: Roma bottle trees
metas.description: If you see couple of those cool bottle trees planted next to the road you will be in Roma in Australia.

metas.name: SA flat sign posts
metas.description: You can only find flat signposts in South Australia and Western Australia (in WA they mostly will be yellow but not always). You will also find rounded sign posts in SA (so don't rule SA if you see rounded one).

metas.name: SA property markers
metas.description: You can find these white property markers on the sides of roads in South Australia.

metas.name: SA stobie pole
metas.description: The iconic Stobie pole, made of steel and concrete, is specific to South Australia.(A few thousand of these poles can be found in other states, most notably Tasmania - super rare)

metas.name: Tasmania pole metas
metas.description: Metas for Tasmiania poles:

metas.name: Vic pole top
metas.description: Victorian pole tops feature 3 circular coils; 2 on the sides, and 1 vertical one at the top.(sometimes might be missing the top one)

metas.name: Victoria hydrant bollard
metas.description: You can find these white hydrant poles that feature a blue circle and a red section on top of it in Victoria.(they have couple different designs but they all follow same color/shape +/- pattern)

metas.name: WA bollard
metas.description: Bollards with brown paint at the bottom are most commonly found in Western Australia.

metas.name: wa pole metas
metas.description: Western Australia pole metas:

metas.name: WA property marker
metas.description: You can find these dark green property markers on the sides of roads in Western Australia.

metas.name: WA stripy bollard
metas.description: Black-and-white stripy bollards are unique to Western Australia.

metas.name: WA yellow sign posts
metas.description: Yellow signposts are specific to Western Australia.

metas.name: Botswana - Vibes
metas.description:
A dry, flat landscape with African vegetation, usually a bit away from the road, is a good clue for Botswana and becomes quite distinct after seeing it couple times.
You can confirm it's Botswana by the white back of the Google car, driving on the left, yellow outer lines, and the sun in the north.
metas.comparison: The only other countries in Africa with that combination are:

metas.name: Eswatini - Vibes
metas.description: Eswatiniâs landscape is characterized by green, wooded hills and tall golden grass. Poles are made of dark brown wood and have a simple design, with insulators mostly mounted on the side.
metas.comparison: You can confirm it's Eswatini by the white back of the Google car, driving on the left, yellow outer lines, and the sun in the north. The only other countries in Africa with that combination are:

metas.name: Ghana - Unique car
metas.description: All regular road coverage in Ghana features a unique Google car with a visible roof rack and a piece of black tape on the right end of the front bar. The hood is usually visible, displaying a Street View car wrapping with a red rectangle and other distinctive elements.

metas.name: Kenya - Follow car
metas.description: In some of the Kenya coverage, you will be followed by a grey Toyota SUV.

metas.name: Kenya - Pickup car
metas.description:
Sometimes you won't see Kenya snorkle and instead you will see gray/white pickup car with/without antenna and sometimes it might be even fully blurred.
But if you have a vibe that you are in Africa and you see pickup truck and you are driving on the left side you should be in Kenya(Or Namibia).
metas.comparison: Note:Other countries in Africa with pickup truck coverage drive on the right.

metas.name: Kenya - Unique car
metas.description: If you see a snorkel on the Google car, youâre in Kenya.
metas.comparison: However, the car is sometimes seen without it, so donât rule out Kenya if the snorkel isnât visible.

metas.name: Lesotho - Landscape
metas.description: One of the best ways to identify Lesotho is by its characteristic âLesotho mountains.â These mountains are bare and treeless, often with tabletop-like shapes and recognizable horizontal rocky ridgelines.
metas.comparison:
You can confirm it's Lesotho by the white back of the Google car, driving on the left, yellow outer lines, and the sun in the north. The only other countries in Africa with that combination are: Eswatini (the hills there have trees and usually tall golden grass around)
Botswana (which is super flat)
South Africa (though this is rare, as most of the coverage now uses the blue back of the Google car).

metas.name: Namibia - Pickup truck
metas.description: Namibia is the newest African country with coverage featuring the white pickup truck.
metas.comparison: The landscape is similar to Botswanaâflat and dry. Roads typically have yellow outer lines, and driving is on the left side. Note: You may not always be on main roads with outer yellow lines. In such cases, it can resemble some parts of Kenya, which also drives on the left and sometimes features the white pickup truck.

metas.name: Nigeria - Police follow car
metas.description: In Nigeria, Street View coverage often includes a police escort car visible "behind" the Street View car. However, it may sometimes be missing, so donât rule out Nigeria if you donât see it.

metas.name: Rwanda - Unique car
metas.description: If you see a pickup truck with a red brake light on top in Africa, you're most likely in Rwanda.
metas.comparison: The car can be white, black, or brown, but it will always have this red brake light. Sometimes, the car might be fully blurred, so donât rule out Rwanda if you donât see it. Note: Similar car can be found in Ecuador so check surroundings before making a guess.

metas.name: Senegal - Blue plates
metas.description: Blue license plates in Africa are unique to Senegal, sometimes you might find license plates that looks like standard europe license plate.

metas.name: Senegal - French infrastructure
metas.description: Senegal used to be French colony so you will see similar ladder poles/bollards/lines that you would normally find in France.

metas.name: Senegal - Pickup truck
metas.description: All of gen4 coverage in Senegal was taken using pickup truck. It's mostly silver/white(rarely black). If you are driving on the right side in Africa and see this pickup truck you should be in Senegal.
metas.comparison:
Note:
Sometimes car will be fully blurred so check around to learn how Senegal looks like. You can find similar car in Nigeria but usually you can see police car escorting google car "behind you" or in Kenya but they drive on the left side there.

metas.name: Senegal - Roof Rack car meta
metas.description: Google Car with a visible roof rack and the right side mirror is seen in Generation 3 Senegal coverage. Rifts can also be seen in the sky.

metas.name: South Africa - Bird Pole
metas.description: The most common type of pole in South Africa features 1 to 5 horizontal bars with thin white insulators that resemble rows of birds, which is why they are referred to as âbird polesâ in the community.

metas.name: South Africa - Yellow Outer Lines
metas.description: In South Africa, most paved roads have single yellow outer lines and white center lines. This can be used to differentiate from Australia which has only white lines and never single yellow lines.
metas.comparison: REMEMBER:

metas.name: Uganda - Unique car
metas.description: Uganda's unique Google car is white with visible square mirrors, and its coverage is limited to Kampala. Some national parks in Uganda are covered with different cars, but these are quite rare.

metas.name: Albania - Rifts
metas.description: If you look up and see a "rift" in the sky, this glitch is most commonly found in Albania or Montenegro within Europe. Most of the time, you will see it, but if you donât, donât rule out these countries.

metas.name: Andorra - Stone buildings
metas.description: Andorra has a lot of these distinct stone buildings, visible almost everywhere in the country.
metas.comparison: These buildings can also be found near Andorra, in the French and Spanish Pyrenees.

metas.name: Austria - Bollard
metas.description: Austria's bollards are white with a black top and dark red or grey reflectors, often featuring a nipple-shaped black cap and sometimes a snow pole.
metas.comparison: Sloveniaâs bollards are similar but always have a white back reflector, whereas in Austria, white reflectors are rare but possible.

metas.name: Belgium - Reddish license plates
metas.description: Belgian license plates should have a red tint visible through the blur because they use red text on a white license plate.

metas.name: Bulgaria - Alternating pole top
metas.description: This style of pole top, featuring 3 large, alternating insulators shaped like upward-facing hooks, is a good clue for Bulgaria. This pole top is likely unique to the country.

metas.name: Bulgaria - Small alternating hooks
metas.description: Most poles in Bulgaria have small, alternating hook-shaped insulators, which can also be found in other countries (mostly on wooden poles, like Latvia, North Macedonia, and a few others). However, if you see them on a concrete pole, you're most likely in Bulgaria. Try using other clues to confirm.

metas.name: Bulgaria - Town signs
metas.description: Town entry signs in Bulgaria have a simple white design and use both the Cyrillic and Latin alphabets. Like directional signs, the two lines of text are clear and visible even from a distance.

metas.name: Croatia - Bollard
metas.description: Croatian bollards are white with a black rectangle and a red or white reflector. From the top, they are shaped like a triangle. Hungarian bollards are similar, but the black part with the reflector is positioned further from the top.

metas.name: Czechia - Arrow-shaped signs
metas.description: Czechia uses arrow-shaped directional signs with a filled in tip. Due to the shape, they are recognizable from behind.

metas.name: Czechia - Bollard
metas.description: Bollards in Czechia have orange double reflectors on the front and a single white reflector on the back, with rarer blue and red variants. The same design is also found in Slovakia.

metas.name: Denmark - Bollard
metas.description: Denmark's bollards are white with a yellow reflector and a distinctive dark orange stripe at the top.
metas.comparison: Belgium's bollards are similar but have a rectangular reflector and no orange stripe at the top.

metas.name: Denmark - Piped signs
metas.description: This signpost, where the pipe frame is bent around the sign, is unique to Denmark.

metas.name: Denmark - Street name ending - vej
metas.description: Most Danish street names end in "vej," which means "street" in Danish. Street signs typically have a blue background with white text.

metas.name: Estonia - Bollard
metas.description: Round bollards with a rectangular reflector on the front and two circular reflectors on the back, which can be either white or orange, are common. Latvia's bollards might look similar, but they have a "half-circle" or flat curved shape, and sometimes feature numbers on them.

metas.name: Estonia - Street name ending - tee
metas.description: In Estonia, the words for street and road are "tÃ¤nav" and "tee," respectively. If you see street signs ending in "tee" or "tn" (with "tÃ¤nav" often abbreviated as 'tn'), you know you're in Estonia.

metas.name: Estonia - Street name ending - tn
metas.description: In Estonia, the words for street and road are "tÃ¤nav" and "tee," respectively. If you see street signs ending in "tee" or "tn" (with "tÃ¤nav" often abbreviated as 'tn'), you know you're in Estonia.

metas.name: Finland - Street name ending - tie
metas.description: Street signs in Finland typically have a white background with black text, and most street names end in "tie."

metas.name: France - Blue sticker
metas.description: Small blue rectangular markings on utility poles are unique to France. They are often referred to as âstickersâ by the community, but are actually small plates.

metas.name: France - Bollard
metas.description:
The French bollard is extremely recognizable and appears very often. It is a round white post with a pointed top and a reflector band going all the way around. The band can be grey or red. Some rare variations have a fully red top.
A bollard that is commonly found in Scotland looks similar, but has a blunt top instead of a pointed one.

metas.name: France - Ladder Poles
metas.description:
In France, these concrete ladder poles are pretty common.
They're called "ladder" poles because of its similarity to the steps of a ladder.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Spain can have the same poles, try using landscape or language to tell them apart.

metas.name: France - Road Numbers
metas.description: Small yellow signs displaying the road number, which typically starts with a âDâ, are unique to France. They are commonly placed on top of directional signs or town entry signs.

metas.name: France - Weird roadlines
metas.description: These middle road lines, where each dash consists of two offset blocks, are unique to France. They are not extremely common, but when you see them, you can safely guess France.

metas.name: France - Word for street - RUE
metas.description: The French word for street is ârueâ. Street signs with "rue" can also be found in Belgium.

metas.name: Germany - Bollard
metas.description: Germany uses these black and white bollards, with white and light-grey reflectors. The reflector will be orange on bollards next to intersections. They sometimes have plates containing the road number, and potentially other useful information. Many bollards also feature blue attachments on the side.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Many European countries have similar bollards, however most will have different coloured reflectors. Luxembourg uses almost identical bollards, but they have 3 bolts instead of 2 on the reflector.

metas.name: Greece - Bollard
metas.description: Greek bollards are wedge-shaped with almost square reflectors, being red on the front and white on the back.
metas.comparison: Andorra bollards are similar but landscape/vegetation will be way different most of the time.

metas.name: Greece - Greece double white lines
metas.description: In Greece you will commonly see slightly faded, solid white double middle lines. This can be used to distinguish it from most other Mediterranean countries.

metas.name: Greece - Greek harp pole
metas.description: These distinctive poletops, which have a metal frame shaped vaguely like a harp, are unique to Greece.

metas.name: Greece - Greek lamps
metas.description: Poles in Greece are usually wooden and often will have this lamp with round shade above the light bulb. (You can sometimes find similar lamps in Serbia/North Macedonia so use other clues to confirm it's Greece)

metas.name: Greece - Greek language
metas.description: The Greek language features a unique alphabet not used in any other language. It shares similarities with both the latin and cyrillic alphabet, however the lower case letters generally have softer shapes than the cyrillic letters.

metas.name: Hungary - Bollard
metas.description: Hungarian bollards are black-and-white, wedge-shaped, and typically have a red reflector at the front, and a white reflector at the back. (Croatian bollards are similar but the black part with reflector is closer to the top).

metas.name: Hungary - Holey pole
metas.description: Concrete holey poles with medium-sized holes going all the way to the bottom are common. They are similar to those in Poland and Romania, but Polish poles have holes that don't go all the way to the top or bottom, and Romanian poles are usually wider and painted white at the bottom.

metas.name: Hungary - Kilometer markers
metas.description: These green kilometre markers can be seen along most Hungarian roads.

metas.name: Iceland - Bollards
metas.description: Iceland's yellow bollards with a white reflector are unique and extremely common, found on almost every section of rural road across the country.

metas.name: Ireland - Dashed yellow lines
metas.description: Yellow dashed lines like this are super common in Ireland. You can find sometimes similar lines in New Zealand so if you are not sure use other clues like landscape/vegetation etc.

metas.name: Italy - Bollard
metas.description: Italian bollards are triangular in shape, white with a black top, and feature a red front and a white rear reflector. Albania and San Marino use the same bollards.

metas.name: Italy - Guardrail endings
metas.description: Italian guardrails commonly end in this distinct shape. The guardrail gets flatter, wider, and it bends away from the road.(San Marino can have same guardrail ending)

metas.name: Italy - License plates
metas.description: A short license plate with a double blue strip on the front and a long plate with a double blue strip on the back is unique to Italy. Similar long plates with a double blue strip can be found in Albania and France, but the front plates wonât be short.

metas.name: Latvia - Bollard
metas.description: Half-circle/flat curved shape bollards with a rectangular reflector on the front and two circular reflectors on the back are common. The reflectors can be white or orange, and sometimes these bollards have numbers on them.
metas.comparison: Estonian bollards might look similar, but they have a rounded shape and will never have numbers on them.

metas.name: Latvia - Electricity marker
metas.description: You can find these electricity markers in Latvia â they have a distinct shape with a black tip and a different color underneath.

metas.name: Latvia - Hook pole
metas.description: Wooden poles with alternating pattern of hook-shaped insulators are really common in Latvia. They might appear sometimes in other countries but if you see them with flat landscape you gonna be most likely in Latvia(If you vibe baltics). Always try using other clues to confirm it.

metas.name: Latvia - Street name ending - iela
metas.description: The Latvian word for street is "iela." This word is unique to Latvian, so if you see a street sign with it, you can be sure you're in Latvia.

metas.name: Lithuania - Bollard
metas.description: Lithuanian bollards are wedge-shaped with rectangular reflectors: an orange one on the front and a white one on the back.

metas.name: Lithuania - Street name ending - g.
metas.description: The Lithuanian word for street is "gatvÄ," often abbreviated as "g." on street signs. If you see a street sign ending in "g.," you're likely in Lithuania.
metas.comparison: This word is almost entirely unique to Lithuanian, though very rarely, you might see "gatve" (abbreviated as "gat.") in the Latvian capital, Riga.

metas.name: Luxembourg - Bollard
metas.description: Bollards in Luxembourg are black and white, wedge-shaped, and feature grey reflectors. Some have a distinctive indent in the lower half.
metas.comparison: They look very similar to German bollards, with the main difference being that the reflectors on German bollards are attached with two bolts, while those in Luxembourg have three.

metas.name: Luxembourg - Yellow license plates
metas.description:
Luxembourg uses long yellow plates with a blue strip on the left.
Since Luxembourg is a small country, foreign cars with white plates are somewhat common.
metas.comparison: There are only a few other European countries that use yellow plates for private vehicles:

metas.name: Malta - Vibes
metas.description: If you see a license plate with a blue strip while driving left with this climate/landscape, you know you're in Malta. If you can't see the driving direction, use other clues like limestone rock walls to recognize Malta.

metas.name: Montenegro - Rifts
metas.description: If you look up and see a "rift" in the sky, this glitch is most commonly found in Albania or Montenegro within Europe. Most of the time, you will see it, but if you donât, donât rule out these countries.

metas.name: Netherlands - Yellow plates
metas.description: If you see yellow license plates on both the front and back in Europe with a super flat landscape, itâs likely the Netherlands. Luxembourg also uses all-yellow plates but is much hillier. Denmark may have yellow plates for commercial vehicles, so use other clues like architecture, bike lanes, and surroundings to confirm itâs the Netherlands.

metas.name: North Macedonia - Bollard
metas.description: North Macedonia uses two types of bollards. One is rounded and very thin, while the other one is wedge-shaped(looks like Croatia bollard). They both are white and have red or white reflectors, typically on a black surface.

metas.name: Norway - Bamboo snow poles
metas.description: Bamboo snow poles are regional and can mostly be found in Innlandet, Akershus, Ãstfold, Buskerud and Vestfold but can also be found rarely in TrÃ¸ndelag, Vestland, Agder, Telemark and Rogaland.

metas.name: Norway - Green Plates
metas.description: In Norway, commercial plates are green. These can often be seen on vans or big trucks(not semi-trucks).
metas.comparison: NOTE: In Europe, green licence plates are almost unique to Norway, but can also be found on electric vehicles in Hungary and Romania.

metas.name: Norway - Long outer lines
metas.description: If you see long dashed outer lines, you'll know it's Norway. You can find similar dashed lines with the same climate in Sweden, but they will be half the length, and Finland uses full outer lines.
metas.comparison: (N)orway for normal, (S)weden for short, and (F)inland for full.

metas.name: Norway - Long yellow-orange middle lines.
metas.description: Many larger roads in Norway have solid outer lines and yellow middle lines. The yellow lines have a distinct tinge of orange, making them easily recognizable.

metas.name: Poland - Bollard
metas.description: Polish bollards feature a red strip that wraps around the entire bollard, with a red reflector on the front (sometimes hard to see) and a white reflector on the back. They may also have numbers on them. (from Plonkit)

metas.name: Poland - Holey pole
metas.description: Holey poles with smaller holes are common in Poland. Similar poles can be found in Hungary and Romania, but in Poland, the holes don't extend all the way to the bottom or the top.

metas.name: Poland - Town signs
metas.description: Polish entering town signs have green background and white text with distinct font.

metas.name: Portugal - Bollards
metas.description: Portuguese bollards are either wedge-shaped with a noticeably thin white top, or flat with a wide reflector. While most reflectors will be white, you may also find orange reflectors. These are noticeably darker than the yellow reflectors in Spain.

metas.name: Portugal - Chevrons
metas.description: Portuguese chevrons are black with yellow arrows.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Portugal is the only Mediterranean country with this chevron colour scheme.

metas.name: Portugal - License plate
metas.description: Old Portuguese license plates have a yellow strip on the right side. New plates follow the standard EU design without the yellow strip.

metas.name: Portugal - No hunting signs
metas.description: Hunting signs with a red and white color scheme are commonly seen in rural areas of Portugal. They can be either diamond-shaped or rectangular.

metas.name: Portugal - Pole
metas.description: Concrete ladder poles with very tall ladder steps are common in Portugal. Each step often has a small see-through hole.

metas.name: Portugal - Side walks
metas.description: Cobblestone sidewalks made of distinctly bright stones are very common in Portugal.

metas.name: Portugal - Word for street - RUA
metas.description: The Portuguese word for street is âRuaâ.
metas.comparison: NOTE: In Galician, the word for road is âRÃºaâ, with an accent on the âuâ.

metas.name: Romania - Holey pole
metas.description: Concrete holey poles with wide holes and usually painted white at the bottom are common in Romania. They are similar to poles in Poland and Hungary, but Polish poles have smaller holes that donât go all the way to the bottom or top, and Hungarian poles typically have smaller holes as well.

metas.name: Romania - KM Marker
metas.description: Within Europe, those red/blue/white KM markers are unique to Romania, the color representing the color the road will show up on the map.
metas.comparison: How to use: On the side is the road number and usually on the front are two cities, the first one is the closest largest city and the second one is the closest town.

metas.name: Russia - Black sock sign post
metas.description: White signposts painted black at the bottom are very common in both Russia and Kazakhstan. However, Kazakhstan's entire coverage was done with a pickup truck, making it easy to rule out, indicating you're in Russia.

metas.name: Russia - Eastern bollard
metas.description: This unique very thin type of bollard that is attached to a stick is almost exclusively found in eastern part of Russia (east of Omsk +/-). Russia has a lot more different designs of bollards that you can find anywhere(even in eastern part)

metas.name: Serbia - Bollard
metas.description: Serbian bollards might look like Austria/Slovenia bollards but reflector will be always off-center. They have couple other designs but reflector will be always off-center.

metas.name: Slovakia - Blue directional signs
metas.description: Slovakia uses blue directional signs, with small white arrows.
metas.comparison: This is mostly tip to differentiate it from Czechia which uses arrow-shaped signs.

metas.name: Slovakia - Bollard
metas.description: Slovakian bollards have orange double reflectors on the front and a single white reflector on the back, with rarer blue and red variants. The same design is also found in Czechia.

metas.name: Slovenia - Bollard
metas.description: Slovenian bollards are white with a black top, featuring a bright red reflector on the front and a white reflector on the back.
metas.comparison: Austria uses similar bollards, but the back reflector is usually black rather than white.

metas.name: Spain - Aragon Bollards
metas.description: In AragÃ³n, it is common to see this bollard design on regional roads.
metas.comparison: It has a simple design, consisting of a short flat rectangular white stick with a grey reflector on both sides. NOTE: There are similar bollards in other regions, but they appear much less frequently than in AragÃ³n.

metas.name: Spain - Asturias snow poles
metas.description: Yellow snow poles with one or two reflectors are unique to Asturias. They are usually found in the south of the region.

metas.name: Spain - Bollard
metas.description: Standard Spanish bollards have a yellow-orange reflector on the front and two white dots on the back, though the back can sometimes be blank. They are typically hollow.

metas.name: Spain - Catalan language - carrer
metas.description: If you're in Spain and see a street sign with "Carrer" instead of "Calle", you're likely in a Catalan-speaking region, such as Catalonia, Valencia, or the Balearic Islands.
metas.comparison: Andorra also uses Catalan as its official language.

metas.name: Spain - Cogersa bins
metas.description: Trash containers in Asturias frequently have the logo of COGERSA, the logoâs shape is distinct and can be recognized from afar.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Recycling bins can also feature this logo.

metas.name: Spain - Extremadura bollards
metas.description: In the region of Extremadura, it is common to see the normal Spanish bollards with green tops. This bollard variant is exclusive to this region.

metas.name: Spain - Ladder poles
metas.description:
In Spain, these concrete ladder poles can be found amongst other types.
They're called "ladder" poles because of its similarity to the steps of a ladder.
metas.comparison: NOTE: France can have the same poles, try using landscape or language to tell them apart.

metas.name: Spain - No hunting sign
metas.description: In rural areas of Spain, you will often find no hunting signs. There are two versions, both unique to Spain. One is a simple white sign with text starting with "coto" and ending in "caza." The other has a diagonally divided black and white background.

metas.name: Spain - Pedestrian crossing sign
metas.description: Spanish pedestrian crossing signs have 8 stripes. This is the highest number of stripes in Europe, and almost unique to Spain.
metas.comparison: NOTE: The only other European country with 8 stripes is Andorra.

metas.name: Spain - Road Markers
metas.description: Spain has distinct road markers, easy to recognize being usually square and having colourful borders. The code on top is the number of the road.
metas.comparison: NOTE:: The letter codes before the road number on these markers are often an important region-specific clue, check plonkit for all the code regions.

metas.name: Spain - Yellow guardrail reflectors
metas.description: Spain has yellow reflectors on rounded A-type guardrails.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Belgium, Andorra and Gibraltar also have yellow reflectors. For a good overview of European guardrails, see this infographic.

metas.name: Sweden - Blue and yellow chevrons
metas.description: Sweden is the only country in Europe whose chevrons have yellow arrows on a blue background.
metas.comparison: NOTE: While very rare, yellow on blue chevrons also exist in Luxembourg.

metas.name: Sweden - M letter sign
metas.description: On smaller roads, it is common to see these blue signs with a large white M.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Similar signs can be found in Norway, however the font is distinctly different. The middle point of the M extends to the bottom of the letter. There are no similar signs in Finland.

metas.name: Sweden - Short outer lines
metas.description: If you feel like you're in one of the Nordic countries and see short dashed outer lines, you're likely in Sweden. Norway uses long dashed outer lines, and Finland uses full lines. (N)orway for normal, (S)weden for short, and (F)inland for full).
metas.comparison: Warning: Many countries in Europe might also use short or medium dashed outer lines, so be cautious.

metas.name: Switzerland - Low cam
metas.description: All the coverage in Switzerland is taken with a low-cam. The only other two countries with low-cam are Japan and Sri Lanka, but they look different.
metas.comparison: You can recognize low-cam by the wide blur of the Street View car and the lower vantage point compared to the normal camera.

metas.name: Turkey - Bollard
metas.description: Turkish bollards are white and rectangular with a red reflector on the front, making them quite unique. Similar bollards exist in Romania but are very rare. Australian bollards typically have a reflector on the back and a slightly different design(also they drive left in Australia/NZ comparing it to Turkey)

metas.name: Turkey - Pickup car
metas.description: You can find this grey pickup truck in some of Turkey generation 4 coverage.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Similar pickup trucks can also be found in Senegal and Kenya.

metas.name: Turkey - Stop signs
metas.description: All stop signs in Turkey feature the text "DUR," making them unique to the country. No other country uses this stop sign.

metas.name: Ukraine - Red car meta
metas.description: A red Google car, with or without an antenna, in Generation 3 and on crappy roads is always Ukraine. However, the car may not always be visible, so donât rule out Ukraine if you donât see it.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Scottish passing place signs
metas.description: These âPassing Placeâ signs are unique to Scotland.

metas.name: United Kingdom - UK license plates
metas.description: In the UK, license plates are white on the front and yellow on the back. In Ireland, both the front and back plates are white.

metas.name: United Kingdom - UK road lines
metas.description: These middle lines, that consist of long dashes with catâs eyes (reflectors) in the gaps between the dashes, are a good clue for the UK.
metas.comparison: Note: You can find it rarely in Ireland.

metas.name: Abaza road sample1
metas.description:
Black car B type long antenna summer coverage
Very hilly with vegetation consisting of various birches, pines and larches
Driving north which helps distinguish from the Tanzybey road
South of Abaza, there is a smudge to the front right of the driving direction

metas.name: Altai Krai gen 4 sample
metas.description:
No car gen 4 summer coverage
Very flat with open agricultural fields
May look like Omsk, but the birches are in rows instead of clusters. In addition, thereâs a wider assortment of foliage such as oaks and olive trees.
Very gravelly light brown soil

metas.name: Bashkortostan May sample
metas.description:
No car gen 4 May coverage
Signature Bashkortostan red soil
Rolling hills with intermittent random inselberg-esque rock formations

metas.name: Belgorod
metas.description:
Black car A type and tilted left long antenna fall coverage
Very hilly with dark black soil
Agricultural fields are abundant, especially with sunflowers

metas.name: Bryansk sample
metas.description:
Black car blurred long antenna fall coverage
Relatively flat compared to other fall coverage western oblast regions such as Tula, Belgorod, and Lipetsk
Darkish soil accompanied by tall pines
If you find yourself on a flat and straight forest road in fall coverage, youâre probably in Bryansk

metas.name: Chelyabinsk M-5 sample
metas.description:
No car with antenna August gen 4
Sometimes antenna will not be visible, but landscape and season should suffice
Looks nearly September
Ural mountains visible in open areas, else heavily forested
