metas.description: These concrete poles with insulators suspended below the crossbars are unique to the Yucatan peninsula.

metas.name: Mexico - Guanajuato extremely dark fields
metas.description: Extremely dark fields are common in Guanajuato.

metas.name: Mexico - Hexagonal tiles pavement
metas.description: This pavement consisting of hexagonal tiles is found in Puebla and Tlaxcala.

metas.name: Mexico - Light coloured rock walls
metas.description: These walls made of light coloured rock are found in the Yucatan peninsula, but most common in Yucatan state.
metas.comparison: Comment from Vincent: When not in the sun, the rock walls appear darker, but it's likely the same type of rock.

metas.name: Mexico - Nayarit bollard
metas.description: Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit, apart from one exception being Federal Highway 190 on the Oaxaca-Chiapas border.

metas.name: Mexico - Oaxaca pavement
metas.description: This exact pavement design with three lines of cobblestone patterning is exclusive to Oaxaca.

metas.name: Mexico - Oil palm plantations
metas.description: Oil palm plantations are most common in Chiapas, and occasionally on the outskirts of the state in Veracruz, Tabasco, and Campeche.

metas.name: Mexico - Red agricultural fields
metas.description: Red agricultural fields are commonly seen in Zacatecas and occasionally southern Durango.

metas.name: Mexico - Saguaro Cacti
metas.description: The Saguaro Cacti can be spotted in the western half of Sonora, featuring short curving arms that stem from a main trunk.

metas.name: Mexico - Wooden hanging insulator pole
metas.description: The wooden variant of the hanging pole is found on the Baja California peninsula.

metas.name: Chubu Plate
metas.description: Chubu plate is super unique because of the rounded shape, you can spot it from far away.

metas.name: Chugoku plate
metas.description: Chugoku plates will have usually written Energia in latin and sometimes they will include logo.

metas.name: Hokkaido Plate
metas.description: Hokkaido plate can be recognized by having a lot of numbers in rows of 2.

metas.name: Hokuriku plates
metas.description: Silver horizontal plates with logo on the top right. NTT plates will be also horizontal(in Tohoku NTT plates are vertical, and only Tohoku plate is horizontal).

metas.name: Kansai plate
metas.description: One of the hardest plate to recognize. Have different designs but will have  Japanese written in the middle/or the right and then characters below it in rows of 2 and will usually have 2 numbers at the bottom left/right.

metas.name: Kanto plate
metas.description:
Often silver and handwritten characters.
Horizontal characters above three vertical digits.

metas.name: Kyushu Plates
metas.description: Distinc logo(sometimes might be missing). Three numbers horizontally near the top, with 4 vertical characters below them on the right(1 kana and 3 numbers).

metas.name: Okinawa plates
metas.description: Plate with multiple numbers and lines in between them. Often will have more than 2 plates.

metas.name: Shikoku plate
metas.description: Distinct logo that you can remember since it has 4 dots representing 4 prefectures of Shikoku.

metas.name: Tohoku plate
metas.description: Silver horizontal plates with logo in top left. NTT plate will be vertical.(In Hokuriku all the plates will be horizontal)

metas.name: Architecture in Bali
metas.description: Architecture in Bali is unique because it was influenced by old Balinese culture and Hinduism. The most important thing to look for are these crown-like roof pinnacles, found everywhere in Bali. Guardian statues and slit-drum towers are common too. Andesite, a dark, volcanic rock, is a common building material in Bali. You can often see gates, walls, and other intricately carved ornaments built from this material.

metas.name: Blue Green
metas.description: You can often see thin, black poles next to regular poles near the East Peninsula of Central Sulawesi. Two pieces of tape can be seen near the top of the poles, usually light blue and green. These can rarely be seen in northern South East Sulawesi.

metas.name: Boat Shaped Roofs North Sumatra
metas.description:
North Sumatra features similarly distinct boat-shaped roofs, however the roofs are less angled upward and they do not feature spires.
*These roofs are most commonly found near Lake Toba, due to its sacred history.

metas.name: Boat Shaped Roofs West Sumatra
metas.description: West Sumatra features these distinct boat-shaped roofs.

metas.name: Central Sula Bollards
metas.description: Central Sulawesi features these unique bollards that are painted black on the bottom, white in the middle, and yellow on the top.

metas.name: Extra Attachment
metas.description: Pole tops in North and Central Sulawesi, and Gorontalo commonly feature an extra attachment right under the horizontal bar.

metas.name: Extra Support
metas.description: On the Lesser Sunda Islands (âNusasâ), you can find poles with an extra support on the pole top. Sometimes, two supports can be present.

metas.name: Gable Horns Roofs
metas.description:
Roofs with gable horns can be found most commonly in South Sulawesi, Riau and Central and South Kalimantan.
*Horned roofs are often found with Bugis roofs in South Sulawesi. Use this tip along with other clues to determine which region you are in.

metas.name: Green Paint Bridges
metas.description: Green paint can often be seen on the side of bridges in South and Central Kalimantan.

metas.name: High Peatched Peaks
metas.description: You can find these distinct roofs with uniquely high-pitched peaks on Sumba.

metas.name: Horizontal Slots
metas.description:
These horizontal slots inside the triangles of the roofs are almost unique to Southern Sulawesi.
*They can rarely be found in East Kalimantan and West Nusa.

metas.name: Painted Fences
metas.description: These painted fences are typically found on Sulawesi. They will be mostly painted white with blue or red.

metas.name: Rectangle
metas.description: Bali features both even and uneven poles, as well as the Lesser Sunda island variants. You can also find this unique rectangle attachment on the pole tops in Bali.

metas.name: Red Soil
metas.description: Red soil can often be found on Batam and the Bangka Belitung islands, located east of mainland Sumatra.

metas.name: Savannah
metas.description:
This savannah landscape is occasionally seen on North Sumba.
*In Generation 3, you will always see a white car.

metas.name: Tongkonan
metas.description: A small region of South Sulawesi, around the city of Rante Pao, features these very unique houses, called Tongkonan, that have saddle-shaped roofs. The houses themselves are also elevated from the ground.

metas.name: Triangle
metas.description:
You can find these poles with a triangle attachment under the horizontal bar in the following regions.
*This does not apply to stacked poles.

metas.name: Trident
metas.description: Trident style pole tops are most commonly found in Central Java and Yogyakarta, and rarely in South and West Kalimantan, and North Sumatra and Riau.

metas.name: Uneven
metas.description: These poles are almost exclusive to North Sumatra. The bar which holds the insulators is even, but features uneven insulators with one on one side and two on the other.

metas.name: Wooden Roofs
metas.description: On Kalimantan, you can find these unique roofs made out of wooden chips.

metas.name: Alabama license plates
metas.description: Front plates are NOT required.

metas.name: Alaska license plates
metas.description: There are three variants of Alaska license plates.

metas.name: Arizona license plates
metas.description: Front plates are NOT required.

metas.name: Colorado license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: Connecticut license plates
metas.description: Connecticut license plates are blue on top and fades into white on the bottom. Front plates are required.

metas.name: Delaware license plates
metas.description: Delaware license plates has gold text on dark blue background, it shows up as a dark blue blur with gold in the middle, and is easy to spot. Front plates are NOT required. Note: A similar plate can be found in Michigan.

metas.name: Florida license plates
metas.description: Florida license plates has green text on a white background, and it has oranges in the middle, which makes the plate unique. Front plates are NOT required.

metas.name: Georgia license plates

The landscape of the Faroe islands is characterised by long, wide fjords with jagged green mountains that rise straight out of the water, with rocky ridge lines along the mountainsides.
The mountains generally look more imposing and greener than coastal mountains in Iceland, which can often be used to tell them apart.

Iceland has unique yellow bollards with a white reflector.
These bollards are extremely common and can be found throughout the country on almost every section of rural road.

metas.description: The Generation 4 coverage was captured with red and white pickup trucks, which have been well blurred.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape
metas.description:
Iceland is a very geologically active country, where plate tectonics and volcanic processes have shaped the landscape.
As a result, many regions are rugged, mountainous and a sight to behold.
In addition, strange and bewildering landscapes can be found all over, such as geothermal lakes, lava fields, rift valleys, and towering rock formations.

metas.description: Similar to the United Kingdom, the Isle of Man uses white front licence plates with yellow rears, but with a red strip on the left.

metas.name: Italy - Architecture
metas.description:
Italian architecture mainly consists of pastel coloured stone houses, generally with terracotta roofs.
Houses will very commonly have wooden shutters, which will typically be divided in two and open sideways.

The guardrail gets flatter, wider, and it bends away from the road.

metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.description:
One of the most common types of Italian road lines are white solid outer lines with no middle line.
This is generally less common in other Mediterranean countries.

metas.name: Italy - Trident Pole Tops
metas.description:
The most common pole tops in Italy are concrete trident pole tops.
There are several possible configurations of insulators.
The two shown in the image are the most common ones.

metas.name: Italy - Via & Street Signs
metas.description:
Street signs are typically white with a thin blue border and black text.
The name for âRoadâ or âWayâ in Italian is Via.

metas.name: Italy - White Pole Sticker
metas.description: Wooden poles in Italy will commonly feature a small white pole sticker.

metas.name: Jersey - Landscape
metas.description:
The island is shaped by a unique mix of British and Norman influences.
The many winding roads and hedgerows are reminiscent of English country lanes, with tree-covered roads being particularly common.
All images were taken by a Generation 2 camera.

metas.name: Jersey - Red Granite
metas.description:
Jersey is home to large reserves of red granite.
As a result, it is a popular building material used for the construction of many walls and houses throughout the island.

metas.name: Latvia - Bollards
metas.description:
Latvian bollards have a thin, slightly curved shape.
They have a rectangular reflector on the front, and two circular reflectors on the back.
The reflectors can be white or orange.
The black strip is slightly angled.
Bollards often have numbers below the front reflector.

metas.name: Latvia - Bus Stop Sign
metas.description:
The bus has five windows.
Within the Baltics, this is unique to Latvia.
The other two Baltic countries have four windows.

metas.description:
The Latvian word for street is iela.
This word is unique to Latvian.
Very rarely, you might see âgatveâ in Riga (abbreviated as gat.).

metas.name: Latvia - Kilometre Markers
metas.description:
All Baltic countries use the same blue kilometre marker.
However, they can be distinguished from each other by their angle relative to the road.
In Latvia, the marker will be parallel to the road.
It only has a number on one side.

metas.name: Latvia - Thick Red Border Signs
metas.description:
Each Baltic country has a slightly different border for its warning and speed signs.
Latvian signs have a thick red border, with a thin white outline around it.

metas.name: Lithuania - Bollards
metas.description:
Lithuanian bollards are wedge-shaped.

Both reflectors are rectangular.
You may find this thin version as well.

The Lithuanian word for street is gatve, often abbreviated as g. on signs and Google Maps.
This word is almost entirely unique to Lithuanian.
However, very rarely, you might see gat. in the Latvian capital of Riga.

metas.name: Lithuania - Kilometre Markers
metas.description:
All Baltic countries use the same blue kilometre marker.
However, they can be distinguished from each other by their angle relative to the road.
In Lithuania, the marker will be at a 45Â° angle towards the road.
The sign itself has an L-shape.

metas.name: Lithuania - Less Forest Cover
metas.description:
Lithuania has less forest cover than the other two Baltic countries.
As a result, the landscape appears more open and agricultural.
Your mileage may vary depending on the round however, so use this meta with some caution.

metas.description:
Madeira commonly uses small and unique stone bollards with a red reflector.
They are either cuboidal or cylindrical in shape.

metas.name: Malta - Architecture
metas.description:
The vast majority of buildings in Malta consist of low storey buildings, with white to beige coloured walls.
Buildings made of limestone are also fairly common.

metas.name: Malta - Landscape
metas.description:
The general landscape of Malta consists of slightly hilly dry agricultural fields.
Many roads are also only 1 or 2 lanes wide, due to the islandâs size.
Having a mediterranean climate, cacti and various dry shrubs can be seen.

metas.name: Malta - Left Driving Side
metas.description: Malta drives on the left.

metas.name: Malta - Rock Walls
metas.description:
Limestone rock walls are extremely common in Malta.
This alone is usually enough to determine that you are in Malta.

metas.name: Malta - Triq
metas.description: The Maltese word for street is âtriqâ, which can be seen on almost every street sign.

metas.name: Monaco - Palm Trees
metas.description: Planted palm trees are common.

metas.name: Monaco - Vibe
metas.description:
Monaco is a rich and densely populated city state, with a Mediterranean feel to it.
The architecture is similar to cities in southern France and northern Italy, but more luxurious.
You will see a lot of apartment buildings, neoclassical details, and pastel colours.

Montenegro is a small, mountainous country.
Inland mountains are lush and green, while most coastal mountains have distinct exposed, light coloured rock.
Most roads are also only 1 or 2 lanes wide.

metas.name: Netherlands - Bicycle Paths
metas.description:
Many Dutch roads are flanked by bicycle paths.
Different designs exist, but a very common one is a reddish-pink lane.
Cycling is one of the most common modes of transportation in the Netherlands.
You will see cyclists and bicycles everywhere.

metas.name: Netherlands - Bollards
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Netherlands - Brick Roads
metas.description:
Brick roads are common in the Netherlands, both in rural and urban areas.
The brick pattern shown in the image is especially common.

metas.name: Netherlands - Bulky Yellow Signposts
metas.description: Road signs on traffic islands often have these bulky yellow signposts.

metas.name: Netherlands - Flat Landscape
metas.description:
The Netherlands is extraordinarily flat.
In most of the country, you will get no more than a few metres of elevation.
Large swathes of the country are reclaimed land that is at or even below sea level.

Many rural roads feature a sort of brick rumble strip on the sides.
This is fairly unique to the Netherlands and a good way to identify the country in very rural rounds.

metas.name: Netherlands - Yellow Plates
metas.description:
The Netherlands has long, yellow licence plates with the standard European blue strip on the left.
Dutch taxis have blue plates.

metas.name: Portugal - Architecture
metas.description: White painted stone houses with orange tiled roofs are extremely common in Portugal.

metas.name: Portugal - Bollards
metas.description:
Portuguese bollards are either wedge-shaped with a noticeably thin white top, or flat with a wide reflector.
While most reflectors will be white, you may also find orange reflectors.
These are noticeably darker than the yellow reflectors in Spain.

metas.name: Portugal - Chevrons
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Portugal - Cobblestone Roads
metas.description:
Cobblestone roads are very common in Portugal.
These will typically be made of square cobblestones arranged diagonally compared to the road direction.

metas.name: Portugal - Cobblestone Sidewalks
metas.description: Similarly, cobblestone sidewalks made of distinctly bright stones are very common.

metas.name: Portugal - Eucalyptus Trees
metas.description:
Eucalyptus trees are very common in Portugal.
The only other part of Europe where youâll commonly see eucalyptus is northern Spain.

metas.name: Portugal - License Plates
metas.description:
Portuguese plates are long and white, with a blue strip on the left.
Most plates have a yellow strip on the right, which is unique to Portugal.
The yellow strip was discontinued in 2020, so in Generation 4 coverage you may sometimes see plates with just the blue strip.

metas.name: Romania - Dashed Roadlines
metas.description: While there are many types of roadlines in Romania, these outer lines, consisting of short dashes with narrow spaces, can be a good clue for the country.

metas.name: Romania - Thick Roadlines
metas.description:
Middle lines are often noticeably thicker than average.
This is especially useful to tell Romania apart from Bulgaria, which generally has thinner road lines.

metas.name: Romania - Waystones
metas.description:
It is very common to see waystones in Romania.
They are typically fairly large, with red or blue framing with the road number on the side, or made of actual stone and somewhat rugged-looking.
There is also a very small variant which is all white.

metas.name: Romania - Yield Sign
metas.description:
This yield sign, with an extremely thick red border, with a thin white outline, is unique to Romania.
Beware that different yield signs also exist in Romania.

metas.name: Russia - Bollards
metas.description: Russia has three main types of bollards:

metas.name: Russia - Decorated Windows
metas.description:
This style of richly decorated window frames is commonly found on traditional Russian homes, especially on log cabins.
They are often painted blue.

metas.name: Russia - Gen 3 Cars
metas.description:
Three Generation 3 Street View cars are commonly found in Russia.
The two most useful ones for recognising Russia are a black and a white car, both with a long antenna.
You may also see a short antenna without a visible car.

metas.name: Russia - Large Apartments
metas.description:
The vast majority of urban housing in Russia are large rectangular apartment buildings made of simple concrete.
Newer buildings in wealthier areas appear more modern.

metas.name: Russia - Rural Housing
metas.description: Rural housing in Russia consists mostly of a basic wooden structure with metal roofs.

metas.name: Russia - Wide Intersections
metas.description: Along with containing a large number of bollards, many intersections are unusually wide compared to other countries.

The most common roof shape is half-hipped roofs.

metas.name: Spain - Hunting Signs
metas.description:
In rural areas you will often find hunting signs.
There are two versions, both of which are unique to Spain.
One is a simple white sign with a text starting with âcotoâ and ending in âcazaâ.
The other one has a diagonally divided black and white background.

metas.name: Spain - Ladder Poles
metas.description:
In Spain, you can find a variety of electricity poles and pole tops.
In small towns and sparsely populated rural areas concrete ladder poles and wooden poles are the most common.
âLadderâ poles have indents that resemble a ladder, hence the name.

metas.name: Sweden - Architecture
metas.description: Houses in the Swedish countryside are most commonly wooden and often painted with a distinct dark red paint, which is almost exclusively found in Sweden, Norway and Finland.

metas.name: Sweden - Bollards
metas.description:
Swedish bollards are black-and-white, typically with a grey reflector.
Reflectors by intersections are commonly orange instead.
They can be either wedge-shaped, round, or thin and curved.

metas.name: Sweden - Short Dashed Roadlines
metas.description:
On smaller roads, the outer road lines are white and dashed.
They are distinctly shorter than the Norwegian dashed lines.
In contrast to Norway and Finland, all road lines are white.

metas.name: Sweden - Unique Roadlines
metas.description:
The outer road lines on highways look solid from a distance, but are typically divided into small sections with a unique pattern, which is different from the solid lines in Finland and Norway.
Road lines in Denmark can have a similar pattern, however the individual sections should be rectangular.

metas.description:
Swiss bollards are black-and-white with white or grey reflectors.
They can be either wedge-shaped or cylindrical with a rounded top.

metas.name: Switzerland - Pedestrian Sign
metas.description:
Swiss pedestrian signs have seven stripes, making it almost unique for Europe.
Furthermore, rather than the typical European square shape, the signs appear as tall blue rectangles.

metas.name: Ukraine - Bad Road Quality
metas.description:
On average, Ukraine has some of the worst roads in Europe.
Most rural roads have lots of potholes, cracks and warped pavement.
This abysmal road quality can really help with tough 50-50s with Russia, which generally has somewhat better roads.

metas.name: Indonesia  -  (N) Sumatra Palm (Areca)
metas.description: Areca palms, often called Sumatra palms w/in indo, basically mostly found within Sumatra. probably most often found in western North Sumatra (and the rest of the west coast). west coast of all of sumatra often hilly, North (eastish) coast often flat.
metas.comparison: (i have seen them in the nusas, but you probably shouldnt confuse sumatra w/ the nusas)

metas.name: Indonesia  -  bali pole
metas.description: the rectangle below the crossbar on an even pole is unique to bali.

metas.name: Indonesia  -  bali script
metas.description: unique bali script

metas.name: Indonesia  -  Bali Shrine
metas.description: these hindu shrines are quite common on bali

metas.name: Indonesia  -  Icelandic hills
metas.description: very specific, but If you see these green Icelandic looking hills, you are probably around Mebula.

metas.name: Indonesia  -  Nusa Huts
metas.description: little huts in front of houses that offer shade. Found in the Nusas, where it is dry, and often in Lombok. can be much smaller than the one in the picture

metas.name: Indonesia  -  peleng 21c
metas.description: on peleng you will always find 2021 copyright. it is not exclusive within sula, but most common.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Aceh vibe
metas.description: Looks like North Sumatra, (roofs, oil palms, vibe, etc) but has uneven poles. Very limited coverage

metas.name: Indonesia  - Bali "thatched" roof
metas.description: bali has these weird thatched lookin roofs, very common in Bali, sometimes in like rice fields, or on side of road etc. does not have to be a full roof for a house

metas.name: Indonesia  - Bali Bridge
metas.description: this is what the typical bridge in bali looks like w/ the gold and black. but what makes it unique is the little statue patron things on the ends of the bridge. the actualy stutue thing doesnt have to be there just the pedestal.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Bali Hanging things
metas.description: idk what these are, but they are most common on bali.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Bali Pavement
metas.description: square bali pavement. not exclusive, but most common.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Bali Sticker
metas.description: dark blue sticker on the pole is only found in Bali and Nusa Pineda i think, and i think a lighter version can be found in west nusas maybe lombok aswell, but both can get faded. If you see a blue sticker your prolly somewhere there. most likely bali i think.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Bali Walls
metas.description: These two types, the one with this grey bricks, and the orange brick. again not exclusive but quite common on bali.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Bangka Belitung roof
metas.description: tiles only on like the creases in the roofs. can be found eslewhere (like nusas i think) but if its on like all the roofs its prolly Bangka Belitung

metas.name: Indonesia  - Batam Red Soil
metas.description: Batam has red soil. remember, batam is like an offbrand singapore

metas.name: Indonesia  - Batam Vibe
metas.description: if it feels like Singapore, but isnt singapore, its prolly Batam.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Bintan constructing
metas.description: bintan is a Batam wannabe. they are basically prepping it to be built up like Batam. So lots of like big buildings with no others around it that seem out of place. Lots of emptiness. click around a little bit and you will get a vibe for it.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Cambo Palms
metas.description: idk what exaclty they are called but if you see this palm your prolly in this general area.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Central Java Pavement
metas.description: central java pavement. like 80% accurate w/in Java probably.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Central Java Pole
metas.description: can be a trident pole but doenst have to be. the way the central insulator is attached to the pole on the side with that extra peice is what makes it unique.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Central Kali Camera Glitch
metas.description: I found this camera glitch while searching. If you look 90 degrees to the left of the front of the car, there is a glitch that is easier seen when you zoom in fully with a bunch of little lines. in some panos it is more purple aswell. Found within Central Kali on these roads. some parts may have ben ovverrun with newer coverage. It will have 2024 copyright

metas.name: Indonesia  - Central Sula Bollard
metas.description: Central Sulawesi features these unique bollards that are painted black on the bottom, white in the middle, and yellow on the top.

metas.name: Indonesia  - East Java Pavement
metas.description: East java pavement. mostly around Surabaya. sometimes called surabaya pavement.

metas.name: Indonesia  - East Java Pole
metas.description: uneven pole, which within Java is most likely east java. The unique poles are the ones that are uneven and the pole continues much higher than the crossbar.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Flat Lombok
metas.description: Within the Nusas(besides Sumba), if it is flat its prolly Lombok

metas.name: Indonesia  - Flat w/ lone mt. w kali
metas.meta_label: Flat w/ lone mt. w kali
metas.description: west kali is mostly flat, except for the occasional hill or mountain. so you will often see a flat landscape with one or two hills/mountains near you.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Flores In the Hills/mountains
metas.description: In the Nusas, and you are in the mountains/tall hills, your probably in Flores

metas.name: Indonesia  - Gorontalo Hills
metas.description: Gorontalo has these unique green hills almost roundish rolling hills. sort of a lack of trees, but there are often some oil palms, often corn growing. click around gorontalo and get a vibe for it.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Jambi occasional tiled roof
metas.description: jambi has mostly tin roofs w/ the occasional tiled roof. remember gradient from most to least w/in sumatra goes from south to north.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Java (and bali) antenna
metas.description: Generation 3 antenna coverage is most commonly found on Java, but can very rarely be seen on Bali in and around Denpasar. It is most commonly seen in East Java, as most of the antenna coverage in the west has been overwritten by Generation 4.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Java Rock walls(volcanic)
metas.description: if within Java, and there are these rock walls, (volcanic most likely), and everything feels volcanic, like for ex. dark fields, rocks on the side of the road, etc., you are prolly here.

metas.name: Indonesia  - JT road
metas.description: most recognizalbe road in Indonesia. Gen 3, really dry, water north.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Kali cut thru forest
metas.description: One way to differentiate Kali from something like Sumatra is that in Kali, most of the roads are like cut through the forest. Everything is bassically on the side of the road again kinda carved into the forest. def more of a vibe

metas.name: Indonesia  - Kali uneven poles
metas.description: If you are in Kali, and you have uneven poles, you will NOT be in West Kali

metas.name: Indonesia  - Kundur Island soil
metas.description: Kunder island has this orange soil. almost yellowish

metas.name: Indonesia  - Lampung Grid
metas.description: Most of Lampung is in a grid, lots of straight rods, not always North-south tho.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Lampung Individual houses
metas.description: houses are kinda just all on their own. very spread out. the landscape is flat (in the east, west too difficult).  lampung architecture is extremely unique. click around and get a feel for it. the houses almost feel more modern to me, often have collums holding up like a small porch in front. often tiled roofs.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Lampung Sticks
metas.description: These sticks on the side of the road are like 100% Lampung 80% of the time. look for other clues cause it could just randomly be like Sulawesi and ur cooked.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Lombok roof
metas.description: unique roof. bell shaped.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Lombok tiles
metas.description: Lombok often has theses really dark, grey even, tiled roofs.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Mahakam River Coal
metas.description: In and around the Mahakam River, you will often see piles of coal being exported.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Malay Border roof curve
metas.description: malaysia has this curve on the edges of the roof sometimes. this is not at all of indo origin, so it is only found in places that border malaysia. So mostly on the east coast of Sumatra, all those islands, and West Kalimantan.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Mamasa Roof
metas.description: very similar to some of the other roofs, but this one the bottom of the roof that is going up is completely straight and not curved.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Mamasa Vibe
metas.description: gen 3 white car, very sunny, can have Mamasa roof, often pines are seen. click around to get a vibe.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Medan Other crops
metas.description: within NS around Medan, you often get other crops in addition to Oil palms, like Corn, Sugarcane, etc. (not often rice). Also most of Medan and surrounding local area is in a North-South Grid

metas.name: Indonesia  - Muna Island blue houses
metas.description: for some reason Muna Island just has a lot of blue, espcially houses. so if you think u may be in Muna island, and u see blue, its a good clue.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Muna Island Vibe
metas.description: lots of blue, kinda dry idk. click around and get a vibe for it you wont miss it.

metas.name: Indonesia  - N Maluku layered roofs
metas.description: these layered roofs are quite common in N Maluku

metas.name: Indonesia  - N maluku porch roofs
metas.description: like extrusions of roof at a slight down angle are common in North maluku.

metas.name: Indonesia  - N Maluku rock
metas.description: North Maluku often has these piles of rock scattered around and then these gutters and other stuff are sometimes made of rock

metas.name: Indonesia  - N Maluku rock house foundation
metas.description: houses on North maluku are often on this rock looking foundation that is a bit off the ground.

metas.name: Indonesia  - N sula volcanoes
metas.description: north sula has a lot of volcanoes

metas.name: Indonesia  - Nias plant
metas.description: This plant is basically everywhere on the island, and is pretty much unique to Nias island within Indonesia. Recognizable red tinted leaves mixed in with the green leaves.
metas.comparison: Being part of North Sumatra, they Nias has the NS poles, often made of metal. Nias also often just has random piles of rock on the side of the road.

metas.name: Indonesia  - North Kali blur
metas.description: most of it is overrun. will be front of the car, in northern north kali. also for more car meta: if its gen 3, you probably shoulndt click kali

metas.name: Indonesia  - North sula Nice small roads
metas.description: like West sumatra, North sula has these nice small roads

metas.name: Indonesia  - North Sumatra Pole
metas.description: These poles are almost exclusive to North Sumatra. The bar which holds the insulators is even, but features uneven insulators with one on one side and two on the other.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Northern Sula Pole
metas.description: Pole tops in North and Central Sulawesi, and Gorontalo commonly feature an extra attachment right under the horizontal bar.

metas.name: Indonesia  - NS lake landscape
metas.description: Hills are cleared of trees, very green (if there are trees they are replanted, standing on their own, not natural looking). mostly a vibe but nothing else in indo looks like this. Hills with nothing on it exept grass = lake

metas.name: Indonesia  - NS lake roof
metas.description: Around the Lake in North Sumatra you get this roof (central NS). Very boat shaped. can often be found as miniature roofs like on side of the road or on shacks or on top of stuff, etc.
metas.comparison: DO NOT confuse it with the West Sumatra roof, that one the ends are steeper and go higher and are "spiky".

metas.name: Indonesia  - NS mount sinabung
metas.description: Very distinct Volcano visible from a decently far away around Berastagi. Also in the plateau the crops are different, farming equipment is differnt, often greenhouses, very small fields. overall very different culture from rest of NS.

metas.name: Indonesia  - NS ugly building
metas.description: block building with no nice things on the side (just concrete). Often above a garage (even if a building is one story, it can often still have a blocky or square feel which is a good clue for NS). Often found in rows, all next to each other This is a good clue for North Sumatra and Sometimes Riau.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Nusa Banana Plant
metas.description: If within the Nusas, u think u might be in Flores, and see banana plants, its prolly east.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Nusa Penida
metas.description: Like Bali, has basically everything bali has, but a bit more dry, has a vibe to the landscape. click around to get a feel for it.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Nusa Pole
metas.description:
On the Lesser Sunda Islands (âNusasâ), you can find poles with an extra support on the pole top. Sometimes, two supports can be present.
The Nusas are very dry.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Palu NSish Ridges
metas.description: The city of Palu in in a roughly north south valley with large mountains on either side.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Pipes to Dumai
metas.description: lots of oil palms in riau. Dumai is the main port so the palm oil is exported through pipes to Dumai. If you see pipes, you think you might be in Riau, your probably around Dumai.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Pontianak Canals
metas.description: Pontianak has a lot of Canals and waterways running through it. good clue for the west coast of Kali overall.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Rante Poa Roof
metas.description: A small region of South Sulawesi, around the city of Rante Pao, features these very unique houses, called Tongkonan, that have saddle-shaped roofs. The houses themselves are also elevated from the ground.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Riau Oil Palms
metas.description: Oil Palms = click Riau basically. Riau has a lot of oil palms.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Riau pole marking
metas.description: within Riau, an oval that says "KJ" in it, w/ blue writing around the oval.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Riau Roof thing
metas.description: This specific Gable Horn (i think thats what its called) is unique to Riau.

metas.name: Indonesia  - S Kali pole sticker
metas.description: silver reflective thing wrapped around the pole, found in S Kali and the majors roads that lead out of it.

metas.name: Indonesia  - S/C Kali green bridge
metas.description: Green paint can often be seen on the side of bridges in South and Central Kalimantan.

metas.name: Indonesia  - SE Sula grid
metas.description: southeast sula is often in a grid like lampung, can look like lampung at times

metas.name: Indonesia  - South Sula Roof
metas.description: this shape of roof with the trinagle and then the flaps coming off the sides at a different angle is extremely common in South Sula. They also often have gable horns. The more unique ones have peices of wood horizontal supporting the top triangle

metas.name: Indonesia  - South Sumatra Architecture
metas.description: often tiled roofs, with wooden front of the house. House is kinda elevated off the ground. once you see it you wont unsee it.

metas.name: Indonesia  - South Sumatra Rubber Trees
metas.description: Lots of rubber trees in South sumatra. Ive also seen them in north sumatra though, but should be able to tell the difference w/ other clues w/in Sumatra

metas.name: Indonesia  - SS mixed side plantations
metas.description: South Sumatra has terrible land management. so if you feel like the land is being poorly managed, its prolly south sumatra. one effect of this is that there are often mixed types of plantations on each side of the road, or a plantation on one side, and then its wild on the other, etc.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Stereotypical Bali Roofs
metas.description: Tiled roofs, often have a crown, and the things on the corners of the roof also.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Sula Fence
metas.description: These painted fences are typically found on Sulawesi. They will be mostly painted white with blue or red.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Sumatra (southern)  bright tiles
metas.description: very bright tiles tiles mixed in with the "normal" colored tiles. you wont really see this in java. remember theres a gradient of how many roofs are tiled from Lampung to Jambi.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Sumba Hills
metas.description: If in the Nusas, and are in the hills (not mountains/taller hills like Flores) you are probably in Sumbra, mostly west/south

metas.name: Indonesia  - Sumba Roof
metas.description: You can find these distinct roofs with uniquely high-pitched peaks on Sumba.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Sumba Savannah
metas.description: Sumba is the only place that has this extremely flat, extremely dry Savannah landscape.
metas.comparison: if gen 3, it will be white car

metas.name: Indonesia  - Sumbawa Fence
metas.description: Within the Nusas, the Sulawesi style fence is common on the Island of Sumbawa.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Sumbawa inbetween hills
metas.description: most of the coverage in Sumbawa is in between the hills/mountains in the flat areas. So if you are in the Nusas, but in flat area between mountains/hills (you can see them in the distance) you are prolly in Sumbawa.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Timor Roofs
metas.description: these "thatched" roofs are exclusive to Timor. Usually southeast.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Timor white brick
metas.description: If you think u might be on Timor, (very dry, has a distinct vibe cause its the most east), white brick buildings are a good clue for Timor.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Triangle
metas.description: You can find these poles with a triangle attachment under the horizontal bar in the following regions.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This does not apply to stacked poles

metas.name: Indonesia  - Triangle
metas.description: You can find these poles with a triangle attachment under the horizontal bar in the following regions.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This does not apply to stacked poles

metas.name: Indonesia  - Typical North Sumatra
metas.description: Many oil palms, very flat, often straight roads (in grids). (and ofc NS pole)

metas.name: Indonesia  - W Kali red dirt
metas.description: west kali sometimes has red dirt.

metas.name: Indonesia  - W Kali/Maluku pole
metas.description: Even Pole, with the supports coming down directly to the pole at a 45 degree angle. found in North Maluku and West Kali

metas.name: Indonesia  - W kali/Maluku pole2
metas.description: Even Pole, with the supports coming down directly to the pole at a 45 degree angle. found in North Maluku and West Kali

metas.name: Indonesia  - West Sumatra nice roads
metas.description: Like the richest part of sumatra, the roads are all paved really well, often road lines on smaller roads that usually wouldnt be there.

metas.name: Indonesia  - West Sumatra Pole
metas.description: symmetrical pole, often metal, has connecting bars that go in at like a 35-40 degree angle from the middle of crossbar to NOT the pole itself, but to little connecting bits. NOT 45 degrees.

metas.name: Indonesia  - West Sumatra Rice
metas.description: within Sumatra, basically the only place you will see rice is in West Sumatra.

metas.name: Indonesia  - West Sumatra Steep Roofs
metas.description: West Sumatra features these distinct boat-shaped roofs. the ends go up into a spike unlike the ones in North Sumatra (and south sula)

metas.name: Indonesia  - white w/ green tip sula fence
metas.meta_label: white w/ green tip sula fence
metas.description: if you see a white w/ green tip sula fence, you are probably on Peleng island. should be 2021copyright as well.

metas.name: Indonesia  - Wood Chipping roof
metas.description: On Kalimantan, you can find these unique roofs made out of wooden chips.

metas.name: north maluku bollard - north maluku bollard
metas.description: this yellow, blue yellow bollard is found in North Maluku. In fact, a lot of stuff in north Maluku is Yellow and blue.

metas.name: Agave salmiana
metas.description: Agave salmiana, also known as pulque agaves, have wide, smooth, curling leaves, and a crown-like appearance. They are common in the central Mexican valley and further north around the city of San Luis Potosi.

metas.name: Agave tequilana
metas.description: Vast fields of blue agave (Agave tequilana), used to produce tequila, are mostly found in Jalisco and Nayarit.

metas.name: Asymmetric mushroom-like insulator pole
metas.description: Poles with an asymmetric crossbar and double-stacked insulators are exclusive to Mexico City, State of Mexico, Hidalgo, and Morelos.

metas.name: Black tar
metas.description: Black tar on both sides of the yellow centre line can be seen in Sinaloa, Durango, and Guerrero.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This is most reliable when the tar is not faded.

metas.name: Blindingly white soil
metas.description: Almost blindingly white soil in the Yucatan peninsula is most common in Quintana Roo.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This is only consistent in Generation 3.

metas.name: Blue Myrtle Cacti
metas.description: The Blue Myrtle Cacti have short arms that uniformly curve and point upwards. It is abundantly found in San Luis Potosi, but also common in Queretaro and Hidalgo.

metas.name: Boojum trees
metas.description: Boojum trees can be recognized by their alien, tentacle-like appearance. They are almost exclusively found in the southern half of Baja California.

metas.name: Brittlebush
metas.description: Brittlebush are small shrubs with bright silver-grey leaves that are most commonly found in Sonora, especially around Hermosillo.

metas.name: Chihuahua cross
metas.description: A thick cross can be seen on the back of signs in Chihuahua.

metas.name: Coahuila gold tufts
metas.description: These gold tufts of grass in a line right next to the road are most commonly found in Coahuila.

metas.name: Cobblestone pavement
metas.description: This style of cobblestone pavement, unorganised with irregular tiles, can be found in most of the central states, but is by far most commonly found in the states of Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima, and Queretaro.

metas.name: Concrete hanging insulator pole
metas.description: These concrete poles with insulators suspended below the crossbars are unique to the Yucatan peninsula.

metas.name: Giant Cardon
metas.description: The Mexican Giant Cardon is an extremely common cacti in the Baja California peninsula. It can be identified through its large sprawling arms stemming from a singular trunk and ribbed exterior.

metas.name: Grainy pavement
metas.description: Grainy pavement with a blue-ish grey tinge is a common sight for the states of Tamaulipas and Nuevo Leon.
metas.comparison: NOTE: In Tamaulipas, larger roads very commonly feature dashed outer lines.

metas.name: Guanajuato extremely dark fields
metas.description: Extremely dark fields are common in Guanajuato.

metas.name: Hexagonal tiles pavement
metas.description: This pavement consisting of hexagonal tiles is found in Puebla and Tlaxcala.

metas.name: Jalisco bollards
metas.description: Jalisco bollards will sometimes have a crown and the text âJaliscoâ written on it. These are usually barely legible unless very close, however no other Mexican bollard will have writing on it.

metas.name: Light coloured rock walls
metas.description: These walls made of light coloured rock are found in the Yucatan peninsula, but most common in Yucatan state.
metas.comparison: Comment from Vincent: When not in the sun, the rock walls appear darker, but it's likely the same type of rock.

metas.name: Mesh body pole
metas.description: Poles with a mesh body are most commonly found in San Luis Potosi, Guanajuato, and Queretaro.

metas.name: Nayarit bollard
metas.description: Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit, apart from one exception being Federal Highway 190 on the Oaxaca-Chiapas border.

metas.name: Oaxaca pavement
metas.description: This exact pavement design with three lines of cobblestone patterning is exclusive to Oaxaca.

metas.name: Oil palm plantations
metas.description: Oil palm plantations are most common in Chiapas, and occasionally on the outskirts of the state in Veracruz, Tabasco, and Campeche.

metas.name: Red agricultural fields
metas.description: Red agricultural fields are commonly seen in Zacatecas and occasionally southern Durango.

metas.name: Saguaro Cacti
metas.description: The Saguaro Cacti can be spotted in the western half of Sonora, featuring short curving arms that stem from a main trunk.

metas.name: Western, shorter pine forest
metas.description: The western parts of Chihuahua and Durango can feature a rocky mountainous landscape covered with pine forests. In general, these pines are shorter and more stunted in appearance than pine forests of the central or south.

metas.name: White middle roadlines
metas.description: White middle roadlines are most commonly found in Tabasco.

metas.name: Wooden hanging insulator pole
metas.description: The wooden variant of the hanging pole is found on the Baja California peninsula.

metas.name: Yucca filifera
metas.description: Yucca filifera, also known as tree yucca, as well as yucca decipiens are most commonly seen in San Luis Potosi and Zacatecas as well as some of the bordering northern states. They can be recognised by their oblong rosettes of sharp green leaves branching from a single trunk, similar to a tree.

metas.name: Alternating Insulators Pole
metas.description:
Poles with 3 alternating insulators sticking out horizontally at the top are mostly seen in the four northern provinces of Limpopo, Gauteng, North West and Mpumalanga.
They can also sometimes be found in Northern Cape.
In the rest of the country, these pole tops are exceedingly rare.

metas.name: Bird Nest Pole
metas.description: Big bird nests on top of poles are commonly seen in the northern part of the Northern Cape Province.

metas.name: Cook Pine Trees
metas.description: NOTE:

metas.name: Dry Landscape & Red Soil
metas.description: A dry landscape with red soil is typically found in the Northern Cape.

metas.name: Eastern Cape Pole
metas.description: A similar poletop can be found in Eastern Cape, however the A-shape is noticeably wider and the bottom insulators are attached directly to the âAâ rather than a horizontal bar.

metas.name: Flat & Subtropical Vegetation
metas.description: The landscape near the Mozambique border in the highlighted area is noticeably flat, with green subtropical vegetation.

metas.name: Grainy Pavement
metas.description: You can find this grainy, almost Texas-like pavement with a hint of pink in Limpopo.

metas.name: Grassy Rolling Hills
metas.description:
Grassy rolling hills are generally located in the coastal area of Western Cape between Cape Town and George, and just north of Cape Town.
Tall ridges are usually visible to the north or east.

metas.name: Kruger Park Car
metas.description: NOTE:

metas.name: KwaZulu-Natal Pole
metas.description: Trident pole tops are almost unique to KwaZulu-Natal.

metas.name: Limpopo Pole
metas.description: Poles with 2 diagonal bars forming a â

metas.name: Mpumalanga Pole
metas.description: NOTE FROM MYSELF:

metas.name: Northeast Landscape
metas.description: NOTE:

metas.name: Pine Tree Plantations
metas.description: NOTE:

metas.name: Power Plants
metas.description: Power plants are often seen in between the town of Secunda and eMalahleni in Mpumalanga.

metas.name: Red Sticker
metas.description: NOTE:

metas.name: Rocky Mountains
metas.description: NOTE:

metas.name: Sugarcane Plantations
metas.description:
Sugarcane plantations are most commonly seen in KwaZulu-Natal, mostly along the coast.
However, they can also be seen in Mpumalanga on the Mozambique border.

metas.name: Vineyards
metas.description:
Vineyards are almost exclusively found in Western Cape, mostly in valleys near the coast.
You can also commonly find them near Upington, in Northern Cape.

metas.name: Western Cape Pole
metas.description: Poles with 3 bars forming the letter âAâ, with the bottom insulators being attached at the edges of a horizontal bar, can be found almost exclusively in Western Cape, and rarely in bordering provinces.

metas.name: White Sticker
metas.description: White stickers on the back of chevrons are often seen in the Cape provinces.

title: A Learnable Meta World - Stop Signs

metas.name: Australia - NSW-Three holes
metas.description: In New South Wales, especially in Sydney, some stop signs have three big holes making it unique for this region.

metas.name: Cambodia - ááá/Stop
metas.description: Stop signs in Cambodia always have the word "Stop" written in Khmer (ááá) in addition to the English word.

Stop signs in QuÃ©bec always have the word "Stop" written in France (ArrÃªt).

metas.name: Guatemala - Alto
metas.description: Guatemala, Panama, Costa Rica and Mexico are the only countries using the word "Alto" on their stop signs.

metas.description: Israel is the only country that uses a symbol on their stop sign making it unique and easily recognizable.

metas.name: Malaysia - Berhenti

metas.name: Mexico - Alto

metas.name: Panama - Alto

metas.name: SA - South America Pare
metas.description: The word "Pare" on stop signs is widely used in all of Latin America excluding Mexico Panama, Costa Rica and Guatemala. That means you can spot it in Columbia, Ecuador, Bolivia, Peru, Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Puerto Rico and Dominican Republic.

metas.name: Singapore - White  square
metas.description: The edge of the stop signs in Singapore has a white square outline making it unique.

metas.description: Stop signs in Thailand always have the word "Stop" written in Thai (à¸«à¸¢à¸¸à¸).

metas.name: TÃ¼rkiye - Dur
metas.description: Stop signs in TÃ¼rkiye always have the word "Stop" written in Turkish (Dur).

metas.name: Alaska - Alaska Gen 4
metas.description: Generation 4 coverage in Alaska is concentrated around the city of Anchorage. (As of April 25')

metas.name: Alaska - Alaska Shitcam
metas.description: Shitcam is only found around Anchorage and Fairbanks, and parts of the road that connects them.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This map shows all places where this camera can be found. Keep in mind coverage may be updated in some places, therefore you may come across regular coverage in places highlighted here.

metas.name: Alaska - Anchorage Fire Hydrant
metas.description: Fire hydrants in Anchorage are typically pale pink or pale yellow in colour.

metas.name: Alaska - Fairbanks Fire Hydrant
metas.description: Fire hydrants in Fairbanks are commonly either bright yellow or a combination of colours (most commonly yellow and blue).

metas.name: California - San Diego Warning Sticker
metas.description: Almost all plates in San Diego County and southern Orange County have this warning plate, similar to those in Wisconsin. These are unique within California.

metas.name: California - San Francisco Architecture
metas.description: Row Houses and other buildings in San Francisco are often in the style of Victorian architecture, with many bay windows, turrets, and ornate exterior details. These homes are built close together and can be very colourful.

metas.name: License Plate Meta
metas.description: The US, as well as most of the Americas, uses short licence plates, in contrast to longer European ones. Each US state has their own unique licence plate design. Some of these are recognizable through the blur, and are thus worth learning. Around half of the states also do not require front plates, which can also be useful in determining the state.

metas.name: Palms
metas.description: Palm trees are common in coastal areas of the Southeastern states, as well as the Desert Southwest region. Shown here is the Mexican Fan Palm, which is most common in California and along the Gulf Coast, but other palm tree types have a similar range.

metas.name: United States - Alabama Pole Plates
metas.description: You can see these fine plates with a round part on the side on most poles in Alabama and I have never seen anything like this elsewhere.

metas.name: United States - Alabama Vertical End of Guardrail
metas.description:
Guardrails in Alabama feature vertical yellow and black patterns, distinguishing them from other southern states.
Note: This only applies within the Southern states

metas.name: United States - Alaska Northern Trees
metas.description: Trees in Alaska are generally thinner and have less broad leaves than those seen in the other 49 states.

metas.name: United States - Appalachian Fence
metas.description: Dark-coloured wooden fences with several horizontal wooden supports are common in farming areas of central and southern Appalachia, stretching from Pennsylvania to Georgia.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These types of fences can be found elsewhere to a lesser extent, so use other clues before guessing.

metas.name: United States - Appalachians
metas.description: The Appalachian mountain range is a low mountain range that runs through the eastern states. The general landscape consists of low, forested mountains, with beech and oak trees being a common sight.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Houses in the south generally have less storeys. New England architecture, commonly consisting of wood panelling, high roofs and a porch, is also more common toward the north, especially in New England.

metas.name: United States - ATV Signs
metas.description: These green ATV Route signs are unique to Wisconsin.

metas.name: United States - Black Tar
metas.description: A black stripe can sometimes be seen in between the two yellow, middle road lines in California.

metas.name: United States - Brownstone Buildings
metas.description: Brownstone buildings are typically row houses or government buildings made out of various types of brick and sandstone. They are most commonly found in dense urban areas of the Northeast US, as well as Chicago.

metas.name: United States - California Stripes
metas.description: Utility poles in California usually have markings at the bottom of the pole that consist of 3 yellow stripes.

metas.name: United States - Canola
metas.description: Along the Canadian border in North Dakota, and rarely Montana, fields filled with short yellow canola flowers (Brassica napus) can commonly be seen from the road.

metas.name: United States - Central Appalachians
metas.description: In the Appalachian area stretching from southern New York to southern Virginia, there are a lot of forest-covered rolling hills, with flat valleys dividing them. A majority of the ridges are oriented Southwest to Northeast.

metas.name: United States - Central Valley
metas.description: Central Valley, California can be recognized by its Mediterranean climate. This is reflected in its agriculture, seen in the vineyards and olive trees that can commonly be found here.
metas.comparison: In addition, rolling hills can be seen toward the edges of the valley.

metas.name: United States - Concrete Paving
metas.description: Concrete paving on main highways is much more common in Iowa than in other states.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Concrete paving on residential streets is commonly seen throughout the Midwest states and parts of the East Coast.

metas.name: United States - Corn
metas.description: Corn fields can most commonly be found in these regions:-Iowa
metas.comparison: -North of Iowa -Nebraska without NW

metas.name: United States - Cotton
metas.description: Cotton is a crop that produces large fields of fluffy white flowers. It is most commonly produced in coastal Southeast States, the Lower Mississippi River Valley, Western Texas, and parts of California and Arizona.

metas.name: United States - Diamond Bollard
metas.description: The most common type of roadside bollard in South Dakota and Montana features a dark metal post with a white diamond on each side of the top.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These bollards can be found to a lesser extent in other western states.

metas.name: United States - Dormant Grass
metas.description: Grass that is used in lawns in the southern US (colloquially known as Bermuda and St. Augustine grasses) go dormant in the winter months. This causes the lawns to turn beige or light brown in winter; whereas grasses used in more northern areas of the US stay much greener in winter.

metas.name: United States - Double Sign Posts
metas.description: Signs attached to two signposts can be seen in Michigan. Not all signs are attached to two signposts.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Double signposts can also be seen in other states, but are not as common.

metas.name: United States - Douglas Fir
metas.description: Extremely tall conifer trees (Douglas firs) with a dark brown bark, and dark green leaves, can most commonly be seen in Cascadia. Notably, they can also be found in northern California, Idaho and as far east as Montana.
metas.comparison: Beware that they are also commonly found in British Columbia.

metas.name: United States - Golden Fields
metas.description: Agricultural golden fields can commonly be seen in eastern Washington.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Flat areas of northern and eastern Oregon can have a similar appearance.

metas.name: United States - Great Basin
metas.description: The Great Basin, centred around Nevada, can be recognized by the tall, sometimes snow-capped mountains in the background. There are dry, but grassy, and slightly shrubby plains leading up to the mountains.

metas.name: United States - Great Basin - Green
metas.description: Within the Great Basin, greener mountains can be seen in Idaho and central Utah.

metas.name: United States - Great Basin - Oregon
metas.description: Within the Great Basin, more gradual, rocky hills can be seen in Oregon.

metas.name: United States - Great Plains
metas.description: The Great Plains are in the middle of the United States and stretch from the Canadian border in the North, to central Texas in the South. This area is primarily flat with few trees. Some areas feature agriculture fields, while others feature dry and barren grassy fields.

metas.name: United States - Green Bollard
metas.description: Green bollards are common and (almost) unique to Idaho and Colorado, they exist in different forms, not only the one on this picture.

metas.name: United States - Green/Red Rectangular Signs
metas.description: Maine, New Hampshire, and Massachusetts use small green and red rectangular signs to mark the ends of bridges and guardrails.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Not all bridges and guardrails in these states will have these markers.

metas.name: United States - H-Reflector
metas.description: Snowplowable raised pavement markers can only be found on highways in the eastern states shown in the image. They are built into the road and somewhat resemble the letter H.

metas.name: United States - Hanging Lights
metas.description: Many large intersections in Michigan have stop lights and signs that hang from wires that stretch across the middle of the intersection. These markers are commonly in yellow boxes.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These are not completely unique to Michigan, but are most commonly seen there

metas.name: United States - Hawaii Antenna
metas.description: A stubby antenna can be seen in most Generation 3 coverage on Hawaii.
metas.comparison:
NOTE: The antenna is not always visible, so make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.
(This antenna can also be seen in Cambodia, New Zealand, and US National Parks)

metas.name: United States - Hawaii Smallcam
metas.description: Hawaii also has Generation 4 âsmallcamâ coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front, with parts of the black car being visible. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.

metas.name: United States - Hawaiian Place names
metas.description: Hawaii is the only state to use its own language, though English is still predominantly used. Most place names are in Hawaiian, so you can spot it on street signs, and other road markers.
metas.comparison: Hawaiian is a vowel-oriented language that only uses eight consonants: H, K, L, M, N, P, W, and (Ê»), called an Ê»Okina. Every Hawaiian word ends in one of 5 vowels: A, E, I, O, or U. Each vowel can also have a macron over it: Ä, Ä, Äª, Å, and Åª. These vowels are often combined to make Diphthongs. I.e. UI, AI, AE, etc...

metas.name: United States - Idaho Rectangular Bollard
metas.description: These bollards with a rectangle on top are common in Idaho and can only be seen there in western US. The rectangle can be white or yellow. Montana has a similar yellow version, but the reflector is much larger.

metas.name: United States - Iowa Sidepost
metas.description: The signpost on the side, as shown below, is unique to the state of Iowa in the Plains and Midwest. (only applies if you are in the Plains or Midwest)

metas.name: United States - Kansas Signpost Reflectors
metas.description: These white reflectors on signposts are unique to Kansas. They are most commonly seen on âstopâ signs in rural areas.

metas.name: United States - Kentucky Thin Strips
metas.description: Kentucky commonly uses thin strips on the edge of the road, which is unique to the state. These strips are not to be confused with long thin strips that do not reach the edge of the road, which can also be used in Kentucky but also elsewhere.

metas.name: United States - Large Center Line Gap
metas.description: Yellow lines with a noticeably larger gap in between them are most common in Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Oregon. They can also be found to a lesser extent in Washington, Alabama, and Michigan.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Wide middle lines can also rarely appear in other states, so consider other clues before guessing.

metas.name: United States - Massachusetts Pole Plates
metas.description: These rectangular  plates, which can be white or yellow, can be seen on the side of poles in eastern Massachusetts, Rhode Island and Connecticut. These plates can very rarely be seen elsewhere.

metas.name: United States - Minnesota Bridge Marker
metas.description: In Minnesota, these yellow signs with vertical, black triangles are placed before bridges at most major river crossings and at the beginnings and ends of guardrail sections on large highways. (I have seen these in other states but they are upsidown)

metas.name: United States - Minnesota Signpost reflectors
metas.description: On most rural âstopâ signposts in Minnesota, a black-and-white marker is attached to the posts horizontally. The shape may vary slightly.

metas.name: United States - Mississippi River Valley
metas.description: The Lower Mississippi River Valley is a very flat and open landscape with red soil in areas of Tennessee, Arkansas, Mississippi, and Northeast Louisiana. Corn and other crops are common in this area.

metas.name: United States - Nebraska Sandhills
metas.description: The Nebraska Sandhills are a recognizable region of rolling hills covered with prairie grass in the central-north part of the state.

metas.name: United States - Nevada Bollard
metas.description: This bollard is found in Nevada. It consists of a reflector on a thin stick. The reflector is a vertical rectangle that consists of a white field surrounded by a black outline.

metas.name: United States - New England Rock Walls
metas.description: In rural areas of Connecticut, Rhode Island, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire, short rock walls are commonly visible adjacent to the road.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These rock walls can be found rarely in adjacent states.

metas.name: United States - New England Shingled Walls
metas.description: Houses in coastal New England often feature shingle walls, which are layered wood panels overlapping each other.
metas.comparison: A similar style of panelling can also be seen, however, having a wider range than the one shown above.

metas.name: United States - No Center Lines
metas.description: Some small roads in California lack a middle yellow line; instead only feature solid white lines on each side of the road.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This can rarely be seen in other states, notably Kentucky

metas.name: United States - North Carolina Signpost white Signs
metas.description: White signs attached to signposts can commonly be seen in North Carolina.

metas.name: United States - North Carolina Street Signs
metas.description: North Carolina commonly uses a style of street signs showing street numbers and arrows in addition to the street name.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Other states occasionally feature street signs with similar designs, so use other clues before guessing.

metas.name: United States - Number/Direction Street Signs
metas.description: Streets in Utah and Idaho, particularly in urban areas, are often named by using a combination of a number and cardinal direction (i.e. â600 South.â)
metas.comparison: NOTE: This style of street naming can be found rarely in other Western states.

metas.name: United States - Ohio Gap
metas.description: In Ohio, you can often see gaps in road lines where there is a RPM (raised pavement marker). It can also sometimes be seen elsewhere (Tennessee or New Jersey) but it is much rarer.

metas.name: United States - Oil Pumpjack
metas.description: Oil pumpjacks are short, industrial-looking metal structures located at the surface of oil fields and are used to pump crude oil from the earth below. They are most common in western states, particularly in Texas, Eastern New Mexico, and North Dakota.

metas.name: United States - Oklahoma Fence
metas.description: Red metallic fences are very common in Oklahoma and the surrounding states, particularly Kansas, Texas, and Arkansas. This is not 100% so look for other clues before sending.

metas.name: United States - Oklahoma No Guardrail Reflectors
metas.description:
Oklahoma has no guardrails with reflectors inside it. If you see a guardrail with reflectors, donât guess
Oklahoma.

metas.name: United States - Oklahoma Stop Sign
metas.description: In Oklahoma, you can often find a green rectangular sign with 3 rows of numbers attached to the back of stop signs at rural intersections

metas.name: United States - Oregon Bollard
metas.description: This bollard is extremely common in Oregon and is almost exclusive to this state. It can rarely be seen in California (but usually when it is the case, it is not exactly this bollard, the white rectangle will be bigger or it wonât be all the way on top for example).

metas.name: United States - Oregon Roadlines
metas.description: These short and fine lines can often be seen in between Oregon roadlines which are usually wide, you can see similar lines elsewhere but it is useful to distinguish Oregon from surrounding states especially Washington who also often uses wide roadlines.

metas.name: United States - Oregon Speed
metas.description: Speed signs in Oregon often simply have the word âSpeedâ instead of the standard âSpeed Limitâ.

metas.name: United States - Ouachita Mountains
metas.description: The Ouachita Mountains stretch from Eastern Oklahoma into West-Central Arkansas. Unlike the nearby Ozark Mountains, these mountains are typically more steep in nature and easier to see from a distance.

metas.name: United States - PA Bollards
metas.description:
Pennsylvania bollards are very common on guardrails and sometimes elsewhere. They can be white or
yellow and are recognizable by their shape and black cap.

metas.name: United States - PA Rectangular white signs
metas.description: Rectangular white signs can sometimes be seen attached to signposts at intersections in Pennsylvania. On top, the number of the converging state route is written.

metas.name: United States - Pacific Rainforest
metas.description: Temperate rainforests are found in coastal areas of Washington, Oregon, and Northern California. These rainforests feature many broadleaf trees, large conifers, and ferns.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These rainforests stretch north into coastal British Columbia and Southeast Alaska as well.

metas.name: United States - Prairie Pothole
metas.description: The area spanning from the Montana Border with Saskatchewan to the Western Great Lakes features many âprairie potholes.â These are areas of low-lying wetlands that feature marshy grasses and small, shallow ponds.

metas.name: United States - Publix
metas.description: âPublixâ is a regional supermarket chain that has locations primarily in Florida and adjacent areas of the Deep South.

metas.name: United States - Pueblo Architecture
metas.description: Pueblo Revival style houses are commonly seen in New Mexico. They are typically constructed of adobe or brick and concrete. They have rounded edges and flat roofs, and are usually sand-brown in colour.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Pueblo style houses can also be seen in Arizona and Colorado to a lesser extent.

metas.name: United States - Rectangular Reflector
metas.description: These rectangular raised pavement markers are found in the south and west of the US and also in Massachusetts.

metas.name: United States - Reddish Soil
metas.description: Many parts of the Deep South, stretching from Oklahoma to South Carolina, have reddish soil. The exact tint of the soil can range from yellow to deep red.

metas.name: United States - Rice
metas.description: Rice production only occurs in a few areas of the US, so it is very useful for region guessing. It is typically grown in large, flat fields that resemble low prairies. It is only grown in north-central California and the Lower Mississippi River Valley in Arkansas, Louisiana, Texas, and Mississippi.

metas.name: United States - Rio Grande Valley
metas.description: The Rio Grande Valley in South Texas is extremely flat and features shrubby trees and agricultural fields. This area borders the Mexican state of Tamaulipas.

metas.name: United States - Rocky Mountains
metas.description: The area stretching from the Canadian border to Northern New Mexico is home to the Rocky Mountains. These jagged, rocky formations often feature many pine trees and visible snow all-year round at the highest peaks. Some areas of the Rocky Mountain Range are noticeably dry, with few trees.

metas.name: United States - Sagebrush
metas.description: Great Basin Sagebrush (Artemisia tridentata) is a short, shrubby blue-green bush that is common in the interior western United States.It is most common in arid areas.

metas.name: United States - Saguaro
metas.description: Saguaro cacti are most commonly shaped like tall, straight tubes with several branches extending from the main tube. They are most commonly found in southern Arizona, on the Sonoran border.

metas.name: United States - SC Black Street Signs
metas.description: Black street signs with white text can commonly be found at intersections in South Carolina.

metas.name: United States - SC Reflectors (No Roadlines)
metas.description:
If you see a small road without roadlines that has Southern Reflectors in the middle, you will most likely be in South Carolina.
In other states the reflectors will always be next to roadlines. Sometimes these roadlines can be faded so be careful.

metas.name: United States - Shoprite
metas.description: âShopriteâ is a regional supermarket chain that has locations in 6 states in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic region of the US; Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware, and Maryland.

metas.name: United States - Short Stilts
metas.description: Similar in style to aforementioned stilt houses, houses with much shorter stilts are common in the western and central Gulf Coast. These houses typically feature short stilts made of concrete or wood (1-3 feet off the ground) and are primarily found in areas near the coast and any adjacent rivers.

metas.name: United States - Shotgun Houses
metas.description: Very narrow, one-storey houses made out of wood are called âshotgun houses.â They are most common in and around New Orleans (LA,) Houston (TX,) Louisville (KY,) and the state of Mississippi.

metas.name: United States - Sloped Roofs
metas.description: Buildings with very large, sloped roofs are most common in the states of Oklahoma, Texas, and Louisiana. They can also be seen in neighbouring states to a lesser extent.

metas.name: United States - Southern Pines
metas.description: The loblolly pine (Pinus taeda), and longleaf pine (Pinus palustris), commonly referred to as southern pines in the community, are found throughout the southeastern US. They are a great way to recognize this region, as they are abundant, recognizable and mostly limited to this part of the country. They tend to be tall, with fluffy-looking clusters of pine needles.

metas.name: United States - Soy
metas.description: Soybeans are short, dark green crops organised in long rows and are found in similar regions where corn is grown. They are most common in the Eastern Plains, Midwest, Lower Mississippi Valley, and areas of the Mid Atlantic.

metas.name: United States - Spanish Colonial Revival
metas.description: Spanish Colonial Revival Architecture can be categorised as buildings with lightly-coloured stucco walls and red clay-tile roofs. They can be found in the desert southwest states of California, Nevada, Arizona, and Texas. You can also find similar types of buildings in Florida and coastal Georgia.

metas.name: United States - Spanish Moss
metas.description: Spanish moss, appearing as greyish white drapes, can sometimes be seen on trees in the deep south.

metas.name: United States - Square Guardrails
metas.description: Square guardrails are the most dominant (but not the only) type of guardrail in the states of New York and Wyoming. They have a long bar across the top, with several square legs supporting them.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These guardrails can be found, to a lesser extent, in some adjacent states.

metas.name: United States - Stacked Triplexes
metas.description: Older three story wooden houses, also called âstacked triplexes,â are very common in urban areas of the Northeast. They are most prevalent in New York, Connecticut, Rhode Island, and Massachusetts.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These types of houses are also somewhat common in cities in Atlantic Canada.

metas.name: United States - Stilt Houses
metas.description: Stilt houses can sometimes be seen on the coast. These are especially common toward the south, and on the Atlantic and Gulf coasts.

metas.name: United States - Tablelands
metas.description: The Southwest, centred around the Four Corners region of Utah, Arizona, New Mexico, and Colorado, feature many mesas and tablelands. Often, these rock formations will be red in colour. Additionally, red soil is common in these areas.

metas.name: United States - Texas Bands
metas.description: Yellow or red bands can commonly be seen around signposts in Texas.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Similar reflectors can sometimes be seen in other states, such as Hawaii.

metas.name: United States - Texas Bumps
metas.description: These littles rectangular bumps on center lines are unique to Texas. You can see some round bumps in some other states but rectangular ones are only in Texas.

metas.name: United States - Texas Guardrail Bollards
metas.description:
White Bollard + Grey/Yellow Square.
These bollards are unique to Texas on guardrails in the southern United States.

metas.name: United States - Texas Hills
metas.description: Just west of the metropolitan areas of Austin and San Antonio Texas lies a large area of dry, rocky hills featuring many yucca and prickly pear plants. Texas Live Oak trees are the predominant tree type in this area.

metas.name: United States - Texas Pavement
metas.description: Texan roads often have a grainy, âsalt and pepperâ-like road surface.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Similar pavement can sometimes be seen in adjacent states such as New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Colorado.

metas.name: United States - Thick Center Lines
metas.description: Some roads in West Virginia, Virginia, and Maryland use middle yellow lines that are thicker than traditional yellow road lines.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These are not present on all roads in these states, and can be found elsewhere, so use this tip in conjunction with other clues.

metas.name: United States - Utah Bollard
metas.description: This bollard is unique to Utah.

metas.name: United States - Utah Idaho Bollard
metas.description: This type of bollard with a white square on top is unique to Utah and Idaho. If the square is not totally on top then it should be Idaho.

metas.name: United States - Vermont Small Green Stop Signs
metas.description: Vermont features small rectangular green signs on stop sign posts with three rows of horizontal numbers. The top row of numbers correlates to the highway or road number that the road with the stop sign intersects with. For example, this image is taken from Vermont State Road 116, looking towards the intersecting road.
metas.comparison: The State of New York uses similar style signs. However, these signs can be attached to different types of sign posts (town entry signs, highway signs, etc.)

metas.name: United States - Vertical House Numbers
