metas.description: Properties in rural and exurban Ohio, Lower Michigan, and Indiana commonly feature a vertically-oriented metal sign with white numbers, indicating the house number of the adjacent building. These signs are most commonly blue or green, and are commonly attached to mailboxes.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These may be rarely found in other states.

metas.name: United States - Virginia Rectangle white signs
metas.description: Rectangular white signs can sometimes be seen at intersections in Virginia.

metas.name: United States - Washington Bollard
metas.description: The state of Washington uses bollards that consist of a white or brown post with a white rectangle on the front of the bollard, and two smaller white or silver squares on the back of the bollard.

metas.name: United States - WI Bollard
metas.description: These simple white bollards with black reflectors are unique to Wisconsin.

metas.name: United States - WI Property Markers
metas.description: A horizontal blue, red, or green sign can commonly be seen at the ends of driveways in Wisconsin and the Michigan peninsula. The house number is present, in addition to either the town name and or the road name (usually.)
metas.comparison: NOTE: Nearby states often use similar markers, but typically lack any town or street name information and only feature numbers.

metas.name: United States - WI Warning Pole Plate
metas.description: A rectangular white metal plate, with an orange rectangle and diamond, can be seen on most poles in Wisconsin and the Michigan peninsula.

metas.name: United States - WI/MO Letters
metas.description: Wisconsin and Missouri are the only two states that use a lettering system (A - ZZZ) for their county highways. Wisconsin signs typically have the word âcountyâ above the letter, while Missouri signs typically do not. The borders of the signs also vary slightly.

metas.name: United States - Wyoming Bollard
metas.description: Roadside bollards in Wyoming often feature a dark metal pole with a white circular reflector at the top. The top of the metal pole is sometimes painted white or grey, which is unique to Wyoming.

metas.name: United States - Yellow Posts
metas.description:
Yellow posts like this one are common in Colorado and can be seen more rarely in Utah or Texas. It can rarely be seen in other states.
(Very rare and not the most consistant; I have also seen it twice in Virginia)

metas.name: Albania - Cylinder Water Tanks
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Albania - Italian Style Buildings
metas.description: Albania has a lot of Italian-style buildings:

metas.name: Andorra - Stone Buildings
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Argentina - Jujuy - Red Bricks
metas.description: Red bricks, similar to what is common in Bolivia, can be found in the northwest of the country, especially in western Jujuy.

metas.name: Austria - Alpine Architecture
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Azores - White & Pastel Colors
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Belgium - Red Bricks
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Belgium - South - Gray Tone Stones
metas.description: Houses in the South of the country use a lot of stone, have gray tones and generally look more French.

metas.name: Bermuda - Hamilton
metas.description: Hamilton is by far the largest town on Bermuda, and as such, the downtown area is distinct due to its many large, densely built multi-floor buildings.

metas.name: Bermuda - White Roofs
metas.description:
Most buildings on Bermuda are single family stone houses painted in pastel colours.
They will almost always have completely white roofs.

metas.name: Bhutan - Unique Architecture
metas.description:
The traditional Bhutanese architecture is very distinct.
Most of the houses have tin roofs and wooden painted frames, which give them a unique look.

metas.name: Bolivia - Unfinished Look
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Botswana - Shacks & Bungalows
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Brazil - Acre - Houses On Stilts
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Brazil - Orange Tiled Roofs
metas.description: Many houses throughout Brazil have orange tiled roofs.

metas.name: Brazil - Santa Catarina - European Influence
metas.description: Buildings in the southern states, mainly Santa Catarina, can be of European influence (typically vaguely German) in design and style.

metas.name: Bulgaria - Ghetto-Like Look
metas.description: Suburbs in Bulgaria are generally among the poorest areas in Europe, with small, densely built houses and generally an almost ghetto-like look.

metas.name: Bulgaria - Patches Of Mortar
metas.description: Famously, Bulgarian roofs often seem poorly constructed:

metas.name: Bulgaria - South - Alpine Architecture
metas.description: Buildings with features similar to Alpine architecture, such as white walls with brown wooden details are commonly found in and around the Smoljan region in the south.

metas.name: Cambodia - Blue Windows
metas.description: Traditional Cambodian wooden stilt houses tend to have very recognizable colour schemes:
metas.comparison: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Cambodia - Stilts & Double Roofs
metas.description:
Wooden houses on stilts are common.
Walls are often made of vertical planks.
Many homes have double or triple roofs.

metas.name: Cambodia - Temples
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Cambodia - Tiled & Red Roofs
metas.description:
Many traditional homes have tiled orange or red roofs, sometimes with ornaments on the ridges and corners.
Corrugated and plain metal roofs are also common.
On other, more modern buildings, you can see a wider variety of roof colours and materials.

metas.name: Croatia - Adriatic Coast - Beige Bricks
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Croatia - Red Brick Walls
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: CuraÃ§ao - One Storey Bungalows
metas.description:
Much of the architecture on CuraÃ§ao consists of simple, one storey bungalows that are pastel coloured.
Metal roofs are common on smaller shacks, while tiled roofs can be seen on more expensive houses.
Additionally, multi storey villas can sometimes be seen.

metas.name: Czechia - ÄeskÃ© BudÄjovice - Baroque Architecture
metas.description:
A variant of baroque architecture called SelskÃ© Baroko (folk baroque) can be found in the region surrounding ÄeskÃ© BudÄjovice.
The style is characterised by highly decorated walls, with the setting being small villages rather than towns and cities.

metas.name: Czechia - Diamond Shaped Tiles
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Czechia - Moravia - Architecture
metas.description: Town houses in Moravia typically have two distinctive features:
metas.comparison: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Czechia - North - Dark Wooden Supports
metas.description: Houses with thick, dark wooden poles supporting the upper floors are common in the northernmost parts of the country.

metas.name: Czechia - North - Timber Framed Houses
metas.description: Timber framed houses in Czechia are mostly found along the northern parts of the German border.

metas.name: Czechia - North - White Stripes
metas.description: Dark wooden houses, with white stripes shining through the wood, are common in most of northern Czechia.

metas.name: Czechia - Northwest - Single Pane Windows
metas.description: It is more common to see houses with single pane windows in the northwestern parts of the country.

metas.name: Czechia - Pair Houses
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Czechia - Prefabricated Panel Apartments
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Denmark - Red Bricks
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Denmark - Thatched & Corrugated Roofs
metas.description:
Some houses in Denmark have thatched roofs, especially in rural areas.
You can also sometimes find grey corrugated roofs.
These look somewhat similar to roofs commonly found in Baltic countries.

metas.name: Denmark - Timer Frame Walls
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Ecuador - Grey Bricks
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Estonia - Wood & White Brick
metas.description:
Estonian architecture generally consists of a combination of wood and white brick, typically with somewhat steep corrugated metal roofs.
Painted stone walls are also somewhat common.
While wooden buildings can be found in all three Baltic countries, they are more common in Estonia.

metas.name: Faroe Islands - Above Ground Basements
metas.description:
Faroese houses are typically made of wood, often with an above ground basement made of stone which is painted in a different colour than the wooden part.
Roofs will usually be either metal or have grass on top (turf).

metas.name: Finland - Modern & Utilitarian Architecture
metas.description:
Finnish architecture is mostly modern and utilitarian.
Downtown areas tend to be very modern, with lots of apartment buildings and use of concrete.
Suburbs mostly consist of freestanding single family homes.
Like Sweden and Norway, some wooden buildings, especially in the countryside, are painted in a distinctive dark red colour.

metas.name: France - Alps - Alpine Architecture
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: France - Alsace - Germanic Architecture
metas.description:
Many elements of Germanic architecture are concentrated in Alsace, such as timber framing and half-hip roof.
Furthermore, roofs with fish scale tiles are more common in this region.
Beware that these elements are sometimes incorporated into architecture in other parts of France, and are most reliable in conjunction with one another.

metas.name: France - Basque - Colorful Timber Framing
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: France - Belgian Border - Dark Red Bricks
metas.description:
Rows of dark red brick houses, most similar to Flemish architecture in Belgium, are unsurprisingly found near the Belgian border.
The individual bricks may be outlined by white mortar.

metas.name: France - Brittany - Architecture
metas.description:
Brittany has one of the most recognizable and consistent architectures in the country.
Common elements include, in addition to black roofs, edge chimneys, black slate walls and stones surrounding doors and windows.
The walls will be either very light coloured or made of stone.

metas.name: France - French Riviera - Architecture
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: France - General Architecture
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: France - Northwest - Black Shingle Roofs
metas.description:
Black shingle roofs are primarily found in the northwest, the rough cutoff being the Loire river.
Other areas include near the Belgian border, the south-centre, and the Pyrenees, making black roofs a good clue for Alps-Pyrenees toss-ups.

metas.name: France - Paris - Uneven & Cream Colored Stones
metas.description:
Walls made of uneven cream coloured to orange stones, glued with mortar and often incorporating red brick details can be found in the towns surrounding Paris.
Note that the city of Paris itself generally does not have this architecture.

metas.name: France - South - Rounded Tiles
metas.description: Roofs in the south of the country will often be made up of rounded tiles overlapping one another, often varying in colour.

metas.name: France - Toulouse - Architecture
metas.description:
In and around Toulouse, mainly in old towns, you will commonly find bright orange brick buildings.
They differ from brick houses near Belgium by the bricks being brighter, as well as somewhat Mediterranean looking architectural features, such as wooden shutters, being common.

metas.name: Germany - Central - Black Fish Scale Roofs & Walls
metas.meta_label: Central - Black Fish Scale Roofs & Walls
metas.description: Houses with black slate walls, resembling fish scales, are commonly found in a large area of central Germany.

metas.name: Germany - East - Large Apartment Buildings
metas.description: These large, utilitarian apartment buildings constructed during the socialist era, that are also known as âCommie blocksâ are common in all of former East Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Northwest - Brick Houses
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Germany - Schleswig-Holstein - Thatched Roofs
metas.description:
Thatched roofs and rock walls are most common on the North Frisian Islands, as well as mainland Schleswig-Holstein.
You can also commonly find them in coastal resort towns in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.

metas.name: Greece - Cyclade Islands - White Walls & Blue Doors
metas.meta_label: Cyclade Islands - White Walls & Blue Doors
metas.description: One of the most well-known types of Greek architecture:

metas.name: Greece - Mediterranean Architecture
metas.description: Greek architecture shares a lot of features with other Mediterranean countries:

metas.name: Greece - Thessaloniki - Tall Antennas
metas.description: In Thessaloniki, you will often see a large amount of unusually tall antennas on top of buildings.

metas.name: Greenland - Colorful Wooden Houses
metas.description:
Greenlandic architecture mainly consists of small, colourful, simple looking wooden houses, which even in cities are typically placed quite sparsely.
The major cities have some larger buildings, which normally look fairly minimalistic.

metas.name: Guatemala - Pastel Stone Houses
metas.description:
Guatemalan architecture mainly consists of pastel painted stone houses, commonly with rusted sheet metal roofs.
It is also somewhat common for buildings to be made out of exposed white brick.

metas.name: Hongkong - Tall Apartment Buildings
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Hungary - Red Tiles Roofs & Light Colors
metas.description:
Hungarian houses are typically made of stone, painted in a light colour and almost always with red tiled roofs.
Suburban houses are typically only one storeyed, while more central houses may be taller.
Houses in town and city centres are often fairly old but well-kept.

metas.name: India - Central - Rounded Roof Tiles
metas.description:
Rounded roof tiles are common in central India.
They often appear disorganised and are kept in rows/columns that are not completely straight.

metas.name: India - East Coast - Thatched Roofs
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: India - Goa & Kerala - Modern Homes
metas.description: Goa and Kerala are two of the most developed states in India and often have very wealthy and modern homes.

metas.name: India - Northeast - Square Panels
metas.description: Houses made of square panels separated by thin beams are found in Northeast India.

metas.name: India - Northeast - Triangle Metal Roofs
metas.description: Metal roofs, with a small triangle near the top, are common in Northeast India.

metas.name: India - Punjab - White Domes
metas.description:
Gurdwaras, which can typically be recognised by their white domes and ornate walls, are most common in Punjab.
You can also sometimes recognise them by the Sikh Khanda symbol, which represents the religion.

metas.name: India - South - Organized Tiles
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: India - West Bengal - Diamond Protrusion
metas.description: Flat roof tiles, similar to the ones found in the south, with a small diamond shaped protrusion in the middle, are commonly found in and around West Bengal.

metas.name: India - West Bengal - Metal Hip Roofs
metas.description: Large hip roofs made of corrugated sheet metal are found in West Bengal and adjacent areas in Bihar and Odisha.

metas.name: Indonesia - Bali - Architecture
metas.description:
Architecture in Bali is unique because it was influenced by old Balinese culture and Hinduism.
The most important thing to look for are these crown-like roof pinnacles, found everywhere in Bali.
Guardian statues and slit-drum towers are common too.

metas.name: Indonesia - Churches
metas.description: Indonesia is religiously a Muslim majority country, so seeing churches, and other Christian signs, is a good clue for these regions.

metas.name: Indonesia - Gable Horns
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Indonesia - Java - Tiled Roofs
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Indonesia - Kalimantan - Wooden Chips
metas.description: On Kalimantan, you can find these unique roofs made out of wooden chips.

metas.name: Indonesia - North - Plain Sheet Metal Roofs
metas.description:
Plain sheet metal roofs are more commonly found toward the north, where tiled roofs are not found.
They are most commonly found on Kalimantan, Sulawesi and Sumatra.

metas.name: Indonesia - North Sumatra - Boat Roofs
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Indonesia - Rante Pao - Tongkonan
metas.description:
A small region of South Sulawesi, around the city of Rante Pao, features these very unique houses, called Tongkonan, that have saddle-shaped roofs.
The houses themselves are also elevated from the ground.

metas.name: Indonesia - South Sulawesi - Slots Inside Triangles
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Indonesia - Sumba - High-Pitched Peaks
metas.description: You can find these distinct roofs with uniquely high-pitched peaks on Sumba.

metas.name: Indonesia - West Sumatra - Boat Roofs
metas.description: West Sumatra features these distinct boat-shaped roofs.

metas.name: Ireland - Cream Colors & Black Roofs
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Isle Of Man - Whitewashed Walls
metas.description: Houses with whitewashed walls and entrance walls are a common sight, similar to Ireland.

metas.name: Israel - Blocky Buildings
metas.description:
Architecture tends to consist of bright and warm-coloured stone buildings, often with a blocky appearance.
While Mediterranean-style houses with orange tiled roofs are more common than in other Middle Eastern countries, flat roofs are still just as common.

metas.name: Italy - Alps - Alpine Architecture
metas.description: Alpine architecture, which typically features large buildings with white stone walls and wooden details, are found in the Alpine region.

metas.name: Italy - Aosta Valley - Grey Uneven Bricks
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Italy - Apulian - Flat Roofs
metas.description:
Houses in the Apulian region are generally very light coloured, and have flat roofs, typically with two to three floors.
The architecture is sometimes reminiscent of the Middle East.

metas.name: Italy - General Architecture
metas.description:
Italian architecture mainly consists of pastel coloured stone houses, generally with terracotta roofs.
Houses will very commonly have wooden shutters, which will typically be divided in two and open sideways.

metas.name: Italy - Northeast - Solid Wooden Shutters
metas.description: Solid wooden shutters with black metal hinges is a common feature in the northeast of Italy, particularly in Veneto.

metas.name: Italy - Southeast - Trullo Roofs
metas.description:
This particular style of roof, called a trullo, is unique to the Itria valley in southeastern Italy.
It is particularly common in and around the town of Alberobello.

metas.name: Italy - Tuscany - Unpainted Bricks
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Japan - Chugoku - Red Tiled Roofs
metas.description: These unique red-tiled roofs are most commonly found in Chugoku, especially in the prefectures of Hiroshima and Shimane.

metas.name: Japan - General Architecture
metas.description:
Japanese architecture has many distinct and expressive styles, with many unique buildings.
These can range from traditional country houses, regional designs, modern large cities, coastal reinforced buildings, and anything in between.

metas.name: Japan - North & South - Roof Transition
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Japan - Okinawa - White Buildings & Flat Roofs
metas.description: Okinawa can often be recognised by the white concrete buildings with flat roofs.

metas.name: Jersey - Northern France Architecture
metas.description:
Similarly, the local architecture shares many characteristics with that of northern France.
This includes pastel-coloured walls and dark slate roofs.
However, British-style terraced houses are also common.

metas.name: Jersey - Red Granite
metas.description:
Jersey is home to large reserves of red granite.
As a result, it is a popular building material used for the construction of many walls and houses throughout the island.

metas.name: Jordan - Sandstone Bricks
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Laos - Historical Architecture
metas.description:
Luang Prabang is the former royal capital of Laos and a UNESCO heritage site.
The city has a lot of historical architecture, including several temples.
Many buildings make use of traditional dark wooden architectural elements.

metas.name: Latvia - White Bricks & Corrugated Roofs
metas.description:
Latvian architecture generally consists of a combination of wood and white brick, typically with somewhat steep corrugated metal roofs.
Slightly modern houses with pastel coloured stone walls and houses with a combination of wood with another material, particularly white brick, are also common.

metas.name: Lesotho - Round Huts
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Lithuania - Light Colored Bricks
metas.description:
Lithuanian architecture primarily consists of light coloured brick buildings, usually with somewhat steep corrugated metal roofs.
Wooden buildings are also fairly common, however less so than in Estonia.
Pastel painted stone buildings are somewhat common, especially in newer suburbs.

metas.name: Luxembourg - Dark Slate Roofs
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Macao - Dense Buildings
metas.description: Dense apartment buildings with gridded, narrow streets and cars parked on both sides can be found in this region in the northern half of Macau.

metas.name: Madeira - White, Yellow & Pink Painting
metas.description:
Houses are mainly painted white, grey, or pastel colours such as yellow and pink.
In addition, the red tile roofs will often be in a good condition.

metas.name: Malta - Covered Balconies
metas.description:
This style of traditional covered balconies is very common on Maltese buildings.
They are often painted in bright colours.

metas.name: Malta - Low Storey Buildings
metas.description:
The vast majority of buildings in Malta consist of low storey buildings, with white to beige coloured walls.
Buildings made of limestone are also fairly common.

metas.name: Mexico - Durango - Mud Bricks
metas.description:
Mud brick buildings are most abundant in Durango, especially full houses constructed with mud brick.
However, they can essentially be found in almost all of the dry desert states.

metas.name: Mexico - East - White Concrete Blocks
metas.description:
White concrete block buildings are highly concentrated in the states surrounding Mexico city, and are generally more common to the east.
They can however still be found all over the country.

metas.name: Mexico - North - American Style Bungalows
metas.description:
Architecture in northern Mexico often features design elements from American style bungalows.
Many houses are coloured with light or pastel colours, gated and commonly have front yards.
Orange tiles inspired by Spanish colonial architecture are also typical.

metas.name: Mexico - West - Red Bricks
metas.description: Red brick buildings are mostly concentrated in the states west of Mexico City, specifically Jalisco, Michoacan, Guanajuato, and Aguascalientes.

metas.name: Mexico - Yucatan - Light Colored Rocks
metas.description: These walls made of light coloured rock are found in the Yucatan peninsula, but most common in Yucatan state.

metas.name: Mexico - Yucatan - Thatched Roofs
metas.description:
Thatched roofs are most common in the Yucatan peninsula and eastern San Luis Potosi.
They can also be found elsewhere, mainly in the southeast.

metas.name: Monaco - Luxurious Architecture
metas.description:
Monaco is a rich and densely populated city state, with a Mediterranean feel to it.
The architecture is similar to cities in southern France and northern Italy, but more luxurious.
You will see a lot of apartment buildings, neoclassical details, and pastel colours.

metas.name: Netherlands - North - Very Large Roofs
metas.description: Farms in the north of the Netherlands often have very large roofs.

metas.name: Netherlands - Red-Brownish Bricks
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Netherlands - Row Houses
metas.description:
As mentioned before, row houses are very common in the Netherlands.
Almost half of the Dutch housing stock are row houses, significantly more than almost all other European countries.

metas.name: Netherlands - South - Rolling Shutters
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Nigeria - Steeply Pitched Roofs
metas.description:
Most Nigerian houses are single-storey, with steeply pitched roofs commonly made of metal sheets.
Cinder block walls surrounding the houses are also common.

metas.name: Norway - Black & White Houses
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Norway - Grass Roofs
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Norway - South Coast - Full White Wooden Houses
metas.meta_label: South Coast - Full White Wooden Houses
metas.description: While completely white wooden houses can be found in the entire country, theyâre especially common on the southern coast, where youâll commonly see entire villages made up of them.

metas.name: Oman - Light-Colored Stone
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Panama - Spanish Influence
metas.description:
Panamanian architecture often reflects Spanish colonial influences, featuring vibrant colours, and some ornate detailing.
The most common type of building has painted concrete or sometimes brick walls with red metal sheets or tiles for a roof.
Many windows have bars on them for security.

metas.name: Peru - Diverse Architecture
metas.description: Here are a few examples of types of buildings commonly seen in Peru:

metas.name: Peru - North - Overhanging Roofs
metas.description:
Buildings with overhanging roofs with wooden supports are mostly found in northern regions of Peru.
These buildings are sometimes brightly coloured as well.

metas.name: Peru - South - Red Brick Transition
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Philippines - Marawi - Destroyed Houses
metas.description: In and around the city of Marawi, Mindanao you can find many destroyed houses and ruins from the Marawi siege in 2017.

metas.name: Philippines - Palawan - Diagonal Woven Pattern
metas.description: Houses built with amakan walls (referred to as Sawali in the north) with a diagonally woven pattern are mostly found on the island of Palawan, but can also be found throughout the northern half of the country.

metas.name: Philippines - South - Diamond Pattern
metas.description: Houses built with amakan walls, a traditionally woven bamboo mat, with a diamond pattern are almost exclusively found in the southern half of the country.

metas.name: Poland - East - Traditional Wooden Houses
metas.description: Traditional wooden houses are commonly found in the east, mainly in Podlaskie Voivodeship.

metas.name: Poland - General Architecture
metas.description:
Buildings usually have plain stone walls covered in light or pastel stucco.
Frequent roofing colours are orange or red, black, and brown.
Roof tiles and panes often have a tidy, almost plastic-like look.
Some rural houses have corrugated sheet roofs similar to those often found in the Baltics.
Detached single family homes are common throughout Poland.
They sometimes have a blocky look.

metas.name: Poland - General Architecture #2
metas.description:
In bigger towns, apartment buildings are common.
Many date from communist times, and some of them still have a somewhat austere look.
However, many have been renovated and look nice and well-kept.
Downtown areas are usually dense and often have historic buildings.

metas.name: Portugal - Blue / Yellow Paints
metas.description: Youâll commonly see blue or yellow lines painted around windows and doors, as well as around the edges of walls.

metas.name: Portugal - Mosaic Tiles
metas.description: Houses made of decorative mosaic tiles are somewhat common in Portugal.

metas.name: Portugal - North - Square Blocks & White Mortar
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Portugal - White Stone & Orange Roofs
metas.description: White painted stone houses with orange tiled roofs are extremely common in Portugal.

metas.name: Romania - East - Metal & Fake Tiled Roofs
metas.description: If you see several houses and almost all of them have metal or plastic fake tiled roofs, you will probably be in the eastern half of the country.

metas.name: Romania - Hungarian Border - Hungarian Style
metas.description:
Villages near the Hungarian border will often be built in the same style as villages in Hungary.
This style can be summarised as having long, straight streets with single-storey houses being evenly spaced along the road, typically having the short side of the house facing the road.
The vast majority of roofs will have orange tiles.

metas.name: Romania - MaramureÈ - Decorated Wooden Gates
metas.description: Elaborately decorated wooden gates are commonly found in the region of MaramureÈ.

metas.name: Romania - Single Family Houses
metas.description:
Romanian architecture primarily consists of single-family houses made of stone, typically painted in different pastel colours and with roofs ranging from orange tiles to grey metal.
It is also somewhat common to see houses with walls made of painted square tiles in different patterns.

metas.name: Romania - West - Orange Tiled Roofs
metas.description: If you see several houses and almost all of them have orange tiled roofs, you are likely to be in the western half of the country.

metas.name: Russia - Dagestan - Limestone Bricks
metas.description: Buildings made of white limestone brick are indicative of Dagestan, as well as adjacent regions.

metas.name: Russia - Decorated Window Frames
metas.description:
This style of richly decorated window frames is commonly found on traditional Russian homes, especially on log cabins.
They are often painted blue.

metas.name: Russia - Rectangular Apartments
metas.description:
The vast majority of urban housing in Russia are large rectangular apartment buildings made of simple concrete.
Newer buildings in wealthier areas appear more modern.

metas.name: Russia - Rural Housing
metas.description: Rural housing in Russia consists mostly of a basic wooden structure with metal roofs.

metas.name: Russia - South - Red Bricks
metas.description: Buildings built almost entirely of red brick are mostly found south, but other notable exceptions include Magnitogorsk, Orsk, and Omsk.

metas.name: Rwanda - Ventilation Bricks
metas.description:
Rwandan architecture features a lot of brick and concrete.
Most houses in Rwanda are single family houses, which can have rather steep roofs. Houses also often have fences for protection.
The most notable feature of Rwandan architecture are the âventilation bricks,â which are present in many houses.

metas.name: Slovakia - Diamond Shaped Tiles
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Slovakia - East - Grey Metal Roofs
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Slovakia - Hip End
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Slovakia - Prefabricated Panel Apartments
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Slovenia - Alpine Architecture
metas.description:
Slovenian architecture takes much inspiration from alpine architecture, with light coloured walls, dark wooden details and semi-steep roofs.
The most common roof shape is half-hipped roofs.

metas.name: South Korea - Red Bricks
metas.description: Red brick is a very common building material in South Korea.

metas.name: South Korea - Traditional Tiled Roofs
metas.description:
Many buildings have traditional tiled roofs like these.
These often have decorative elements on the corners, and tend to have sides that curve slightly upwards.
Blue roofs are quite common.

metas.name: Spain - Asturias - Square HÃ³rreos
metas.description:
In Asturias, âhÃ³rreosâ are bigger, generally with a square design, and are built above four pillars, with or without walls.
You will sometimes find a rectangular variation, usually built on top of six or eight pillars called âpaneraâ.
If you find an âhorreoâ with a slate roof, you will be in western Asturias.

metas.name: Spain - Balearic - Full White Houses
metas.description:
The stereotypical Balearic house is painted completely white.
You can find flat roofs, but tiled roofs with a small incline are the most common.

metas.name: Spain - Basque - White Houses
metas.description: Large white houses with wooden frames are common in the Basque Country, the Basque part of Navarra, and Cantabria.

metas.name: Spain - Catalonia & AragÃ³n - Masias
metas.description:
Traditional farm houses called âmasÃ­asâ are common in Catalonia, eastern AragÃ³n and parts of the Valencian Community.
They are usually made of stone and stand isolated or as part of a small complex.

metas.name: Spain - Centre & South - White Towns
metas.description:
Within the centre and south of Spain, towns made completely out of white painted houses are very common in AndalucÃ­a and Extremadura.
You can still see a fair amount of white painted houses in Castilla la Mancha but streets where every house is white will not be common.

metas.name: Spain - Galicia - Big Concrete Blocks
metas.description:
Many houses in Galicia are built with big concrete blocks, sometimes textured to resemble natural stone.
Plain concrete blocks are also an extremely common material for walls and miscellaneous buildings like garages.

metas.name: Spain - Galicia - Cabazos
metas.description:
In Galicia, these unique granaries called âhorreos gallegosâ, or âcabazosâ, are very common.
Note that they can be made from various materials, but the shape remains the same.

metas.name: Spain - Northwest - Slate Roofs
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Orange / Red Tiled Roofs
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Sweden - Dalarna - Wooden Craftsmanship
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Sweden - Diamond Tiled Roofs
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Sweden - General Architecture
metas.description:
Houses in the Swedish countryside are most commonly wooden and often painted with a distinct dark red paint, which is almost exclusively found in Sweden, Norway and Finland.
Urban architecture is usually modern and made of concrete and bricks, while suburban buildings are commonly freestanding single family houses built of either wood or brick.

metas.name: Sweden - Gotland - Limestone
metas.description:
Houses on Gotland are commonly made of limestone and often have a dirty-looking white facade.
Churches on Gotland are very distinct looking, with either grey walls or white walls with grey corners, a large portal around the door and small windows typically divided in two by a pillar.

metas.name: Sweden - Grey Metal Roofs
metas.description:
Grey metal roofs on residential buildings generally get more common the further north in the country you get.
Note that metal roofs on barns and sheds can be found significantly further south.

metas.name: Sweden - HÃ¤lsingland - Big Farmhouses
metas.description:
HÃ¤lsingland has many big, mostly red, farmhouses.
They are characterised by many large windows, 2â3 floors, and the front facade being long and grand-looking.
Barns can also be seen having an unusual amount of windows in the region.

metas.name: Sweden - Northeast Coast - Octagonal Sheds
metas.description:
Along the northern coast you will commonly encounter agricultural sheds which are either octagonal or rectangular, with the walls noticeably leaning outwards.
They will typically be made out of red-painted logs.

metas.name: Sweden - Northwest Coast - Dense Shed Rows
metas.description: Dense rows of very small red sheds are commonly found in coastal towns on the northern west coast.

metas.name: Sweden - Ãland - Stone Bricks
metas.description: This type of uneven stone brick is typically found in houses and rock walls on Ãland, and less commonly in rock walls on Gotland.

metas.name: Sweden - SkÃ¥ne - Colored Triangle
metas.description:
Houses in SkÃ¥ne commonly have either a white stone, or a red brick wall with a coloured wooden triangle beneath the roof on the sides.
Similar houses with other materials (such as grey brick) for the walls can be found elsewhere in the southern half of the country.

metas.name: Sweden - SkÃ¥ne - Red Bricks
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Sweden - SkÃ¥ne & Blekinge - Corrugated Moss Roofs
metas.description:
Corrugated square metal roof panels with moss growing on them are typically found in southern Sweden, particularly in SkÃ¥ne and Blekinge.
It is mainly found on large barns, and the roofs are often very steep.

metas.name: Sweden - South SkÃ¥ne - Half Timbered Houses
metas.description:
Half-timbered houses can be found mainly in the southern half of SkÃ¥ne, but also in the northern half and southern Halland.
It can also be found in Visby on rare occasions.

metas.name: Sweden - West Coast - White Houses
metas.description:
While houses in Sweden are mostly very colourful, on the west coast they are commonly much lighter.
There are an especially large number of white and light yellow houses along the coast between Gothenburg and the Norwegian border.

metas.name: Switzerland - Alpine & Stone Buildings
metas.description:
Swiss and Alpine architecture in general largely consists of stone buildings painted in light and warm colours, often combined with wooden parts and details.
Roofs are typically tiled and of a gable type.
It is extremely common for windows to have wooden shutters which open horizontally in two parts.

metas.name: Switzerland - Appenzell - Barn Connections
metas.description:
Around Appenzell, most houses will consist of a large living house connected to a long barn, such that the roof of the living house and the barn are at a 90Â° angle.
The front facade of the living house will often be divided into small squares, with each window being perfectly contained within a square.

metas.name: Switzerland - Bern - Arch Shapes
metas.description: Large houses with thick roofs, which are shaped like an arch underneath, are common around Bern.

metas.name: Switzerland - GraubÃ¼nden - Decorative Details
metas.description: In the canton of GraubÃ¼nden, you will often come across houses entirely made of stone, with, most commonly white, decorative painted details around windows and the edges of the house.

metas.name: Switzerland - Northeast - Elaborate Timber Frames
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Switzerland - Ticino - Italian Architecture
metas.description:
Not unexpectedly, seeing typical Italian architecture in Switzerland should imply that you are in the Italian-speaking areas in the south, principally the canton of Ticino.
The architectural style is characterized by, typically very smooth, orange-yellow stone walls with multiple floors and orange or brownish tiled roofs.
Green and brown Italian-style window shutters are common.

metas.name: Taiwan - General Architecture
metas.description:
Architecture in Taiwan varies in designs, ranging from cramped, multiple-story housing to flat, single-story houses with backyards.
Many residential buildings have a very boxy look.
A lot of walls are covered in tiles, usually white.
Sheds made out of tin are also featured, commonly painted in a light green colour.

metas.name: Taiwan - Kinmen - Traditional Architecture
metas.description: You can find these small, traditional-looking houses in Kinmen.

metas.name: Taiwan - North - Old & Disorganized Buildings
metas.description: Old and disorganised housing units as well as tall dingy-looking apartment blocks are frequently seen in the urban areas of northern Taiwan.

metas.name: Taiwan - Penghu - Cream Houses
metas.description: White-tinged cream coloured houses are frequently seen in Penghu.

metas.name: Taiwan - Taoyuan - Red Bricks
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Taiwan - Yilan - Multiple-Story Villas
metas.description:
In Yilan, you can find these rich multiple-story villas.
They come in all types of designs and are often gated.

metas.name: Thailand - Corrugated Metal Roofs
metas.description: Gray corrugated metal roofs are most commonly found in the north and south of the country, but can occasionally be found throughout the country.

metas.name: Tunisia - Traditional Blue Paint
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Turkey - Apartment Blocks
metas.description: Tall and somewhat square apartment blocks are very common in Turkey.

metas.name: Turkey - Batman - Spherical Water Tanks
metas.description: White spherical water tanks can be found in the southeast, mainly south of Batman.

metas.name: Turkey - Central - Vertical Water Tanks
metas.description: Vertical water tanks can be found in most of Turkey, but are notably uncommon along the south and west coast.

metas.name: Turkey - East - Metal Roofs
metas.description: Metal roofs are most common in the east.

metas.name: Turkey - Lake Van - Pyramid Shapes
metas.description: Sheet metal roofs shaped like low pyramids are mainly found far east, particularly in the general area surrounding Lake Van.

metas.name: Turkey - NevÅehir - Sandstone Bricks
metas.description: Many buildings in the NevÅehir Province are built by large, light and unevenly coloured, sandstone bricks.

metas.name: Turkey - South - Square Water Tanks
metas.description: Square water tanks with angled corners are found in the south, approximately from Ä°skenderun to Sanliurfa.

metas.name: Turkey - South Coast - Flat Roofs
metas.description: Flat roofs are mostly found in the southeast and to a lesser extent along the south coast.

metas.name: Turkey - South Coast - Horizontal Water Tanks
metas.description: Horizontal water tanks placed on top of vertical water tanks are primarily found in a line following the south coast and going up to ElÃ¢zÄ±Ä.

metas.name: Turkey - West - Tiled Roofs
metas.description:
Tiled roofs are mostly found in the western two thirds of the country.
Note that for this and the following roof-related tips to be reliable, the majority of all visible roofs should preferably be of that type.

metas.name: Ukraine - Single Family Homes
metas.description:
Single-family homes are very common in suburbs and small towns.
These neighbourhoods are often heavily vegetated and tend to look rundown.
Most roads are unpaved.
Buildings are usually made of bricks, often have corrugated roofs, and are invariably surrounded by fences.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Light-Colored Stone
metas.description:
Houses in residential areas are typically made of light-coloured stone.
Reddish stones are often used for sidewalks.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Chimney Pots
metas.description:
Many British buildings have distinct-looking chimneys with multiple so-called chimney pots.
These pots are usually round and brick-coloured.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Identical Look
metas.description:
Suburbs in UK towns tend to have a recognizable look.
They typically feature near-identical houses, often semi-detached, usually with well-manicured lawns.
The road layout can be maze-like, with lots of cul-de-sacs and curvy roads.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Red Bricks
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: United Kingdom - Scotland - Sandstone & Granite
metas.description:
It is common to see houses made of large blocks of sandstone or granite in Scotland.
Granite buildings are common in Aberdeen, red sandstone is common in Glasgow and Dumfries, and yellow sandstone is common in Edinburgh.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Terraced Houses
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: United Kingdom - Timber Framing
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Uruguay - Cube Shaped Houses
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: US Virgin Islands - Unique Architecture
metas.description:
A unique blend of architecture is found on the United States Virgin Islands.
The primary influences are European Renaissance, Spanish Baroque, Rococo and Victorian styles.
Facades with large arches are common, as well as central plazas and courtyards.

metas.name: Black on Yellow Chevron
metas.description: Black on yellow chevrons are mainly found north of Izmir. (The yellow is somewhat orange-ish)

metas.name: Bodrum Architecture
metas.description: Around the city of Bodrum you will commonly find this type of whitewashed buildings with flat roofs, often combined with blue (or light pink) details or unpainted stone walls.

metas.name: Bursa Green Signs and Infrastructure
metas.description: Street signs in Bursa are green, and generally have slightly extruded letters, meaning the signs are not completely flat.

metas.name: Cotton Fields in Turkey
metas.description: Cotton is mainly found in the region surrounding the city of ÅanlÄ±urfa.

metas.name: Eastern Divider
metas.description: Four-lane divided highways with no divider, other than double middle road lines, are almost exclusively found in the eastern half of the country.

metas.name: Flat Roofs
metas.description: Flat roofs are mostly found in the southeast and to a lesser extent along the south coast.

metas.name: Goreme
metas.description: GÃ¶reme, west of Kayseri, can be recognised by the tall sandstone monoliths with ancient dwellings carved into them.

metas.name: Horizontal Tanks with Vertical Tanks Under
metas.country: Horizontal Tanks with Vertical Tanks Under
metas.description: Horizontal water tanks placed on top of vertical water tanks are primarily found in a line following the south coast and going up to ElÃ¢zÄ±Ä.

metas.name: Istanbul Street Signs
metas.description: Red street signs with a coloured bottom strip are found in several cities. In the bottom right corner, you can find a white arrow and some numbers. If this arrow is pointing in both directions and has a single arrowhead, rather than double, then you are almost certainly in Istanbul.

metas.name: Izmir Province Street Signs
metas.description: Street signs in the Izmir Province are dark blue, noticeably bulge outwards and very commonly have the emblem of Izmir in white at the top of the sign.

metas.name: Lake Van
metas.description: Lake Van is by far the biggest lake in Turkey and has a semi-arid landscape, being surrounded by dry grassy hills and occasional trees and agricultural fields near the shore.

metas.name: Metal Roofs
metas.description: Metal roofs are most common in the east.

metas.name: Mount Ararat
metas.description: Mount Ararat, labelled as AÄrÄ± DaÄÄ± on Google Maps, is a dormant volcano in far eastern Turkey and the tallest mountain in the country. It is often seen together with KÃ¼Ã§Ã¼k AÄrÄ±, a smaller volcano to the southeast.

metas.name: NevÅehir Province Buildings
metas.description: Many buildings in the NevÅehir Province are built by large, light and unevenly coloured, sandstone bricks.

metas.name: Northeast Hills
metas.description: In the northeast you will find uncultivated grasslands in valleys surrounded by round hills. Trees are very limited in the region. In Generation 3 the area has an extremely distinct look, with deep green grass covering the hills. It is significantly more difficult to recognise in Generation 4, where the grass has a more arid look.
metas.comparison: Some of the new Gen 4 truck coverage is greener since it was also taken in the spring.

metas.name: Olive Trees
metas.description: Olive trees are mainly found on the Mediterranean coast.

metas.name: Phone Codes in Turkey
metas.description: Turkish area codes follow a fairly easy to learn pattern and can be very useful to get the general region. Most notably, the first digit of area codes are ordered from 2 in the west to 4 in the east.

metas.name: Pyramid Metal Roofs
metas.description: Sheet metal roofs shaped like low pyramids are mainly found far east, particularly in the general area surrounding Lake Van.

metas.name: River Cliff Valleys
metas.description: River valleys surrounded by steep, barren and rocky cliff sides can be found between the cities of Erzurum and Artvin and in the southeast near the city of HakkÃ¢ri.

metas.name: Road with Extreme Fog
metas.description: This Road with extreme fog and yellow lines can be seen southeast of Izmit.

metas.name: Spherical Water Tanks
metas.description: White spherical water tanks can be found in the southeast, mainly south of Batman.

metas.name: Square Water Tanks
metas.description: Square water tanks with angled corners are found in the south, approximately from Ä°skenderun to Sanliurfa.

metas.name: Street Signs in Ankara Province
metas.description: Street signs in the Ankara Province are blue with a small round top. Similar street signs can very rarely be found in Giresun.
metas.comparison: Beware that some newer street signs are red.

metas.name: Sunflowers
metas.description: Sunflowers are mainly found in northwestern Turkey.

metas.name: Tea Plantations
metas.description: Tea plantations are common in the province of Rize

metas.name: Tiled Roofs
metas.description: Tiled roofs are mostly found in the western two thirds of the country.

metas.name: Turkish Greenhouses
metas.description: If you find yourself surrounded by greenhouses, you are likely to be along the south coast west of Adana.

metas.name: Turkish Pines
metas.description: Turkish pines (pinus brutia) are mainly found near the Mediterranean coast.

metas.name: Turkish Vineyards
metas.description: A majority of all vineyards in Turkey can be found in a region east of Izmir.

metas.name: Volcanic Rocks
metas.description: Dark, volcanic rocks are commonly found between the cities of ÅanlÄ±urfa and DiyarbakÄ±r.

metas.name: Yellow on Black Chevron
metas.description: Yellow on black chevrons are mainly found in and around the BalÄ±kesir Province in the west and in the Kars Province in the far east. Beware that you may very rarely find them elsewhere.

metas.name: 45Â° angle transformers
metas.description: Transformers on Prince Edward Island and Nova Scotia will be installed at a 45Â° angle relative to the road. On PEI, red numbers will usually be written on the side.

metas.name: Alberta bollards
metas.description: Alberta has a unique black and white bollard that is often found at intersections. It has a cylindrical shape and two black bands that wrap all the way around. It is one of the most useful Canadian bollards to learn because it appears so frequently.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Some Alberta bollards have a yellow band between the two black bands, instead of a white one. Blue bands can also rarely be seen, particularly in and around Calgary, while green bands are rarely seen in and around Edmonton.

metas.name: Alberta license plates
metas.description: Alberta license plates has red text on white background, it shows up as a red tint in the blur. It can be hard to see and it takes some time to get used to spotting it. Front plates are NOT required. Note: New Brunswick has similar license plates.

metas.name: British Columbian speed limit signs
metas.description: Some provinces have unique speed signs.
metas.comparison: British Columbian signs include the âkm/hâ but lack the black section in the Ontario sign.

metas.name: Concrete barriers
metas.description: British Columbia predominantly uses concrete barriers instead of guardrails.

metas.name: Exposed rocks
metas.description: The Canadian Shield extends through the eastern part of Canada. Therefore, you will commonly see exposed rocks on street view in the highlighted area.

metas.name: Green and white striped sticker
metas.description: You can sometimes find a green and white striped sticker on signposts in Manitoba.

metas.name: Manitoba bollards
metas.description: Manitoba uses black and grey painted bollards. Most of the time an orange stripe will be present below the grey one.
metas.comparison: Wooden, rectangular bollards of this form are typically found further north in Manitoba NOTE: Bollards in this format with just a black top are seen in Manitoba and Saskatchewan.

metas.name: Manitoba license plates
metas.description: Manitoba license plates has green on both sides. Front plates are required.

metas.name: Newfoundland bins
metas.description: Bins made of wood planks can be seen on Newfoundland driveways. These are most commonly octagonal, however they can have other shapes.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Although they are most common in Newfoundland, they can also sometimes be seen in other provinces, such as New Brunswick.

metas.name: Newfoundland fire hydrant markers
metas.description: Fire hydrants in Newfoundland often have a diamond-shaped marker next to them.

metas.name: Ontario diamond-shaped markers
metas.description: You can find these diamond-shaped markers on the sides of the roads in Ontario. The colours can vary.

metas.name: Ontario KM markers
metas.description: Ontario KM markers have a white square at the bottom, which is unique to the province.

metas.name: Ontario pole tops
metas.description: These distinctive pole tops are most commonly found in Ontario. They have two insulators to the side, and one on top. The side insulators are affixed to the pole with a distinct attachment. Sometimes, multiple of them can be stacked on top of each other.
metas.comparison: NOTE: They can occasionally appear in British Columbia, Nova Scotia, or other provinces more rarely.

metas.name: Ontario speed limit signs
metas.description: Some provinces have unique speed signs.
metas.comparison: Ontario speed limit signs may have a black section on the bottom with the words âkm/hâ or âbeginsâ written in white.

metas.name: Ontario traffic cones
metas.description: Ontario uses distinct orange and black striped traffic cones.

metas.name: Ontario wooden guardrail posts
metas.description: In Ontario, you will often see these types of guardrails. They consist of cylindrical wooden posts, held together by precisely three metal wires. Some posts are marked by a reflective white band.

metas.name: Prince Edward Island red soil
metas.description: Prince Edward Island soil has a distinct red tint to it. Potato farming is also very common on PEI.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This type of soil can occasionally be seen in certain areas of New Brunswick and Nova Scotia.

metas.name: QuÃ©bec bollards
metas.description: QuÃ©bec has unique bollards that are always attached to guardrails. They are long, thin white poles with a red or green reflector at the top.

metas.name: QuÃ©bec fire hydrant markers
metas.description: You will often find these yellow fire hydrant markers atop signposts in QuÃ©bec.
metas.comparison: In QuÃ©bec City these markers will usually have a blue rectangle and markers in Trois-RiviÃ¨res are distinctly small. NOTE: Sometimes the markers will have different colours. Beware that Edmundston, in New Brunswick, uses these too.

metas.name: QuÃ©bec French speed limit signs
metas.description: Some provinces have unique speed signs.
metas.comparison: QuÃ©bec can sometimes have French on their speed limit signs.

metas.name: QuÃ©bec poles
metas.description: Some QuÃ©bec poles have recognizable pole tops with insulator rods that are angled slightly upwards.

metas.name: QuÃ©bec traffic cones
metas.description: QuÃ©bec has unique orange and white striped traffic cones.

metas.name: Saskatchewan alternating insulators
metas.description: Pole top insulators in Saskatchewan alternate. While one pole will have one insulator on the left and two on the right, the next will have two on the left and one on the right.

metas.name: Saskatchewan license plates
metas.description: Saskatchewan license plates has green text on white background, it shows up as a green tint in the blur. It can be hard to see and it takes some time to get used to spotting it. Front plates are NOT required.

metas.name: Stop and ArrÃªt signs
metas.description: Stop signs with both âStopâ and âArrÃªtâ are most commonly found in New Brunswick.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Such stop signs can rarely be found in other provinces.

metas.name: Transformers facing the road
metas.description: The transformers on poles will face the road in British Columbia and New Brunswick, while in other provinces, it will be parallel with the wires.

metas.name: White triangles on signpost
metas.description: Signposts in Saskatchewan can feature these white triangles. The number can vary.

metas.name: Wooden post pyramid top
metas.description: In Newfoundland and Labrador, most wooden posts on guardrails have this pyramid shaped top. Occasionally, you can spot them on standalone posts and signposts as well.

metas.name: Canada - Bollard
metas.description: Alberta has a unique black and white bollard that is often found at intersections. It has a cylindrical shape and two black bands that wrap all the way around. It is one of the most useful Canadian bollards to learn because it appears so frequently.

metas.name: Canada - Quebec guardrail Bollards
metas.description: Quebec has unique bollards that are always attached to guardrails. They are long, thin white poles with a red or green reflector at the top.

metas.name: Canada - Saskatchewan & Manitoba Bollard
metas.description: Manitoba uses black and grey painted bollards. Most of the time an orange stripe will be present below the grey one.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Bollards in this format with just a black top are seen in Manitoba and Saskatchewan.

metas.name: Chile - Bollards
metas.description: Chilean bollards are similar to Spanish style bollards, with a white reflector at the front and a yellow-orange reflector at the back. They are not super common. While regular bollards are somewhat rare in Chile, you may sometimes find this orange, temporary bollard, with two white stripes at the top.

metas.name: Colombia - Spanish bollard
metas.description: This spanish bollard is mostly found in Cundinamarca, the area surrounding BogotÃ¡, but also on the 40 towards Villavicencio.

metas.name: Ecuador - Bollards
metas.description: Ecuador is one of the few Latin American countries where bollards are very common.
metas.comparison: You will find two main types of bollards: A round bollard with two red stripes, A flat bollard with two red reflectors on black. Many other bollards can be found, however, they will almost always have the same colour scheme and style. NOTE: A similar rectangular bollard can sometimes be found in Malaysia.

metas.name: Mexico - Bollard
metas.description: These small, cylindrical white bollards with a black base are unique to Mexico. A yellow reflector is sometimes seen, as well as a flat version.

metas.name: Mexico - Jalisco Bollard
metas.description: Jalisco bollards will sometimes have a crown and the text âJaliscoâ written on it. These are usually barely legible unless very close, however no other Mexican bollard will have writing on it.

metas.name: Mexico - Nayarit Bollard
metas.description: Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit, apart from one exception being Federal Highway 190 on the Oaxaca-Chiapas border.

metas.name: Peru - Bollards
metas.description: Bollards in Peru are painted red or yellow, and the country mainly uses a variety of triangularshaped concrete bollards. Occasionally you will also spot other designs, such as these circular concrete variants.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These concrete variants can also be found in Bolivia and Brazil so do not rule out these countries if you find such bollards.

metas.name: Peru - Lima/Ica 1S Bollard
metas.description: These bollards are only found on the 1S highway between the towns of Ica and Lima.

metas.name: Peru - Moquegua Bollard
metas.description: This cylindrical bollard, with a black and yellow stripe at the top, is unique to the state of Moquegua, which is located in the south of Peru.

metas.name: Peru - North Lima Bollard
metas.description: This bollard is only found on the 1N highway north of Lima (still within Lima region).

metas.name: Peru - Tacna Bollard
metas.description: This bollard is almost exclusive to Tacna region. It does spill into Moquegua but it is by far most common in Tacna.

metas.name: United States - Idaho/Utah Bollard
metas.description: This thin bollard with a small white reflector at the top is unique to Utah and Idaho

metas.name: United States - Montana/South Dakota Bollard
metas.description: The most common type of roadside bollard in South Dakota and Montana features a dark metal post with a white diamond on each side of the top.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These bollards can be found to a lesser extent in other western states.

metas.name: United States - Nevada Bollard
metas.description: This bollard is found in Nevada. It consists of a reflector on a thin stick. The reflector is a vertical rectangle that consists of a white field surrounded by a black outline.

metas.name: United States - Oregon Bollard
metas.description: This bollard is unique to Oregon state in US.

metas.name: United States - Washington Bollard
metas.description: The state of Washington uses bollards that consist of a white or brown post with a white rectangle on the front of the bollard, and two smaller white or silver squares on the back of the bollard.

metas.name: United States - Western Bollards
metas.description: These bollards are found in the upper western states from Utah to Washington.
metas.comparison: The white version is more common in Washington, Oregon and Idaho The green version is more common in Montana, Idaho and Utah The black version is more common in Wyoming, Utah, South Dakota and colorado NOTE: Technically, all colors can be found in every western state, but the likelihood of finding them is higher in the states listed.

metas.name: United States - Wyoming Bollard
metas.description: Roadside bollards in Wyoming often feature a dark metal pole with a white circular reflector at the top. The top of the metal pole is sometimes painted white or grey, which is unique to Wyoming

metas.name: Uruguay - Bollard
metas.description: These white bollards, with one side often painted yellow, and stone barriers, are specific to Uruguay.

metas.name: Austria - Austria
metas.description: Hat - Austria, Bulgaria, Czechia, Slovakia. > those with Horizontal Crosswalk - Austria.

metas.name: Belgium - Belgium Lego Man
metas.description: Horizontal Zebra stripe: Austria, Belgium, Greece, Poland, Serbia. > LEGO MAN: Belgium.

metas.name: Bosnia - Belt + Straight Legs Croatia/Bosnia
metas.description: White Belt: Croatia/Bosnia, Portugal, Germany, Hungary. > Non-Pointed Shoes: Croatia/Bosnia, Portugal. > Straight legs: Croatia/Bosnia.

metas.name: Bulgaria - 4 Stripes + Hat Bulgaria
metas.description: Hat - Austria, Bulgaria, Czechia, Slovakia. > those with 4 Zebra Stripes: Bulgaria.

metas.name: Croatia - Belt + Straight Legs Croatia/Bosnia
metas.description: White Belt: Croatia/Bosnia, Portugal, Germany, Hungary. > Non-Pointed Shoes: Croatia/Bosnia, Portugal. > Straight legs: Croatia/Bosnia.

metas.name: Czech - Tucked-in Czechia
metas.description: Hat - Austria, Bulgaria, Czechia, Slovakia. > Those with 5 Zebra Stripes: Czechia, Slovakia. > Extra blue border on edge and Tucked-in shirt: Czechia. White border on edge and Draping jacket at waist: Slovakia.

metas.name: Denmark - 3Denmark
metas.description: Denmark's guy has a chill walking posture and has rounded edges on the person. Often found on thicker, 3D blue squares. His arms are also pointed down, unlike some similar signs found in Scandinavia.

metas.name: Estonia - Estonia Detailed 3 Stripes
metas.description: 3 Zebra Stripes: Estonia, Lithuania, Russia, Ukraine. Neck / Shoes / Detailed outline is unique to Estonia.

metas.name: Finland - Five Stripe Finland
metas.description: Detailed man without a hat and 5 Zebra stripes is Finland. Features both the detailed man's outline and the bold rounded, non-detailed person. Finland's bold non-detailed man with 5 zebra stripes has one arm pointed up, unlike Denmark.

metas.name: France - Fat White Border France
metas.description: Has 2 designs, one of them has no bent elbow on the left arm which is unique to France. The other is the standard Italy-styled one, but French pedestrian signs all share a fat white border not found elsewhere.

metas.name: Germany - Flat-Arm-on-Inside Germany
metas.description: White Belt: Croatia, Portugal, Germany, Hungary. > Pointed Shoes: Germany, Hungary. > Germany Belt: Above hip. Hungary Belt: Bottom of hip. Germany arm: Flat side on left. Hungary arm: Flat side on right.

metas.name: Greece - Greece
metas.description: Horizontal Zebra stripe: Austria, Belgium, Greece, Poland, Serbia. > Detailed guy with no hat: Greece. Note that Greece's icon has hair that may almost look like a hat but it's just hair. Kinda looks like the Dame Tu Cosita guy

metas.name: Hungary - Flat-Arm-on-Outside Hungary
metas.description: White Belt: Croatia, Portugal, Germany, Hungary. > Pointed Shoes: Germany, Hungary. > Germany Belt: Above hip. Hungary Belt: Bottom of hip. Germany arm: Flat side on left. Hungary arm: Flat side on right.

metas.name: Iceland - Yellow Iceland
metas.description: Iceland is the only sign with a yellow triangle instead of white.

metas.name: Italy - Blue-Corners Italy
metas.description: Italy, Romania, Serbia, and Slovenia all look about the same. Thankfully Romania will not have a white/silver border. Italy will have blue corners visible outside the white edge.

metas.name: Latvia - Long Leg Latvia
metas.description: You can identify Latvia from their guy with weirdly long legs. Long as hell for what. It's arguable Russia/Ukraine/Lithuania has long legs but even so they have 3 zebra stripes, not 5.

metas.name: Lithuania - Lithuania Fatty
metas.description: 3 Zebra Stripes: Estonia, Lithuania, Russia, Ukraine. > Cross off Estonia and Russia (detailed guy in Estonia, Yellow borders in Russia) and you're left with Lithuania and Ukraine. Lithuania's guy is a liiittle bit more fat in the torso than Ukraine and the blue is generally more vibrant than Ukraine.

metas.name: Netherlands - Zeester
metas.description: Netherlands' guy has funny limbs, they shrink towards the end sorta like a starfish.

metas.name: Norway - Norway
metas.description: 4 Zebra Stripes: Norway, Sweden, Bulgaria. > Bold, non-detailed person: only Norway.

metas.name: Poland - Poland
metas.description: Horizontal Zebra stripe: Austria, Belgium, Greece, Poland, Serbia. > Single & continuous line: Only Poland.

metas.name: Portugal - Belt + Bent Knees Portugal
metas.description: White Belt: Croatia/Bosnia, Portugal, Germany, Hungary. > Non-Pointed Shoes: Croatia/Bosnia, Portugal. Bent knees: Portugal.

metas.name: Romania - Romania
metas.description: Italy, Romania, Serbia, and Slovenia all look about the same. Thankfully Romania will not have a white/silver border.

metas.name: Russia - Russia
metas.description: 3 Zebra Stripes: Estonia, Lithuania, Russia, Ukraine. > Russia is the only one with yellow borders.

metas.name: Serbia - Switch-up Serbia
metas.description: Serbia has 2 different pedestrian signs. Horizontal Zebra stripe: Austria, Belgium, Greece, Poland, Serbia. > No hat + rounded, non-detailed guy: Serbia. OR 5 Zebra stripes + rounded guy + no belt + white/silver border + no blue corners: Serbia, and Slovenia.

metas.name: Slovakia - Hanging Jacket Slovakia
metas.description: Hat - Austria, Bulgaria, Czechia, Slovakia. > Those with 5 Zebra Stripes: Czechia, Slovakia. > Extra blue border on edge and Tucked-in shirt: Czechia. White border on edge and Draping jacket at waist: Slovakia.

metas.name: Slovenia - Slovenia
metas.description: Italy, Romania, Serbia, and Slovenia all look about the same. Thankfully Romania will not have a white/silver border. Italy will have blue corners visible outside the white edge.

metas.name: Spain - Bola Ocho
metas.description: Spain has a whopping 8 zebra stripes.

metas.name: Sweden - Swedish Gyatt
metas.description: 4 Zebra Stripes: Norway, Sweden, Bulgaria. > Detailed man without a hat: only Sweden. Personally I easily identify Sweden from the gyatt

metas.name: Turkey - Extra Height Turkey
metas.description: Turkey's sign has extra blue space above the triangle compared to the rest.

metas.name: Ukraine - Skinny Ukraine
metas.description: 3 Zebra Stripes: Estonia, Lithuania, Russia, Ukraine. > Cross off Estonia and Russia (detailed guy in Estonia, Yellow borders in Russia) and you're left with Lithuania and Ukraine. Lithuania's guy is a liiittle bit more fat in the torso than Ukraine and the blue is generally more vibrant than Ukraine.

metas.name: Agricultural golden fields
metas.description: Agricultural golden fields can commonly be seen in eastern Washington.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Flat areas of northern and eastern Oregon can have a similar appearance.

metas.name: Alaska license plates
metas.description: There are three variants of Alaska license plates.

metas.name: Alaskan highway shield
metas.description: The Alaskan highway shield has an image of the Big Dipper constellation on the bottom left.

metas.name: California utility poles
metas.description: Utility poles in California usually have markings at the bottom of the pole that consist of 3 yellow stripes.

metas.name: Connecticut license plates
metas.description: Connecticut license plates are blue on top and fades into white on the bottom. Front plates are required.

metas.name: Corn fields
metas.description: Corn fields can most commonly be found in these regions. For a detailed overview, see this map.

metas.name: Delaware license plates
metas.description: Delaware license plates has gold text on dark blue background, it shows up as a dark blue blur with gold in the middle, and is easy to spot. Front plates are NOT required. Note: A similar plate can be found in Michigan.

metas.name: Hanging traffic lights and signs
metas.description: Many large intersections in Michigan have stop lights and signs that hang from wires that stretch across the middle of the intersection. These markers are commonly in yellow boxes.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These are not completely unique to Michigan, but are most commonly seen there.

metas.name: Hawaiian language
metas.description: Hawaii is the only state to use its own language, though English is still predominantly used. Most place names are in Hawaiian, so you can spot it on street signs, and other road markers.
metas.comparison: Hawaiian is a vowel-oriented language that only uses eight consonants: H, K, L, M, N, P, W, and (Ê»), called an Ê»Okina. Every Hawaiian word ends in one of 5 vowels: A, E, I, O, or U. Each vowel can also have a macron over it: Ä, Ä, Äª, Å, and Åª. These vowels are often combined to make Diphthongs. I.e. UI, AI, AE, etc...

metas.name: Hawaiian topography
metas.description: Topography on Hawaii is characterised by many sloping volcanoes, rugged cliffs, hills, valleys and craters. Such distinct topography combined with tropical vegetation is a good way to identify Hawaii.

metas.name: Minnesota black-and-white marker
metas.description: On most rural âstopâ signposts in Minnesota, a black-and-white marker is attached to the posts horizontally. The shape may vary slightly.

metas.name: Nebraska Sandhills
metas.description: The Nebraska Sandhills are a recognizable region of rolling hills covered with prairie grass in the central-north part of the state.

metas.name: Nevada Bollards
metas.description: This bollard is found in Nevada. It consists of a reflector on a thin stick. The reflector is a vertical rectangle that consists of a white field surrounded by a black outline.

metas.name: New Mexico license plates
metas.description: New Mexico license plates has red text on yellow background or yellow text on green background, it shows up as a mostly yellow or green blur, and is easy to spot. Front plates are NOT required.

metas.name: Oil pumpjacks
metas.description: Oil pumpjacks are short, industrial-looking metal structures located at the surface of oil fields and are used to pump crude oil from the earth below. They are most common in western states, particularly in Texas, Eastern New Mexico, and North Dakota.

metas.name: Red mesas and tablelands
metas.description: The Southwest, centred around the Four Corners region of Utah, Arizona, New Mexico, and Colorado, feature many mesas and tablelands. Often, these rock formations will be red in colour. Additionally, red soil is common in these areas.

metas.name: Red soil
metas.description: Many parts of the Deep South, stretching from Oklahoma to South Carolina, have reddish soil. The exact tint of the soil can range from yellow to deep red.

metas.name: Southern pines
metas.description: The loblolly pine (Pinus taeda), and longleaf pine (Pinus palustris), commonly referred to as southern pines in the community, are found throughout the southeastern US. They are a great way to recognize this region, as they are abundant, recognizable and mostly limited to this part of the country. They tend to be tall, with fluffy-looking clusters of pine needles.

metas.name: Texan roads
metas.description: Texan roads often have a grainy, âsalt and pepperâ-like road surface.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Similar pavement can sometimes be seen in adjacent states such as New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Colorado.

metas.name: The Great Basin
metas.description: The Great Basin, centred around Nevada, can be recognized by the tall, sometimes snow-capped mountains in the background. There are dry, but grassy, and slightly shrubby plains leading up to the mountains.
metas.comparison: The tallest mountains are in Nevada, Utah and California. More gradual, rocky hills can be seen in Oregon, and greener mountains can be seen in Idaho and central Utah. Keep in mind that there are exceptions, so make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

metas.name: The Rocky Mountains
metas.description: The area stretching from the Canadian border to Northern New Mexico is home to the Rocky Mountains. These jagged, rocky formations often feature many pine trees and visible snow all-year round at the highest peaks. Some areas of the Rocky Mountain Range are noticeably dry, with few trees.

metas.name: Vermont license plates
metas.description: Vermont license plates has white text on green background, it shows up as a green blur with white on the sides, and is easy to spot. Front plates are required.

metas.name: Washington bollards
metas.description: The state of Washington uses bollards that consist of a white or brown post with a white rectangle on the front of the bollard, and two smaller white or silver squares on the back of the bollard.

metas.name: Wide middle lines
metas.description: Yellow lines with a noticeably larger gap in between them are most common in Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Oregon. They can also be found to a lesser extent in Washington, Alabama, and Michigan.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Wide middle lines can also rarely appear in other states, so consider other clues before guessing.

metas.name: Wisconsin pole plate
metas.description: A rectangular white metal plate, with an orange rectangle and diamond, can be seen on most poles in Wisconsin and the Michigan peninsula.

metas.name: Alabama license plates
metas.description: Front plates are NOT required.

metas.name: Arizona license plates
metas.description: Front plates are NOT required.

metas.name: Black between middle lines
metas.description: A black stripe can sometimes be seen in between the two yellow, middle road lines in California.

metas.name: California Central Valley
metas.description: Central Valley, California can be recognized by its Mediterranean climate. This is reflected in its agriculture, seen in the vineyards and olive trees that can commonly be found here.
metas.comparison: In addition, rolling hills can be seen toward the edges of the valley.

metas.name: Colorado license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: Concrete highways
metas.description: Concrete paving on main highways is much more common in Iowa than in other states.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Concrete paving on residential streets is commonly seen throughout the Midwest states and parts of the East Coast.

metas.name: Cotton
metas.description: Cotton is a crop that produces large fields of fluffy white flowers. It is most commonly produced in coastal Southeast States, the Lower Mississippi River Valley, Western Texas, and parts of California and Arizona. You can click here for a more detailed map.
metas.comparison: NOTE: When cotton is not fully grown (earlier in the year) cotton fields often look like image number 2.

metas.name: Diamond bollards
metas.description: The most common type of roadside bollard in South Dakota and Montana features a dark metal post with a white diamond on each side of the top.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These bollards can be found to a lesser extent in other western states.

metas.name: Double signpost
metas.description: Signs attached to two signposts can be seen in Michigan. Not all signs are attached to two signposts.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Double signposts can also be seen in other states, but are not as common.

metas.name: Douglas firs
metas.description: Extremely tall conifer trees (Douglas firs) with a dark brown bark, and dark green leaves, can most commonly be seen in Cascadia. Notably, they can also be found in northern California, Idaho and as far east as Montana.
metas.comparison: Beware that they are also commonly found in British Columbia.

metas.name: Eastern white pine
metas.description: The Eastern white pine (Pinus strobus) is a large pine native to eastern North America. It can be found in the Great Lakes region and in the Appalachian Mountains.
metas.comparison: Image source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/nrs/atlas/tree/v3/129

metas.name: Florida license plates
metas.description: Florida license plates has green text on a white background, and it has oranges in the middle, which makes the plate unique. Front plates are NOT required.

metas.name: Georgia license plates
metas.description: Front plates are NOT required.

metas.name: Hawaii license plates
metas.description: Hawaii license plates has black text on a white background. It also has a rainbow in the background that is somtimes more or less visible. Front plates are required.

metas.name: Idaho license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: Illinois license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: Indiana license plates
metas.description: Front plates are NOT required.

metas.name: Kansas white reflectors
metas.description: These white reflectors on signposts are unique to Kansas. They are most commonly seen on âstopâ signs in rural areas.

metas.name: Maryland license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: Massachusetts license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: Minnesota yellow signs
metas.description: In Minnesota, these yellow signs with vertical, black triangles are placed before bridges at most major river crossings and at the beginnings and ends of guardrail sections on large highways.

metas.name: Nevada license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: New Hampshire license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: New Jersey license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: New York license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: No middle line
metas.description: Some small roads in California lack a middle yellow line; instead only feature solid white lines on each side of the road.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This can rarely be seen in other states.

metas.name: North Dakota license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: Oklahoma license plates
metas.description: Front plates are NOT required.

metas.name: Oregon license plates
