metas.description: Oregon license plates has blue text on white background with a green tree in the middle, it shows up as a green dot in the white/blue blur on the sides. Front plates are required.

metas.name: Prairie potholes
metas.description: The area spanning from the Montana Border with Saskatchewan to the Western Great Lakes features many âprairie potholes.â These are areas of low-lying wetlands that feature marshy grasses and small, shallow ponds.

metas.name: Rice
metas.description: Rice production only occurs in a few areas of the US, so it is very useful for region guessing. It is typically grown in large, flat fields that resemble low prairies. It is only grown in north-central California and the Lower Mississippi River Valley in Arkansas, Louisiana, Texas, and Mississippi. You can click here for a more detailed map.
metas.comparison: NOTE: When rice is not fully grown, rice fields often look similar to image 2.

metas.name: Sagebrush
metas.description: Great Basin Sagebrush (Artemisia tridentata) is a short, shrubby blue-green bush that is common in the interior western United States.It is most common in arid areas.

metas.name: Saguaro cacti
metas.description: Saguaro cacti are most commonly shaped like tall, straight tubes with several branches extending from the main tube. They are most commonly found in southern Arizona, on the Sonoran border.

metas.name: South Dakota license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: Soybeans
metas.description: Soybeans are short, dark green crops organised in long rows and are found in similar regions where corn is grown. They are most common in the Eastern Plains, Midwest, Lower Mississippi Valley, and areas of the Mid Atlantic.

metas.name: Spanish moss
metas.description: Spanish moss, appearing as greyish white drapes, can sometimes be seen on trees in the deep south.

metas.name: Speed instead of Speed Limit
metas.description: Speed signs in Oregon often simply have the word âSpeedâ instead of the standard âSpeed Limitâ.

metas.name: Temperate rainforests
metas.description: Temperate rainforests are found in coastal areas of Washington, Oregon, and Northern California. These rainforests feature many broadleaf trees, large conifers, and ferns.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These rainforests stretch north into coastal British Columbia and Southeast Alaska as well.

metas.name: Texas license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: Thick road lines
metas.description: Some roads in West Virginia, Virginia, and Maryland use middle yellow lines that are thicker than traditional yellow road lines.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These are not present on all roads in these states, and can be found elsewhere, so use this tip in conjunction with other clues.

metas.name: Utah license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: Washington license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: Wisconsin ATV Route signs
metas.description: These green ATV Route signs are unique to Wisconsin.

metas.name: Wisconsin bollard
metas.description: These simple white bollards with black reflectors are unique to Wisconsin.

metas.name: Wyoming license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: Yellow or red bands
metas.description: Yellow or red bands can commonly be seen around signposts in Texas.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Similar reflectors can sometimes be seen in other states, such as Hawaii.

metas.name: Alaska - Camera Meta - Gen 4 coverage
metas.description: Generation 4 coverage in Alaska is concentrated around the city of Anchorage.

metas.name: Alaska - Camera Meta - Shitcam
metas.description: Shitcam is only found around Anchorage and Fairbanks, and parts of the road that connects them.

metas.name: Alaska - Coverage Meta - Taylor (East of Chicken)
metas.description: Taylor Highway (5), from the Yukon border to Tetlin Junction, can be recognized by the foggy, rainy weather, and Generation 2 camera. East of Chicken, the road is unpaved.

metas.name: Alaska - Coverage Meta - Taylor (West of Chicken)
metas.description: Taylor Highway (5), from the Yukon border to Tetlin Junction, can be recognized by the foggy, rainy weather, and Generation 2 camera. West of Chicken, the road is paved.

metas.name: Alaska - Infrastructure - Alaskan Pipeline
metas.description: The Alaskan pipeline which is usually visible from main roads, can be seen at these points. This is an easy way to identify Alaska as there are no similar pipelines in the rest of the US.

metas.name: Alaska - Infrastructure - Anchorage Hydrant
metas.description: Fire hydrants in Anchorage are typically pale pink or pale yellow in colour.

metas.name: Alaska - Infrastructure - Fairbanks Hydrant
metas.description: Fire hydrants in Fairbanks are commonly either bright yellow or a combination of colours (most commonly yellow and blue).

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Agricultural Fields
metas.description: Due to Alaskaâs very cold climate; agricultural fields are mainly found in the south of the state, mostly in the Matanuska Valley and Kenai Peninsula.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Alexander Archipelago (Gen 2)
metas.description: The Alaskan towns in the Alexander Archipelago, on the British Columbia border have a unique look. Tall mountains with lush green forests can be seen in the background, with the majority of buildings made of wood. In addition, Generation 2 coverage is often overcast and misty.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Coastal areas of Oregon and Washington can have a similar appearance in terms of landscape and foliage.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Alexander Archipelago Landscape
metas.description: The Alaskan towns in the Alexander Archipelago, on the British Columbia border have a unique look. Tall mountains with lush green forests can be seen in the background, with the majority of buildings made of wood.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Coastal areas of Oregon and Washington can have a similar appearance in terms of landscape and foliage.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Denali Highway
metas.description: The Denali highway (8), stretching from Cantwell to Paxson in central Alaska, is a mostly gravel highway in the âAlaskaâ mountain range. This road runs generally east to west, is covered in the generation 2 camera, and was taken in late summer, so wildflowers and green shrubby plants are common.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Juneau
metas.description: Juneau, Alaskaâs Capital city, is the largest settlement in the Alaskan panhandle. Therefore, it is much more âbuilt upâ than other towns in this area. The city is surrounded by heavily forested mountains and hills.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Kenai Peninsula
metas.description: The Kenai peninsula can be recognized by its massive amount of fireweed along the roads. Most of the coverage is Gen 3 Autumn. Along AK-1 you will often see a bay to the west with mountains on the other side.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Max North Landscape
metas.description: The North end of the Dalton Highway (11) features a flat and snowy landscape and an overcast sky. A small ridge of hills can be seen to the west of the highway in certain spots.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Prudhoe Bay
metas.description: Prudhoe Bay, the northernmost town in America covered by street view, can be recognized by cold, dead landscape, overcast clouds and lack of tall buildings. A second Google car can sometimes be seen.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Steese Highway
metas.description: The Steese Highway (6) is a gravel highway that goes from Fairbanks to the town of âCentral.â Similar to the Denali highway, this road runs generally east to west and is covered in generation 2. The difference, however, is that the mountains along this road are noticeably lower than the ones adjacent to the Denali Highway.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Suburban Area with Mountains
metas.description: Suburban areas around Anchorage feature wide roads, commercial districts, and sometimes heavy traffic. Mountains can commonly be seen in the distance.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Suburban Area without Mountains
metas.description: Suburban areas around Anchorage feature wide roads, commercial districts, and sometimes heavy traffic. Compared to Anchorage, the landscape is flatter.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Tundra
metas.description: Most of interior and northern Alaska lies in subarctic or tundra climate zones. These areas feature relatively low amounts of forest undergrowth and shorter trees.

metas.name: Alaska - Landscape - Urban Coverage
metas.description: The only two major urban areas in Alaska are Anchorage and Fairbanks.

metas.name: Alaska - Trekker - Black Beanie Trekker
metas.description: The trekkerâs black and white bandana can only be seen in Nome.

metas.name: Alaska - Trekker - Shrekker
metas.description: Nome, Unalakleet and Galena are three isolated Alaskan towns which are covered only by trekker. The trekkerâs lime green hat can be seen.

metas.name: Alaska - Vegetation - Aspen Trees
metas.description: Aspen trees (Populus tremuloides) can be found in lower elevation areas of  interior and south-central regions of Alaska. These trees have white bark and rounded leaves.

metas.name: American Samoa - Car Meta - Manu'a Car
metas.description: The front of a silver-grey truck with side mirrors can be seen on Manuâa and Olosega, which are connected by a bridge.

metas.name: American Samoa - Car Meta - Tau Car
metas.description: The front of a similar truck can be seen on the easternmost covered island of Tau. However, the truck will be glossy black, with side mirrors visible.

metas.name: American Samoa - Car Meta - Tutuila Car
metas.description: A slightly rusted black truck bed can be seen on the main island of Tutuila.
metas.comparison: This is the most common car that will be seen as it has the most coverage.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Bridge
metas.description: The single-lane bridge, connecting the islands of Manuâa and Olosega, can be easily recognized by the thin wire guardrail, with the two islands on either side of the bridge.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Coconut / Powerline / Guardrail
metas.description: Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.
metas.comparison: If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you see a lot of Coconut Palms, you're in the central part of the road, east of the river. The short stretch immediately east of the river only shows the Coconuts in the distance towards East. There's both a Powerline and a Guardrail.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Manu'a/Olosega Sand Road
metas.description: From slightly North of the town entry of Olosega until the southernmost house WEST of the road, you will have a plain sand road, with no grass verge in the middle.
metas.comparison: This is the only road of this kind on the two islands with this Google Car.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Ofu Airport
metas.description: Ofu Airport is small with a concrete runway. The Google Car covering it has two orange straps on the roof. Many palm trees can also be seen on the other side of the runway.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Super Straight Road
metas.description: This section of the Rte 014 is by far the straightest covered road on Tutuila. Use the road angle to confirm. The appearance is quite varied, but it's also very flat

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tau - Asphalt
metas.description: Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.
metas.comparison: If you're generally heading East-West and have Asphalt pavement, you're on the far west part of the road.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tau - Coconut / No Powerline
metas.description: Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.
metas.comparison: If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you see a lot of Coconut Palms, you're in the central part of the road, east of the river. The short stretch immediately east of the little sideroad has no powerline, unlike the other locs with Coconuts.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tau - Coconut / Powerline / No Guardrail
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Tau - Coconut / Powerline / No Guardrail
metas.description: Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.
metas.comparison: If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you see a lot of Coconut Palms, you're in the central part of the road, east of the river. On this stretch, if you have a powerline, but no guardrail, you're east of the river, and west of the small sideroad on the map.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tau - Concrete / Overgrown / Guardrail / No Powerline
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Tau - Concrete / Overgrown / Guardrail / No Powerline
metas.description: Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.
metas.comparison: If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and a lot of overgrowth between you and the coast, you're generally in the Western Part of the road. If additionally, you have a guardrail, but no powerline, you're on the east-west stretch west of the river.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tau - Concrete / Overgrown / No Guardrail
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Tau - Concrete / Overgrown / No Guardrail
metas.description: Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.
metas.comparison: If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and a lot of overgrowth between you and the coast, you're generally in the Western Part of the road. If additionally, you have no guardrail, you're on the stretch marked on the second image, south of a smooth coast protrusion west of the river.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tau - Overgrown - Powerline
metas.description: Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.
metas.comparison: If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and a lot of overgrowth between you and the coast, you're generally in the Western Part of the road. If additionally, you have a powerline visible, you're on the SW-NE stretch immediately west of the river.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tau - Visible Coast / Guardrail
metas.description: Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.
metas.comparison: If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you have the coast North of you, with no significant vegetation in the way, you're on the Easternmost part of the road, east of the little sideroad. The western half of this stretch has a guardrail, the eastern half does not.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tau - Visible Coast / No Guardrail
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Tau - Visible Coast / No Guardrail
metas.description: Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.
metas.comparison: If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you have the coast North of you, with no significant vegetation in the way, you're on the Easternmost part of the road, east of the little sideroad. The western half of this stretch has a guardrail, the eastern half does not.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tutuila Airport
metas.description: On the roads along the airport on Tutuila, you will always see these fences surrounding the airport. This is obviously common for airports, but since Tutuila only has one airstrip, this road is a free 5k together with the Tutuila car.

metas.name: American Samoa - Infrastructure - Tutuila Concrete Road
metas.description: If you are on Tutuila and have a Concrete Road with no coast visible, you're on the far Eastern Part of the island, between Onenoa and Matatula Elementary school.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Afono Bay
metas.description: Afono Bay is the only Bay with coverage that is opened towards straight North. Note that Fagasa Bay is opened towards Northwest, while Vatia Bay is opened towards Northeast.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Camel Rock
metas.description: Behold: The Camel Rock. Two little peaks reaching into the ocean.
metas.comparison: It is marked as a POI on Google Maps.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - East of Summit 001 - Overcast
metas.description: This road crosses the district border on the 001. It is characterized through the unique angle and the mountains in the north. Often you can see a unique summit in the west. The driving direction is eastwards.
metas.comparison: There is a stretch of the 001 with a similar angle near Malaeimi, but it has a clearly visible valley in the North which is not found on this road. The road can further be divided as it is overcast in the Western District and sunny in the Eastern District.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - East of Summit 001 - Sunny
metas.description: This road crosses the district border on the 001. It is characterized through the unique angle and the mountains in the north. Often you can see a unique summit in the west. The driving direction is eastwards.
metas.comparison: There is a stretch of the 001 with a similar angle near Malaeimi, but it has a clearly visible valley in the North which is not found on this road. The road can further be divided as it is overcast in the Western District and sunny in the Eastern District.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Eastern South Coast Road
metas.description: This long stretch of road (which is probably further regionguessable) is easily recognizable because it has a South Coast and the Car Drives westward (unlike the Western Coastal Road). That means that when you pan onto the back of the truck, the water will be to your right.
metas.comparison: There is one annoying exception, around the POI 'Amouli Beach Fales' east of the town Amouli.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Fagasa Bay
metas.description: Afono Bay is the only Bay with coverage that is opened towards Northwest. Note that Afono is opened towards North proper, while Vatia Bay is opened towards Northeast.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Manu'a - North Coast road (paved)
metas.description: On Manu'a/Olosega (which have a unique car), there are two covered roads with North coast: The roads east and west of the famous bridge. They can easily be differentiated, because the Olosega (east) road is unpaved, while the Manu'a (west) road has concrete pavement.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Manu'a - North Coast road (unpaved)
metas.description: On Manu'a/Olosega (which have a unique car), there are two covered roads with North coast: The roads east and west of the famous bridge. They can easily be differentiated, because the Olosega (east) road is unpaved, while the Manu'a (west) road has concrete pavement.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Manu'a - Ofu
metas.description: The town Ofu on Manu'a has a West Coast. This road can be distinguished from the West Coast of Olosega, because:

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Pago Pago Harbour
metas.description: The roads alonog the Pago Pago Harbour are recognizable because they're generally very urban (for American Samoa), and you can often see the harbour when it isn't blocked by buildings.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Tau - Faleasao
metas.description: Faleasao is a little town on Tau (and thus has the Tau car). It has a coast in the North and is otherwise surrounded by mountains. Together with the Tau car, it is unique.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Tutuila - Rte 018
metas.description: The Rte 018 in Tafuna is urban and uniquely shows this mountain in the North. The alignment is generally North-South. The road has double yellow lines (not that common in AS) and a power line in the East. The driving direction is to the North.
metas.comparison: Make sure that parts of the Rte 001 can look similar with a similar road angle. To confirm it's the Rte 018, you can pan exactly North. If you look at the mountain, it's the Rte 018, otherwise it's not.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Tutuila East Coast
metas.description: This is the only part of Tutuila where you can see Coast on the east, without other parts of Tutuila visible. You will often see Aunu'u in the Southeast.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Vatia Bay
metas.description: Vatia Bay is the only Bay with coverage that is opened towards Northeast. Note that Fagasa Bay is opened towards Northwest, while Afono Bay is opened towards North proper.

metas.name: American Samoa - Landscape - Western South Coast Road
metas.description: This road is easily recognizable because it has a South Coast and the Car drives eastward (unlike the Eastern Coastal Road). That means that when you pan onto the back of the truck, the water will be to your left.
metas.comparison: On the eastern south coast road, there is a tiny part that also drives eastward for some reason, which can be baity.

metas.name: American Samoa - Trekker - Aunu Ferry
metas.description: The only ferry Trekker of American Samoa. If you're on a boat between two islands in AS, you're here.

metas.name: American Samoa - Trekker - Ofu Beach
metas.description: Ofu Beach is easy to recognize, with the coast to the Southeast and three distinct peaks in the Northeast.

metas.name: Argentina - Agriculture - Corn
metas.description: Corn fields can be found in most of northern Argentina, however they are most common in CÃ³rdoba, Buenos Aires and Santiago del Estero.

metas.name: Argentina - Agriculture - Mendoza Vineyards
metas.description: If you see vineyards with mountains in the west and flatness in the east, you are most likely in the outskirts of Mendoza.

metas.name: Argentina - Agriculture - Sorghum
metas.description: Fields of sorghum can most commonly be seen in Santa Fe, CÃ³rdoba and Buenos Aires. It can be identified by its dark red flowerheads.

metas.name: Argentina - Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.description: Sugarcane plantations are most common in TucumÃ¡n, with hotspots appearing in Salta and Jujuy.

metas.name: Argentina - Agriculture - Sunflower
metas.description: Fields of sunflowers are mainly found in southern Chaco, and less commonly in Buenos Aires and southern CÃ³rdoba.

metas.name: Argentina - Agriculture - Tree Plantations
metas.description: The majority of tree plantations in Argentina are located in the Entre Rios province.

metas.name: Argentina - Architecture - Mar del Plata Architecture
metas.description: In Mar Del Plata and surrounding cities (such as Miramar and Necochea), a unique style of architecture can be found. Its main features include quartzite stoned facades, orange tiled roofs, attached garages, and vault shaped porches.

metas.name: Argentina - Architecture - Red Brick Architecture
metas.description: Red bricks, similar to what is common in Bolivia, can be found in the northwest of the country, especially in western Jujuy.

metas.name: Argentina - Car Meta - Sawdust Car Meta
metas.description: The âsawdustâ car is found in centre-south Argentina and has a unique sandy dust on its visible black back.

metas.name: Argentina - Coverage Meta - Low Quality Sunset Coverage
metas.meta_label: Coverage Meta - Low Quality Sunset Coverage
metas.description: Sunset coverage with degraded image quality is found on the RN40 just south of the Mendoza border with NeuquÃ©n.

metas.name: Argentina - Coverage Meta - Melted Snow Coverage
metas.description: Melting snow coverage is seen on the eastern RN293 close to the Chilean border in southwestern Santa Cruz.

metas.name: Argentina - Coverage Meta - Snow Coverage
metas.description: This snow coverage is found on the eastern RP25 in eastern Santa Cruz.

metas.name: Argentina - Coverage Meta - Sunrise Coverage with Blurs
metas.meta_label: Coverage Meta - Sunrise Coverage with Blurs
metas.description: Sunrise coverage with bad image quality and multiple blurs is found on a short part of the RN251 and RN22, west of RÃ­o Colorado.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Bariloche Taxi
metas.description: This taxi with the white body, blue roof and blue logo is unique to the city of Bariloche.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Buenos Aires Taxi
metas.description: This taxi with a black body and yellow roof is common in Buenos Aires. Note that taxis from Jujuy and RosarÃ­o have the same combination. However, Buenos Aires is the only city where the taxi has the middle bar (behind the driver) painted.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Comodoro Rivadavia Taxi
metas.description: This all white taxi with a black logo is unique to Comodoro Rivadavia.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Cordoba km-marker
metas.description: You can find these unique markers on provincial roads in Cordoba.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Cordoba Taxi
metas.description: These all green or all yellow taxis with an oval shape beneath the driver door are unique to Cordoba.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Jujuy Taxi
metas.description: Taxis in Jujuy have a black body and a yellow roof. Notably, only the top of the roof is yellow, making it distinct from Rosario or Buenos Aires taxis.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - km-marker
metas.description: Argentinian kilometer markers are typically white with a black strip displaying the road number at the top. RN stands for ruta national (white on the map), RP stands for ruta provincial (green on the map).

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - La Pampa Junction Sign
metas.description: T-Junctions in La Pampa sometimes have these yellow rectangular signs, with a chevron pattern on the bottom, and the Road Number(s) above, with an arrow on both sides.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - La Plata Taxi
metas.description: La Plata has white taxis with green elements.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Latvian-style Poles
metas.description: Within Argentina, these Latvian style wooden hook poles are unique to La Rioja and Mendoza.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Mendoza Taxi
metas.description: This black and yellow taxi is unique to Mendoza. Jujuy, Rosario and Buenos Aires also have black and yellow taxis, but on those taxis, the body is completely black.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Neuquen Taxi
metas.description: Taxis in Neuquen are all yellow. What distinguishes them from Cordoba taxis is that their doors have no logos or paintings on them.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Resistencia Taxi
metas.description: Taxis with a red-white-green stripe (hungarian flag) are unique to Resistencia.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Rosario Taxi
metas.description: Taxis in Rosario have a black body and a yellow roof. The outer bars are yellow, while the middle bar (behind the driver) is black. This makes them distinguishable from taxis in Jujuy and Buenos Aires.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Salta Taxi
metas.description: Red taxis with a black stripe are unique to Salta.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - San Juan Taxi
metas.description: White taxis with a yellow roof are unique to San Juan.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - San Luis Taxi
metas.description: White taxis with two light-blue stripes (resembling the Argentinian flag) are unique to San Luis.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Santiago del Estero Taxi
metas.description: White taxis with light-green roofs are unique to Santiago del Estero.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Single Hook Insulator
metas.description: In Mendoza, poles with a single insulator attached to the side of the pole can be found.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Tucuman Pole ID
metas.description: White vertical pole stickers with several digits can be found in TucumÃ¡n.

metas.name: Argentina - Infrastructure - Tucuman Taxi
metas.description: These old-school, white taxis with a yellow-black checkerboard stripe are unique to Tucuman.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Bahia Blanca Hills
metas.description: Semi-coastal grass hills are seen in southern Buenos Aires, especially northeast of BahÃ­a Blanca.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Chaco & Formosa Landscape
metas.description: In the Chaco and Formosa provinces, you will often see sandy soil with an abundance of vegetation; mainly low trees and bushes.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Chenque Hill
metas.description: Comodoro Rivadavia is built on the slopes of Chenque hill, making the city recognisable.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Cordoba Mountains
metas.description: These mountains are typically found west of CÃ³rdoba.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Flat & Barren Landscape
metas.description: Flat and barren landscapes like this are typically found in central southern Argentina.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Grassland
metas.description: Grassland with a few separated tree plantations is generally found in this area.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Mars Coverage
metas.description: The RP1 in Neuquen has dark, cloudy coverage. It is a dark red dirt road and thus resembles Mars. There is some spill onto the RP7 in the North and the RP10 in the South.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Max South Landscape
metas.description: If you see this kind of vegetation with flat grass and a low number of bushes, you are almost certainly in the state of Tierra del Fuego or southeastern Santa Cruz.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Mountains
metas.description: Far western Argentina typically features a mountainous landscape.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Red Mountains
metas.description: These red mountains are unique to the RN68 valley in southern Salta.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Red Soil
metas.description: Red soil is typically found in the Misiones province.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Road of Death
metas.description: The western part of the RN65 in western TucumÃ¡n can easily be recognized by this bendy unpaved road up in the mountains.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Road of Death - Cloudy
metas.description: The western part of the RN65 in western TucumÃ¡n can easily be recognized by this bendy unpaved road up in the mountains with its western part up in the clouds.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Salt Pans
metas.description: Salt pans in Argentina are typically found in Jujuy.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - San Luis Roads
metas.description: Roads with reddish pavement lined with long Argentine needle-grass are common in San Luis.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Small Lakes and Ponds
metas.description: Small lakes near the road are occasionally seen in the province of Buenos Aires.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Talampaya National Park
metas.description: Red soil with a barren landscape and mountain ranges, can often be seen on the RN76 in Parque Nacional Talampaya in western La Rioja.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Ushuaia
metas.description: These snowy mountains to the north can only be found in Ushuaia.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino
metas.description: Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino in northeastern Chubut is surrounded by these rock formations.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino Dam
metas.meta_label: Landscape - Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino Dam
metas.description: This unique dam with the rock formations typical for Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino can be found west of the town.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape - Volcanic Rocks
metas.description: These volcanic rocks in Generation 4 coverage can only be found on the RP43 south of Antofagasta de la Sierra in northwestern Catamarca.

metas.name: Argentina - Trekker - Horse Trekker
metas.description: This horse trekker can be found in southwestern San Juan.

metas.name: Argentina - Vegetation - Azorella Prolifera - Light Green
metas.description:
Azorella Prolifera is a plant that looks like "cushions". It is found throughout Patagonia.
It's appearence depends on season.
metas.comparison: You can see this plant in a distinctive light green color in these regions:

metas.name: Argentina - Vegetation - Beech Forest
metas.description: Beech forests are commonly found in the state of Tierra del Fuego.

metas.name: Argentina - Vegetation - Butia Yatay Palm
metas.description: The Butia yatay palm has arching, pinnate leaves and often grows at an incline with varying heights. It is most common in Corrientes and Parque Nacional El Palmar, Entre Rios.

metas.name: Argentina - Vegetation - CaldÃ©n
metas.description: Prosopis caldenia, known as the caldÃ©n, is a decently large deciduous tree with small leaves and sinuous branches. It is mainly found in La Pampa.

metas.name: Argentina - Vegetation - Caranday Palm
metas.description: Trithrinax Campestris, or the caranday palm, not to be confused with the Caranday Wax Palm, is a rustic palm native to the Sierras de CÃ³rdoba with a broader distribution in San Luis and northern mountainous Argentina. It can be identified by its compact fan-like leaves with a trunk hidden by a coat of dead-leaves.

metas.name: Argentina - Vegetation - Caranday Wax Palm
metas.description: Coperinicia alba, also known as the Caranday Wax Palm, have short, fan-like leaves that tend to grow in low-density, single-species forests. Most common in Formosa, they can also be found in Chaco, Corrientes and northern Santa Fe.

metas.name: Argentina - Vegetation - CardÃ³n
metas.description: Trichocereus atacamensis, or the cardÃ³n, is a cactus native to the high elevation mountain ranges of Catamarca, TucumÃ¡n, Salta and Jujuy. It can be identified by its candelabra-like appearance and fuzzy golden brown spines.

metas.name: Argentina - Vegetation - Macaw Palm
metas.description: The Macaw Palm has small thin leaves with a visible spear shaped top. It can be found as a decorational plant all across Argentina, however in the wild it is most common in Formosa, Chaco and Misiones.

metas.name: Argentina - Vegetation - Monkey Puzzle Tree
metas.description: The monkey puzzle tree can be found in western Neuquen. The most specimens are seen on provincial road 23 + offroads, between Caviahue and Atreuco.

metas.name: Argentina - Vegetation - Pampas Grass
metas.description: Pampas grass (Cortaderia selloana) is one of the most defining flora of the Pampas region. It is recognizable by its long bunched reeds and white fluffy flowerheads.

metas.name: Argentina - Vegetation - Pink Trumpet Tree
metas.description: The Pink Trumpet Tree (Handroanthus impetiginosus) can be found in cities in northern Salta such as OrÃ¡n, Tartagal and General Mosconi.

metas.name: Argentina - Vegetation - Poplar Plantation - Mediterranean
metas.description: Poplar Trees are thin and tall decidiuous trees. They can be found all over Argentina.
metas.comparison: If you see them planted in single rows accompanied by hilly to mountainous, mediterranean landscape, as well as mediterranean agriculture (e.g. vineyards and olives) and vegetation (e.g. palm trees, platanus trees), you are likely in a town or city in the provinces of Mendoza and San Juan.

metas.name: Argentina - Vegetation - Red Baron
metas.description: Red Baron is a grass species that has a very distinctive red hue. It's found in

metas.name: Argentina - Vegetation - Red Baron - Dense
metas.description: Red Baron is a grass species that has a very distinctive red hue.
metas.comparison: In very dense assemblages, it can appear here:

metas.name: Argentina - Vegetation - Single Row Poplar - Flat
metas.description: Poplar Trees are thin and tall decidiuous trees. They can be found all over Argentina.
metas.comparison: If you see them planted in a single row and accompanied by a very flat landscape, you are in one of these places:

metas.name: Argentina - Vegetation - Toothpick Cactus
metas.description: Stetsonia coryne, or the toothpick cactus, is a large tree-like cactus with many branches and spines resembling toothpicks. Its habitat includes a hotspot between Catamarca and Cordoba as well as the border area between Chaco, Salta and Formosa.

metas.name: Argentina - Vegetation - Wild Sunflower
metas.description: Wild sunflowers (Verbesina encelioides) are often found in Salta, Jujuy and TucumÃ¡n.

metas.name: Australia - Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.description: Sugarcane plantations are very common in Northern Queensland, due to its tropical climate.

metas.name: Australia - Car Meta - Open Trunk Meta
metas.description: The town of Gascoyne Junction in Western Australia is distinct, as the driver left the car boot open while covering this town, creating a very unique car meta.

metas.name: Australia - Car Meta - Snorkel Car
metas.description: Australia is home to dozens of rare Google cars, which can usually be found in natural reserves.
metas.comparison: Most rare Google cars with snorkels are located in New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory. The only snorkel cars outside of NSW are in the northwestern part of Wunaamin Conservation Area (northern WA) and along Lucky Bay (south coastal WA).

metas.name: Australia - Car Meta - Wire Car Meta
metas.description: On most of the Northern Territory section of the Barkly Highway and a small part of the Queensland section, a wire can be seen on the left side of the car.

metas.name: Australia - Coverage Meta - Gen 2
metas.description: Generation 2 coverage cannot be found in Northern Territory. It can also help in 50/50s between Victoria and Tasmania, where Gen 2 is more common in Tasmania.

metas.name: Australia - Coverage Meta - Gen 2 Twig Meta
metas.description: In Generation 2 coverage in an area of Eastern NSW, a twig is visible in the Generation 2 halo.

metas.name: Australia - Coverage Meta - Gen 2 Whole Leaf
metas.description: In a lot of Generation 2 around the towns of Morwell and Traralgon in Eastern Victoria, an entire leaf is visible in the Generation 2 halo. A version with only the top half of a leaf can also be seen in eastern SA.

metas.name: Australia - Coverage Meta - Half Leaf
metas.description: The upper half of a leaf can sometimes be seen on the Generation 2 halo in southeastern South Australia. If it's an entire leaf, it is in Eastern Victoria.

metas.name: Australia - Coverage Meta - Jervis Bay Meta
metas.description: Jervis Bay only has Gen 1 coverage, all of which has a 2021 copyright.

metas.name: Australia - Coverage Meta - Smoke Coverage
metas.description: Around the Devils Marbles, north of Davenport in the Northern Territory, smoke from a bushfire is visible.

metas.name: Australia - Coverage Meta - Splodgey Sun
metas.description: A sun with "splodges" around it can be observed on the 95 in Western Australia, between Newman and Ex Doolgunna.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - â-Poletop - Round
metas.description: The â-Poletop is found in South Australia and New South Wales. In SA, the pole will be a stobie pole, while in NSW it will be round.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - 130 km/h speed limit
metas.description: Within Australia, a speed limit of 130 km/h can only be found in the Northern Territory.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - 25 school zone
metas.description: South Australia is the only Australian state that uses a 25 speed limit in school zones.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - 90Â° poletop
metas.description: Poletops in Tasmania often consist of a thin metal crossbar bent 90 degrees to form an L-shape.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - ACT Bus Stop
metas.description: Unique to Australian Capital Territory (Canberra).

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Black pole marking
metas.description: These black markings are specific to electricity poles in Queensland. They are often accompanied by diagonal numbers.
metas.comparison: They are almost exclusively found between Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - black-white striped bollard
metas.description: These black-and-white stripy bollards are unique to Western Australia.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - black-yellow striped bollard
metas.description: This black-and-yellow bollard is exclusive to Queensland.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Blue Square on Pole
metas.description: Melbourne poles commonly feature these white, rectangular stickers, with a smaller blue square inside it.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - bollard with brown bottom
metas.description: Bollards with brown paint at the bottom are most commonly found in Western Australia.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - bollard with short reflector
metas.description: Reflectors that are shorter than the regular ones are most common in Queensland and South Australia.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Brisbane Streetsign
metas.description: Identified by the little symbol.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - C-Road
metas.description: Roads that start with the letter âCâ are only found in Victoria and Tasmania. In addition, South Australia has some C roads near the border with Victoria.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Charters Towers Red Roads
metas.description: As a general rule in Queensland state, Australia, red tinted roads are found mostly around Charters Towers (especially when you have more trees), they can also be found on the A2 near label, and the 1 further north. These areas are indicated in the distribution, but there may be minor exceptions.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - concrete pole
metas.description: According to a 2006 review, 64% of all concrete poles are located in the state of Victoria.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Darwin Bus Stop
metas.description: The city of Darwin, NT uses concrete shelters as bus stops.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Dorat Road
metas.description: Dorat Road (23) in the Northern Territory can be easily recognized thanks to its distinct Darwin area landscape and lack of road lines.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Dotted Concrete Pole
metas.description: These round concrete poles with dots going up on them are found in New South Wales.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - flat signpost
metas.description: Some signposts in South Australia and Western Australia are flat rather than round.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - fluoresecent sign border
metas.description: Road signs with a fluorescent border are almost exclusively found in Queensland.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Gold Coast Streetsign
metas.description: This street sign is unique to Gold Coast City Council.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Green Dot on Pole
metas.description: This Green Dot on poles is sometimes found in New South Wales.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - green pole bottom
metas.description: Poles in Western Australia often have green painted bases, and sometimes a white sticker or a red and white band attached.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - green property marker
metas.description: You can find these dark green property markers on the sides of roads in Western Australia.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Hanging Insulator
metas.description: These poles with hanging insulators are found in Queensland and New South Wales.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - hydrant with blue circle
metas.description: You can find these white hydrant poles that feature a blue circle and a red section on top of it in Victoria.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - hydrant with red top
metas.description: These fire hydrants with red painted tops are unique to Victoria.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - License Plate - Slim NSW
metas.description: Very slim license plate (similar to Swiss front plates) are found in Victoria and New South Wales. While in Victoria, you can usually see two blue blocks of texts, in NSW they appear plain.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - License Plate - Slim Victoria
metas.description: Very slim license plate (similar to Swiss front plates) are found in Victoria and New South Wales. While in Victoria, you can usually see two blue blocks of texts, in NSW they appear plain.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - License Plate - Taxi - Blue
metas.description: Blue plates on Taxis are found exclusively in New South Wales.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Mount Kosciuszko
metas.description: All-yellow road lines can be seen on roads around Mount Kosciuszko.
metas.comparison: In addition, a unique white truck with a snorkel, and cab guard can be found.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - No-Stopping-sign with text
metas.description: The white âNo Stoppingâ and âNo Parkingâ signs that include text are unique to the Australian Capital Territory.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - NSW Bus Stop
metas.description: New South Wales uses these two designs for bus stops. One is blue and has a white B in a circle with it, the other has the signpost bending over the actual sign.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - NSW guardrail ending
metas.description: This guardrail ending, featuring a black dash on a yellow background, is almost exclusive to New South Wales and the ACT.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - NT License Plate
metas.description: License Plates in Northern Territory have bright red lettering which shines through the blur. Looks kind of similar to the Queensland plates, which are a bit darker.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Octagonal Pole
metas.description: Octagonal Poles in Australia are found mostly in and around Sydney.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - olive-green possum guard
metas.description: Olive-green possum guards are only found on electricity poles in Tasmania.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Poletag - H
metas.description: The 'H' poletag is found in New South Wales.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Poletag - HP
metas.description: This poletag with 'HP' is found in New South Wales.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Poletag - NSW - Horizontal
metas.description: Within New South Wales, purely horizontal poletags (i.e. no vertical on the same pole), are not found around Sydney.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Poletag - NSW - Letter Code
metas.description: In NSW, poletags in the triangle formed by Sydney, Newcastle and Scone (view map) almost always have one or two letters in their codes.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Poletag - NSW - Vertical / Outer White
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Poletag - NSW - Vertical / Outer White
metas.description: Within NSW, these vertical plates with white ends are not found near Sydney. Note that otherwise, vertical plates will be close to Sydney within NSW.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Poletag - QLD - Vertical
metas.description: Poletags with a blue sticker, and a vertical steel tag are found in Queensland, north of Rockhampton.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Poletag - Vertical / Regular
metas.description: Within NSW, regular vertical poletags are found south and west of Sydney.
metas.comparison: Note that if the poletags have white ends on each side, they are NOT close to Sydney, but rather throughout the rest of NSW.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Poletag - Yellow T
metas.description: This poletag which consists of rectangular yellow stickers that usually form a T, is exclusive to New South Wales.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Queensland Bus Stop
metas.description: Bus stops in Queensland have a yellow signpost bending over the actual sign.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Queensland License Plate
metas.description: The Queensland License Plate has dark red letters which can shine through the blur. Looks similar to the NT plate, which has a lighter red tone. There is also an old, green version, which could theoretically show up.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Queensland poletop
metas.description: Queensland features these unique pole tops with coils that are angled upwards on the sides.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Queensland sticker
metas.description: Circular blue stickers can be found on Queensland poles. You may occasionally see the same type of sticker in a different colour, or with the colour almost completely faded.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - red "No Stopping" sign
metas.description: New South Wales is the only state to use red âNo Stoppingâ signs.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Roadline Gap with no Reflector
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Roadline Gap with no Reflector
metas.description: In South Australia and the ACT, you can sometimes find gaps in the outer roadlines. If this gap has no reflector, it is South Australia.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Roadline gap with Reflector
metas.description: In South Australia and the ACT, you can sometimes find gaps in the outer roadlines. In ACT, there will always be a reflector in the gap. This can also appear occasionally in South Australia.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - rusty holey pole
metas.description: These rusty metal poles, containing several holes, are unique to the Northern Territory, and rarely the northern part of Western Australia.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Sloped Kerbs
metas.description: You can sometimes see sloped kerbs in Perth, where it gradually declines to the road, whilst in other cities kerbs go straight down at a 90 degree angle.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - South Australia Bus Stop
metas.description: Orange signpost, sign extending over the signpost.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Stobie pole
metas.description: The iconic Stobie pole, made of steel and concrete, is specific to South Australia. Outside of SA, it sometimes occurs in Broken Hill, NSW or Tasmania.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Sydney Streetsign
metas.description: This street sign is unique to the City of Sydney.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Tasmania Bus Stop
metas.description: Different versions, but usually have "Metro" written on them.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - thin "Keep Left" sign
metas.description: Some âKeep Leftâ signs in New South Wales, Queensland, and the Northern Territory use this thinner version, which does not include an arrow.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - traffic light with no outline
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - traffic light with no outline
metas.description: Traffic lights without a border are found in Northern Territory, South Australia and Victoria.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - traffic light with white outline
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - traffic light with white outline
metas.description: Traffic lights with a white outline around the frame are found in the eastern and western states of WA, QLD, NSW, ACT and Tas. Traffic lights without a border are found in the remaining, central states.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Triple Broken Roadlines
metas.description: The Sturt Highway from Wentworth to Wagga Wagga can have triple broken centre lines. They can also be found on other major roads in NSW, such as the Gwydir Highway.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - upward pointing trident pole
metas.description: A trident-like pole top with the insulators pointing to the top can sometimes be seen in Western Australia and Victoria.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Victoria Bus Stop
metas.description: Bus Stops in Victoria can be recognized by their color scheme: White-Orange-Black-Grey-White.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Victoria License Plate
metas.description: License plates in Victoria have a little small triangle at the top, which can sometimes be recognized through the blur.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Victoria poletop
metas.description: Victorian pole tops feature 3 circular coils; 2 on the sides, and 1 vertical one at the top. At times, other extensions can be seen on these poles.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Western Australia Bus Stop
metas.description: Bus Stops in Australia are marked by these horizontal poles with information on them.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Western Australia License Plate
metas.description: Western Australian License Plate have blue letters and a thin blue stripe at the top, which can sometimes be recognized through the blur.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - white directional sign
metas.description: White directional signs can only be found in Tasmania.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - white property marker
metas.description: You can find these white property markers on the sides of roads in South Australia.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Yellow License Plate
metas.description: Yellow license plates can occasionally be found in New South Wales. Most license plates are still white, though. The old design of Western Australian plates is also yellow, so you might stumble upon them in WA very rarely.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - yellow signpost
metas.description: Yellow signposts are specific to Western Australia.

metas.name: Australia - Infrastructure - Ñ-shaped poletop
metas.description: Poletops that resemble the cyrillic letter Ñ are unique to South Australia.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Alice Springs
metas.description: Alice Springs, an isolated town in the southern part of the Northern Territory, features distinct orange rocks that can be seen in the distance or at the end of roads.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Cairns Landscape
metas.description: The northern QLD city of Cairns is distinct due to its tropical vegetation and big green mountains around the city.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Darwin Landscape
metas.description: The vegetation in the area surrounding Darwin is extremely distinct. It features dark red soil, as well as rich green grass and trees. The tree trunks are typically black.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Eastern South Australia Landscape
metas.description: The dry area east of Adelaide and into northwestern Victoria has quite dry vegetation and is made up of shrubs and wide cronwed eucalyptus. In addition, the soil is sandy with a white tint.
metas.comparison: Western South Australia has a similar landscape, but with orangish soil.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Green & Golden Fields
metas.description: Lush green or golden fields can be found in this band from the south of the Yorke Peninsula to Echuca. In the SA side, the landscape should be drier than the Victorian side and more wide crowned eucalyptus can be seen. On the Victorian side, the trees generally have more leaves and are taller.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Inland New South Wales Landscape
metas.meta_label: Landscape - Inland New South Wales Landscape
metas.description: The landscape in inland NSW is mostly flat, and the soil gets redder the more inland you go. Vegetation consists of mostly dry pale-green shrubs. Further east and on the Queensland and Victorian borders, the climate gets more temperate but is still quite dry and more eucalyptus trees can be seen, with the soil transitioning into a more sandy colour as well as more hills being visible.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Kangaroo Island Landscape
metas.description: Kangaroo Island in South Australia tends to have a distinct look. The vegetation mostly consists of bushes and low, stubby eucalyptus trees with puffy clusters of leaves. The orange soil colour is reminiscent of Western Australia.
metas.comparison: In addition, the island only has Generation 2 and Generation 4 coverage, with Generation 2 being most common.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Mount Gambier Tree Plantations
metas.description: The area around Mount Gambier, SA features white soil and extensive pine tree plantations, making it recognisable.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Northern Queensland Landscape
metas.description: Coastal northern Queensland is very tropical. Typical vegetation consists of palm trees and dark green vegetation.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Nullarbor Highway
metas.description: The Nullarbor Highway (Latin for âno treeâ) can be easily recognized thanks to the flatness, overall grey look and very low vegetation.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Use the road angle or road lines to determine whether you are on the WA or SA side.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Reddish-Orange Soil
metas.description: Western Australia, and especially the Perth area, is known for its reddish-orange soil.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Stuart Highway with Blue Car
metas.meta_label: Landscape - Stuart Highway with Blue Car
metas.description: The Stuart Highway from Alice Springs to around Pimba, SA can be easily recognized by its bright orange dirt, short trees and blue car Generation 4.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Tasmania Landscape
metas.description: Tasmania has a cool temperate climate which is uncommon in the rest of Australia and is comparable to central-southern Chile or New Zealand. Typical landscape consists of green rolling hills that can look dry in winter coverage. Eucalyptus trees can be seen on the side of roads and on hills in the distance. Rural Tasmania is also quite hilly with dense eucalyptus forests making up the landscape.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Termite Hills
metas.description: Termite mounds can sometimes be seen in the Northern Territory and rarely northern WA and QLD. They appear as brown, spiky formations rising out of the ground.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Tom Price Landscape
metas.description: The area around Tom Price can be recognized by its red soil and rocky hills.

metas.name: Australia - Landscape - Western South Australia Landscape
metas.description: The area around Warramboo in SA to Madura in WA has a unique landscape. Vegetation is quite dry and is made up of shrubs and wide crowned eucalyptus. In addition, the soil is sandy with a slight orange tint.
metas.comparison: The dry area east of Adelaide and into northwestern Victoria has a similar landscape, with the same vegetation but usually with whiter soil.

metas.name: Australia - Vegetation - Bottle Tree
metas.description: While Bottle Trees can be found throughout Queensland, they are planted everywhere in the city of Roma.

metas.name: Australia - Vegetation - Brush Plant
metas.description: These brush plants are commonly seen in Western Australia.

metas.name: Australia - Vegetation - Gregory Tree
metas.description: Excoecaria parvifolia is an odd looking tree with almost creepy looking thin vine outgrowths as leaves. It seems to be found primarily found around the new 2025 white car coverage around the northern Queensland city of Gregory, Australia.

metas.name: Australia - Vegetation - Queensland Fan Palm
metas.description: The Queensland fan palm or Australian fan palm, is a species endemic to northeastern Queensland, Australia (Specially around Cairns).

metas.name: Australia - Vegetation - Sand Palm
metas.description: The sand palm is endemic to the north of the Northern Territory of Australia, from the Fitzmaurice River to Cape Arnhem and inland as far as Katherine.

metas.name: Brazil - Agriculture - Coffee
metas.description: Coffee beans are by far the most common in Minas Gerais, but also can be found in Espirito Santo and northeastern Sao Paulo.

metas.name: Brazil - Agriculture - Cotton
metas.description:
73% of Cotton Production in Brazil takes place in Mato Grosso.
20% take place in the western border of Bahia.
Other minor spots are western Minas Gerais, Southern Goias and Northern MGDS

metas.name: Brazil - Agriculture - Eucalyptus Grandis
metas.description: Eucalyptus Grandis, when fully grown, is a very tall tree with plantations all over Brazil. You can find them in both large and very small plantations, as well as randomly growing anywhere. You can see them all over the south, but there are some large plantations in Amapa too.

metas.name: Brazil - Agriculture - Soybeans
metas.description: Soybeans appear as small, leafy soil grown plants. They are most commonly grown in Mato Grosso, ParanÃ¡, and GoiÃ¡s.

metas.name: Brazil - Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.description: Sugarcane plantations are by far most common in the state of Sao Paulo, and in the coastal north east states, especially Alagoas and Pernambuco.

metas.name: Brazil - Architecture - European Architecture
metas.description: Buildings in the southern states, mainly Santa Catarina, can be of European influence (typically vaguely German) in design and style.

metas.name: Brazil - Architecture - Red Brick Architecture
metas.description: Houses made out of red brick are more common in Northeastern Brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Architecture - Stilt Houses
metas.description: Wooden houses on stilts are very common in the state of Acre.

metas.name: Brazil - Car Meta - Noronha Car Meta
metas.description: Ilha de Fernando de Noronha is covered by a white buggy which sometimes has a visible front.

metas.name: Brazil - Coverage Meta - Amapa Blur
metas.description: In all Generation 4 coverage in AmapÃ¡, the front right of the camera is smudged. In addition, all Generation 4 coverage in AmapÃ¡ features the white car with the blue stripe.

metas.name: Brazil - Coverage Meta - BR-156 in Northern Amapa
metas.meta_label: Coverage Meta - BR-156 in Northern Amapa
metas.description: This road is characterized by the Amapa Blur (slight blur at the front of a blue-striped car), the red, and the road angle to Northwest. There are frequently Areca palms growing near this road.

metas.name: Brazil - Coverage Meta - Camera Glitch
metas.description: Northwest Rio Grande do Sul has coverage with this camera glitch in Generation 3.

metas.name: Brazil - Coverage Meta - East-West BR156 in Amapa
metas.meta_label: Coverage Meta - East-West BR156 in Amapa
metas.description: This part of the BR156 can be recognized by the Amapa Blur (slight blur at the front right of the blue-striped car). It's the only Amapa Blur coverage on a road that goes East-West. This part of the road is paved.

metas.name: Brazil - Coverage Meta - Flooded Coverage
metas.description: Flooded coverage can be found between Macau and Macauzinho in Rio Grande do Norte.

metas.name: Brazil - Coverage Meta - Hazy Sky
metas.description: Hazy Sky Coverage is very common in Porto Velho.

metas.name: Brazil - Coverage Meta - Post Bushfire Coverage
metas.description: The road between Caico, RGDN and Santa Luzia, Paraiba is unique with its post bushfire coverage. The part in Paraiba often has outer dashed lines

metas.name: Brazil - Coverage Meta - Rifts
metas.description: You can often see rifts in Alagoas Generation 3 coverage.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - 2 Ridge Insulator
metas.description: Memorize the distribution map.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - 3 Ridge Insulator
metas.description:
Most commonly found in Paraiba in the North, and in Parana, Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro.
It's pretty rare.
metas.comparison: Memorize the distribution map for more details. Note by MB: They're also different to the lollipop insulator, where the ridges have different sizes.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - 4 Ridge Insulator
metas.description: Widespread, but can still resolve some 50/50s. Memorize the map.
metas.comparison: Also, in Sao Paulo, it's common in Sao Paulo city, and uncommon outside of it.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - 5 Ridges Insulator
metas.description: Insulators with 5 ridges are very common in Sao Paulo.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - 90Â° Crossbar
metas.description: Right angle top bars are common in BrasÃ­lia

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Aerodynamic Lamp
metas.description: Aerodynamic Lamp Heads are common in Fortaleza.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Alagoas Lamp
metas.description: Different colors possible

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Aracaju Lamp Arm ID
metas.description: Unique ID on a common lamp head. Sometimes, you can't see much of the code, only zip ties.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Aracaju Road Sign
metas.description: Aracaju, Sergipe

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Barra Do Garcas Lamp Arm
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Barra Do Garcas Lamp Arm
metas.description: Barra Do Garcas, Mato Grosso (border to Goias)

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Belem ID
metas.description: Lots of rare pole IDs in the city

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Belo Horizonte Lamp
metas.description: Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Bend Attached to Pole
metas.description: The vast majority of poles in Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul, ParÃ¡, AmapÃ¡, Rio Grande do Norte, Pernambuco and Santa Catarina have the lamp arm attached to the pole, as opposed to it being attached with a plate, which is much more common generally.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Big Electricity Counter on Pole
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Big Electricity Counter on Pole
metas.description: Big electricity counters on the pole are most common in Mato Grosso, Para and Amapa.
metas.comparison: Unlike their smaller version, they do not appear in Paraiba.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Black&Yellow Bollards
metas.description: Black & Yellow bollards of different kinds are common in Salvador.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Blue ID
metas.description: Unique to Rio Branco

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Blue Lamp Arm ID
metas.description:
Small, blue, hanging from the lamp arm.
Found in Cuiaba (bend attached to pole), and in the cities of Riberao Preto and Sao Paulo (normal lamp arm)

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Boa Vista ID
metas.description: Boa Vista, Roraima

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - BR-101 in the Northeast
metas.description: This road is divided. What makes it special is that one direction as asphalt and the other direction has concrete pavement.
metas.comparison: This does not apply to the entire road anymore

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Brasilia Streetsign
metas.description: Brasilia, Distrito Federal

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Brown Mushroom Insulator
metas.description: Pernambuco sometimes uses these brown mushroom insulators.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Campinas Sidewalk
metas.description: The city of Campinas, SP is known for it's unique and artistic patterns of black and white stones on its sidewalks.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Cascavel Black Number Arrow
metas.description: A tiny black pole paint, containing a white number with a triangle-shaped arrow. Unique to Cascavel, Parana.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Cascavel Blue Lamp
metas.description: The town of Cascavel, ParanÃ¡ uses this blue lamp. However, in newer coverage it is very rare to find.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Ceara Lamp Arms
metas.description: Lamps in CearÃ¡ often have a fancy and colourful arm, whether as lampposts or attached to utility poles. It sometimes says the town on the arm.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Ceara Poletop
metas.description: This assymetrical pole with no supports appears statewide in Ceara and sometimes Rondonia. (The Sao Paulo pole has a support bar)

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Center White Lines
metas.description: White Center lines are very common in Joao Pessoa. Yellow dashed lines are rare.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Chessboard Sidewalk
metas.description: The sidewalks with a chessboard pattern are common in Curitiba, PR.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Cobblestone Pavement
metas.description: Cobblestone pavement is most common in the northeast and in Rio Grande do Sul.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Colorful Signpost
metas.description: These colorful, thick signposts can be found in different cities in the state of Sao Paulo.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Compact Electricity Counter on Pole
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Compact Electricity Counter on Pole
metas.description: An electricity counter with a compact design can be seen in Mato Grosso, Para, Amapa and Paraiba.
metas.comparison: The "less compact" variant with several counters does not exist in Paraiba.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Concrete Trash Bins
metas.description: Brazil often uses metal trash baskets outside houses. In Acre and RondÃ´nia, however, it is much more common to see them made of concrete.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Connector in Bend
metas.description: Meta for Sao Paulo. Only counts when the connector is pointing downwards. The connectors pointing upwards are generic.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Corroded Streetsign
metas.description: All the street signs in Palmas are corroded.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Crossbar with no support
metas.description: Crossbars with no support bars are almost exclusively found in Piaui, Ceara, Rio Grande do Norte and Alagoas. They also frequently appear in the North-East in general, and in Rondonia and Roraima.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Curitiba Sidewalk
metas.description: The two most typical sidewalk patterns in Curitiba, PR.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Dark Brown Insulator on Grey Base
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Dark Brown Insulator on Grey Base
metas.description: These dark brown insulators with grey bases are found almost exclusively in Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Divided Highway
metas.description: SÃ£o Paulo has far more divided highways than any other state.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Embedded Pole ID
metas.description: Yellow plate embedded into pole. Mainly in Maranhao, spill into Para and Piaui.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Exremely Long Insulator
metas.description: This one is basically a sub-category of the 6+ Ridge Insulator. It's common in Para, Parana, Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul.
metas.comparison: However, it's not always easy to tell apart, but the longer the insulator feels, the more you should consider those states.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Fancy Lamp - Campo MourÃ£o
metas.description: "Fancy Lamps" are unique to Northwest-ParanÃ¡. This specific one is unique to the town of Campo MourÃ£o.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Fancy Lamp - Cidade Gaucha
metas.description: "Fancy Lamps" are unique to Northwest-ParanÃ¡. This specific one is unique to the town of Cidade Gaucha. Notably, it's very similar to the one from Campo Mourao.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Fancy Lamp - Goioere
metas.description: "Fancy Lamps" are unique to Northwest-ParanÃ¡. This specific one - with the yellow support - is unique to the town of Goioere. However, in newer coverage, the yellow supports are rarer to find.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Fancy Lamp - Loanda
metas.description: "Fancy Lamps" are unique to Northwest-ParanÃ¡. This specific one - with a plain white lamp and no painted patterns on it - is unique to the town of Loanda.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Fancy Lamp - Umuarama
metas.description: "Fancy Lamps" are unique to Northwest-ParanÃ¡. This specific one is unique to the town of Umuarama. It is strikingly similar to the lamp from Cidade Gaucha.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Fancy Lamp - Umuarama
metas.description: "Fancy Lamps" are unique to Northwest-ParanÃ¡. This specific, uniquely shaped one is unique to the town of Umuarama.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Florianopolis Pole
metas.description: Poles on Florianopolis, especially on Santa Catarina Island are painted white with blue and red stripes.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Florianopolis Sign
metas.description: Sometimes also with a white line instead of a red line.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Fortaleza ID
metas.description: These two types of IDs are common in Fortaleza (two pictures)

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Gamma + Box
metas.description: Gamma pole with an electricity box at the end of the crossbeam. Most common in Belem, Salvador and Rio de Janeiro. Can appear occasionally in Ceara and Alagoas.
metas.comparison: In RJ, they are particularly common in Sao Goncalo, but appear statewide.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Goias Pole ID
metas.description: The Goias pole ID uses yellow paint with black numbers or a black plate with yellow numbers. Unlike the Bahia and Pernambuco IDs, the ID consists exclusively of digits.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Grass Verge
metas.description: Grass verges between the sidewalk and the road are common in Curitiba.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Green Lamp
metas.description: There are three large cities with green lamps: Cuiaba, Manaus and Vitoria

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Hexagonal Pavement
metas.description: Roads with hexagonal concrete tiles can be found across Brazil, but they are more common in Santa Catarina and Minas Gerais.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - High attached ID
metas.description: Yellow plate attached by zip tie or metal strip. If it is higher up on the pole, it's in Pernambuco.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Holey Ladder Pole
metas.description: Ladder Poles with holes in them are very common in Joao Pessoa (but not unique)

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Horizontal Insulators
metas.description: Poles with horizontal insulators are very common in ParÃ¡ and less so in Mato Grosso. They are rarely found in Acre, AmapÃ¡, Tocantins, Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Horizontal Insulators with Top
metas.description: Poles that have one insulator on top and alternating horizontal insulators can be found in Mato Grosso and southern Acre. It is also very rare in Rio Grande do Sul.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Huge Electric Box on Pole
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Huge Electric Box on Pole
metas.description: Electric meter boxes can be seen in other cities, but in Cuiaba, there are usually 3-6 or even more on one pole.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Huge pole ID
metas.description: This rather large pole ID is common in Betim, Minas Gerais.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Imperatriz holey ID
metas.description: This city ID is distinct thanks to the holes on the sides.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Imperatriz Ornate Lamp
metas.description: Imperatriz, Maranhao

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Internet Poster
metas.description:
Internet Advertisements attached to poles are very common in Natal.
Mnemonic: Internatal :)

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Ipiranga Lamp
metas.description: These red lamps that resemble BelÃ©m lamps can be found in the neighborhood of Ipiranga in Florianopolis.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Irregular Cobblestone
metas.description: Cobblestone roads with randomly sized stones are most common in southeast Rio Grande do Sul and Minas Gerais.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Itumbiara Red Lamp
metas.description: Itumbiara, Goias

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Joao de Barro nests
metas.description: These spheres on top of utility poles are JoÃ£o-de-Barro nests. They are common across the south of Brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Joao Pessoa Stone Pavement
metas.description: Distinct stone sidewalks & driveways in Joao Pessoa.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Joinville Lamp
metas.description: Joinville, Santa Catarina

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Joinville Street Sign
metas.description: Not to be confused with the Curitiba sign, which can also be attached to a pole.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Kilometer Marker with Phone Number
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Kilometer Marker with Phone Number
metas.description: Phone numbers can sometimes be seen underneath kilometre markers in SÃ£o Paulo.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Lack of Poles
metas.description: Suspicious lack of poles, and curved lamp posts in their place, are indicative of BrasÃ­lia.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Little Guy Lamp
metas.description: This cute lamp is unique to Gurupi.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Lollipop Insulators
metas.description: These insulators are spherical or cone shaped and suspended on a rod above the insulator bar. They are often referred to as âlollipopâ insulators. They are very common in Rio Grande de Norte, ParaÃ­ba, Pernambuco, and more rarely, Sergipe.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Londrina Black Pole ID
metas.description: These black pole IDs are common in the state of ParanÃ¡, except for the capital Curitiba. If the black pole has a decimal marker (.) in the number, it's in Londrina.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Londrina Blue Number on Pole
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Londrina Blue Number on Pole
metas.description: The town of Londrina, ParanÃ¡ sometimes has little blue numbers painted on its poles.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Low Attached ID
metas.description: Yellow plate attached by zip tie or metal strip. If it is lower on the pole, it is RGDN.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - MA006
metas.description: Most of this road has a thick (1m) stripe of red dirt on the sides of the road. The road is oriented North-South and frequently shows Babassu palms

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Macapa Lamp
metas.description: Macapa, Amapa

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Macapa Pole ID
metas.description: Macapa, Amapa

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Maceio ID
metas.description: These two IDs are rare but unique to Maceio.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Maceio Lamp
metas.description: Long posts with top arm bend and yellow or grey top dot at the bottom.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Maceio Streetsign
metas.description: Also available in blue.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Manaus Pole ID
metas.description: Pole IDs in Manaus are usually above the lamp attachment.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Maraba Skull Box
metas.description: Yellow skull stickers are common on electric boxes in Maraba.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - MGDS Flag
metas.description: In urban settings, state flags might show up. Might pay off sometimes.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Minas Gerais ID with 0/1
metas.description: These pole IDs are specific for Minas Gerais. If they start with 0 or 1, it's Belo Horizonte.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Natal ID
metas.description: Natal, Rio Grande do Norte

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Neon-Yellow Horizontal ID
metas.description: Neon-yellow horizontal IDs are specific to Sao Paulo. Do not confuse with Campo Grande or Vitoria (they have vertical, and smaller, neon-yellow IDs)

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Neon-Yellow Pole ID
metas.description: Neon-yellow, vertical IDs can be found in Campo Grande, MS and Vitoria, ES. Do not confuse with horizontal neon-yellow IDs (Sao Paulo)

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Onitel Sticker
metas.description: Unique to Luziania, GO

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Open Electric Box
metas.description: Open or trashed electric boxes appear frequently in Maraba and SantarÃ©m (both Para).

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Orange Lamp
metas.description: Orange Lamps are common in Belem.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Orange Lamp Arm
metas.description: Very common in Teresina, one of the most well-known urban Brazil metas.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Outer Dashed Lines
metas.description: Outer Dashed Lines can rarely be found in Rio Grande do Norte or other northeast states.
