metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Para specific Pole ID
metas.description: Pare uses these state-wide pole IDs.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Paraiba ID
metas.description: This ID is uncommon, but unique to Paraiba (most common in the capital Joao Pessoa).

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Paraiba Lamp
metas.description: The shape matters.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Parana Black Paint Pole ID
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Parana Black Paint Pole ID
metas.description: Pole IDs in ParanÃ¡ are usually made up of black paint and yellow or white painted text. They do not appear in the capital of ParanÃ¡: Curitiba.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Parana Black Square
metas.description: This tiny black paint is rarely found on larger poles in ParanÃ¡. Still worth a quick scan, especially in urban locs.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Parana Road Pole Paint
metas.description: Utility poles in ParanÃ¡ on intersections are sometimes painted with the street name. This is because metal signs are expensive. This is also possible on Northern Rio Grande do Sul ladder poles. An exception is the town of Sinop, Mato Grosso.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - PARE on stone
metas.description: Stone road markings are unique to Caxias do Sul, RS.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Pencil Pole Top
metas.description: This little hat on the top, which makes the whole pole resemble a pencil, is most common in Rio de Janeiro, but can also be found in Manaus and Distrito Federal.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Piles of Dirt Meta
metas.description: Common in Boa Vista

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Pole Company
metas.description: Electricity company names in Brazil are commonly engraved onto the poles, with their names sometimes corresponding to state names. For example, CELPA stands for Para, COSERN for Rio Grande do Norte or COELCE for Ceara.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Pole Paint starting with letter
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Pole Paint starting with letter
metas.description: Yellow paint with black numbers, starts with a letter. Possible in Bahia and Pernambuco. The letter is often specific to a town. Goias uses similar paint IDs, but they consist only of digits.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Pole-Attached Sign
metas.description: Some poles in Curitiba, PR have street signs attached to them. Curitiba still uses regular, generic street signs, though.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Pole-Wrapped Sign
metas.description: These blue pole-wrapped signs are unique to Campo Grande.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Porto Alegre ID
metas.description: Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Porto Velho Pole ID
metas.description: Porto Velho, Rondonia

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Recife Lamp
metas.description: Recife, Pernambuco

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Rectangle on Pole Arm
metas.description: Unique for Recife. Can be faded or even have different colors. It's the shape that matters.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Red Brick Pavement
metas.description: Some roads in Acre are made of red brick.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Red Gravel
metas.description: Most roads in PiauÃ­ have red gravel on the side of the road. Some roads in Generation 4 now have tarmac and kerbs, but some gravel shoulders remain.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Red Sticker on Lamp
metas.description: This red sticker below the lamp is unique to Fortaleza.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Rio de Janeiro Lamp
metas.description: Curvy lamp arm, usually big head.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Rio de Janeiro Landbridge
metas.description: This map west of the city of Rio de Janeiro is unique due to the water in the south, the roadlines (double yellow - double broken yellow - single broken white) and the little wall in the North. Rio mountains can be seen in most sections of the road to the North.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Rio De Janeiro Polepaint
metas.description: This yellow polepaint, similar to Sao Paulo, but with all numbers, can be found in Rio de Janeiro.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Rio de Janeiro Taxi
metas.description: Taxis in Rio de Janeiro are completely yellow.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Rio Weird Pole
metas.description: When there is something out of the ordinary happening with the pole, it's Rio de Janeiro.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Roraima Lamps
metas.description: Lamps in Roraima have a similar style but have different colours in the main cities. Boa Vista, Normandia, and MucajaÃ­ have red lamps, RorainÃ³polis has blue lamps, Pacaraima and Iracema have green, and CaracaraÃ­ has yellow.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Round Pole
metas.description: Alongside ladder poles, round poles can often be found across the south of Brazil, especially SÃ£o Paulo. These poles are cylindrical and made of concrete.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Salvador Lamp Arm ID
metas.description: Long yellow ID on the lamp arm, can be very hard to spot.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Salvador Sidewalk
metas.description: Unique sidewalk, can have other black and white broken tile patterns.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Santarem Lamp
metas.description: Santarem, Para

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Sao Luis ID
metas.description: This rare ID is specific to Sao Luis. However, the embedded Maranhao IDs are more common.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Sao Luis Pointy Lamp
metas.description: Pointy front of lamp head, blue or yellow top light.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Sao Paulo Lamp
metas.description: Straight long lamp neck, with tight top bend, usually thin head.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Sao Paulo Pole
metas.description: Assymetrical crossbeam and insulator position with a long support bar reaching to the middle of the longer part of the crossbeam.
metas.comparison: Extremely common in Sao Paulo, common in Rio Grande do Sul. Less common Rio de Janeiro, Espirito Santo and Mato Grosso do Sul (where it appears most oftenly in Tres Lagoas). Rare in Mato Grosso.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Sao Paulo Polepaint
metas.description: Sao Paulo Metropolitan Area has these yellow pole paints with a three letter code. The letters stand for the town. SPU is the most important code, standing for the main city.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Serra dos Orgaos
metas.description: This road can be found North of Rio de Janeiro (city). It is a concrete road with black tar behind the road lines.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Short Gamma + Box
metas.description: Short crossbeam, support bar and electricity box at the end of the crossbeam. Only found in Belem. (unlike the regular Gamma pole with box which can also be found in Salvador and Rio de Janeiro).

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Small Red Tactile Pavement
metas.description: Small tile, circular bumps, red tactile pavement is very common in Vitoria, ES. (Do not confuse with Florianopolis, which has large tile red tactile pavement).

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Southern Sidewalk
metas.description: You can often see pavements in Rio Grande do Sul that have brown tiles but are either jagged and random, or square. This style can sometimes be seen in Santa Catarina.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Speedbumps
metas.description: Yellow dashed lines and speedbumps are very common in BrasÃ­lia. (but not unique)

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Spool Insulators
metas.description: These insulators have a shape resembling a spool of thread. They are found mostly in Rio de Janeiro and EspÃ­rito Santo, and have been seen in CearÃ¡.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Square Paint ID
metas.description: This ID with two sections, the upper one being a square with a number in it, appears in Pernambuco.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Striped Curbs
metas.description: Black and white striped curbs are common in Boa Vista.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Surprising Wooden Pole
metas.description: In Porto Alegre, there is noticeably more foliage, cleaner, and more spacious than any other city which makes the common wooden poles look somewhat out of place.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Teresina ID
metas.description: Long & Horizontal ID

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Thick Bottom Insulator
metas.description: They're found almost anywhere, but can still resolve some 50/50s:
metas.comparison: They are only rarely found in Rio Grande do Norte. Also they're less common in Pernambuco, Parana, Santa Catarina.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Thin Long Insulator
metas.description: Insulators in CearÃ¡ can sometimes be uniquely long and thin. They are in GoiÃ¡s too, but are rare.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Thin Red Stripe
metas.description: A road with a thin, red stripe out of gravel can be found east of Teresina, Piaui.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tiny Lamp - Araruna
metas.description: "Tiny Lamps" are unique to Northwest-ParanÃ¡. This specific one is unique to the town of Araruna.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tiny Lamp - Cianorte
metas.description: "Tiny Lamps" are unique to Northwest-ParanÃ¡. This specific one is unique to the town of Cianorte.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tiny Lamp - Cruzeiro do Oeste
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Tiny Lamp - Cruzeiro do Oeste
metas.description: "Tiny Lamps" are unique to Northwest-ParanÃ¡. This specific one is unique to the town of Cruzeiro do Oeste.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tiny Lamp - Loanda
metas.description: "Tiny Lamps" are unique to Northwest-ParanÃ¡. This specific one is unique to the town of Loanda.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tiny Lamp - Maringa
metas.description: "Tiny Lamps" are unique to Northwest-ParanÃ¡. This specific one is unique to the town of Maringa.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tiny Lamp - Paranavai
metas.description: "Tiny Lamps" are unique to Northwest-ParanÃ¡. This specific one is unique to the town of Paranavai.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tocantins specific lamp
metas.description: This lamp with a short arm and top light is specific to Tocantins.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tocantins specific lamp
metas.description: This blue lamp with top light and the unique pattern on the underside is specific to Tocantins.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tocantins specific lamp
metas.description: This long blue lamp with a top light and a unique pattern on the underside is specific to Tocantins.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Transparent Mushroom Insulator
metas.description:
Transparent, mushroom-shaped insulators are common in Alagoas.
They less frequently appear in Coastal Santa Catarina.
Rarely, they also appear in coastal Rio Grande do Sul, coastal Sao Paulo and in Sergipe.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Trident Pole
metas.description: Poles with these wide insulators in a trident formation are common in MaranhÃ£o. The insulator itself is common across many states, but not in this configuration.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Two Part Lamp - Goias Variant
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Two Part Lamp - Goias Variant
metas.description: 2-part lamp, most commonly seen in Minas Gerais and Goias. This particular variant with a the pole visible underneath is more common in Goias.
metas.comparison: Otherwise, this pole appears in Rio Grande do Norte and Rio Grande do Sul (very useful if you have North/South vibe), spill in Distrito Federal and extremely rarely in Para, Mato Grosso and Rondonia.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Two Part Lamp - Minas Gerais Variant
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Two Part Lamp - Minas Gerais Variant
metas.description: 2-part lamp, most commonly seen in Minas Gerais and Goias. This particular variant - with both parts enveloping the lamp - is more common in Minas Gerais.
metas.comparison: Otherwise, this pole appears in Rio Grande do Norte and Rio Grande do Sul (very useful if you have North/South vibe), spill in Distrito Federal and extremely rarely in Para, Mato Grosso and Rondonia.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Uberaba ID
metas.description: In Uberaba, pole IDs start with 2 or 3, and sometimes with 1. In Belo Horizonte, meanwhile, they start with 0 or 1. They do not appear in any other cities in MG.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Uneven Stone Pavement
metas.description: These uneven but mostly square stone roads are seen in western Rio Grande do Sul and west Santa Catarina. The soil will often be very dark in these regions too.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Vitoria Electric Boxes
metas.description: Metal electricity box, sandwiched between plastic electricity boxes are very common in Vitoria, ES.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Vitoria ID
metas.description: Red pole ID.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Vitoria Streetsign
metas.description: Unique streetsign design in Vitoria.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Weird Road Layout
metas.description: Roundabouts and weird layout roads that are mostly empty, and perfectly flat, are common in Palmas.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - White Mushroom Insulator
metas.description: Bahia uses these unique white insulators sometimes.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - WiFi-Password Pole-ID
metas.description: If you find pole IDs with codes that resemble WiFi-passwords (mix of digits, upper- and lowercase letters), you're in Curitiba, PR.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Wooden Pole
metas.description: Some states also use wooden poles. They are most commonly seen in Rio Grande do Sul, Roraima, Amazonas, and Rio de Janeiro.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Yellow Outer Lines
metas.description: Yellow outer lines on urban roads are very common in Curitiba.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Yellow Stick
metas.description: This yellow stick is common in Rio Branco, and often has a sign attached to it.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Zig-Zag lamp arm
metas.description: In Brazil, this Zig-Zag lamp arm is unique to Caxias do Sul.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - ZigZag-Topbar
metas.description: This pole configuration, featuring a zigzag-shaped top bar resting atop a flat crossbar, is exclusive to Ceara and Roraima. The pole is usually much larger than a regular electricity pole.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure -6+ Ridge Insulators
metas.description: These insulators have six or more ridges.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Acre Landscape
metas.description: Acre has a unique landscape of small grass hills and sparsely growing trees. The roads often do not cut around the hills like in most of Brazil, but ride the hills instead. A similar landscape can also be seen near Maraba in the state of ParÃ¡.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Amazon Rainforest
metas.description: The Amazon is a dense rainforest that compromises 40% of Brazil's total area. Not many roads are within it, but those that are, mostly go through either biodiverse forest or grassy hills with sparse trees.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Amazonas 319
metas.description: The Amazonas 319 has a very lush, bright green and tropical landscape, as it cuts through the Amazon rainforest. The road is flat and mostly unpaved, featuring bright orange soil. However, closer to Manaus the road becomes paved. There are wooden or ladder poles alongside the entire stretch. It is covered by the blue Generation 4 car.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - BR-163 in Para
metas.description: The ParÃ¡ section of the 163 is often hilly, curvy, dry, and sometimes hazy. It has a wide range of amazonian vegetation. The road is frequently trafficked, usually by transportation trucks. It is covered by the blue Generation 4 car.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - BR174 in Amazonas
metas.description: This road can be recognized by the Amazonian looking trees and the NW/SE angle. It always has Gen 4 and an exposed, blue car front.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - BR230 in Amazonas
metas.description: This wide dirt road has Amazonian trees and a blurred car. You will not find other cars on the road. It's the only East-to-West angle road in that area.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - BR230 in Para
metas.description: This road looks like an Amazonian road with the trees and dense rainforest. It runs east-west, slightly to the south. The road looks like its stained with mud

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - BR319, North of Porto Velho
metas.meta_label: Landscape - BR319, North of Porto Velho
metas.description: This road is characterized by it's Amazonian look and the SW-NE road angle. Some sections of this road are overcast and/or showcase a flat landscape.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Caatinga landscape
metas.description: Northeastern Brazil can be identified by its dry soil, shrubs and succulents (the Caatinga landscape).

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Caatinga landscape - rain coverage
metas.description: Northeastern Brazil can be identified by its dry soil, shrubs and succulents (the Caatinga landscape). In rainy season coverage, the shrubs are still recognizable, but can be deceptively green.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Corvo Branco
metas.description: This road in eastern Santa Catarina is characterized by its windyness and by the steep mountains and cliffs along its side. It can feel like your driving with the clouds. The road goes through Corvo Branco which is a famous tourist attraction.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Dunas da Sabiaguaba
metas.description: This road east of Fortaleza is characterized by its unique pavement and the sanddunes along the road.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Exposed Rock
metas.description: EspÃ­rito Santo, and the surrounding areas, often have large mountains with exposed rock.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Flat Wetland
metas.description: Coastal regions in Rio Grande do Sul are recognisable due to being a rare flat wetland, which is uncommon in Brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Landbridge in Rio Grande do Sul
metas.meta_label: Landscape - Landbridge in Rio Grande do Sul
metas.description: Recognizable by the swamp-like landscape, the pine trees along the road and the Lagoon It runs at a SE-NW angle.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Noronha Rocks
metas.description: Ilha de Fernando de Noronha is similar in vegetation to NE-Brazil and has large exposed rocks.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - North of Uiramuta road
metas.description: This very unique looking road features rolling hills, which is unusual for the rather flat Roraima. It is a windy dirt road and despite being green, it lacks trees. What seperates this from the road south of Uiramuta is that it's more skinny and steeper.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Rio Grande do Sul Landscape
metas.meta_label: Landscape - Rio Grande do Sul Landscape
metas.description: The landscape in Rio Grande do Sul can be hilly or flat with lush, green fields. Southern areas can have some resemblance to Uruguay.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Rollercoaster Road
metas.description: The 364 through Acre is very recognisable due to the rollercoaster-like landscape and road: the road uniquely rides the hills rather than snaking around them. There is usually no traffic, and is covered mostly by Generation 3 with an antenna.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Roraima Landscape
metas.description: Rural locations in Roraima are mostly open grassy plains with large, distant mountains in the background. Occasionally, you are on roads within the mountains. Furthermore, the grass in Roraima is distinctly thin, and grows in bunches.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Serra do Mar
metas.description: Serra do Mar is a high mountain range that runs close to the coast from Parana to Northern RGDS.
metas.comparison: If you have a high altitude road going on the mountains, instead of in the valleys, you're likely here.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - South of Uiramuta
metas.description: This very unique looking road features rolling hills, which is unusual for the rather flat Roraima. It is a windy dirt road and despite being green, it lacks trees. What seperates this from the road south of Uiramuta is that it's less skinny and less steep.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Southeast Hills
metas.description: Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro and EspÃ­rito Santo often have rolling grassy hills.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Swampy Road
metas.description: A very swampy road (PA-154) can be found Northwest of BelÃ©m. Notably, there are very few trees, and the soil is very red.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Uneven Stone + Corn
metas.description: This beautiful road west of Cascavel and South of Toledo, by the PR-585 is characterized by the uneven red stone pavement and the corn plantation next to it.

metas.name: Brazil - Trekker - Amazonian Trekker
metas.description: This Amazonian trekker combines boat and walking coverage on and near the Madeira and Aripuana rivers, south of the 319. They are seen travelling through dense rainforest and small villages.

metas.name: Brazil - Trekker - LenÃ§Ã³is Maranhenses National Park
metas.description: The beautiful National Park of Northeast MaranhÃ£o, known for its sand dunes with pools of water, has walking trekker and vehicle coverage. The truck is white with a black bed. The landscape can vary from beach to sandy wetland.

metas.name: Brazil - Trekker - Noronha Boat Trekker
metas.description: There is boat coverage around the island of Ilha de Fernando de Noronha.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Acai Palm
metas.description: AÃ§ai palms produce fruits that are popular globally. Most of these palms are found near Belem, but can be seen across the Amazon. They are distinct in the way the leaflets droop downward along with their unusually thin trunks.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: They are very similar to the Jucara Palm (which grows in Southern Brazil). Tips for differentiation:

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Acrocomia Totai (Paraguay Palm)
metas.description: This palm is commonly mistaken to be a Macaw Palm (Acrocomia Aculeata). The key difference is that the trunk of the "Paraguay Palm" is often smoother and less irregular. The crown can also give some hints although it's difficult to catch the differences
metas.comparison: The distribution is also a bit different, as this palm usually is closer to Paraguay than the Macaw Palm which stretches further.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Babassu Palm
metas.description: Babassu palms have long, robust leaves comprised of many leaflets. Trunk length can vary from short to tall. They are found throughout the Amazon, or more rarely, down the east coast.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Carnauba Palm
metas.description: CarnaÃºba palms have short but strong, fan-like leaves and a trunk that is smooth at the top and spiked at the bottom. They are common in CearÃ¡ but are also in PiauÃ­ and Rio Grande do Norte.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Coconut Palm
metas.description: Coconut palm trees have long leaves, can grow very tall, and have thin trunks. They are common across the north eastern states and sometimes further west or south along the coast.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Jucara Palm
metas.description: Closely related to the AÃ§aÃ­ palm, they are really hard to distinguish apart from each other. However, the AÃ§aÃ­ palm grows mostly in the northern flat regions of Brazil, while the JuÃ§ara grows in the mountainous south-east regions of Brazil anywhere from Espirito Santo down to Rio Grande do Sul.
metas.comparison: Here some tips for differences:

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Macaw Palm
metas.description: Macaw palms, often called Paraguay palms, have thin leaves compared to other palms, and often have a visible spear shaped top. They are very common around Mato Grosso do Sul and the surrounding states, but can be seen much further out sometimes. These palms should be used with caution, and single trees are much less of an indicator than multiple trees.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Moriche Palm
metas.description: Moriche palms have leaves with a rounded fan shape. They are most common in Amazonas, Acre, and Roraima, but can be found in all of the Amazonian states.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Mysterious Northeastern Plant
metas.description: This species of plant, with long stems and many leaves growing up, are very common in CearÃ¡, Rio Grande do Norte, and ParaÃ­ba. In the dry season, you can still make out the distinct long stems without leaves.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Parana Pine
metas.description: These distinct trees, called ParanÃ¡ pines, have long horizontal branches with leaves only at the end. They grow mainly in the southern Brazilian states of ParanÃ¡, Santa Catarina, and Rio Grande do Sul.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Pine Trees
metas.description: Pine Trees are common in Southern Brazil, but are rarely ever found north of Belo Horizonte.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Queen Palm
metas.description: Queen palms have leaf stems that point upwards on the trunk and then "bow down" again to the ground due to gravity. They are native to South America. In Brazil, they are mainly found along the coast between Rio de Janeiro and Porto Alegre.
metas.comparison: Outside of South America, they're also found in Florida and East Coast Queensland.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Tocantins Grass
metas.description: Very tall grass can be often seen in the centre of the country, most notably in the Tocantins, GoiÃ¡s, Bahia, and Minas Gerais states.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Clay Brick Walls
metas.description: San Pedro de Atacama can be recognized by its clay brick walls, commonly with triangles at the top.

metas.comparison: NOTE: Orange lamps can rarely be found in other smaller cities. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Orange Street Signs
metas.description: Orange street signs can be seen in the city of Lanco, present at almost every intersection.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Photocell Lamps
metas.description: Lamps in Santiago very commonly have photocells. You will rarely find them in other cities such as Valparaiso, Osorno and Loncoche.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Round Pole & Black Paint
metas.description: Round poles with black paint can be seen in the town of El Salvador.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Ruta 9
metas.description: All yellow lines on a concrete road are a good indicator that you are on the paved section of Ruta 9, in the very south of Chile. The landscape tends to be barren, grassy, and treeless.

metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Yellow Pole Paint in the Desert
metas.description: Poles in Arica feature white paint with a black number, while the other cities in the Atacama Desert feature poles with yellow paint. Keep in mind the paint may have faded, making it look white.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - A-31
metas.description: The A-31 can be recognised by its high altitude, with a steep drop into a valley to the north. The road also has Gen 3 sunset coverage.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - A11 - Barren
metas.description: After crossing the Lluta River at Poconchile, the Ruta 11 continues out of the valley and up into the mountains. The road is all newly paved (except for a few small segments with ongoing construction) and is generally quite wide. This section of Ruta 11 features:
metas.comparison: The landscape is bare of vegetation until around Zapahuira, east of which the landscape becomes open and covered with small green bushes.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - A11 - Lluta River Valley
metas.description:
Along the Lluta River, the Ruta 11 passes through a wide valley lined by sloping, sandy mountains that often feature distinctly round rock protrusions.
The valley is home to a large amount of agriculture relative to other parts of the Atacama Desert. Youâll often see sizable green fields lined by bushes, trees, or wooden fences, as well as bunches of planted Mexican fan palms.
A railroad track also follows the Lluta River on both sides, so if youâre in a green valley next to both a river and a railroad, youâre almost certainly on Ruta 11.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - A11 - Shrubby
metas.description: After crossing the Lluta River at Poconchile, the Ruta 11 continues out of the valley and up into the mountains. The road is all newly paved (except for a few small segments with ongoing construction) and is generally quite wide. The landscape is bare of vegetation until around Zapahuira, east of which the landscape becomes open and covered with small green bushes.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Alto Bio Bio National Reserve
metas.meta_label: Landscape - Alto Bio Bio National Reserve
metas.description: A vast, mostly treeless landscape combined with triple yellow lines are seen in Alto Bio Bio National Reserve. While the reserve may look dry, there is a distinct cold and high altitude feel.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Alto Bio Bio National Reserve - Monkey Puzzle Trees
metas.meta_label: Landscape - Alto Bio Bio National Reserve - Monkey Puzzle Trees
metas.description: A vast, mostly treeless landscape combined with triple yellow lines are seen in Alto Bio Bio National Reserve. While the reserve may look dry, there is a distinct cold and high altitude feel. Monkey puzzles are also seen toward the east.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Alto Loa National Reserve
metas.description: Alto Loa National Reserve can be recognized by the vast, open landscape, followed by salt pans leading up to snow-capped volcanoes. The reserve does not have any paved roads.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Antofagasta Ridge
metas.description: A rockier, and more uneven ridge can be seen in Antofagasta.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Arica Mountains
metas.description: The province of Arica y Parinacota can be recognized by the smooth, sandy mountains that may look slightly eroded, or have bulbous formations. Valleys are also common, which are rarely seen in other parts of Chile.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Arica Ridge
metas.description: A slight, sandy ridge with a gradual incline can be seen in Arica.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Atacama Desert
metas.description: The Atacama is an extremely arid desert covering the northern third of Chile. Some parts of it experience the lowest rainfall on the planet. As a result, many locations in this desert are almost completely devoid of any vegetation: you will often just see sand and bare rock without any plants in sight anywhere.
metas.comparison: NOTE: The Atacama Desert also covers parts of southern Peru, western Bolivia and northwestern Argentina.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Atacama Mountains
metas.description: These rocky, uneven mountains are most commonly seen in Atacama and northern Coquimbo.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Brownish Red Soil (Gen 3)
metas.description: This brownish red soil can sometimes be seen in Atacama province.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This is most reliable in Generation 3. This soil can be seen in other provinces in Generation 4.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - ChiloÃ© Landscape
metas.description: A rolling, agricultural landscape, comparable to New Zealand, can be seen on Isla Grande de ChiloÃ©.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Similar looking landscapes exist in some other parts of the country, but usually more level.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Dry Hills
metas.description: The region around Santiago can be recognized by its semi-arid climate, having dry hills and scattered vegetation.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Eucalyptus
metas.description: Eucalyptus plantations combined with a somewhat dry climate are a good indicator that you are in southwestern ValparaÃ­so.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Iquique Ridge
metas.description: A large, towering ridge can be seen in Iquique.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Lauca National Park
metas.description: East of Putre, Ruta 11 enters Lauca National Park which has a flatter landscape, with tall snow-capped mountains in the background, and features unique Andean Plateau vegetation like Peruvian feather grass and the recognizable cushion plant yareta (Azorella compacta). You can also find Chilean bollards lining the road, which are extremely rare.
metas.comparison: Lauca can look very similar to other areas in the east Andes of northern Chile, but itâs recognizable for the iconic VolcÃ¡n Parinacota, a tall snow-capped volcano that stands alone and away from other mountain ridges. Itâs visible from basically every location in the park, though it can be shrouded by clouds.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Llanos de Challe National Park
metas.meta_label: Landscape - Llanos de Challe National Park
metas.description: Llanos de Challe National Park can be recognized by the brown coloured dirt on the roadside, patches of light sand, juniper plants, and dark coloured mountains. The sky is overcast in most of the coverage.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Los Flamencos National Reserve
metas.description: Smooth mountains with a reddish tint are seen in Los Flamencos National Reserve. Salt pans are also a common sight. The reserve uses triple yellow lines.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Los FLamencos National Reserve - Short Dashes
metas.meta_label: Landscape - Los FLamencos National Reserve - Short Dashes
metas.description: Smooth mountains with a reddish tint are seen in Los Flamencos National Reserve. Salt pans are also a common sight. The reserve uses triple yellow lines, with short dashes in the west.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Lush Green Valleys
metas.description: Lush green valleys, with rocky mountains and often overcast coverage, can be seen in southern Los Lagos and northern AysÃ©n.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Maule Landscape
metas.description: Compared to the area around Santiago, the Maule province has a similar look. However, it has a Mediterranean climate, and is generally greener.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Narrow Roads & Trees
metas.description: Narrow roads with trees on both sides can commonly be seen in the provinces of Bio Bio and Araucania.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Nevado Tres Cruces National Park
metas.meta_label: Landscape - Nevado Tres Cruces National Park
metas.description: In the west, Nevado Tres Cruces National Park can be recognized by the vast, open landscape, followed by salt pans leading up to a line of mountains. The sand has a reddish tint.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Nevado Tres Cruces National Park - Snow
metas.meta_label: Landscape - Nevado Tres Cruces National Park - Snow
metas.description: In the east of this park, the Google Car drives up a mountain pass with views of lightly snow-capped volcanoes and snow on the side of the road. The roads in the National Park are paved.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Pampa del Tamarugal
metas.description: The northern section of Pampa del Tamarugal National Reserve can be recognized by the Tamarugo trees lining the road. The road itself is mediocre quality, and in a consistent north-west direction.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Pan de Azucar National Park
metas.meta_label: Landscape - Pan de Azucar National Park

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Puyehue National Park
metas.description: Puyehue National Park can be recognized by the dense vegetation surrounding the road. The pavement itself has triple yellow lines, and tar snakes are frequently seen.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Puyehue National Park - Dead Trees
metas.meta_label: Landscape - Puyehue National Park - Dead Trees

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Ruta 1

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Ruta 181

metas.description: OâHiggins can be recognized by the large mountains to the east, often casting a shadow over the town. To the west, snow-capped mountains are seen further in the distance.

metas.name: Chile - Trekker - ACA

metas.name: Chile - Trekker - ALMA-OSF
metas.description: ALMA OSF can be recognized by the large radio telescopes and rural facilities.

metas.name: Chile - Trekker - Horse Trekker

metas.name: Chile - Trekker - Torres Del Paine

metas.name: Chile - Vegetation - Purple Flowers

metas.description: Rainy coverage is most common on the highways 20, 24, 50 and 64.

metas.name: Colombia - Coverage Meta - Sogamoso Lake
metas.description: If you see a lake, paired with an overexposed Gen 4 camera, you're probably on this lake south of Sogamoso.

metas.name: Colombia - Coverage Meta - Stick Meta
metas.description: This stick on the camera can be found between El Guio and El Boral (near the Cundinamarca-Meta border near Villavicencio)

metas.name: Colombia - Coverage Meta - Unique Road - Tame to Arauca
metas.meta_label: Coverage Meta - Unique Road - Tame to Arauca
metas.description: On this road, you can see a sunset through the clouds. It's not always easy to recognize, however.

metas.name: Colombia - Coverage Meta - Unique Road - Tame to Hato Corozal
metas.meta_label: Coverage Meta - Unique Road - Tame to Hato Corozal
metas.description: On this road, you can see a slight sunset through the clouds. It is pretty flat, with mountains in the Northwest.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Barichara Pavement
metas.description: This unique cobblestone pavement is found is the historic town of Barichara, Santander.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Barranquilla Roadbollard
metas.description: In Barranquilla, you can often find this bollard with roadnames on intersections.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Buenaventura Truck Spam Road
metas.description: The stretch of the 40 to Buenaventura is an important route for trucks, so if you see many trucks, it's worth a thought.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Caldas Polepaint
metas.description: orange & blue

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Cauca/Narino Polepaint
metas.description: Yellow with dark numbers

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Coastal Antioquia Polepaint
metas.description: Green paint with yellow numbers

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Electricity Counter - Oval
metas.description: Usually pretty tall with oval windows, circle windows might not be as trustworthy.
metas.comparison: Very common as there are few plastic counters in this region.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - European Bollard
metas.description: This european-style (specifically spanish style bollard) is found in Cundinamarca, but also on the 40 towards Villavicencio.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - H-shaped lamp attachment
metas.description: H-shaped lamp attachment plates can be found in Bogota.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Huila Polepaint
metas.description: Orange paint with black numbers

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Ibague Lamp
metas.description: This red lamp style is unique to Tolima province.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: I only found it in Ibague, not in any other towns in Tolima. Also, the meta is more about the color and the shape of the lamp, not about the arrangement of the lights.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Megabus
metas.description: Green or yellow, modern bus. Often on a dedicated bus lane. Found in Pereira metropolitan area.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Pole Marking - Antioquia
metas.description: These pole markings with one short black strip on the top and bottom, and a longer yellow section in the middle, are most commonly found in the Antioquia department. Sometimes, you can find them in the Cordoba department as well.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - QR-Code Sticker
metas.description: Found in Barranquilla and Santa Marta

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Rectangular lamp attachment
metas.description: Rectangular lamp attachment plates can be found mainly in Medellin, sometimes further North, especially in Monteria and Cucuta.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Risaralda/Choco Polepaint
metas.description: Yellow paint with red numbers. Found all over Risaralda and the towns of Istmina and Quibdo in Choco.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Sarawak Pole
metas.description: Asymmetrical poles with a "Sarawak" extension (a vertical stalk coming out the top), can often be found East of Andes. Note that this pole is not 100%, and has been spotted elsewhere.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Spikes
metas.description: These spikes can be found on the 40 and the 62.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Street Lamps - Barranquilla
metas.description: The uniquely shaped supporting metal piece can be found in Barranquilla. (Similar to the Providencia design)

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Street Lamps - Providencia
metas.description: Providencia street lights are green and supported by a trapezoidal sheet of metal underneath. (The metal sheet without a green lamp can also be found in Barranquilla)

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Tinto Bus
metas.description: This red bus drives in the town (not the country) Armenia.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Tolima Poletag
metas.description: Orange tag with white numbers

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - TransLago vans
metas.description: TransLogo vans are common throughtout Boyaca Department. You will most often see them on the routes Tunja-Sogamoso and Tunja-Duitama.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Transmetro
metas.description: White Transmetro buses can be found in Barranquilla.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Tumaco
metas.description: If you see many puddles and a pavement out of '+' shaped stones, you're in Tumaco.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Valle de Cauca Pole
metas.description: If you see these poletops you will find yourself in Valle Del Cauca.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Valle de Cauca Polepaint
metas.description: Yellow, with black numbers. Several digits can be in one row.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Villavicencio Bike Lane Road
metas.description: If you see a bike lane, and get East of Andes vibes, you're most likely on the road through Los Tobitos to Villavicencio.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Deep grey & stony soil in Gen 3
metas.meta_label: Landscape - Deep grey & stony soil in Gen 3
metas.description: This type of soil can be found in towns near the pacific coast.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - East of Andes Landscape
metas.description: East of the Andes lies a vast lowland called Llanos. It is characterised by open tropical grasslands, savannas with scattered trees, small areas of forest and seasonal flooding.
metas.comparison: Since it's to the east of the Andes, you may see mountains in the west, but never in the east.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Guatape Hill
metas.description: This striking cone-shaped mountain can often be seen from the surrounding area of Guatape.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Guaviare Orange Road
metas.description: The only road in Guaviare goes from to Guaviare (city), and continues south up until Vda. El Trueno. It can be recognized by the orange-looking dust on the road.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - La Guajira
metas.description: This landscape is typical of the far Northern province of La Guajira: extreme dryness, low vegetation and occasional cacti.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Northern Landscape
metas.description: The Northern part of the country is characterised by white, sandy soil and an arid landscape.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Paramos
metas.description: Paramos refers to alpine tundra ecosystems located in the mountains. These kinds of regions are easy to guess by how little vegetation grows here. The best clue is these odd looking pants. ( giant rosette plants ).
metas.comparison: Note by MB: In my experience, this appears most commonly south of Bogota, still in the capital district.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Pasto Hills
metas.description:
In southern Colombia, around the city of Pasto, there are hilly fields that are unique in that they are bordered by hedges. The hedges are very thick and form very distinctive lines on the hills. It almost gives off a âBritishâ vibe.
If you are sure that it is Colombia, this is a very good meta, but such fields with hedges also occur in Ecuador.
metas.comparison:
!!
In very rare cases, such hedges on hills can also occur in other parts of Colombia.
!!

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Santa Rosalia
metas.description: Santa Rosalia is the only town covered in Vichada. So if you see red/orange dirt in an urban Gen 4 loc, you should go there.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Swamp Road + Extremely Sunny
metas.description: If you see a swamp road with extremely sunny coverage, you're probably on the 74 in Sucre.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Swamp Roads
metas.description: The 74, the 78 and a few other roads more north have very swampy parts, you can see on the map where these are by zooming.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Unique Road - 78 west of Pailitas
metas.meta_label: Landscape - Unique Road - 78 west of Pailitas
metas.description: This road is characterised by low clouds and a towering mountain in the east.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Unique Road - Ruta 90 Landbridge
metas.description: You can recognise the narrow Ruta 90 landbridge between Barranquilla and Cienaga thanks to the dashed yellow lines and shallow bodies of water next to the road. Open ocean can often be seen to the north.
metas.comparison: NOTE: In the older Generation 3 coverage, you will also see tall mountains in the distance.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Unique Road - Uribia to Puerto Boliviar
metas.meta_label: Landscape - Unique Road - Uribia to Puerto Boliviar
metas.description: You can often recognise the Uribia-Puerto Bolivar road because of La Guajira landscape (extreme dryness, low vegetation and occasional cacti), the straightness and the train track always present to the East.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Vichada Red Dirt
metas.description: Vichada is characterize by hazy Gen 4 coverage and Red Dirt.

metas.name: Colombia - Misc - Afro-Colombians
metas.description: As a result of slave trade, the Pacific coast of Colombia is home to an overwhelming majority of Afro-Colombians.

metas.name: Colombia - Trekker - Trebal Resort Trekker
metas.description: This trekker can be recognized by the unique pavement and houses.

metas.name: Colombia - Vegetation - Cacti
metas.description: Cacti are most commonly found in the North near Valledupar. Sometimes they can appear in Huila, too.

metas.name: Colombia - Vegetation - Colombian Mahogany
metas.description: This tree is found mainly around Medellin, but it has been spotted in other random spots.

metas.name: Colombia - Vegetation - Kapok Tree
metas.description: The Kapok tree can be found throughout Colombia, but is most common between the central and eastern mountain range.

metas.name: Colombia - Vegetation - Quindio Wax Palm
metas.description: This palm is found in mountainous regions of Colombia, mainly in Quindio, as the name suggests.

metas.name: Colombia - Vegetation - Veracruz Trees
metas.description: In Colombia you will most commonly find these trees that appear to have a knot on top of their trunk in the dark red areas. The province of Cordoba has the most gen 4 out of the others so if you see these in gen 4 consider Cordoba. (If the area is flat/semi hilly, You can find these trees in the mountains aswell everywhere)

metas.name: Colombia - Vegetation - Wide Trees
metas.description: These wide trees, usually near fences, are found in Northern regions, especially near Monteria and Sincelejo.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - 29 south of Ibri
metas.description: Road 29 south of Ibri features a fairly shrubby landscape, with low and jagged mountains on the eastern side of the road. The low-lying sun to the northwest is particularly distinct.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - 37 (Sunset Coverage)
metas.description: Road 37 travels in a generally northwest direction through a very generic, flat desert landscape. The angle is one of the best clues for this road. On the northern half, you can find distinct sunset coverage.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - 42 south of Shalim
metas.description: Just south of Shalim, youâll find a stretch of overcast coverage, along with a power line to the west of the road.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - 43 south of Ubar
metas.description: Road 43, also south of Ubar, is unpaved and features sunset coverage along with a dust trail behind the car.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - 45
metas.description: Roads 45 and the western stretch of 39 both feature a similar slightly hilly desert landscape, sunny weather, and a general east-to-west direction. What makes them unique is the light-coloured shoulders the roads share, though it is most pronounced on Road 45. The roads also mostly have a faded white middle line. To tell the 45 and western 39 apart, look at the sun, which is overhead on the 39, but to the west on 45. The section north of Mudayy is also the 45, but unlabelled on Google Maps.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Dirty Gen 2 Halo
metas.description: In some of New South Walesâ Generation 2, the halo looks very dirty. This is most common west of ACT and south of Barrington Tops.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Hazy Adam
metas.description: In and close to Adam, the coverage is usually quite hazy, and the ridge and hills from the previous tip can be seen to the north. Though sometimes, only one or two are visible. Unlike north of Adam, you wonât see mountains in any other direction.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Max South 32
metas.description: The southernmost section of Road 32 has a somewhat hilly landscape. The puffy cumulus clouds are what make this stretch recognisable. You can also look for the power line that runs west of the road for confirmation.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Max West 39
metas.description: Roads 45 and the western stretch of 39 both feature a similar slightly hilly desert landscape, sunny weather, and a general east-to-west direction. What makes them unique is the light-coloured shoulders the roads share, though it is most pronounced on Road 45. The roads also mostly have a faded white middle line. To tell the 45 and western 39 apart, look at the sun, which is overhead on the 39, but to the west on 45. The section north of Mudayy is also the 45, but unlabelled on Google Maps.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Ruta 21
metas.description: Generation 4 sunset coverage can be seen on Ruta 21 from Calama to San Francisco de Chiu Chiu. In the west near Calama, the sun has just started to set, causing a giant white dome in the sky. In the east, the sky has a warm gradient, and the tops of the volcanoes are seen glowing pink.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Western 41 - Cloudy
metas.description: The western stretch of Road 41 has wide shoulders similar to Road 31, however, the more northwest-bound angle along with the reddish soil should tell them apart. The eastern half has cloudy coverage.

metas.name: France - Agriculture - Breeding
metas.description: It is not so rare to see cows, horses, or sheep in France in Geoguessr. If that ever happens, you should consider the West of the country (Brittany, Normandy), as well as the mountainous regions (Pyrenees and Alps). This is where you have the most chances to find animals in France in Google Street View.

metas.name: France - Agriculture - Corn
metas.description: Corn fields are mostly located in the Western part of the country, as well as in some areas in the East of Paris, and around Lyon and Strasbourg.

metas.name: France - Agriculture - Lavender Fields
metas.description: Lavender fields can be found in the southeast, appearing as small grey bushes when not fully grown.

metas.name: France - Agriculture - Salt Farms
metas.description: Salt farms, which appear as flooded trenches with grass medians, are unique to the west coastal islands of Ãle de RÃ© and Ãle d'OlÃ©ron as well as the nearby coast, as well as some very niche areas in the South of France (Camargue).

metas.name: France - Agriculture - Sunflower
metas.description: Sunflowers are mostly found in the southwest of the country, particularly around Toulouse.

metas.name: France - Agriculture - Wine
metas.description: France is the second largest wine producer in the world, with many famed wine regions. The most common include the area around Bordeaux, southern coast and Champagne, East of Paris. Other regions include, but are not limited to, Loire Valley, Alsace and Corsica.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Alpine Architecture
metas.description: Alpine architecture, unmistakable for its light coloured base and extensive wooden elements, is unsurprisingly found in the Alps.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Similar houses can be found in the touristic parts of Pyrenees.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Basque Architecture
metas.description: White houses with, often colourful, timber framing are a staple of Basque architecture that extends beyond the Basque speaking area. The timber frame colour (in this case red) will be consistent with other wooden elements, like window shutters and gates.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Theyâre also common in parts of Northern Spain, where the timber frames are usually unpainted.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Belle-Ãle-en-Mer Architecture
metas.description: On the Breton island Belle-Ãle-en-Mer you can find houses typical for Brittany combined with colourful faÃ§ades and outlines, superficially similar to houses in Portugal.
metas.comparison: NOTE: The entire island was only covered with an often oversaturated Generation 2 camera.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Black Shingle Roof
metas.description: Black shingle roofs are primarily found in the northwest, the rough cutoff being the Loire river. Other areas include near the Belgian border, the south-centre, and the Pyrenees, making black roofs a good clue for Alps-Pyrenees toss-ups.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Black Shingle Roofs with Mountains
metas.meta_label: Architecture - Black Shingle Roofs with Mountains
metas.description: Black shingle roofs are often found in the Pyrenees, making black roofs a good clue for Alps-Pyrenees toss-ups.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Brick House / Black Roof
metas.description: Found in the North (mostly Belgium border)
metas.comparison: Note by MB: Brick Houses also often have Red Roofs. Houses with Black Roofs do not appear around Toulouse (unlike those with red roofs). What I find more useful to differentiate the roof types is the materials. "Black Roofs" are shingles, while "Red Roofs" are actual tiles (which can also get very dark)

metas.name: France - Architecture - Brick House / Red Rooftiles
metas.description: Brick roofs with red rooftiles can be found in the North mostly. Sometimes, they're also found around Toulouse.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: With red tiles, Toulouse is an option, with black shingles, it isn't. What I find more useful to differentiate the roof types is the materials. "Black Roofs" are shingles, while "Red Roofs" are actual tiles (which can also get very dark)

metas.name: France - Architecture - Brittany Architecture
metas.description: Brittany has one of the most recognizable and consistent architectures in the country. Common elements include, in addition to black roofs, edge chimneys, black slate walls and stones surrounding doors and windows. The walls will be either very light coloured or made of stone.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Germanic Architecture
metas.description: Many elements of Germanic architecture are concentrated in Alsace, such as timber framing and half-hip roof. Furthermore, roofs with fish scale tiles are more common in this region.
metas.comparison: Beware that these elements are sometimes incorporated into architecture in other parts of France, and are most reliable in conjunction with one another.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Ile de France Architecture
metas.description: Walls made of uneven cream coloured to orange stones, glued with mortar and often incorporating red brick details can be found in the towns surrounding Paris. Note that the city of Paris itself generally does not have this architecture.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Mansard Roof
metas.description: Mansard roofs, also known as French windows, are a very common feature of Parisian architecture. Theyâre made up of steep black shingle roofs with inserted dormer windows. While not unique to Paris, it is a good clue in abundance and on wide boulevards.
metas.comparison: On some occasions, they can also be found in the North of France.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Old Toulouse Architecture
metas.description: In and around Toulouse, mainly in old towns, you will commonly find bright orange brick buildings. They differ from brick houses near Belgium by the bricks being brighter, as well as somewhat Mediterranean looking architectural features, such as wooden shutters, being common.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Stone House / Black Shingle Roof
metas.meta_label: Architecture - Stone House / Black Shingle Roof
metas.description: Found in Western France, mainly in Bretagne.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: What I find more useful to differentiate the roof types is the materials. "Black Roofs" are shingles, while "Red Roofs" are actual tiles (which can also get very dark)

metas.name: France - Architecture - Stone House / Red Rooftiles
metas.description: Can be found all over France, but mainly central and southern.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: What I find more useful to differentiate the roof types is the materials. "Black Roofs" are shingles, while "Red Roofs" are actual tiles (which can also get very dark)

metas.name: France - Architecture - U-Tiles
metas.description: Roofs in the south of the country will often be made up of rounded tiles overlapping one another, often varying in colour.

metas.name: France - Architecture - West Coast Architecture
metas.description: The houses along the West Coast, from Nantes to Bayonne are usually low, with white walls, and red roofs.

metas.name: France - Car Meta - Rare Antenna - Black & White
metas.meta_label: Car Meta - Rare Antenna - Black & White
metas.description: On rare occasions, you may find a flag attached to the antenna in the generation 3 coverage. While much of the highlighted areas has been overwritten, learning the distribution of each antenna can yield very high scores.
metas.comparison: The black/white flag can be found in Calvados, Orne, Eastern Bourgogne and Loire/Haut de Loire

metas.name: France - Car Meta - Rare Antenna - Blue
metas.description: On rare occasions, you may find a flag attached to the antenna in the generation 3 coverage. While much of the highlighted areas has been overwritten, learning the distribution of each antenna can yield very high scores.
metas.comparison: The blue flag can be found in Bas-Rhin, Aube and the Correze/Haute-Vienne/Dordogne Tristate

metas.name: France - Car Meta - Rare Antenna - Red
metas.description: On rare occasions, you may find a flag attached to the antenna in the generation 3 coverage. While much of the highlighted areas has been overwritten, learning the distribution of each antenna can yield very high scores.
metas.comparison: The red flag can be found in the eastern part of the Nord-Department

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Azure Blue Signpost
metas.description: On the French Riviera (CÃ´te d'Azur in French, literally translated as Blue Coast), you can find regular traffic signposts painted azure blue. Uniquely, Cagnes-sur-mer, west of Nice, will feature lighter, powder blue infrastructure.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Blue infrastructure can be found to a lesser extent all across France, particularly Brittany, so consider the landscape as well.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Bordeaux Signpost
metas.description: In the outskirts of Bordeaux, you may find square traffic signposts with the Bordeaux shade of red, named after the wine grown in the region.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Red posts by themselves are not unique to Bordeaux, so apply this meta with caution.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Bordeaux Streetsign
metas.description: Small tables with 'Arráµ' written on a small separate sign, are found in Bordeaux, despite being a city not divided into arrondissements.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Brown Signback
metas.description: Road signs where both the post and back are painted brown are most commonly found in Seine-et-Marne, and rarely in Ille-et-Vilaine. It is more reliable when the post is square, however round signposts are equally common.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Beware that this, and other colored infrastructure can rarely be found in other parts of the country.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Cityname Roadsign
metas.description: Street signs in the metropolitan area of Paris often say the name of the city, which is generally atypical for street signs in France. The signs will often be made in a modern design, and many city names will be river based, notably named after Seine and Marne.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This can be seen sporadically throughout the country, so consider other clues.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Cuboid Barrier
metas.description: Cuboid barriers made of stones and mortar are commonly found on Corsica. While by no means unique to Corsica, it is good to consider the island when you see them in rounds with a plausible Mediterranean landscape.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Stone barriers with a rounded top are not found on Corsica.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Dark Green Signpost
metas.description: Dark green road signposts and backs are most commonly found in Brittany and around Paris, but also various southern regions in the country.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Beware that this, and other colored infrastructure can rarely be found in other parts of the country.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Eure-et-Loir Sticker
metas.description: Signbacks in Eure-et-Loir may include a green sticker, the departmentâs logo. Theyâre usually placed on a dark green back, without a matching post.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Grey Signback / Green Signpost
metas.description: A greyish green signback supported by a darker green post, is found in three areas: Brittany (CÃ´tes-d'Armor and eastern half of Ille-et-Vilaine), PyrÃ©nÃ©es-Atlantiques and rarely near the Alps.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Beware that this, and other colored infrastructure can rarely be found in other parts of the country.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Lille Streetsign
metas.description: Street signs with a red slanted fleur-de-lis are unique to Lille.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Lyon Streetsign
metas.description: Lyonâs street signs feature four corner bolts and an uninterrupted inner white border that cuts a notch for the arrondissement and each bolt.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Outside Lyon proper, the street sign will display the name of the suburb instead.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Marseille Streetsign
metas.description: Marseilleâs street signs will usually feature the cityâs emblem, a variation of the Greek cross. The white border will usually be interrupted at the top, even when the cross is absent.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Montpellier Streetsign
metas.description: Montpellier street signs will typically contain a blue âMâ on a white background in the top left corner.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Paris Streetsign
metas.description: Paris uses an iconic green & Prussian blue design with a top arch that has also been replicated in Bucharest, which is sometimes referred to as Paris of the east.
metas.comparison: NOTE: The simple rectangular form of the sign can be found in the towns nearby and rarely in other cities.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Pas-de-Calais Sign
metas.description: In the Pas-de-Calais department, you may find road signs with the following colour arrangement: a dark green post paired with a signback of a lighter shade of green, ranging from matcha green to greenish turquoise. The departmentâs logo, a green and blue triangle, is occasionally present on the signback.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Under certain lighting, they can appear similar to the greyish road signs. Also, beware that this, and other colored infrastructure can rarely be found in other parts of the country.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Powder Blue Infrastructure
metas.description: Uniquely, Cagnes-sur-mer, west of Nice, will feature lighter, powder blue infrastructure.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Reddish Road
metas.description: Roads with a significant red, purple or burgundy tint are most commonly found in an area between Paris and Dijon, with Normandy being a notable exception. The historical region of Burgundy, which gave the name to the shade of red, roughly corresponds to the highlighted area.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Normal roads may deceptively look reddish under some lighting, so use this with caution.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Thin B-Type Guardrail
metas.description: Thin B type guardrail, typical for Czechia and Slovakia, is sometimes found on highways in the northern half of the country, often coming from Le Mans, Tours, Paris, Reims and Metz.
metas.comparison: NOTE: On the highlighted sections, thin B can be the minority guardrail, and short sections of any highway will have no guardrails at all. It is also more common on smaller roads in the North, but less consistent as a clue.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Wind Turbine
metas.description: Wind turbines are considerably more common in the north of the country.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Yellow Front License Plates
metas.description: France can sometimes have yellow back license plates, especially in old coverage. Should you see several yellow plates on the front, you're probably near Luxembourg.

metas.name: France - Landscape - British Hedges
metas.description: Rural roads surrounded by hedges blocking the view, reminiscent of the British Isles, are primarily found in the northwest, particularly in Normandy.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Hedges by themselves are not sufficient for recognizing this area and are common all over France.

metas.name: France - Landscape - Cote d'Azur
metas.description: The French Riviera (Cote d'Azur) will mirror many characteristics of Monaco. Rich areas with planted palms and light coloured multi story buildings with wide balconies are good indications youâre in this area, with the rest of the southern coast and Corsican Bastia sharing similar vibes.

metas.name: France - Landscape - La Beauce
metas.description: La Beauce is one of the flattest regions of France, located South of Paris.
metas.comparison:
Apart from the flatness of the area, the important thing to notice about the fields in the Beauce region is that they are industrialized. You will not see hedges around the fields like you could see in the West of France.
So, if you see very flat and industrialized fields with potatoes or cereals, you can be in this area. Still, the Paris hedge remains good because there are many fields North and East of Paris (but you will never get a 5K by guessing Paris out of fields).

metas.name: France - Landscape - Mountains
metas.description: The tallest mountains are found in the southeast and on the Spanish border.

metas.name: France - Language - Alsatian
metas.description: Alsatian, a dialect of German, is occasionally found in Alsace, a region that changed countries 4 times in modern history. Most bilingual street signs use some variation of gasse or strasse.

metas.name: France - Language - Basque
metas.description: Bilingual signs in Basque, a language isolate, are concentrated In the western half of the PyrÃ©nÃ©es-Atlantiques department, bordering the Basque speaking regions in Spain. Common letters include K, X and Z. On directional signs, itâs written with a thinner font, which is unique within all minority languages in France.
metas.comparison: The word for street is karrika, in contrast to âkaleaâ in the Spanish Basque country.

metas.name: France - Language - Breton
metas.description: Breton is a Celtic language, visually most similar to Welsh. Common letters include d, k, w and the letter Ã±, which is not found in French. It is commonly found on the Breton peninsula, with bilingual street signs as east as Rennes and rarely Nantes. The Breton word for street is straed.

metas.name: France - Language - Catalan
metas.description: The far southern department PyrÃ©nÃ©es-Orientales, also known as Catalunya Nord (Northern Catalonia), uses Catalan on their various signage.
metas.comparison: It is closely related to both Spanish and French, with Ã being considerably more common than in French. The word for street is carrer.

metas.name: France - Language - Corsican
metas.description: On the island of Corsica, you may find bilingual signs in Corsican, a Romance language that utilises many features found in Italian, like words almost always ending in vowels. In particular, the endings u/iu/ju, changed from o/io, are common in Corsican. Moreover, placenames will usually have an Italian origin.

metas.name: France - Language - German Roadnames
metas.description: Streets containing German names are concentrated in Alsace.

metas.name: France - Language - Occitan
metas.description: Occitan is a Romance language closely related to Catalan thatâs sparsely concentrated in the South of France, most often found on street signs in big cities, and very rarely on town entry signs. It can be divided into dialects, each using a slightly different word for street, all similar to Catalan âcarrerâ. For example, in Toulouse, youâll find the Languedocian carriÃ¨ra and in Avignon carriero, in the ProvenÃ§al dialect

metas.name: France - Language - Occitan - Carriera
metas.description: Different dialects of Occitan use different words for 'road'. Carriera can be found in South Central France.

metas.name: France - Language - Occitan - Carriero

metas.name: France - Language - Water Town Name
metas.description: Many French cities contain the name of the river they lay on, usually in the format -sur-[river]. On signage, sur are often shortened to Ë¢/, in this case Chalonnes-sur-Loire (Chalonnes upon Loire). The picture shows five of the longest and therefore most common origins of river based names, but cities can bear the name of any river, regardless of length.
metas.comparison: Similarly, city names containing -sur-mer (=on sea) or -plage (=beach) are found exclusively on the coast.

metas.name: France - Trekker - Boat Trekker
metas.description: Several cities along the Cote d'Azur host boat trekkers in their harbours.

metas.name: France - Vegetation - Maritime Pine Forest
metas.description: Forests made up entirely of Maritime pines (pinus pinaster) are found in the southwest of the country (Gironde and Landes departments). The whole area will be fairly flat, which is not typical of other areas with such pines.

metas.name: France - Vegetation - Meditteranean Vegetation
metas.description: The vegetation near the South-East coast looks very Mediterranean.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: This is more of a vibe thing tbh.

metas.name: France - Vegetation - Stone Pine
metas.description: Stone pines are commonly found along the southern coast, often planted alongside urban roads. You may however find them as north as Nantes.

metas.name: Germany - Agriculture - Hop
metas.description: Hop fields are mainly found between Ingolstadt and Landshut - an area called 'Hallertau/Holledau' in Bavaria. There are some minor regions in Thuringia, Saxony-Anhalt and Saxony as well.

metas.name: Germany - Agriculture - Vineyards
metas.description: There are 13 wine regions in Germany. They are mostly concentrated in the southwest of Germany. However, there are a couple regions further east as well, along the border between Thuringia and Saxony-Anhalt, as well as along the Elbe in Saxony.

metas.name: Germany - Architecture - Arches in Half-Timbered houses
metas.description: This type of half-timbered house with arches at the ground floor is very common in this region of Saxony.

metas.name: Germany - Architecture - Commie Blocks
metas.description: These large, utilitarian apartment buildings constructed during the socialist era, that are also known as 'Commie blocks' are common in all of former East Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Architecture - Fishscale Walls
metas.description: Houses with black slate walls, resembling fish scales, are commonly found in a large area of central Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Architecture - Frisian Architecture
metas.description: Thatched roofs and rock walls are most common on the North Frisian Islands, as well as mainland Schleswig-Holstein. You can also commonly find them in coastal resort towns in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.

metas.name: Germany - Architecture - Red Brick
metas.description: These brick houses are generally concentrated in northwestern Germany.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This map is very approximate.

metas.name: Germany - Camera Meta - Low Cam
metas.description: Lowcam coverage can be found around Singen and near Switzerland.

metas.name: Germany - Car Meta - Gen 3 / Antenna
metas.description: This rare Generation 3 car coverage with an antenna can be found in central Hamburg (Speicherstadt). Note by MB: This is officially a trekker, so you won't find any copyright.

metas.name: Germany - Car Meta - Gen 3 Black Car
metas.description: You can find a Generation 3 black car in this safari park southeast of Bielefeld.
metas.comparison: You can commonly see 4x4s painted with a zebra pattern in the park. NOTE: This car is unique to this park within all of Europe.

metas.name: Germany - Car Meta - White/Black Gen 4 Car
metas.description: You can find this rare white and black Generation 4 car in Hamburg and around Frankfurt.
metas.comparison: NOTE: You can also find the same car around London and in Ireland.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - ALDI SÃ¼d

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Black Disk Bollard
metas.description: Bollards standing on these black disks are commonly found in all of eastern Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Bus Stop - Berlin
metas.description: Berlin uses segmented bus stops, with a yellow signpost.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Bus Stop - Bremen
metas.description: Bremen proper uses simple bus stops, which have the bus stop name within a red section. The edges can be rounded.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Bus Stop - Bremerhaven
metas.description: Bremerhaven, which is still part of Bremen, uses bus stops with a grey section on the opposite side of the signpost. And the bus stop name is red within a yellow section.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Bus Stop - Hamburg
metas.description: Hamburg bus stops have a red signpost, and the route numbers are within hexagons. Note that they can be found outside of Hamburg as well

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Capped Bollard
metas.description: Some bollards in North Rhine-Westphalia have a green bit at the top. The top can also be another colour.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Cologne Lamppost Plate
metas.description: Lampposts in Cologne will often feature these bright yellow numbers on a black piece of plastic.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Similar looking things can be found elsewhere as well.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Curved Poletop
metas.description: Pole tops which have a curved horizontal bar can be found in Bavaria, though they are rare.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Dark Reflector
metas.description: Bollards with darker reflectors than usual are commonly found in Schleswig-Holstein, Niedersachsen, Nordrhein-Westfalen, Bavaria. They can sometimes be found in Baden-WÃ¼rttemberg and rarely in Hesse.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Folded Sign
metas.description: Folded Signs are most common in Bremen, then Saxony-Anhalt and Saarland.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Lower Saxony km Marker
metas.description: You can find these simple rectangular markers, with rounded edges in Lower Saxony.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - LVR Cap
metas.description: Some of the green caps will have the text âLVRâ, along with a small coat of arms. These specific green caps are unique to southern North Rhine-Westphalia.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Metal Border km Marker - Lower Saxony

metas.description: These markers with a metallic border around the marker itself are found in Schleswig-Holstein and Lower Saxony. The numbers after the comma are usually smaller on the markers in Lower Saxony.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Metal Border km Marker - Schleswig-Holstein

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - No-Fold Signback

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Orange Bollard Plate
metas.description: Rhineland-Palatinate is the only state where the plates on the bollards are orange instead of white.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Orange Posts
metas.description: These simple orange posts are most commonly found in Bavaria, and also in the other highlighted states.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Red Bicycle Sign
metas.description: Red bicycle signs can be found in Northrhine-Westphalia, Southern Lower Saxony and Hamburg.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Red Cap Bollard
metas.description: These white posts with a red cap are found in all of former East Germany, but most commonly in the state of Saxony-Anhalt.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Round Concrete Poles

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Saarland Bicycle Sign

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Schleswig-Holstein Bicycle Sign

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Darmstadt

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Dortmund
metas.description: Dortmund uses blue signs with a white border and a grey frame. The signs also have a separate section for numbers under the street name.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Dresden
metas.description: Dresden has blue signs with a unique font.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - DÃ¼sseldorf

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Essen

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Hanover
metas.description: Hanover uses white signs with a wider than usual gap between the sign and metallic frame.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Mainz
metas.description: Mainz has a mix of blue signs, and this unique red variant.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Munich
metas.description: Munich has blue street signs with a white decorative border that does not touch the corners. Also note the unique font.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Nuremberg
metas.description: Nuremberg has blue signs with a unique font. The signs also have a grey frame with a small gap between it and the sign.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Stuttgart
metas.description: Stuttgart uses black signs without a border.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Wuppertal
metas.description: Wuppertal uses white signs with a unique font and a white painted frame with a small gap between it and the sign.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - T-Signback

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Triangle Poletop

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Triangle Post - Grey

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Triangle Post - North Rhine-Westphalia
