metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Trident Poles
metas.description: These trident-like pole tops can be found in Bavaria, Saxony-Anhalt, and Baden-WÃ¼rttemberg.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Type A Guardrail

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Type B Guardrail

metas.comparison: NOTE: Sometimes there is only 1 plate, which can make it hard to tell apart from a Brandenburg post.

metas.name: Germany - Landscape - Alps
metas.description: The German Alps is the most mountainous region in Germany, it is mostly concentrated on the Austrian Border.

metas.name: Germany - Landscape - Flat Landscape
metas.description: The North and especially Northwest of Germany is very flat.

metas.name: Germany - Landscape - Hilliness
metas.description: Central Germany is hilly.

metas.name: Germany - Landscape - Regensburg Plains & Ridge
metas.description: The flat plains southeast of Regensburg can be recognised by the slight ridge often visible to the northeast. The plains themselves are flat, and quite agricultural.

metas.name: Germany - Landscape - Sylt
metas.description: The shrub and sand covered hills are unique to the island of Sylt. And like the rest of the North Frisian Islands, rock walls, brick houses, and thatched roofs are common.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Some parts of Sylt look more generic, but still very flat.

metas.name: Germany - Language - Sorbian
metas.description: Sorbian, a Slavic language, is spoken near the Polish and Czech border. You can find it on a variety of signs in this region between Cottbus and Bautzen.

metas.name: Germany - Language - Town Suffix: -weiler

metas.name: Germany - Vegetation - Baltic Pines
metas.description: Baltic Pines or Pinus sylvestris are generally more concentrated in the northeast of Germany. They can be recognized by their orange-tinged trunk.

metas.name: Hawaii - Agriculture - Eucalyptus Plantation

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Central Maui
metas.description: The Island of Maui sits southeast of MolokaÊ»i. In the centre of the island, you will find somewhat flat grasslands. It has the very recognizable West Maui Mountains to the west, and Haleakala to the east.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Coastal Big Island
metas.description: The coastal areas of the island of Hawaiâi are where most of the towns and built-up areas on the island are located. These areas are typically more lush and have more trees and fern plants than the interior.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: There is a similar road, the Hana Highway on Maui, which is more narrow and has narrower shoulders than the typical road on Hawai'i.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Coastal Lana'i
metas.description: Towards the coasts of the island of LÄnaÊ»i, hills dotted with dry grass and shrubby vegetation are commonly seen. These areas are very rural with few buildings.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Coastal Maui
metas.description: Coastal areas of Maui are noticeably lush and green. Banana plants, palm trees, and views of the mountains are all common.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - East Molokai Volcano
metas.description: Rather flat and wide volcano, making it's shape quite unique.
metas.comparison: As the name suggests, it's found in the East of Moloka'i island.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Flat Forest
metas.description: Rural roads going through forests within a flat landscape are commonly found south of the city of Hilo, on the island of HawaiÊ»i.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Haleakala Foothills
metas.description: The area near Kula is at the foot of Haleakala and often looks over the rest of the island.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Hana Highway (North)
metas.description: The Hana Highway runs along the coast of Maui and is narrow and lush in the North.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: Note that unlike in the picture, Hana Highway also has center lines on some parts. That creates a possible toss-up with Hawai'i island. However, Hana Highway is more narrow and has very narrow shoulders, unlike most roads on Hawai'i.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Hana Highway (South)
metas.description: The Hana Highway runs along the coast of Maui and is narrow. In the south, the landscape is fairly open and you can often see the southern coast, as no trees are in the way.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: Note that unlike in the picture, Hana Highway also has center lines on some parts. That creates a possible toss-up with Hawai'i island. However, Hana Highway is more narrow and has very narrow shoulders, unlike most roads on Hawai'i.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Hawaiian Lattice
metas.description: The infamous 'Hawaiian lattice' can be recognized by the volcanic soil and rocks that are abundant in the region. Volcanic vegetation can also be seen lining the roads. Note that the angle of the roads is a big clue for the area, and that this lattice was built on the slope of Mauna Loa.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Hilo
metas.description: Hilo fits nicely into the coastal Hawai'i landscape (lush and somewhat built up). What makes it unique is the grid format of many of its roads. You can also sometimes see Mauna Kea in the west.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: Other grids also exist on Hawaii island (notably Hawaiian Lattice, and the area south of Hilo), but they look very different. Each has their own meta describing them.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Honolulu
metas.description: Honolulu, located on southern OÊ»ahu, is by far the largest city and urban area in Hawaii. If you are in a dense urban area and can see tall buildings, you will always be in or near Honolulu.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Houses on Hills
metas.description: In most of Hawaii, houses are built on flat plains. If you see Houses on hillsides, you are most likely around the Ko'olau range in eastern Oahu, often in suburbs of Honolulu.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Hualalai
metas.description: Hualalaei (a large mountain) rises to the east of Kona.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Interior Big Island
metas.description: The Island of Hawaiâi (also referred to as The Big Island) is both the largest and farthest southeast island with Street View coverage in the state. The interior areas feature rolling, grassy plains and volcanic rocks. You can typically see one or more of the islandâs volcanoes from the road.
metas.comparison: What sets apart the mountains on this island is that they are more sloping and gradual than on other islands.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Kauai
metas.description: The Island of Kauai is the furthest west island in Hawaii with official Google coverage. This island has deep red soil and has large rugged hills with lush, jungle-like vegetation. This island also has exclusively Generation 3 and Smallcam coverage.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Other islands such as Maui and MolokaÊ»i have similar soil colours, but the hillsides on them will typically have less dense vegetation.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Kaunakakai
metas.description: The town of Kaunakakai is the largest settlement on the Island of MolokaÊ»i. It is the only area on the island with an âurbanâ vibe.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Lana'i
metas.description: The Island of LÄnaÊ»i is a small, yet distinct island that lies just south of Molokaâi. A volcano is found just east of the centre of the island, adjacent to the town of LÄnaÊ»i. In this area, tall Cook pines are abundant. In addition, some main roads near the centre of the island are lined with younger Cook pines.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Maui West Coast
metas.description: West Maui can often see Molokai and/or Lanai to the west. The northern part of the west coast has the West Maui Mountains rising to the east.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Mauna Loa Observatory Road
metas.description: This road "looks like Mars", and has large volcanic rocks on its sides.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: Unlike the road on Red Hill, this road does not have center lines.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Moloka'i
metas.description: The Island of MolokaÊ»i is just southeast of the Island of OÊ»ahu. This island features deep red soil, dry-looking vegetation, and a prominent volcano on the eastern end of the island. MolokaÊ»i is also very sparsely populated. This island only has Generation 3 and Smallcam coverage.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: In the newest smallcam coverage, the island doesn't look as dry as in Gen 3 (due to different season).

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - O'ahu
metas.description: The Island of OÊ»ahu lies southeast of Kauai. It is known for being home to the Honolulu urban area. It also is home to steep, lush hills, which can be commonly seen from all around the island, especially in Honoluluâs suburbs. Generation 4 coverage is common on OÊ»ahu.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Red Hill
metas.description: The Red Hill can easily be recognised by this unique barren, rocky landscape. Due to the high altitude, clouds are usually visible below you.
metas.comparison:
Note by MB: In newer smallcam coverage the hill looks not that red, but the coverage is still recognizable.
Also, unlike the Mauna Lea observatory road on Hawai'i, this road has yellow center lines.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Seaview Road
metas.description: The road around and east of Seaview (Hawai'i island) is very distinct, as it combines the volcanic rock landscape with water immediately to the South.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Volcanic Rock
metas.description: Hawaii island has the only currently active volcano and is the most recently formed island, so lots of volcanic rock is common.

metas.name: Hawaii - Misc - North-West Road Angle
metas.description: A weirdly good meta for the Kona area (western Hawai'i) is roads that are angled SE-NW.

metas.name: Hawaii - Misc - Oahu Area Codes
metas.description: Signs on Oahu (and sometimes other places) often have a 2-digit number followed by a dash. These correspond to different tax zones.
metas.comparison: They are not used in urban Honolulu. They start with 41 at the east coast, and increase counter-clockwise along the coast.

metas.name: Iceland - Car Meta - Red Truck
metas.description: Iceland can be split in half depending on the colour of the pickup truck, with red being found in the southwest, and white being found in the northeast.
metas.comparison: The Red Truck is found between Sudurland and Vesturland

metas.name: Iceland - Car Meta - White Truck
metas.description: Iceland can be split in half depending on the colour of the pickup truck, with red being found in the southwest, and white being found in the northeast.

metas.name: Iceland - Infrastructure - Divided Highway
metas.description: The 41 and 43 southwest of ReykjavÃ­k, as well as the 1 between Grundarhverfi and Selfoss are divided.

metas.name: Iceland - Infrastructure - Multi Lane Highway
metas.description: Both sides of the HvalfjÃ¶rdur Tunnel have multiple lanes for one driving direction.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Akureyri
metas.description: Akureyri is the second-biggest city in Iceland and is located in a North-South oriented valley, along the western edge of the bay. The city features mountains ranges to the east and west, making it recognisable.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Akureyri Mountains
metas.description: The mountains west of Akureyri contain many valleys, sandwiched between tall, often slightly snowcapped peaks. Most of these valleys generally face north to northeast.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - EiÃ°ar Valley
metas.description: The wide valley around EiÃ°ar is slightly hilly and agricultural, with tall, snowy peaks visible in the distance on either side, to the east and northwest, respectively.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Flat-Topped Mountains
metas.description: The Westfjords region features numerous narrow fjords, surrounded by moderately tall, and mostly flat-topped mountains.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Fog
metas.description: Very foggy coverage can be found around the town of BakkagerÃ°i, in northeastern Iceland. The fog can also be seen from a distance.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Glaciers
metas.description: The southern coast of Iceland features some impressive glaciers visible from the ring road, spilling into the sea from the VatnajÃ¶kull ice cap.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - HallormsstaÃ°ur Valley
metas.description: The valley around HallormsstaÃ°ur has a distinct northeast/southwest angle with low-lying mountains on either side, a wide river flowing through it, and an unusual amount of trees for Iceland. Some of the sideroads are in the forests.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Heimaey
metas.description: The Island of Heimaey can easily be recognised by seeing these ragged rocky cliffs overlooking the town of VestmannaeyjabÃ¦r. Similar cliffs can be seen on the islands off the coast.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Inland Iceland
metas.description: Barren landscapes consisting mostly of dark volcanic gravel, with little to no vegetation or signs of life, are typical of the inland regions of Iceland. Most such covered roads are located in the east.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Large Jagged Mountains
metas.description: The far east of the country is also home to several fjords. What distinguishes them from the Westfjords are the generally larger and more jagged mountains.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - ReykjavÃ­k
metas.description: ReykjavÃ­k is the capital and by far the largest city in Iceland. The city is mostly flat with slight hills, and is located on the south side of a bay. It is most recognizable as it is significantly larger than other Icelandic cities, with a large urban area and âbigger cityâ feel.
metas.comparison: NOTE: The city of Akureyri can feel urban in some places. You can distinguish it from Reykjavik as it has mountains to the east and west.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Selfoss Mountain
metas.description: You can recognise the area near the town of Selfoss from its distinct flat-ridge mountain. Due to the otherwise flat landscape, this mountain can be seen from a wide area.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Southwest Farmland
metas.description: The Southwest agricultural area in Iceland can be identified by its relatively flat farmland landscape scattered with numerous farmsteads, fields, meadows and grasslands.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Although there are other smaller agricultural areas in Iceland, mountains in this area tend to be quite distant, making it unique.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Assam - Corn
metas.description: Within Assam, you can find corn between Guwahati and Nagaon, south of the river.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Assam - Sugarcane
metas.description: Within Assam, sugarcane is mainly found around Lanka

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Bihar - Tea
metas.description: Within Bihar, tea plantations can be found in the far Northeast.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Canola
metas.description: Canola is mostly found in and around Rajasthan.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Cotton
metas.description: Cotton is commonly found in the western parts of India, particularly in Gujarat and Maharashtra.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Grape
metas.description: Maharashtra is by far the state with the highest grape production in India.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Madhya Pradesh - Sugarcane
metas.description: Within Madhya Pradesh, sugar cane can commonly be found southwest and northeast of the Satpura National Park.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Maharashtra - Cotton
metas.description: Cotton (within) is mostly found around Nanded, more generally in the middle/eastern part of Maharashtra.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: Very unreliable in my experience

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Maharashtra - Sugarcane
metas.description: Sugarcane in Maharashtra is mostly central from what I saw.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Oil Palm
metas.description: Oil palm plantations are almost exclusive to Andhra Pradesh and are mostly located around Eluru.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Pineapple
metas.description: Pineapple is very uncommon in India, but if you see it, it's in Bihar in the corridor between Nepal and Bangladesh.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.description: Sugarcane is most commonly found in the north in and around Uttar Pradesh, and in the southwest.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Sugarcane - Tamil Nadu
metas.description: Sugar cane can be found in several areas, the two main ones being near Erode and Thiruvanamalai.
metas.comparison: It is also findable in smaller areas between those two big areas, but it is still mainly a northern Tamil Nadu thing.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Tea - Assam
metas.description: Within Assam, Tea is mostly planted in the eastern and in the southern regions. There are also some patches in Western Assam.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Tea - Tamil Nadu
metas.description: Tea plantations in India are mostly located in the northeast and in Kerala, but it spills in one particular area in Tamil Nadu northwest of Coimbatore

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Tea - Tripura
metas.description: Within Tripura, Tea is found along the Bangladeshi border, and along the Assamese border.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Tea - West Bengal
metas.description: Within West Bengal, tea plantations are found near the northern border to Bhutan.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Tea Plantation
metas.description: Tea plantations can be found in the northeast and the far south.
metas.comparison: NOTE: If you find tea plantations in a flat area, you are likely in Assam or northeastern West Bengal, near the Assam border.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Telangana - Cotton
metas.description: Cotton fields in Telangana are logically next to the big area that produces the most of it in Maharashtra, so it is gonna be found mostly north-west of the state. You can click in Nizamabad for a good score.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: In my experience, it's more common North of Nizamabad.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Andhra Pradesh - Thatched Roofs
metas.description: Within Andhra Pradesh, thatched roofs can commonly be found in three places.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Assam - Thatched Roofs
metas.description: Within Assam, you can find thatched roofs all the way north east in the state.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Assam - Woven Walls
metas.description: In Assam, you can find houses with woven walls along the border to Arunachal Pradesh, north of Tinsukia.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Bihar - Tin Hip Roof
metas.description: If you see these hip roofs made out of tin - which are usually found in West Bengal - in Bihar, you're in the Northeastern Quarter of Bihar.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Bihar - Wide W Tiles
metas.description: Within Bihar, you can find regular Wide W Tiles around Katihar.
metas.comparison: Reminder: This type of tile is like a larger kind of W tile. Another way to tell it apart is the small pike in the middle of the tile.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Blue Walls & Tiles
metas.description: Houses with tiled roofs and blue painted walls are very common in Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh, a little less in Madhya Pradesh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Brick Kiln
metas.description: In poorer parts of the Ganges Valley it is common for villages to construct their own large chimneys to fire clay into bricks. These can be seen from far away and are a good clue for the Ganges Valley specifically, especially UP and Bihar. Note that they are also fairly common in the poorer eastern parts of Tamil Nadu.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Clay House
metas.description: Houses made out of clay are most common in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand. There's some spill in far southwestern Bihar.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Clay House
metas.description: Clay houses exist a lot in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, and some spill can be seen in southwestern Bihar.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Clay Huts
metas.description: White painted clay huts are found in northwestern Bihar, northwest of Muzaffapur.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Colorful Walls
metas.description: Houses with colorful, particularly blue painted walls, can be found in the areas around Eastern Madhya, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Corrugated Hip Roof
metas.description: Large hip roofs made of corrugated sheet metal are found in West Bengal and adjacent areas in Bihar and Odisha.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Dravidian Temple
metas.description: - Shorter and "pyramidal" towers (Vimana) - most easily recognizable
metas.comparison: Found in the South of India.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Dumka House
metas.description: Houses between Dumka and Pakur have long tiled roofs and walls are painted in two colors (green/blue with an orange/brown color at the bottom

metas.name: India - Architecture - Elevated Bengali Roof
metas.description:
Found mostly in the main, southern part of West Bengal, but more in the west.
Sometimes also found in Bihar at the border to eastern Nepal.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: This meta is not sufficiently researched, but it's still good to know

metas.name: India - Architecture - Flat Gooner (actually Guna) Tiles
metas.description: Flat Guna tiles is just a tiled roof full of staple-shaped tiles. It can be found around Prayagraj, south east of the state.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Flat Tiles
metas.description: Flat tiles seem to be the worst type of tile by their appearance. They are mainly found in Madhya Pradesh and southern Uttar pradesh.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Gooner (actually Guna) Tiles
metas.description: It has a âUâ shape but there is a flatter shaped tile connecting tiles to each other.
metas.comparison: Itâs very common in southeastern Uttar Pradesh, western Bihar and rarely in northeastern Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Green House
metas.description: Houses in Odisha are often painted green.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Hay Hut
metas.description: These huts that are made entirely out of hay, and have thatched roofs are found in Southwestern Bihar, mainly between Patna and Gaya.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Jammu Architecture
metas.description: Jammu looks like a fairly developed state compared to most places in India. The architecture looks richer and overall way nicer. Punjab has a similar architecture.
metas.comparison: 50/50 Tip ! It can be hard to differentiate Punjab and Jammu in urban rounds due to the similarity of their architecture. If you see rich looking houses, look at the car to know whether you are in Punjab or in Jammu. If you donât see one of the two Jammu cars (boxy with top right thread or central strap, see image 3&4), click Punjab. Note by MB: This 50/50 tip is not 100% reliable, so look at other clues (like Punjabi language) too.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Jharkhand - Wide W Tiles
metas.description: In the eastern parts of Jharkhand, you can find some West Bengal wide W tiles spill

metas.name: India - Architecture - Madhya Pradesh - Flat Tiles
metas.description: Flat tiles can be spotted in random places in Madhya Pradesh, but mainly around Guna, Chhatarpur and Sagar in the center of the state.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Madhya Pradesh - Slate Roofs
metas.description: Slate roofs in Madhya Pradesh can be found west of Sagar

metas.name: India - Architecture - Madhya Pradesh - U Tiles
metas.description: U tiles are more common in the eastern half of Madhya Pradesh.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Madhya Pradesh - W Tiles
metas.description: W tiles are quite rare in Madhya Pradesh but can still be seen west of Jabalpur and south of Guna

metas.name: India - Architecture - Nalukettu
metas.description:
Nallukettu architecture has distinct roofs, which are often very high and red.
This style is often found around Kerala Backwaters.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Odisha - Thatched Roofs
metas.description: Thatched roofs can be found pretty much all over the eastern coast of India. In the state of Odisha, they can mostly be seen between Balasore and Puri, but also more inland and in the southwest of the state.
metas.comparison: If you see only thatched, the coast is more likely.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Odisha - U-Tiles
metas.description: U tiles are commonly found on the northwest of the state, on the borders with Jharkhand and Chhattsgarh.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Odisha - U-Tiles & Thatched Roofs
metas.description: When mixed with thatched roofs, U Tiles are most commonly found around Umerkote.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Odisha - W-Tiles
metas.description: W tiled roofs can be found in two areas in Odisha:

metas.name: India - Architecture - Odisha - W-Tiles & Thatched Roofs
metas.description: W tiled roofs combined with Thatched Roofs can be found in two areas in Odisha:
metas.comparison: Note by MB: This is also true if you just see W-Tiles, without Thatched Roofs.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Odisha - W-Tiles & U-Tiles
metas.description: When mixed with W-Tiles, U-Tiles are most commonly found around Umerkote.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Orange/Black Wide W Tiles
metas.description: If you see orange/black wide W tiles, you're probably around Madhubani (BR).
metas.comparison: Reminder: This type of tile is like a larger kind of W tile. Another way to tell it apart is the small pike in the middle of the tile.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Plastered Woven Wall
metas.description: Woven walls, plastered with clay are found on the western half of the Bihar-Nepal border.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Red Brick
metas.description: While Red Brick can be found anywhere in India, there is a notable concentration in the Ganges River Valley, especially towards the West.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Shimla Vibes
metas.description: Shimla is definitely the place in the Himalayas with the biggest amount of bright green and bright red roofs (and architecture in general).
metas.comparison: Note by MB: It also spams Himalayan Cedars.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Sikhism
metas.description: Gurdwaras, which can typically be recognised by their white domes and ornate walls, are most common in Punjab. You can also sometimes recognise them by the Sikh Khanda symbol, which represents the religion.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Sikkim Roof
metas.description: Roofs in Sikkim often have this short "curtain" hanging down on the side of the roof.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Slate Roof - Karnataka/Telangana
metas.description: Slate roofs can be found in a very specific area between Kalaburagi and Hyderabad in Telangana.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: This is the same area where they use the thin grey stones (see thin grey stones meta), and thus you can often see them in combination

metas.name: India - Architecture - Square Panel Houses
metas.description: Houses made of square panels separated by thin beams are found in Northeast India, mainly in Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Stick Huts
metas.description: Wooden huts with sticks around can be found in the western half of Bihar, at a latitude between Patna and Muzaffarpur..

metas.name: India - Architecture - Tamil Nadu Colors
metas.description: Houses with very "strong colors", such as dark yellow, pink, purple, are often found in Tamil Nadu, and sometimes in Kerala and Andhra Pradesh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Tamil Nadu House
metas.description: In Tamil Nadu, you will often come across quite good looking houses, the most recognizable are the ones with W tiled roofs and blueish paint. The combination of the color and the tiles should be 95% Tamil Nadu, the remaining 5% being spill in bordering states.
metas.comparison: W tiled roofs are pretty much everywhere but somewhat less common in the northeast and on the eastern coast, where U tiles can be found more commonly.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Thatched Hay Roofs
metas.description: Houses or huts with thatched roofs are mainly found along the east coast and northern plains. Large hay mounds are also generally more common in this region. Thatched roofs from Uttar Pradesh to Odisha tend to be made of fine pieces of hay.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Thatched Palm Roofs
metas.description: Houses or huts with thatched roofs are mainly found along the east coast and northern plains. Large hay mounds are also generally more common in this region. Thatched roofs from Odisha to Tamil Nadu tend to be made of dried palm fans.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Thatched Roofs - Tamil Nadu
metas.description: In Tamil Nadu, thatched roofs are more common south east of Thanjavur.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Thin Grey Stones
metas.description: The area on the border of Telangana and Karnataka often have houses with roofs made out of distinctly thin grey bricks. These grey bricks and similar coloured rocks are sometimes also seen in walls and scattered on the ground in stockyards.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Triangle Metal Roofs
metas.description: Metal roofs, with a small triangle near the top, are common in Northeast India.

metas.name: India - Architecture - U-Tiles
metas.description: These rounded tiles are found mostly in
metas.comparison: You can also find them in

metas.name: India - Architecture - U-Tiles - Tamil Nadu
metas.description: U tiled roofs are quite rare in Tamil Nadu, but if you come across such roofs, it should be in the northeast.
metas.comparison: It is possible to find some further down near Thanjavur, but it will more likely come with the combination of thatched roofs.

metas.name: India - Architecture - W-Tiles
metas.description: W-Tiles are mostly found on the western coast and in Tamil Nadu, but it also goes further inland in western Madhya Pradesh and in Telangana.

metas.name: India - Architecture - W-Tiles - Karnataka
metas.description: If you come across a W tiled roof in Karnataka, you can basically go in the western/southwestern part

metas.name: India - Architecture - W-Tiles - Telangana
metas.description: The only type of tile in Telangana is the W tile type.
metas.comparison: As you can see, it doesnât go in the south of the state.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Wealthy & Modern Homes
metas.description: Goa and Kerala are two of the most developed states in India and often have very wealthy and modern homes.

metas.name: India - Architecture - West Bengal - Dumka House
metas.description: In West Bengal, houses with walls painted in two colors (green/blue with an orange/brown color at the bottom, are usually found near the Jharkhand border.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Wide W-Tiles
metas.description: This type of tile is like a larger kind of W tile. Another way to tell it apart is the small pike in the middle of the tile.
metas.comparison: It is very common in West Bengal, eastern Jharkhand and eastern Bihar, but doesnât go further north than Purnia, Bihar.

metas.name: India - Camera Meta - High Quality Shitcam
metas.description: The coverage on road NH326 (labelled 326) west of Brahmapur in Odisha has a thin grey antenna. The images are generally very high-quality for shitcam, with an especially high quality near the Harabhangi Reservoir.

metas.name: India - Car - Kuno National Park Car
metas.description: This car has a back curving bar, but is mostly blurred. It can be found east of Kuno National Park

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Andaman Car
metas.description: This is the most common, though not only car on Andaman.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Arunachal Pradesh - Back Antenna
metas.meta_label: Car Meta - Arunachal Pradesh - Back Antenna
metas.description: Within Arunachal Pradesh, a back antenna can be found around Chowkam and East of Namsai.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Arunachal Pradesh - White Car with Mirrors
metas.meta_label: Car Meta - Arunachal Pradesh - White Car with Mirrors
metas.description: Within Arunachal Pradesh, a white car with mirrors can be found on the road west of Itanagar.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Assam - Back Antenna
metas.description: If you see a back antenna in Assam, you're in the far east of the state.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Black Car
metas.description: This is not something you will come across very often, but if you have a black car and donât really know where to go/want to confirm your guess, black car is more common in Telangana/Andhra Pradesh, especially in Northern Telangana and Coastal AP.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Black Goa Car
metas.description: This black car, uniquely characterized through the black bars on each the side, is only found in Goa.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Boxy Car
metas.description: Large visible, square shaped cars can be found in all states northwest of Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh, except for Madhya Pradesh. It can also be found in and around Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Chennai.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Boxy Car - 5 Indents
metas.description: A boxy car with 5 indents can be found near the river mouth of the Subarnarekha river near the Odisha/WB border.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Boxy Car - 6 Indents
metas.description: A boxy car with 6 indents is found near Malkangiri, Odisha.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Boxy Car - Karnataka
metas.description: Boxy car in Karnataka is only found in and around Bengaluru.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Boxy Car - Odisha
metas.description: A boxy car with an extra step at the front is found in Odisha.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Flower Car
metas.description: A car with flowers on the front can be found around Keonjhar, on the 49 and the 20.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Goa/Daman Car
metas.description: This car (note the antenna!) can be found in Goa, and in the Union Territory of Daman.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Haryal Car
metas.description: This car is unique to Haryal, PB. It looks similar to the boxy car, but with a rounded front.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Himachal Pradesh - Boxy Car
metas.meta_label: Car Meta - Himachal Pradesh - Boxy Car
metas.description: Shimla is  the only city in Himachal Pradesh to have a boxy car, which is this car with the top right corner visible with a thread (sometimes not visible).

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Jammu/Kashmir Car
metas.description: White car, box car with bars and the central strap leaning right.
metas.comparison: It can be found mainly in Jammu/Kashmir but sometimes in Sultanpur, UP.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Ladakh Car
metas.description: All roads in Ladakh have this white car with visible front.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Adidas Car
metas.description: The "Adidas Car" is characterized by the black stripes on the white car front. Sometimes it has a visible side mirror. It also often has a visible bar at the back.
metas.comparison: It is exclusive to the island of Amini

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Big Blur
metas.description: A big circular blur (either full blurred or transparently blurred) is very common in Retrocam. On Lakshadweep, however, it is only found on Andrott and Kalpeni (both also have a car that's unique for these islands respectively).

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Blurred Black Front
metas.meta_label: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Blurred Black Front
metas.description: This car with the subtle black blur at the front is found in Kalpeni. The blur can be very subtle sometimes, and is confusable with the blurred white edges on Agatti.
metas.comparison: Sometimes the same car has a slightly different blur, where the edges are exposed. Kalpeni can also have a big circular blur, so don't rule out Kalpeni if you don't see this car.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Blurred White Edges
metas.meta_label: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Blurred White Edges
metas.description:
This car is mostly blurred and has subtle white edges at the front. It's found on the island of Agatti.
Sometimes the edges are so subtle that you can overlook them and confuse it with the Kalpeni car (which has a subtle black blur)

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Exposed Black
metas.description: This car with an exposed black front is unique to Kiltan. Note that the front is always exposed on Kiltan, if it's blurred (even partly), it's not the Kiltan car.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Red Car
metas.description: The red front blur can be found on Andrott. Sometimes, the same car has a bit different blur, where there's some exposed red visible.
metas.comparison: Note that Andrott can also have the big circular blur where you see no car.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Lakshadweep - White Car with Mirror
metas.meta_label: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - White Car with Mirror
metas.description: This car is the most likely to encounter if you get Lakshadweep. It has a white front and always a bit of mirror visible on the left. Sometimes a part of the mirror is blurred, but you can always see at least a bit of it exposed. This car is so common because it's on the main island of Lakshadweep, Kavaratti.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Lakshadweep - White Exposed Front
metas.meta_label: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - White Exposed Front
metas.description: This car with an exposed white front is found of Kadmat. This car can be confused with others: It's not the Kadmat car if it has a visible side mirror. It's also not the Kadmat car if the front is blurred.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Mechuka Car
metas.description: Mechuka features a unique car in Arunachal. It can be found in the valley and on the road leading to it from Along on the NH13.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Mizoram - Double Mirror Car
metas.meta_label: Car Meta - Mizoram - Double Mirror Car
metas.description: In Mizoram, a grey car with double mirrors appears in the southernmost coverage, near the NH502.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Mizoram - Long Antenna
metas.description: If you see a long antenna, combined with a black car front in Mizoram, you're on the NH6 north of Serkhan.
metas.comparison: Keep in mind this car is not unique to Mizoram.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Mizoram - Stubby Antenna
metas.description: A car with a black front and a stubby antenna within Mizoram can be found on the roads west of Aizawi.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - NH179B Car
metas.description: This car has an antenna with some kind of a spring. It basically goes from Salem to Chennai.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Open Trunk
metas.description:
In the eastern parts of Ajmer, RJ, you can sometimes see an open trunk in Smallcam.
It can be found north of Shrinagar/west of Circular Rd.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Orange Flag Car
metas.description: A car with an orange flag can be found in the Jharkhand north-east panhandle.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Punjab - Black Boxy Car
metas.meta_label: Car Meta - Punjab - Black Boxy Car
metas.description: Within Punjab, the black boxy car can be found on the Pakistani border between Firozpur and Amritsar.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Punjab - Dasuya Forest Car
metas.meta_label: Car Meta - Punjab - Dasuya Forest Car
metas.description: Within Punjab, this car is is unique to Dasuya Forest. Beware that this car is not unique to Punjab though.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Punjab - Red Boxy Car
metas.meta_label: Car Meta - Punjab - Red Boxy Car
metas.description: Within Punjab, the red boxy car can be found in Ludhiana, Chandigarh, and a bit north between them. The coverage forms a reverse 'v'.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Racecar
metas.description: This cool car with a spoiler at the back can be found in Max-North Andaman, near Daglipur.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Rewa Car
metas.description: This car has a back curving bar at the front and white bars on the side. It's found mostly around Rewa, but also around Raipura.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Roing Car
metas.description:
Within Arunachal Pradesh, both this black and this red car are exclusively found in Roing.
The black car appears mainly on the NH313 and east.
The red car appears mainly west of the main road.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Satpura National Park Car
metas.meta_label: Car Meta - Satpura National Park Car
metas.description: This car has a back-curving bar and a singular black bar. It's found mainly east of Satpura National Park, and sometimes around Raipura.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Tezu-Lohitpur Road
metas.description: If you see this white, boxy-looking car in Arunachal Pradesh, you're on the road between Tezu and Lohitpur.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Western Meghalaya Antenna
metas.description: In the very far western part of the Meghalaya, on the roads north of Purakhasia, you can find a particular car with an antenna on the top left. It can be quite hard to see so be aware it exists so you know what to look for

metas.name: India - Car Meta - White Goa Car with bar
metas.meta_label: Car Meta - White Goa Car with bar
metas.description: This white car, uniquely characterized through the bar on the side, which is black and grey, is only found in Goa.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Yellow Car
metas.description: While the car is blurred most of the time, Sikkim features a noticeable car that gives the western part of Sikkim, starting at Rangpo.
metas.comparison: It can have an antenna, be blurred, almost invisible, but as long as you see a yellow car, you know itâs here.

metas.name: India - Coverage Meta - Andaman Vibes
metas.description: Andaman Islands are remote Islands that have their own distinct vegetation. It is covered in areca palm forests and the roads are often very thin.
metas.comparison: Andaman has been covered using a camera with maxed out saturation somehow. The result is these very bright/white colors.

metas.name: India - Coverage Meta - Kerala Construction Meta
metas.description: In 2025, a large part of the NH-66 in Kerala is under construction, making it very recognizable.
metas.comparison: If you see a long, straight highway with construction in Smallcam, you're likely to be on the NH-66.

metas.name: India - Coverage Meta - Tripura Cam
metas.description: Many locations in Tripura have a pretty low brightness, despite the sun being out and not setting.

metas.name: India - Coverage Meta - Yawal Double Smudge
metas.description: This double smudge can be found in the central-northern parts of the Yawal Wildlife Sanctuary in Madhya Pradesh.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - â-Poletop
metas.description: Poles in Madhya Pradesh often have a metal bar shaped like an upside down A (â) slightly below the top of the pole.
metas.comparison:
94% Madhya Pradesh
2% Jharkhand
1% each: Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - <-Poletop
metas.description: Poles with two diagonal bars forming a â<â shape are common in Meghalaya (75%) and Arunachal Pradesh (20%) and occasionally found in Assam (2%).

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - 1 1/2 Trapezoids
metas.description: This pole configuraiton is mainly found in Tripura and Arunachal Pradesh.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - ACC Cement
metas.description: Found everywhere except for North-East.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Ambuja Cement
metas.description:
Commonly found everywhere, except for North East.
Within North-East, it is sometimes found in Assam.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Andaman Black Sticker
metas.description: These black paint can be circular or square, features 2 letters, an arrow beneath, and some numbers beneath that and can be on metal/concrete poles.
metas.comparison: They're found mostly near the capital (Port Blair/Sri Vijaya Puram) (95%) and rarely near Diglipur (5%)

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Andaman Horizontal Bar Poletop
metas.description: Pole tops in Andaman mostly consist of horizontal bars perpendicular to the pole. They are not 100% unique to Andaman, but are very common there.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Antioquia Pole
metas.description: This black-yellow-black pole painting (which is famous for appearing in Antioquia in Colo), can also be found in Eastern Bihar along the Ganges.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Arunachal Pradesh - Black & White Bollard
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Arunachal Pradesh - Black & White Bollard
metas.description: These bollards are rarer and not unique to Arunachal Pradesh, but if you think you are here, these are the areas these bollards are most commonly found

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Arunachal Pradesh - Divided Road
metas.description: The only divided road in Arunachal Pradesh is the NH415 south of Itanagar

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Arunachal Pradesh - Pole Band
metas.description: A section of the NH13 west of Roing has poles marked with white numbers on blue, red or black paint.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Assam / West Bengal vans
metas.description: These vans (can be white, red, or orange) with specifically yellow plates, in NE India are found only within West Bengal and Assam. Doesnât count with a white plate.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Assam Pavement
metas.description: Many roads in Assam are paved with these tiles. What makes it stand out is that it is also found on very rural roads.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Assam Trident Poles
metas.description: Trident poletops with the tip of the middle bar bent at a 90Â° angle can be found in Assam (98%).

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Bangur Cement
metas.description: Bangur Cement is found in large parts of India.
metas.comparison: It is only sometimes found in Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Delhi (where Bangur Power Cement) is more prevalent. It is never found in

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Bangur Power Cement
metas.description: Found in Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Delhi, and sometimes also in Uttar Pradesh or Madhya Pradesh.
metas.comparison: Don't confuse this with Bangur Cement, which has a different distribution.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Bar underneath Generic Pole
metas.description: Metal crossbar with no insulators
metas.comparison: Most common in Maharahstra (50%) Also occasionally found in other northern states. Within the Northeast, it's exclusive to Tripura.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Big Ring Pole
metas.description: Big rectangular metal ring around the pole.
metas.comparison: Most common in Uttarakhand + Himachal Pradesh and Mizoram + Tripura.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Bihar Pole + Mountains
metas.description: In Uttarakhand, the Bihar pole (yellow and black stripes) can be found on the NH109 North and a small road South of Dwarahat. Since Uttarakhand is mountainous, you shouldn't mistake it for Bihar.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Bihar stripes
metas.description: Pole paint consisting of exactly four thicker black and yellow stripes can be found in Bihar.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Bihar/Jharkhand Guy
metas.description: In Bihar and Jharkhand you will see many ads with this man with a turban and a beard. He's usually accompanied by a hexagonal company logo and a yellow background.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: This sounds ridiculous but he seems to be so popular that there are copycats of him with the same Turban/beard style. So if you see a different company logo, don't trust this.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Black Tuk-Tuks
metas.description: Black Tuk-Tuks are most common in Maharashtra (maybe fake meta)

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Blue & White Bridge
metas.description: The bridges in West Bengal frequently feature blue and white concrete blocks. It is also rarely found in Bihar around the city of Gaya.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Blue Pole Stickers
metas.description: These blue stickers on metal poles can be found on the NH109 near Lohali (UK)

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Buddhism
metas.description:
Buddhist prayer flags and other Buddhist signals are mostly found in the Himalayas.
Sometimes you can also find them in the Northeast, around Bangladesh, especially in Western Meghalaya, Western Mizoram and Southern Tripura.
Rarely you can find it in central-eastern Maharashtra around Nagpur.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: The colors in the map don't exactly match the text. The text is right though (for Geoguessr), not the map.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Chandigarh - Lampe Circles
metas.description: The City of Chandigarh is a planned industrial city. As a result, the city features a lot of unique infrastructure, such as round yellow markings on street lights.
metas.comparison: NOTE: The nearby cities of Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar and Panchkula are also planned industrial cities, which feature somewhat similar signs.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Chandigarh - Large Blue Signs
metas.description: The City of Chandigarh is a planned industrial city. As a result, the city features a lot of unique infrastructure, such as blue signs mentioning sectors and industrial areas.
metas.comparison: NOTE: The nearby cities of Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar and Panchkula are also planned industrial cities, which feature somewhat similar signs.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Chandigarh - Streetsign
metas.description: The City of Chandigarh is a planned industrial city. As a result, the city features a lot of unique infrastructure, such as street signs which will typically feature several numbers rather than street names.
metas.comparison: NOTE: The nearby cities of Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar and Panchkula are also planned industrial cities, which feature somewhat similar signs.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Chandigarh Poletop
metas.description: Trident poletop, V-shaped bars underneath and Punjab Poletop.
metas.comparison: Very hyperspecific for some roads in Chandigarh.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Chennai Wall
metas.description: This wall pattern can be found in and around Chennai (but it is rare).

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Chettinad Cement
metas.description:
Recognizable by the C-Logo
Found in South India, and sometimes in Goa and Maharashtra.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Combination of Even and Uneven Poletop
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Combination of Even and Uneven Poletop
metas.description: In the northeast you may find poles with a combination of an even and uneven poletop.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Complicated Dark Metal Pole
metas.description: Overly complicated, usually dark metal.
metas.comparison: 90% in West Bengal.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Concrete Blocks
metas.description: Concrete blocks, similar to those you see in Bhutan, are commonly found in (but not limited to) North-East India

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Concrete Holey Poles
metas.description:
Concrete holey poles are unique to Gujarat and the Union territory of Daman and Diu, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli.
Gujarat uses a variety of poletops, some of which can be used to identify other states. Beware that holey poles generally take precedence over poletop metas.
metas.comparison: NOTE: They are rarely found in other states:

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Concrete Road / Yellow Lines
metas.description: From the city of Sukma to the border with Andra Pradesh, the NH30 has yellow road lines and is made of concrete. (Kinda similar to the famous Ruta 9 in Chile)

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Concreto Cement
metas.description: Found in East India (i.e. Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha)

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Dark Rock Walls
metas.description: Dark Rock Walls are commonly found around Udaipur, RJ.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Dehradun Sticker
metas.description: These round white stickers can be found all over Dehradun (UK)

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Delhi Bus
metas.description: Orange and bright green buses are typically found in Delhi.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Delhi stripes
metas.description: Pole paint consisting of five or more thin black and yellow stripes can be found in Delhi.
metas.comparison: #1 clue for rural Delhi (98%) Has to be the exact order and color.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Delhi Yellow Sticker
metas.description: Besides Kerala and Uttarakhand, Delhi can also rarely have yellow stickers. All of these regions look very different.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Double Bull Cement
metas.description: Found in Central and East India, in Haryana and Delhi, and sometimes in Gujarat.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Duraguard Cement
metas.description: Found in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Chattisgarh, sometimes in Odisha.
metas.comparison: Don't confuse with Duraton Cement.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Duraton Cement
metas.description: Only found in Punjab and Jammu / Kashmir.
metas.comparison: Don't confuse with Duraguard Cement.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Elevated Jharkhand Structures
metas.description: These elevated structures are found a lot of them between Hazaribagh and Ranchi in Jharkhand.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Extended Vertical Bar
metas.description: Extra vertical bar at the top of the pole, extends significantly over the pole.
metas.comparison:
85% West Bengal
12% Chhattisgarh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Generic Poletop
metas.description: Typically not south of Maharashtra-Chhattisgarh-Odisha except in Kerala. Generic pole does NOT include any bars on the top of pole

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Generic Poletop with Grey Crossbar
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Generic Poletop with Grey Crossbar
metas.description: If the generic poletop has a grey crossbar, you're most likely in Uttar Pradesh. It's less commonly found in Odisha, Bihar, and more rarely in Haryan and Jharkhand.
metas.comparison: If it's in South India, it's 98% Kerala.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Goa Poletops
metas.description: This poletop has two crossbars, the top one is short with 2 insulators, the bottom one is long with 4 insulators.
metas.comparison: It's mostly found in Goa (95%) and rarely in Kerala (2%), Maharashtra (1%) and Karnataka (1%)

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Green Pole Stripes
metas.description: Green pole stripes are commonly found in the far western roads of Arunachal Pradesh. They are often combined with yellow or white stripes.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Gujarat - Non-Holey Pole
metas.description: Almost all poles in Gujarat are holey poles. Generic poles are only found sometimes in very far west Gujarat, near the border with Pakistan

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Harsil Road
metas.description: On the road south of Harsil (UK), you will find a large amount of poles with red/yellow stripes and black bollards with stripes (see UK/JH bollard)

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - HiBond Cement
metas.description:
Recognizable by the wavy triangle logo.
Found only in Gujarat.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Himachal Pradesh - Double Guardrail
metas.description: The NH5 near Sarahan ist the only road in Himachal Pradesh with a double guardrail.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Hollow Metal Pole
metas.description: This means, it has an indent that runs through the whole pole. If you look at it from the top, it looks like a C.
metas.comparison: Most common in Mizoram, seen in Himachal Pradesh as well. Note by MB: Seen this in central states too, but still useful together with landscape ig.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Hyderabad Mesh Pole
metas.description: Mesh pole with three wires on one or both sides, that are connected to the pole in a "pyramid shaped" extension on the side.
metas.comparison: Note that it has to be a pole, not a cellphone tower (which would be a lot larger). Found around Hyderabad, TG

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - JK Lakshmi Cement
metas.description:
Found in North and Central India, plus Jharkhand, Odisha and Gujarat.
Sometimes also in Maharashtra.
metas.comparison: Don't confuse with JK Power Cement (which hasn't been researched yet).

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - JSW Cement
metas.description: Found in South India, Goa + Maharashtra, and Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Karnataka Pole
metas.description: In Karnataka (85%), and sometimes in Haryana (6%), Western Andhra Pradesh (6%) and rarely Uttar Pradesh (1%), you can find trident poletops on concrete poles where the central insulator is attached directly to the top of the pole, while the other two are attached to a horizontal crossbar positioned slightly further down. There are different variants of this poletop that increase the likelihood for Karnataka.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: Make sure not to confuse it with the trident with a small bar at the top (see images).

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Karnataka Pole - Karnataka Insulator
metas.description: If a trident pole has these insulators with three circles and air between them, it is found 98% in Karnataka.
metas.comparison: The other versions of this poletop have lower certainties for Karnataka.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Kerala "Weird" Poletop
metas.description: Made of metal, has a "generic" crossbar, but additionally a very long bar that extends into one direction at the top, which holds the actual insulators.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Kerala Bollard
metas.description: What makes these bollards unique is the red reflector on a stone bollard.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Kerala Bridge
metas.description: Blue and white bridges can commonly be found all over Kerala. They can sometimes be painted in green.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Kerala Yellow Marker
metas.description: Small yellow pole markings are commonly found in Kerala.
metas.comparison: Can also be used to rule out Kerala since 80-90% of all poles have it. Can also be found in Goa (2-3%)

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Konark Cement
metas.description: Found in Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Large Rectangle
metas.description: In West Bengal you may also find poletops containing two crossbars which are connected to each other with thin vertical supports on either side. The lower bar is connected on either side to the pole with diagonal supports.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - License Plates - Andhra Pradesh
metas.description: Sometimes, unblurred license plates can be seen (particularly often on trucks). The first two letters give the state. The next two numbers give the district (really not worth learning)
metas.comparison: AP stands for Andhra Pradesh. The exception is license plates that do not start with letters or with T0. Those rarer license plates are national.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - License Plates - Karnataka
metas.description: Sometimes, unblurred license plates can be seen (particularly often on trucks). The first two letters give the state. The next two numbers give the district (really not worth learning)
metas.comparison: KA stands for Karnataka. The exception is license plates that do not start with letters or with T0. Those rarer license plates are national.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - License Plates - Kerala
metas.description: Sometimes, unblurred license plates can be seen (particularly often on trucks). The first two letters give the state. The next two numbers give the district (really not worth learning)
metas.comparison: KL stands for Kerala. The exception is license plates that do not start with letters or with T0. Those rarer license plates are national.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Madhya Pradesh - Rock Walls
metas.description: In Madhya Pradesh, rock walls are very common around two national parks : Kuno National Park and Panna National Park

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Maharashtra Pole
metas.description: This pole is either metal or concrete (but more skinny than a generic pole). It has one or two small bars near the poletop.
metas.comparison: It's not exclusive to Maharashtra, but very common there.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Manipur Poletop
metas.description: In Manipur you can often find trident poletops on poles made entirely out of metal. They sometimes have small bars on the top of the trident.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Max Cement
metas.description: Found only in North-East India, but not in Nagaland or Arunachal Pradesh.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Meghalaya - Divided Road
metas.description: The NH6 north of Shillong is the only divided highway in Meghalaya.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: A good way to tell you're in Meghalaya is the lack of non-latin scripts.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Metal Holey Poles
metas.description: Metal holey poles are common in Kerala.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Metal Mesh Poles
metas.description: Metal poles with a mesh pattern are commonly found in Sikkim (93%) and rarely in Arunachal Pradesh (5%)

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Mycem Cement
metas.description: Found only in Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Nagaland Auto
metas.description: Auto Rickshaws with a Black Body and a Yellow Roof (i.e. reverse to the Andhra Pradesh / Telangana variant) are commonly found in Nagaland.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - NH51 / Gujarat
metas.description: The NH51 in Gujarat is unique because it is lined with many dark metal poles (unlike most of Gujarat which has concrete holey poles). It is also divided and paved with concrete.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Odisha Bridge
metas.description: Some bridges in Odisha are made of green and white concrete blocks as guardrails

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Orange Pole Paint
metas.description: This Orange Pole Paint is found on the NH15 in Arunachal Pradesh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Orange Pole Stickers
metas.description: These orange stickers on metal poles can be found in Uttarakhand, mostly in the East.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Painted Stripes
metas.description: Metal poles in Uttarakhand sometimes have those red or yellow stripes painted on them.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Pole with Black/White bottom
metas.description: White and black stripes on the bottom of a pole are found in both Meghalaya and Tripura.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: Don't confuse this with the Tamil Nadu polepainting, which is always white-black-white and further up on the pole.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Pole with Red Paint
metas.description: Silver painted poles with a red or brown top.
metas.comparison: Common in Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh, sometimes Tripura & Mizoram.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Punjabi Electricity Counters
metas.description: Electricity counters in Punjab are usually mint green with small window-like squares. They can rarely be seen in Haryana.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Pure Metal in Uttarakhand
metas.description: In the Himalayas, pure metal poles are usually more common in the North-East. If you see them in the Northwest, it's most likely Uttarakhand.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Rajasthan - Rock Walls / Flat Landscape
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Rajasthan - Rock Walls / Flat Landscape
metas.description: Rock walls are not unique to Rajasthan, but if you know or have a feeling youâre in Rajasthan, it is most common south of Udaipur (hilly) and southeast of Kota (flat). This can be used combined with the elevation to get the precise area.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Rajasthan - Rock Walls / Flat Landscape
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Rajasthan - Rock Walls / Flat Landscape
metas.description: Rock walls are not unique to Rajasthan, but if you know or have a feeling youâre in Rajasthan, it is most common south of Udaipur (hilly) and southeast of Kota (flat). This can be used combined with the elevation to get the precise area.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Rajasthan Mesh Pole
metas.description: Found 90% in Rajasthan.
metas.comparison: Sikkim and Telangana also have Mesh poles, but they're different. The Sikkim pole is slimmer, while the Telangana pole has "triangles" at the top.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Ramco Cement
metas.description: Found in South India, however less common in Karnataka. Sometimes also found in West Bengal.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Red & White Bollard
metas.description: It is quite rare to see red and white bollards, but they are mostly found in far west Arunachal Pradesh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Red&White Tree Paint
metas.description: In Bihar, and less commonly Jharkhand, you may find trees with four red and white stripes painted near the bottom.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Rusted Hollow Pole
metas.description: Thin rusted Poles that are hollow, i.e. have an indent going from the bottom to the top, are found in Maharashtra, and sometimes in Chhattisgarh.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Sanghi Cement
metas.description:
Recognizable by the Lion Logo.
Found only in Gujarat.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Seperated Bus Lane
metas.description: On large roads in Ahmedabad and Surat you can find separated middle lanes for buses. Beware that people will still often drive in these lanes.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Shree Cement
metas.description: Found everywhere, except for Himalayan states, North Eastern States, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Sikkim Taxis
metas.description: Taxis in Sikkim often have a painted yellow hood or a small yellow circle on it.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Simple Black Sticker
metas.description: This black sticker usually just has few characters, often just a number.
metas.comparison:
35% Tamil Nadu
35% Andhra Pradesh
20% Telangana Note that it's a weak meta for Andhra over Telangana. Do not confuse for Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Small Extra Bar
metas.description: Short bar at the top of the pole.
metas.comparison:
Mostly in Rajasthan and Telangana
Sometimes Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra
Rarely Jharkhand. In the Northeast, it can be found in Tripura or rarely in Arunachal Pradesh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Small Ring Pole
metas.description: Very similar to a second vertical bar, but it is attached to the pole on its ends, rather than in the middle, giving it a ring shape. What differentiates it from the big ring pole is that the bar isn't far away from the pole.
metas.comparison:
35% Maharashtra
35% Madhya Pradesh
20% Chhattisgarh
2% Rajasthan & Mizoram
1% Tripura

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Small Trapezoid
metas.description: Trapezoid poletop, but the diagonal bars do not reach the end of the crossbar.
metas.comparison:
Most common in flat Arunachal Pradesh
Sometimes in Tripura

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Square Stick Fences
metas.description: In the northeast you will commonly see fences made of thin wooden sticks in a square pattern.
metas.comparison: They can also sometimes be seen in Odisha, which has a very different landscape, making it useful to distinguish Odisha from other eastern states.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Star Cement
metas.description: Found in North-East India, West Bengal and sometimes Bihar.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Symmetric Trident / Asymmetric Insulators
metas.description:
60% Tamil Nadu
20% Telangana
15% Andhra Pradesh
metas.comparison: Important that the crossbar is symmetric, if it's asymmetric, it's usually TG.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - T-shaped Pole Extension
metas.description: This pole extensions (above the pole) with 3 insulators
metas.comparison:
45% Andhra Pradesh
45% Telangana
9% Tamil Nadu

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Tall, Narrow Rectangle Poletop
metas.description: A variety of poletops attached to the pole with two vertical bars forming a tall and narrow rectangle can be found in West Bengal.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Tamil Nadu Pole
metas.description: 3 insulators in a horizontal line, or middle insulator slightly above others
metas.comparison:
88% Tamil Nadu
5% Bihar
3% Haryana
2% Uttar Pradesh
1.5% Andhra Pradesh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Pole
metas.description: In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Pole - Bars in different directions
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Pole - Bars in different directions
metas.description: In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.
metas.comparison: If the bars point in different directions, it's often in Meghalaya.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Pole - Dark Metal / Single Bar
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Pole - Dark Metal / Single Bar
metas.description: In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.
metas.comparison:
If it's a single bar, with dark metal, it's
80% Meghalaya
15% Assam

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Pole - Grey Metal
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Pole - Grey Metal
metas.description: In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.
metas.comparison:
If the pole is made out of bright/grey metal, it's
45% Meghalaya
45% Assam

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Poles - Dark Metal / Double Bar
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Poles - Dark Metal / Double Bar
metas.description: In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.
metas.comparison:
If it's dark metal and has two bars, it's
65% Meghalaya
15% Assam
15% Mizoram

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - TG/AP Bridge
metas.description:
Bridges in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh are often recognizable by the color of their guardrails.
It is often made of vertical red/pink/orange concrete blocks with horizontal white/light yellow blocks.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Thai Bollards
metas.description: "Thai" bollards (white-black-white) are found in Odisha.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Thick Grey Trapezoid
metas.description: Commonly found in Kerala (especially with yellow stickers).
metas.comparison: Note that there's also a version with the two indents, which is not found in Kerala, but in Andhra Pradesh.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Thick Trapezoid - Two Indents
metas.description: Thick gray trapezoid, with two indents in the pole material.
metas.comparison: 97% Andhra Pradesh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Thin Grey Metal Poles
metas.description: Thin grey metal poles are seen all over northeastern India and in the Himalayan region of Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh. You will commonly see two of these poles in close proximity.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Tiny Crossbar
metas.description: A pole with no poletop except for this tiny bar, is often found in Odisha (70-80%)

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Toothbrush + Horizontal Bar
metas.description: Insulators at the top, directly attached to the concrete, pointing in one direction. Below, there is a metal crossbar with no insulators.
metas.comparison:
70% Maharashtra
10% Chhattisgarh
5% Himachal Pradesh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Trapezoid - Dark Metal
metas.description: Trapezoid poletops with poles completely made out of dark metal, are found in Chhattisgarh 95% of the time.
metas.comparison: If it's not made out of dark metal, it's less certain.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Trapezoid Pole (Concrete)
metas.description: A connector on the pole which looks like an upside down trapezoid.
metas.comparison:
80% Chhattisgarh
10% Maharashtra
3% Karnataka
2% Odisha
1% each: Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Assam NOTE: They can also be paired with Holey Poles in Gujarat and Ladder Poles in Andhra Pradesh, thus only use the trapezoid when no other pole meta is present. Northeast India also has some trapezoid poletops that look a bit different.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Triangle Poletop
metas.description: Upside down triangle poletops placed below the top of the pole are commonly found in Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, and less commonly in Madhya Pradesh.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Triangle Poletop / Dumbbell Insulators
metas.description:
32% Maharashtra
32% Madhya Pradesh
32% Chattisgarh
1% Andhra Pradesh
1% Telangana

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Triangle Poletop & Three Insulators
metas.description: Triangle poletops with three insulators on top can be found in Jammu and Kashmir, sometimes in Himachal Pradesh.
metas.comparison: Note: Do not confuse this with the regular triangle poletops which can be found elsewhere. Also even these poletops are not 100% unique to J&K

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Triangle Window
metas.description: Triangle-shaped window insulators on a crossbar.
metas.comparison:
90% Jharkhand
2% Chhattisgarh
1% Bihar

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Trident / Asymmetric Bar
metas.description: This pole has an asymmetric crossbar, with one side double the length of the other, and two insulators on the longer side, and one on the shorter side.
metas.comparison: Research is not conclusive due to its rarity, but it's estimated to be 95% Telangana. Note by MB: It's important that the bar is asymmetric, if it's symmetric, and the insulators are asymmetric, it's a different pole.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Triple Karnataka Poletop
metas.description: Concrete Trident pole with three crossbars.
metas.comparison:
Do not confuse it with the North-Eastern Triple Poletop, which has shorter crossbars and is made out of metal instead of concrete. Found 98% in Karnataka
0.5% in Gujarat

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Tripura Pole
metas.description: Tripura Poles often tend to have an extra bar underneath as well as the small crossbar on top.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Two Section Pole - High Bar
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Two Section Pole - High Bar
metas.description: Two-section poles can sometimes be regionguessed by looking at the bar above the crossbar (which doesn't always exist).
metas.comparison: If it's high on the pole (meaning you can barely see the concrete above it), it's 80% Telangana, 20% Andhra Pradesh (especially western) Sometimes it's hard to tell though, so it can be a bit of a cope

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Two Section Pole - Low Bar
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Two Section Pole - Low Bar
metas.description: Two-section poles can sometimes be regionguessed by looking at the bar above the crossbar (which doesn't always exist).
metas.comparison: If it's lower on the pole (meaning you can see a bit of concrete over the bar), it's 85% Andhra Pradesh, 15% Telangana Sometimes it's hard to tell though, so it can be a bit of a cope

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Two Section Poles
metas.description: Poles divided in two sections, in a similar fashion to Brazilian poles, are common in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - UK/JH Bollard
metas.description: This black bollard with stripes (usually at least one of the colors: red, white, orange) can be found in Jharkhand and Uttarakhand.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Ultra Tech Cement
metas.description: Can be found anywhere except for North-East India.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Uttarakhand - Red/white pole paint
metas.description: In Uttarakhand, you can find these red-white stripes on poles on random roads around Dwarahat.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Vertical Bar
metas.description: Vertical bar at the poletop. It is attached to the pole with two short bars. Note that those bars are not at the end of the vertical bar, which would make it a ring pole (and change the distribution)
metas.comparison:
50% Chhattisgarh
30% Madhya Pradesh
15% Maharashtra
10% West Bengal

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Vertical Insulators
metas.description: 3-5 Insulators pointing upwards, attached to the pole.
metas.comparison: Common in Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, sometimes Bihar.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - West Bengal E-Rickshaw
metas.description: West Bengal only has E-Rickshaws. They have a unique shape and are often blue.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - White Metal Plate
metas.description: Can sometimes be rusted and a bit more brown.
metas.comparison: Found in Northern States: Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Bihar, sometimes Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - White-Black-White Paint
metas.description: Markings on poles and trees, consisting of one black stripe in-between two white ones, are common in Tamil Nadu.
metas.comparison:
Note by MB: This only counts if it's black, not with other colors. 99.3% Tamil Nadu
0.02% Andhra Pradesh
0.01% Madhya Pradesh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Windfarms
metas.description: The places with the most wind farms are indeed Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. This is pretty advanced knowledge, but region guessing states can be possible by learning where wind farms are:

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Window Poletop
metas.description:
Small metal poletops in the shape of a window are found in Punjab and Haryana.
93% Punjab
4% Haryana
1% Delhi & Jammu (on Punjabi border)
0.5% Rajasthan
0.2% Ladakh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Wonder Cement
metas.description: Found Northwest of Madhya Pradesh, however not in Himachal Pradesh or further North.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Yellow Outer Lines
metas.description: Parts of roads NH6 and NH206 southeast of Shillong can be recognised by the presence of khasi pines with distinct yellow outer road lines and fresh dark pavement.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This is the only road in Meghalaya that uses yellow outer road lines, but these lines exist in other states as well.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Yellow Pole Bands
metas.description: Between Aizawl and Champhai on the NH6, poles will have yellow bands.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Yellow Pole Stickers
metas.description: These orange stickers on metal poles can be found in Uttarakhand, mostly in the East.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Yellow Tuk Tuk / Black Roof
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Yellow Tuk Tuk / Black Roof
metas.description: Yellow tuk tuks with black roofs are common in the southern Indian states of Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.
metas.comparison: NOTE: They can also rarely be found elsewhere.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Zuari Cement
metas.description: Found in South India, especially in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.

metas.name: India - Infrasturcutre - Karnataka Symmetrical Poletop
metas.description: 2 insulators on each side, with the top of the pole sticking out.
metas.comparison:
