Found in Karnataka (94%)
and rarely in Tamil Nadu (4%) or Kerala (1%)

metas.name: India - Landscape - Amygdaloidal Basalt
metas.description: This is a volcanic rock, which is recognizable by it's dark color with white mineral patches on it.
metas.comparison: It is mostly found between Pune and Jalgaon. It's important to note that this rock alone, without the mineral patches is more widely spread.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Andhra Pradesh - Red Soil
metas.description: Andhra Pradesh has a long coast along the bay of Bengal and it is fairly recognizable because of the red soil combined with overall flatness. This is the area in which you fill find red soil in Andhra Pradesh.
metas.comparison: Flat landscape with red soil and lots of Palmyra should pretty much always give the eastern India coast.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Anisun River Valley
metas.description: A rocky desert can be found in this valley southwest of Nandyala, AP.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Assam - Hilliness
metas.description: Hilliness in Assam is found mostly South or East of Nagaon.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Assam - North Mountains
metas.description: If you see Mountains to the North in Assam, you're on the border to Arunachal Pradesh. In my experience, this is a particularly common sight on the border east of Itanagar.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Badvel Valley
metas.description: Wind turbines aligned on top of mountain ranges are very common in these mountain ranges valleys I would say. (I know there are some in RJ as well)
metas.comparison: Even without wind turbines, you can click in this valley if you have a good north/south angle. I would even say that it is the only place in India with such big N/S dry ranges to the west AND to the east. Differentiations:

metas.name: India - Landscape - Chaukhamba
metas.description: Chaukhamba, located near the town of Ukhimath, is a mountain massif covered in snow which can be recognised by its three distinct peaks, with the centre peak being the tallest.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Coastal Andhra Pradesh
metas.description: Coastal Andhra Pradesh is characterized by a flat, agricultural landscape with coastal bushes
metas.comparison: 50/50 Tip ! Similar bushes can also be found in Gujarat, but Gujarat will often have distinct holey poles or have a boxy car. Also, Gujarat will primarily have date palms whereas Andhra will have palmyra palms as the main occurrence in palm trees. The harder rounds in Andhra are the coastal, agricultural ones without any Palmyra or any pole. This basically becomes a 50/50 with any other flat & agricultural state.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Dark Soil
metas.description: Distinctly dark soil is mainly found in Maharashtra and adjacent regions.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Dark Soil - Karnataka
metas.description: Dark soil in India is usually found in and around Maharashtra.
metas.comparison: In many cases you can see trident poles together with this dark soil, which will put you in Northern Karnataka, usually near the Maha border (free 4.5k+)

metas.name: India - Landscape - Dry Ganges River Valley
metas.description: Southern Haryana and Southern Uttar Pradesh are very agricultural, but often still look dry. These areas look like a mix of Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Dry Mountains
metas.description: In Ladakh and northern Himachal Pradesh you can find an extremely dry landscape with little to no vegetation within the Himalayan mountains.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Dry TG/AP
metas.description: If you have a Telangana/Andra pole or Telugu with a dry landscape, you are likely in the area between Anantapur, AP and Shadnagar, TG (see image)

metas.name: India - Landscape - Elevated Dry Road
metas.description: Elevated Roads (similar to Bangladesh), with a dry landscape, are common in and around Jharkhand.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Elevated Jammu & Kashmir
metas.description: While a lot of the coverage in Jammu is located in flat parts, there are some areas north and northeast of the city of Jammu with elevation, where you will be able to see a lot of pines.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Ganges River Valley
metas.description: The northern plains, also known as the Ganges River Valley, of India are very fertile with extremely flat and open agricultural fields.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: Agriculture can be found in many parts of India. I think what sets apart these Northern Plains is the lack of palm trees (except for the occasional date palms and the Palmyra palm spam in Bihar).

metas.name: India - Landscape - Gujarat - Dead Landscape
metas.description: Salt flats and coastal marshes with nearly no vegetation, other than short yellow or brown grass, can be found in parts of Gujarat. Shallow bodies of water can often be seen around these areas.
metas.comparison: NOTE: The soil in western Rajasthan will be a lot more sandy and youâll typically be able to see short desert shrubs.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Guntur Landscape
metas.description: Around Guntur in Andhra Pradesh, you can find a landscape that combines the Andhra Pradesh Panhandle and the agricultural east coast further south.
metas.comparison: You will have lots of agriculture (more than in Panhandle) and also many palm trees (more than in the coastal region further south).

metas.name: India - Landscape - Haryana - North Haryana vibes
metas.description: The northern part of Haryana is very green and agricultural.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: Ganges River Valley in general looks like this, but I feel like this area is even greener and lusher, and it also has more sugarcane.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Himachal Pradesh - North/South Valley
metas.description: The city of Manali is fairly recognizable due to it being one of the two areas with coverage in a recognizable north-south valley. The other is from Kullu to Nagwain 50 km south of it.
metas.comparison: The only way I came up with to tell the 2 apart is the vegetation but this is kinda fake since both cities are located in the same valley. According to me, Manali has poplar trees and pines within the city whereas the other area doesnât have much of those and mostly consists of random trees.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Himalayas
metas.description: The by far tallest mountains in India are found in the Himalayas.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Ladakh - Snow Coverage
metas.description: Coverage extends to roads that are very high in altitude, so snow can be visible on the end of the streetview east of Leh.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Madhya - Elevated
metas.description: There are a few places where you can have elevation in Madhya Pradesh. The main elevation areas are around Yawal and satpura park, as well as south of Indore

metas.name: India - Landscape - Madhya Pradesh - Red Soil
metas.description: Within Madhya Pradesh, a reddish or pinkish soil is generally more common towards the East.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Maharashtra West Coast
metas.description: The landscape west of the Western Ghatts in Maharashtra is quite unique. It has a lot of forests, and a dark brown soil. It's mostly a vibe thing, but it looks kinda like Kerala but with less palms.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Mechuka Valley
metas.description: The Mechuka valley is the only place in Northeast India where snowy mountains are visible. The valley contains brownish grass and a plethora of Bhutan white pine. North of Mechuka the coverage gradually becomes overcast and somewhat dark.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Meghalaya Hills
metas.description: The landscape in Mizoram mainly consists of lush, green valleys with fairly low vegetation with eroded, smooth hillsides with a flat top.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Mizoram Hills
metas.description: The landscape in Mizoram mainly consists of lush, green valleys with fairly low vegetation with eroded hillsides having many small peaks scattered around.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Monoliths
metas.description: Near the southern tip of Tamil Nadu, you can find these large monolithic mountains, with huge exposed rocks. Several of these mountains can be seen from afar, especially the Magenthiragiri hills.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Mountains in Tamil Nadu
metas.description: Mountains in Tamil Nadu can be found along the western border. Additionally, there's a lot of mountains west of Madurai and some east of Salem.

metas.name: India - Landscape - NH3 between Gramphu and Dalang
metas.meta_label: Landscape - NH3 between Gramphu and Dalang
metas.description:
This section of road  features huge mountains, with a little bit more **green on their slopes.
**

metas.name: India - Landscape - Panhandle Andhra Pradesh
metas.description: The panhandle of Andhra Pradesh looks quite different than the rest of the state. It is much greener (and has an arguably "darker greener" tone). There are also A LOT more coconut palms here than anywhere else in AP.
metas.comparison: Other parts of Andhra Pradesh do have Palmyra Palms, but Coconut palms are kinda rare outside of the panhandle. The area south of Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh can also look extremely similar, but it has a lot less coverage.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Punjab - Elevated
metas.description: Punjab is generally a very flat state. If you know you're in Punjab, but it's hilly or mountains, you're on the border to Himachal Pradesh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rajasthan - Mountains
metas.description: The biggest mountainous areas in Rajasthan are around Alwar max northeast and Udaipur - Mount Abu area

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rajasthan - NorthEast Ridge
metas.description: In Rajasthan, there is a North-east angled ridge going from Mount Abu area to New Delhi

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rajasthan - Rolling Hills
metas.description: In Rajasthan, rolling hills are common for the area south of Udaipur

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rajasthan Vibes
metas.description: Rajasthan is a state that is drier than its surrounding states. It's difficult to explain, but many locs in Rajasthan just have a certain 'drier' vibe. If you saw this loc and thought 'This looks like Rajasthan', pat yourself on the back :)

metas.name: India - Landscape - Red soil
metas.description: Red soil can be found in several regions, but mainly near the southern west coast and in and around Chhattisgarh and western Odisha.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rewa Ridge
metas.description: A pretty straight east-west range with a slight north east angle can be found near Rewa. It is fairly easy to recognize.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rockiness
metas.description: Telangana and Andra Pradesh have a lot of ârockinessâ. It can be rocks on the side of the road, boulders or even rocky hill slopes but they share that in common.
metas.comparison: I found it to be more in Telangana so the meta is here, but note that it can extend to surrounding states of Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. Note by MB: In my experience, in AP, rockiness is very common west of the ridge from Tirupati to Nallamala Forest.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rural Manipur Landscape
metas.description: Since Imphal is located in a valley, it is fairly simple to recognize it after a few games.
metas.comparison: The landscape around the city consists of agricultural fields surrounded by mountains, so it is pretty easy to know you are in Imphal.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Snow Coverage in the Mountains
metas.meta_label: Landscape - Snow Coverage in the Mountains
metas.description: This coverage can be found on the 3 in Himachal Pradesh near the Ladakh border.
metas.comparison: The coverange extends from Zing Zing Bar to Killingsarai

metas.name: India - Landscape - Southern Tamil Nadu Red Soil
metas.meta_label: Landscape - Southern Tamil Nadu Red Soil
metas.description: A flat, bushy landscape with very red soil can be found in southern Tamil Nadu.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Spiti River Valley
metas.description: The shape of the mountains iin this valley are truly unique : very dry, very high in elevation and sparsely green.
metas.comparison: If you have trouble making the difference between this road and the NH3 to the west because it looks roughly similar, just know that the NH3 is paved whilst the Spiti river valley roads usually are not.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Tirupati
metas.description:
The city of Tirupati, AP can easily be recognized by the huge ridge in the North.
Other metas, like black&yellow Tuk-Tuks, two-indent poles or simply Telugu language, can help confirm.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Western Ganges River Valley
metas.description: The western Ganges River Valley (Punjab/Haryana/Western UP) usually looks wetter and greener than the general Ganges River Valley. You can often see rice and sugarcane. Note that areas like this can still be found in other parts of the river valley, this is not a 100% meta

metas.name: India - Landscape - Western Ghats
metas.description: The Western Ghats Mountains in the western part of Maharashtra can be recognised by their distinct ridgelines, often having plateaus rather than peaks. The northern part is drier while the southern part has more vegetation.
metas.comparison: NOTE: During the rainy season the mountains will turn green and appear quite different.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Western Meghalaya Landscape
metas.description: The western part of Meghalaya basically looks like bangladesh with hills. There are a lot of areca palms, banana trees and palms.
metas.comparison: âHilly forests with areca palms surrounding flat agricultural fieldsâ is how I would best describe this part of Meghalaya.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Western Rajasthan Landscape
metas.description: The western parts of Rajasthan can commonly be recognised by the dry landscape with sandy soil.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Western Uttarakhand Landscape
metas.description: The western half of Uttarakhand is typically far more barren than the other Himalayan regions, due to logging and erosion. The coverage northwest of Dehradun on the Himachal Pradesh Border has some especially barren hills full of brown grass and small roads next to cliffs.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Wonky Hills
metas.description: The Odisha Hills are very "wonky", i.e. they're undulating and can also very greatly in height.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Yawal Wildlife Sanctuary
metas.description: Unique hilly landscape with dead trees. Note that not all coverage in this park looks like this.

metas.name: India - Language - Assamese
metas.description: Assamese, mainly found in Assam, also uses the Bengali script, with the addition of some characters, most notably à§° and à§±.

metas.name: India - Language - Bengali
metas.description: Bengali is found in northeastern India and has a similar look to Devanagari (Hindi), however it can usually be recognised by the many letters featuring left-facing triangular shapes.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This is also the language found in Bangladesh.

metas.name: India - Language - Devanagari Script
metas.description: Hindi is the most common language in India and can be found in many central and northern regions. It uses the Devanagari script, which can be recognised by the line going through the top of each word and the straight vertical lines found in the majority of all letters.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: Maharashtra has a different language that uses the same script.

metas.name: India - Language - Gujarati
metas.description: Gujarati, found in Gujarat, has a script with several similarities to the Hindi script, however it notably lacks the horizontal line at the top of every word.

metas.name: India - Language - Kannada
metas.description: Kannada is found in Karnataka and has a script with a lot of smooth curves and small circles. It is very similar to the Telugu script, with Telugu having one additional feature described in the next tip. Many characters also feature a distinct squiggly tail in the top right corner, which is less common in Telugu.

metas.name: India - Language - Malayalam
metas.description: The Malayalam script can be found in Kerala and mostly consists of somewhat simple-looking curvy letters, often containing upside-down U-shapes.

metas.name: India - Language - Marathi
metas.description: Marathi, found in Maharashtra, also uses the Devanagari script, however it sometimes uses the letter à¤³  which is not found in Hindi.
metas.comparison: Further differences, analyzed by MB:

metas.name: India - Language - Meitei
metas.description: Manipuri, also called Meitei, is the official language of Manipur. It is written using the Meitei script, which can be recognised by its many vertical lines and right angles.

metas.name: India - Language - Mizo
metas.description: Mizo, found in Mizoram, is the language most commonly found on the Indian coverage other than English, which uses the Latin script.

metas.name: India - Language - Only English
metas.description: The state of Meghalaya uses English primarily and no other scripts. Thus if you see a lot of signs and no non-english language, you are most likely in Meghalaya.

metas.name: India - Language - Oriya
metas.description: The Oriya script is found in Odisha and has a curvy look, with many letters having wide semi-circles covering the top. Many letters have a distinct diacritic in the shape of a wide curve above the top of the letter. A useful mnemonic is that the shape of the characters resembles a skull emoji .

metas.name: India - Language - Punjabi
metas.description: Punjabi can be found in Punjab in northwestern India. While the script looks somewhat similar to Hindi, it can generally be differentiated by the softer shape of the letters and the horizontal bar being broken over certain letters. It also has some distinctly different features, such as the letters à¨¨, à¨² and à¨  as well as a diacritic in the shape of a soft curve beneath a letter.

metas.name: India - Language - Tamil
metas.description: The Tamil script is found in Tamil Nadu and has a distinct combination of curves, straight lines and 90Â° angles. Some letters also have diacritics shaped like dots.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Tamil is also commonly found in Sri Lanka.

metas.name: India - Language - Telugu
metas.description: Telugu, found in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, has a script very similar to Kannada, but youâll often see diacritics resembling checkmarks at the top of letters.

metas.name: India - Misc - AGP
metas.description: The AGP's flag is an elephant on the dutch flag.
metas.comparison: It operates only in Assam.

metas.name: India - Misc - BGPM
metas.description: Yellow - Grey - Dark Red Flag with a nice landscape in the middle and some Devanagari (!) text at the top.
metas.comparison: Found in West Bengal near the Sikkim border.

metas.name: India - Misc - BJP
metas.description:
BJP is one of the most popular national parties in India. You can find its flags basically everywhere.
However, they are less popular in Tamil Nadu and Kerala, meaning their flags are rare there.
metas.comparison: Their symbol is a lotus flower.

metas.name: India - Misc - BJP Spam
metas.description: The BJP is a popular national party, and thus it's flags can be found everywhere. Their symbol is a lotus flower.
metas.comparison: It is most popular in Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Odisha, so if you see a lot of BJP flags in one pano, you are likely to be in this belt.

metas.name: India - Misc - Black & Yellow Taxis
metas.description: Black Taxis with yellow roofs are found in Meghalaya and Mumbai.

metas.name: India - Misc - Bodoland People's Front
metas.description: This flag with this tool on an Indian background is found in Bodoland, which consists of the districts in Assam bordering Bhutan.

metas.name: India - Misc - Communism
metas.description: Communist symbolism is mostly found in Kerala. Second mostly, but significantly less, it's found in Tamil Nadu. Sometimes, it's also found in Tripura, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh. You can rarely spot it in Maharashtra, West Bengal, Assam and Manipur.
metas.comparison: The communist party has a youth organisation, the DYFI, with the same distribution.

metas.name: India - Misc - DMK
metas.description: Black and red colored flag. Other objects in this colors are also commonly found in the state of Tamil Nadu.

metas.name: India - Misc - Donyi Polo
metas.description: This flag that resembles the Japanese flag stands for Donyi Polo, a religion found in Arunachal Pradesh between Ziro and Anini.

metas.name: India - Misc - Gandhi Topi
metas.description: This hat is called the Gandhi Topi is almost unique to Maharashtra. Note the shape which resembles a boat.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: White hats in general are a common attire for Muslims in India, so make sure it's the boat shape.

metas.name: India - Misc - Gorkha Seperatist Flag
metas.description: The flag is green-white-yellow and can be found in West Bengal near the Sikkim Border.

metas.name: India - Misc - IELTS
metas.description: Advertisements for IELTS-exams are relatively often seen between Punjab and Western Uttar Pradesh
metas.comparison: Note by MB: Of course, advertisements like this can theoretically be found everywhere.

metas.name: India - Misc - INC
metas.description: INC is a popular national party, and found almost everywhere. The notable exceptions are West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh, where the INC has regional versions, meaning you won't find any INC imagery there.
metas.comparison: Their symbol is a flat hand facing you, on the background of the Indian tricolor.

metas.name: India - Misc - India Union Muslim League
metas.description: Green flag with half moon and star, pointing at the top left corner.
metas.comparison: This party is almost exclusively active in Kerala. Mostly in the districts of Kozhikode and Malappuram.

metas.name: India - Misc - Jainism
metas.description: Jainism is a pretty rare minority religion. Jainist symbols are found mostly in Maharashtra, then Gujarat and Rajasthan, then Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka.

metas.name: India - Misc - Janata Dal
metas.description: Flag is green-white-green, the symbol is an arrow.
metas.comparison: Found only in Bihar.

metas.name: India - Misc - Karbi Colors
metas.description: The Karbi are an ethnic group that inhabit two districts in Assam, Karbi Anglong and West Karbi Anglong.
metas.comparison: Their flag is rarely shown, but you can often find Karbi colors (dark red, black and white) in those districts.

metas.name: India - Misc - Karnataka Flag
metas.description: This is an unofficial flag of Karnataka.

metas.name: India - Misc - Kongunadu Makkal Desia Katchi
metas.description: Flag of a political party active only in Tamil Nadu

metas.name: India - Misc - Lungi
metas.description: People wearing a Lungi, which looks like a towel wrapped around the waist, are more common in South India.

metas.name: India - Misc - Manithaneya Makkal Katchi
metas.description: Flag of a political party only active in Tamil Nadu.

metas.name: India - Misc - Meitei Flag
metas.description: The Meitei people inhabit Manipur state, especially Imphal. Their flag is commonly found in and around that city.

metas.name: India - Misc - Naam Tamilar Katchi
metas.description: Flag of a political party only active in Tamil Nadu.
metas.comparison: The tiger symbol can sometimes be found without the flag.

metas.name: India - Misc - Navayana Buddhism
metas.description: This blue flag with this symbol in the middle is specific for Navayana Buddhism, the branch of Buddhism common in Central-Eastern Maharashtra.

metas.name: India - Misc - Odisha Shell (Political Party)
metas.description:
This shell is the symbol of a Odisha specific political party:
Biju Janata Dal

metas.name: India - Misc - Samajwadi Party
metas.description: Exclusive to Uttar Pradesh, their symbol is a bicycle.

metas.name: India - Misc - Sarnaism
metas.description: This flag and this symbol stand for Sarnaism. They are very localized, found in Ranchi and in Southern Jharkhand.

metas.name: India - Misc - Scarfs
metas.description: People wearing colorful scarfs are generally found in the north of India.

metas.name: India - Misc - Shivaji
metas.description: Shivaji is a person often depicted on statues in Maharashtra. He is always riding a horse, and is often accompanied by an orange flag.

metas.name: India - Misc - SKM
metas.description: This party has an orange-red-green flag and a table lamp as a symbol. It operates exclusively in Sikkim.

metas.name: India - Misc - Trinamool Congress / CMT
metas.description: The flag of this party often has these flowers on some grass with the Indian flag as background.
metas.comparison:
It can be found mainly in West Bengal, however less commonly in the Northern Parts.
Sometimes it's also found in Western Meghalaya

metas.name: India - Misc - Tripra Mothi
metas.description: Tripra Mothi is a Tripura-specific party. Its flag has two vertical stripes, yellow and red.
metas.comparison: Don't confuse it with the Karnataka flag, where the stripes are horizontal.

metas.name: India - Misc - UPPL
metas.description:
The flag of UPPL is yellow white green with a farmer on a tractor on it.
Found in Bodoland, which consists of the Assamese districts bordering Bhutan.
metas.comparison: Don't confuse this with the Gorkha seperatist flag, which is green-white-yellow.

metas.name: India - Misc - VCK
metas.description: Blue and red flag with a Myanmar-style star, found only in Tamil Nadu.

metas.name: India - Misc - YSR Congress
metas.description: This party is exclusive to Andhra Pradesh, and most popular in the South. Their symbol is a ceiling fan.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Agave
metas.description: Agaves are mostly found in Karnataka
metas.comparison: Note by MB: This is generally a fake meta, Agaves can be found in many different places throughout India. But if you have really nothing else to go off, Karnataka is definitely a place to conside.r

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Areca Palm
metas.description: Areca Palms can be recognised by their very thin trunk and a small crown.
metas.comparison: They are most common in Assam, but also in other northeastern areas, stretiching to coastal Odisha. A second common region is Kerala and coastal Karnataka

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Assam - White Flowers
metas.description: In Assam, these white flowers can often be seen along the road in three areas: - The border to West Bengal - The border to Eastern Bhutan - West of Nagaon.

metas.description: Recognition (most visible when you look at the bottom of the crown):

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Calotropis Procera
metas.description: Calotropis Procera is found all over Rajasthan and less in surrounding states so it is a good clue for Rajasthan if you have a lot of it.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Chir Pines
metas.description: Recognition

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Coconut Palms
metas.description:
Coconut palms are most common in Kerala, the Western Half of Karnataka and Southern Coastal Maharashtra
In general, they appear near Coasts, near the border to Bangladesh, and anywhere South of Central Telangana

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Combination of Date Palm & Palmyra Palm
metas.meta_label: Vegetation - Combination of Date Palm & Palmyra Palm
metas.description: In Jharkhand, you will very often see the combination of date palms (a lot of them) and palmyra palms. I think it is one of the best clues for getting Jharkhand because itâs pretty unique. I also saw a lot of that combination of palms in Telangana so be careful and look for text before guessing.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Date Palm
metas.description: Date palms can be found in Central India. They appear North of the Latitude of Chhattisgarh, except for Himalayan states, the Northeast and Western Gujarat/RJ.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Date Palm - Tamil Nadu
metas.description: Within Tamil Nadu, date palms can be found in the North-East.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Dead Trees
metas.description: These 'dead'-looking trees are a very strong point to go to Rajasthan. They are concentrated mostly southwest of Sikar.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Doum Palm
metas.description: Doum palms, which appear similar to Palmyra palms but with multiple branches, are almost exclusive to the union territory of Diu.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Eucalyptus
metas.description: Eucalyptus trees are a good clue for the Uttarakhand foothills and nearby areas in Uttar Pradesh.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Euphorbia Neriifolia
metas.description: This type of cacti (Euphorbia neriifolia) can commonly be seen as part of fences throughout Gujarat, western Maharashtra and the southern half of Rajasthan.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Euphorbia Neriifolia (Hilly Landcape)
metas.description: South of Udaipur, you can find a very distinct landscape with narrow hills and a lot of this type of cactus (Euphorbia).

metas.description: Recognition:

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Indian Pitcher Plant
metas.description: The endangered Indian pitcher plant is exclusive to the Khasi Hills, which are mainly in Meghalaya. They can occasionally be spotted on road sides, especially on the NH206 north of UmlÄrem.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Jand Tree
metas.description: This tree, often called Jand by Indians, can be recognized by the clusters of leaves at the end of thick branches.
metas.comparison: It is found in Northern Rajasthan and Southern Haryana/Punjab.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Japanese Cedar
metas.description: Recognition:
metas.comparison: Found in:

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Macaranga Peltata
metas.description: Parasol leaf tree (Macaranga peltata) is common along the southwestern coast anywhere south of Mumbai and seems to be virtually exclusive to that area, I have yet to find it anywhere else in India. To identify it, look for the teardrop shape of the leaves and the spot where the leaf stem connects to the inner part of the leaf blade.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Palmyra Palms
metas.description: Palmyra Palms have a round crown with fan shaped leaves and a trunk with consistent thickness, giving them a lollipop shape.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Prickly Pear Cactus
metas.description: Found in Gujarat, mainly at the southern peninsula (could be fake)

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Rajasthan - Euphorbia Neriifolia (Flat)
metas.description: West of Mount Abu, you can find a lot of Euphorbia cacti with flat landscape. Note that this meta is only specific for Rajasthan, Euphorbia appears in other states, like Gujarat, too.

metas.description: Recognition:
metas.comparison: Extremely rare in India, so far only a singular tree has been found in Manda La.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Teak Forest
metas.description: Teak forests in wet season with boxy car can be found around the Gujarat-Maharashtra border between Surat and Nashik. The trees are quite distinctive, tall and narrow.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Telangana - Coconut Palms
metas.description: If you see a Coconut, hedge in the south eastern half towards Andhra Pradesh, it has more of them.

metas.name: Indonesia - Agriculture - Cassava
metas.description: Cassava (Manihot esculenta) can be recognised by its small, hand-shaped leaves. It can be found both in plantations as well as semi-wild in residential areas. It is most commonly seen in Lampung and Java with Lampung being the main hot spot.

metas.name: Indonesia - Agriculture - Oil Palms
metas.description: Within Indonesia, oil palm plantations are mostly concentrated in Sumatra and Kalimantan. Palm plantations can rarely be seen in Sulawesi.

metas.name: Indonesia - Agriculture - Rice
metas.description: The majority of rice production is concentrated in Java, but can sometimes be found in other provinces, namely South Sulawesi and South Sumatra. They can rarely be found in other provinces as well.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Andesite
metas.description: Andesite, a dark, volcanic rock, is a common building material in Bali. You can often see gates, walls, and other intricately carved ornaments built from this material.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Bali Architecture
metas.description: Architecture in Bali is unique because it was influenced by old Balinese culture and Hinduism. The most important thing to look for are these crown-like roof pinnacles, found everywhere in Bali. Guardian statues and slit-drum towers are common too.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Boat Roof - Not Spiky
metas.description: North Sumatra features similarly distinct boat-shaped roofs, however the roofs are less angled upward and they do not feature spires.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These roofs are most commonly found near Lake Toba, due to its sacred history.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Boat Roof - Spiky
metas.description: West Sumatra features these distinct boat-shaped roofs.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Flat Tiles
metas.description: The tiles on roofs in South Kalimantan and Jambi look slightly different. The tiles are usually less rounded but flatter.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Horny Roof
metas.description: Roofs with gable horns can be found most commonly in South Sulawesi, Riau and Central and South Kalimantan.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Horned roofs are often found with Bugis roofs in South Sulawesi. Use this tip along with other clues to determine which region you are in.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Java Roof
metas.description: Tiled roofs are most commonly found on the island of Java, and sometimes nearby regions such as southern Sumatra, the Lesser Sunda Islands, and South Kalimantan.
metas.comparison: NOTE: The tiles on roofs in South Kalimantan and Jambi look slightly different. The tiles are usually less rounded but flatter.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Malay Canopies
metas.description: In the regions of Sumatra and Kalimantan that lie opposite Malaysia, many buildings have metal canopies with curved ends. These canopies are often blue or red.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Nias Roof
metas.description: Steeply pitched roofs made of palm tree leaves can sometimes be seen on Nias Island, south west of North Sumatra.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Sheet Roofs
metas.description: Plain sheet metal roofs are more commonly found toward the north, where tiled roofs are not found. They are most commonly found on Kalimantan, Sulawesi and Sumatra.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - South Sula House
metas.description: These horizontal slots inside the triangles of the roofs are almost unique to Southern Sulawesi.
metas.comparison: NOTE: They can rarely be found in East Kalimantan and West Nusa.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Sumba Roof
metas.description: You can find these distinct roofs with uniquely high-pitched peaks on Sumba.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Tongkonan
metas.description: A small region of South Sulawesi, around the city of Rante Pao, features these very unique houses, called Tongkonan, that have saddle-shaped roofs. The houses themselves are also elevated from the ground.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Wooden Chips Roof
metas.description: On Kalimantan, you can find these unique roofs made out of wooden chips.

metas.name: Indonesia - Car Meta - Gen 3 Antenna
metas.description: Generation 3 antenna coverage is most commonly found on Java, but can very rarely be seen on Bali in and around Denpasar. It is most commonly seen in East Java, as most of the antenna coverage in the west has been overwritten by Generation 4.

metas.name: Indonesia - Car Meta - Gen 3 Black
metas.description: Black Generation 3 coverage can be found almost everywhere in Indonesia, but is most common in Sulawesi.

metas.name: Indonesia - Car Meta - Jagasatru Car
metas.description: A black cab with men sitting in the truck bed can be seen near Jagasatru on Bali.

metas.name: Indonesia - Car Meta - Wooden Plank Car
metas.description: A white SUV with black bars and a wooden plank on the roof can rarely be seen in eastern Bali.

metas.name: Indonesia - Coverage Meta - Pink Air
metas.description: In some of the Generation 4 coverage in the city of Batam, a purple tint and a black blurred object can be seen. Although this camera glitch is most commonly found in Batam, you may spot it in nearby regions such as North Sumatra, around Medan. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Cigarette Blocks
metas.description: Central Sulawesi features these unique bollards that are painted black on the bottom, white in the middle, and yellow on the top.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Even Pole
metas.description: Indonesia uses two types of pole tops: even and uneven. This refers to the bar that holds the insulators and whether it is symmetrical to the pole itself. Knowing where even and uneven poles are most commonly found is useful for region guessing.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Green Bridge
metas.description: Green paint can often be seen on the side of bridges in South and Central Kalimantan.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Indented Pole
metas.description: Poles with an indent on both sides are found in West Java, Jakarta, and Banten.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - North Sumatra Pole
metas.description: These poles are almost exclusive to North Sumatra. The bar which holds the insulators is even, but features uneven insulators with one on one side and two on the other.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Nusa Pole
metas.description: On the Lesser Sunda Islands ('Nusas'), you can find poles with an extra long support on the pole top. Sometimes, two supports can be present.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Pole Tape
metas.description: You can often see thin, black poles next to regular poles near the East Peninsula of Central Sulawesi. Two pieces of tape can be seen near the top of the poles, usually light blue and green. These can rarely be seen in northern South East Sulawesi.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Rectangle Attachment
metas.description: Bali features both even and uneven poles, as well as the Lesser Sunda island variants. You can also find this unique rectangle attachment on the pole tops in Bali.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Sulawesi Fences
metas.description: These painted fences are typically found on Sulawesi. They will be mostly painted white with blue or red.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Surabaya Pavement
metas.description: Pavement made out of bricks like this is found in East Java, particularly around Surabaya

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Trapezoid Pole
metas.description: Pole tops in North and Central Sulawesi, and Gorontalo commonly feature an extra attachment right under the horizontal bar.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Triangle Attachment
metas.description: You can find these poles with a triangle attachment under the horizontal bar in the following regions.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This does not apply to stacked poles.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Trident Pole
metas.description: Trident style pole tops are most commonly found in Central Java and Yogyakarta, and rarely in South and West Kalimantan, and North Sumatra and Riau.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Uneven Pole
metas.description: Indonesia uses two types of pole tops: even and uneven. This refers to the bar that holds the insulators and whether it is symmetrical to the pole itself. Knowing where even and uneven poles are most commonly found is useful for region guessing.

metas.name: Indonesia - Landscape - Dryness
metas.description: The Nusas typically look drier than other regions in Indonesia. The islands get especially dry towards the east, especially in Generation 3. Vegetation tends to look less tropical, but instead more brown with a lack of leaves. Sumba Island is also the driest of the Nusas.
metas.comparison: NOTE: While less common, other regions such as Java can look similarly dry. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

metas.name: Indonesia - Landscape - Lake Toba
metas.description: The region around Lake Toba, in North Sumatra, can be recognized by mountains surrounding the lake and Samosir Island in the middle. Overcast coverage is also common for the region.

metas.name: Indonesia - Landscape - Palu Bay
metas.description: Palu Bay is a unique slightly north-west facing bay just north of Palu city, which features mountains to the west of the bay, and a flat, more urbanised landscape to the east.

metas.name: Indonesia - Landscape - Red Soil
metas.description: Red soil can often be found on Batam and the Bangka Belitung islands, located east of mainland Sumatra.

metas.name: Indonesia - Landscape - Savannah
metas.description: This savannah landscape is occasionally seen on North Sumba.
metas.comparison: NOTE: In Generation 3, you will always see a white car.

metas.name: Indonesia - Misc - Christianity
metas.description: Indonesia is religiously a Muslim majority country, so seeing churches, and other Christian signs, is a good clue for these regions.

metas.name: Indonesia - Vegetation - Areca
metas.description: Areca palms (Areca catechu) are most prominent in western Sumatra; however they can also be seen elsewhere less commonly. They can be recognised by their relatively short and thick leaves.

metas.name: Indonesia - Vegetation - Coastal She-Oak
metas.description: Coastal she-oak (Casuarina equisetifolia) can be found along the coast throughout much of the country, but particularly in Sumatra, Kalimantan and Java. Their leaves resemble the needles of pine trees, but are noticeably longer. Another species of she-oak can be found in mountainous regions throughout the country.

metas.name: Indonesia - Vegetation - Coconut
metas.description: Coconut palms (Cocos nucifera) can be found in many regions throughout Indonesia, but are most abundant along the coast, especially in western Sumatra, southern Java, northern Sulawesi and North Maluku.

metas.name: Indonesia - Vegetation - Footstool Palm
metas.description: Footstool palm (Saribus rotundifolius) has fan-shaped leaves similar to those of Palmyra palm; however the crown is more open, the leaves are thinner and the palm itself is usually taller. It can be found most notably in Sulawesi and more rarely in other parts of the country.

metas.name: Indonesia - Vegetation - Gebang Palm
metas.description: Gebang palm (Corypha utan) can at first glance look similar to both Palmyra and footstool palm due to its fan-shaped leaves, however the leaves are noticeably larger, stiffer and more upright in contrast to the round crown shape of both Palmyra and footstool palm. Unlike most palms, the gebang palm will only flower once at the end of its life in a dramatic gesture where the leaves wither away and it shoots one large inflorescence into the heavens before it dies. It is found mainly in the east of the country, namely Sulawesi and the Nusas.

metas.name: Indonesia - Vegetation - Milkweed
metas.description: Giant milkweed (Calotropis gigantea) is a small shrub with thick round leaves and pale flowers. It can be found in dry regions of Indonesia, namely the Nusas and parts of Java and Sulawesi.

metas.name: Indonesia - Vegetation - Palmyra
metas.description: Palmyra palms (Borassus flabellifer) can be recognised by their fan-shaped leaves and dense round crowns. Compared to footstool palm, the crown is more dense, the leaves are heavier and the palm itself is usually shorter. It is found in dry parts of the country, namely the Nusas and South Sulawesi.

metas.name: Indonesia - Vegetation - Sumatran Pine
metas.description: Sumatran pines (Pinus merkusii) in Indonesia can be found in a few pockets across the country, notable areas include North Sumatra and Java. They can be recognised by having long needles for leaves, but be careful not to confuse them with she-oak, which has even longer leaves.

metas.name: Indonesia - Vegetation - White Leadtree
metas.description: White leadtree (Leucaena leucocephala) can be recognised by its delicate featherlike (bipinnate) leaves. Fruits are often also visible in the form of legume pods. It can be found mainly in the Nusas as well as a few other dry areas of the country.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 29 in Ad Dhakhiliyah
metas.description: The southern section of Road 29 only has a middle white line, which along with the greyish and sandy desert landscape makes this road unique.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 31 (divided)
metas.description: The divided section of Road 31 is the only divided road going through a flat desert landscape.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 31 (single lane)
metas.description: This long stretch of Road 31 can be recognised by the light-coloured flat desert landscape along with the wide shoulders and the often faded road lines. The weather is usually somewhat cloudy.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 37 (Powerline)
metas.description: Road 37 travels in a generally northwest direction through a very generic, flat desert landscape. The angle is one of the best clues for this road. On the southern half, a big power line is visible to the northeast.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 39 (flat)
metas.description: Road 39 is also one of the more generic roads. Probably the best way to recognise it are the narrow, or even non-existent shoulders.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 39 (hilly)
metas.description: Road 39 is also one of the more generic roads. Probably the best way to recognise it are the narrow, or even non-existent shoulders. The western parts can get quite hilly

metas.name: Infrastructure - 42 north of Shalim
metas.description: North of Shalim Road 42 turns into a very wide unpaved road, with the soil being quite light in colour. Youâll sometimes see oil drills in the distance along this stretch.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bin Color - Black
metas.description: Black Bins can be found everywhere except for Batina North. They're also rarely found in South-Dhakiliyah.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Even the dark blue and red regions are not 100% a certain colour.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bin Color - Grey
metas.description: Grey Bins can be found in Dharihar, South Dhakhiliyah, Dhofar, Bathina North and west of Muscat.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Even the dark blue and red regions are not 100% a certain colour.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Bin / Black Sticker
metas.description: Black bins with a black sticker on the front can be found in Al Buraimi, Ash Sharqiyah North, and Muscat Governorates.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Bin / No Sticker
metas.description: Black bins without stickers are mainly found in Al Batinah South Governorate and north of Al Khaburah in Al Batinah North Governorate.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Black bins throughout Oman may appear like they lack stickers, so use this with caution.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Bin / White Sticker
metas.description: Black bins with a white sticker are found in Ad Dakhiliyah Governorate, southern Dhofar Governorate, and Muscat Governorate.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Western Bin
metas.description: Western-style small black bins are found in Muscat and eastern Al Batinah North Governorate.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Chevron Bin
metas.description: Bins in Muscat governorate often have white-and-red chevron-like stickers on the sides.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: 'often' really is an overstatement, definitely don't rule Muscat out if you don't have those stickers.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Fahud Road
metas.description: The road west of Fahud goes through a flat desert with pink-greyish soil. The road itself is in poor shape and without roadlines as well as the direction of the road being southeast.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Grey Bin / Black Sticker
metas.description: Grey bins with a black sticker on the front are found in Ad Dhahirah Governorate.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Grey Bin / No Sticker
metas.description: Grey bins without a sticker on the front are found in Al Batinah North Governorate.
metas.comparison: NOTE: They can have a sticker on the side.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Grey Bin / White Sticker
metas.description: Grey bins with a white sticker are commonly found in Ad Dakhiliyah Governorate, and sometimes in Dhofar Governorate.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Ibri Road
metas.description: The road going to Saudi Arabia from Ibri can be recognised by the completely flat desert landscape with bright pink-greyish soil along with the road having very wide shoulders and the overall great road condition. The southern portion goes in a straight northeast direction, and the northern section curves more and can have more shrubs.

metas.name: Infrastructure - License Plates - Assam
metas.description: Sometimes, unblurred license plates can be seen (particularly often on trucks). The first two letters give the state. The next two numbers give the district (really not worth learning)
metas.comparison: AS stands for Assam. The exception is license plates that do not start with letters or with T0. Those rarer license plates are national.

metas.name: Infrastructure - License Plates - Maharashtra
metas.description: Sometimes, unblurred license plates can be seen (particularly often on trucks). The first two letters give the state. The next two numbers give the district (really not worth learning)
metas.comparison: MH stands for Maharashtra. The exception is license plates that do not start with letters or with T0. Those rarer license plates are national.

metas.name: Infrastructure - North of Ubar Road
metas.description: The unlabelled road northwest of Ubar can be recognised by the small white markings between the dashes.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Oil Drills
metas.description: Oil drills are common around Amal and sometimes seen along Road 39.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Road to Yemen
metas.description: Just west of ÙÙØªØ§Ù, only labelled in Arabic on Google Maps, literally translating to methane, there is a stretch of road, which has a uniquely light-coloured pavement. To the north, you can see sand dunes.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Road west of Ubar
metas.description: West of Ubar, the 43 and the unlabelled road west of it are still unpaved but now have a power line to the north. The desert landscape has an orange tint to it.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Side Sticker
metas.description: Regardless of colour, if the bins have a sticker on the side, you should be in one of the North Coast governorates.

metas.name: Infrastructure - signpost with yellow sticker
metas.description: Signposts in the Northern Territory can feature these yellow stickers.

metas.name: Infrastructure - South-East of Ubar Road
metas.description: The road southeast of Ubar has a general northwest bound angle, along with a power line to the left of the road. You will often see signs of life in the form of farms or buildings on this road.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Donât mix this up with the 37, which has a similar angle, but is more desolate and can have sunset coverage.

metas.name: Infrastructure - State Flag - Arizona
metas.description: Each of the 50 states has its own state flag. These appear frequently enough that they are worth learning.

metas.name: Infrastructure - State Flags
metas.description: Each of the 50 states has its own state flag. These appear frequently enough that they are worth learning.

metas.name: Japan - Agriculture - Red Fields
metas.description: Agricultural fields with red soil are commonly found on several southern islands, most notably on the islands of Miyakojima and Ishigaki in southern Okinawa.

metas.name: Japan - Agriculture - Rice
metas.description: Rice is mainly produced north of Tokyo. During growth, it resembles straws of grass. And when ready for harvest, brown husks are visible. They are also commonly planted in beds of water.
metas.comparison: The regions of Chubu (21%), Kanto (15%), Tohoku (27%), and Hokkaido (7%) make up the majority of production.

metas.name: Japan - Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.description: Sugarcane is almost exclusively found on the islands in southern Kyushu and Okinawa.

metas.name: Japan - Agriculture - Tea
metas.description: Green tea plants are often grown in hedged rows. You will often see these fans mounted on poles, which serve the purpose of preventing frost from falling on the plants.
metas.comparison: The prefectures of Shizuoka (36%) and Kagoshima (34%) make up the majority of the production, with Mie (7%), Miyazaki (4%), and other prefectures (17%) making up the minority.

metas.name: Japan - Architecture - Northern Roofs
metas.description: The further you are north, roofs generally transition from tiled to level or flat sloped in order to compensate for heavy snowfall. Northern houses often have ladders attached to the side, giving roof access to clear snow.
metas.comparison: NOTE: In addition to north to south, high-elevation mountainous regions or high snowfall areas often use such roofs, even in more central or southern prefectures.

metas.name: Japan - Architecture - Okinawa House
metas.description: Okinawa can often be recognised by the white concrete buildings with flat roofs.

metas.name: Japan - Architecture - Red Tiled Roof
metas.description: These unique red-tiled roofs are most commonly found in Chugoku, especially in the prefectures of Hiroshima and Shimane.

metas.name: Japan - Architecture - Shisa
metas.description: You can find these âShisaâ guardian lions and house plaques with these specific characters in Okinawa. The colour and shapes of both can vary.

metas.name: Japan - Coverage Meta - Hokkaido Winter
metas.description: Hokkaido has very limited winter and snow coverage. Unless you are certain, it is often better not to guess this prefecture. Though, if you do find yourself in Hokkaido, these regions are most likely. Other low amounts of miscellaneous coverage is primarily in the southern half of the island.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Arrow
metas.description: This infrastructural arrow informs drivers of where the shoulder line is when under snow, and is located almost exclusively in Hokkaido.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Arrow - Bolts
metas.description: This arrow, found in the Aomori prefecture (or more rarely Hokkaido), has distinct silver bolts around the border.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Arrow - Long
metas.description: This variation, found in the Gifu prefecture, is long and thin.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Arrow - Northern 275
metas.description: This alternate yellow and black design can often be found on the northern part of National Highway 275 in Hokkaido.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Arrow - Yellow/Black
metas.description: This yellow and black arrow can be found on Hokkaido.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Arrow - Yellow/Green
metas.description: This yellow and green arrow is found southwest of Sapporo.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Birch Poles
metas.description: These artistically painted poles, made to resemble birch trees, are unique to the city of Date in Hokkaido.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Akita
metas.description: This bollard, much like Tohoku, will be a thick, white bollard with an octagonal reflector. However, this Akita prefecture variation will have two yellow stripes underneath the reflector.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Aomori
metas.description: This bollard, found in the Aomori prefecture, has two yellow stripes, a single circular reflector, and is extendable. Sometimes, only one thicker stripe near the top may be present.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Black Stripe
metas.description: Some bollards on the island of Shikoku can have a black stripe just under the reflector. They can be found normally, attached to guardrails or walls.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Extendable
metas.description: In the northern parts of the Chugoku region, you can primarily find these basic snow poles, with either a thin extended, or thin contracted top. They can also sometimes be found in Iwate.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Okoyama
metas.description: This bollard, with an octagonal reflector, and red stripe underneath it, is exclusive to the Okayama prefecture. Additionally, there will be a sloped connection where the base meets the reflector.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Orange Reflector
metas.description: This flat, white bollard, found on the island of Kyushu and in Yamaguchi Prefecture, will have a series of separated orange reflectors on one side, and the same white on the opposite.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Rarely, you may find similar bollards in Hokkaido. However, both sides will have orange reflectors.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Striped / No Reflector
metas.description: These striped bollards (which cover over the original) have a thinner top half, and no reflectors, and are common to the Tohoku region. They are especially common in Akita prefecture.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Tohoku
metas.description: This thick, white bollard, found in the Tohoku region, will have an octagonal reflector, and yellow stripe just underneath. In addition, you can find the same bollard, but with a rectangular top.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Tohoku (Black Variant)
metas.description: Additionally to regular Tohoku bollards, there are two other variations. You can find a black octagonal, and rectangular version. They are often found on National Highways or Expressways and can have the number printed on them.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Toyama
metas.description: The Toyama prefecture bollard has one reflector, is extendable and has a red stripe underneath the reflector.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Be careful: if there is either a second reflector, or a yellow stripe instead of a red one, these are different bollards. These are more common variations found across many prefectures.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Claymore
metas.description: Kerosine tanks, otherwise known as âClaymoresâ, can be found more commonly the further north you go. They are abundant in Hokkaido, but can be found in prefectures south of it, or in high elevation mountainous areas.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Ehime Cycling Route
metas.description: Cycling routes in Ehime use an outside white, with an inside blue line. They are more commonly found along the coast but may be found further inland too.
metas.comparison: While exceptions do exist, and can be found in other prefectures, they are the extreme minority.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Gas Tank
metas.description: Hot water, gas and propane tanks can be found more frequently in northern prefectures or high elevation mountainous areas. Here are a few common variations you can find:
metas.comparison: The standard hot water tank. Covered propane tanks. Exposed propane tanks. These cylindrical tanks. And finally, these circular tripod tanks. Moreover, these are even more common in rural towns or villages, where major water or gas lines are unavailable.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Guardrail - Green Band
metas.description: Green bands on guardrails are most commonly found in Oita and Miyazaki, but can be found on all of Kyushu.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Guardrail - Hokkaido Sticker
metas.description: You can find these chevron-like stickers, or more rarely orange ones, on guardrails in Hokkaido.
metas.comparison: On the end or side of a guardrail. Stuck to metal posts between wire fences, which are often found in Hokkaido. On railings, which are often found on bridges, underneath the inside of the railing.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Guardrail - Red-Yellow Stripes
metas.description: Guardrail endings with these red and yellow striped stickers can commonly be found across Chugoku, except in Yamaguchi. They can also rarely be found in Niigata.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Guardrail - Yellow
metas.description: These distinctive yellow guardrails can be found in the Yamaguchi Prefecture.

metas.description: Tokyo City features a nice manhole design, with a 5 petal flower and many small circles on the outside.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - 2 or 3 Insulators
metas.description: The transformers in Kanto, which can have three or two insulators, are often mounted on a wooden plate and two bars, or a round plate and a T-shaped bar.
metas.comparison: NOTE: While the Hokkaido transformer may also be mounted on two bars, it will never have a wooden plate. Kanto ones can also be mounted without a wooden plate.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Black Tap Connector
metas.description: The transformers in Chubu, which often have painted yellow numbers and black âtapâ connectors, are either attached with large triangle and horizontal bars, or these thin metal brackets.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Cross (Chugoku Variant)
metas.description: The transformers in Chugoku, which have a cross-shaped bar attached in the middle of the pole, mounted by a full triangle, will have a long horizontal or short vertical insulator(s) at the end.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Cross (Hat Insulator)
metas.description: The transformers in Shikoku, which also have a cross-shaped bar attached in the middle of the pole, mounted by a half triangle, will have âhat shapedâ short horizontal insulators at the end.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Insulator Box
metas.description: These grey âinsulator-esqueâ blocks, which wires are fed through, can be found in the regions of Chubu, Kansai, Chugoku, Shikoku, and very rarely in Hokkaido.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Kyushu
metas.description: The transformers in Kyushu, which have a straight bar attached on the side of the pole with three insulators at the end, will have transformers mounted 180-degrees from one another.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Lamp-Shaped Insulator
metas.description: The transformers in Hokuriku, which are attached with thin metal bars, often have these small âlampâ shaped insulators. There will never be a bar present except for the attachment mentioned above.
metas.comparison: NOTE: The prefecture of Niigata will have the Tohoku transformer design, as opposed to Hokuriku one.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Metal Bracket
metas.description: The transformers in Chubu, which often have painted yellow numbers and black âtapâ connectors, are either attached with large triangle and horizontal bars, or these thin metal brackets.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Okinawa
metas.description: Transformers in Okinawa, which have a T-shaped bar attached on the side of the pole, will have transformers mounted on opposite sides of the pole.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - One on Square
metas.description: In Tohoku, you may also find transformers mounted on the side of a square, with a straight bar mounted on the top of the square. Rarely, you may find a square without a bar.
metas.comparison: NOTE: While Kansai may have a square attachment as well, the bar will be mounted on the bottom rather than the top.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Plus-Shaped Bar
metas.description: The electrical poles in Hokkaido either have this plus-shaped bar attached to the side of the pole, or one transformer mounted on two bars.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Red Number
metas.description: In Chugoku, a white sticker will often be stuck to the bottom of the transformer with red numbers. They may also be painted on the side.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Round Plate / T-Bar
metas.description: The transformers in Kanto, which can have three or two insulators, are often mounted on a wooden plate and two bars, or a round plate and a T-shaped bar.
metas.comparison: NOTE: While the Hokkaido transformer may also be mounted on two bars, it will never have a wooden plate. Kanto ones can also be mounted without a wooden plate.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Round Plate / Zigzag Bar
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Transformer - Round Plate / Zigzag Bar
metas.description: The transformers in Tohoku, which often have additional square holding brackets and the logo of the Tohoku Electrical Company, are sometimes mounted on a round plate with a zigzag bar.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Square / Bottom Bar
metas.description: The transformers in Kansai have either a straight or zigzag bar mounted on the bottom of a square. The transformer(s) will be mounted on the sides of that same square.
metas.comparison: While this is uncommon, the bar and transformer(s) may be mounted on a vertical bar, rather than a square. NOTE: While Tohoku may have a square attachment as well, the bar will be mounted on the top rather than the bottom

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Triangle
metas.description: The transformers in Chubu, which often have painted yellow numbers and black âtapâ connectors, are either attached with large triangle and horizontal bars, or these thin metal brackets.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Two Bars
metas.description: The electrical poles in Hokkaido either have this plus-shaped bar attached to the side of the pole, or one transformer mounted on two bars. The Kanto Transformer may also be mounted on two bars.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Two on Square
metas.description: In Hokkaido, if there is more than one transformer, they will often be mounted on the sides of a square.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - White Sticker
metas.description: A white sticker will often be stuck to the bottom of the transformer with black numbers.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Wooden Plate
metas.description: The transformers in Kanto, which can have three or two insulators, are often mounted on a wooden plate and two bars, or a round plate and a T-shaped bar.
metas.comparison: NOTE: While the Hokkaido transformer may also be mounted on two bars, it will never have a wooden plate. Kanto ones can also be mounted without a wooden plate.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Tuning Fork - Chubu
metas.description: This tuning fork pole top, with a short top bar and horizontal bar below, is found the majority of the time in the Chubu region.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Tuning Fork - Kansai
metas.description: This tuning fork pole top, with a thin wire and horizontal bar below, is common in the Kansai region.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Tuning Fork - Kanto
metas.description: This tuning fork pole top, with a long top bar that sticks out each end and horizontal bar(s) below, is found the majority of the time in the Kanto region.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Vertical Traffic Light
metas.description: Vertical traffic lights can be found in Hokkaido, and along the northwestern coast. The usual horizontal traffic lights can be found everywhere else.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Yellow Circle Sign
metas.description: These specific black signs with two yellow circles are found in Kagawa. Other variations can be seen, including them stacked on top of each other, or with an arrow attached above.

metas.name: Japan - Landscape - Mount Fuji
metas.description: Mount Fuji is the tallest mountain in Japan, with a gradual incline and often snowy summit.
metas.comparison: Depending on the elevation, it can be seen from far away. This can create some excellent region guesses, especially if you account for direction and distance.

metas.name: Japan - Landscape - Plains
metas.description: Japan is notably a very mountainous country. However, there are some regions that are quite flat, being the Nobi and Kanto plains. While at times they can look very similar, determining that it is one or the other can be very helpful.
metas.comparison: NOTE: While there are, of course, other flat areas in Japan, these two are the most recognizable.

metas.name: Japan - Language - Cyrillic
metas.description: Cyrillic can be found on signs in the cities of Wakkanai and Nemuro, in northern Hokkaido.

metas.name: Japan - Vegetation - Bamboo
metas.description: In general, bamboo grows more often in the south, and slowly decreases further north. Population size and areas where it grows can vary, so use this information primarily in helping assist your region guess.

metas.name: Japan - Vegetation - Chinese Silver Grass
metas.description: Chinese Silver Grass, referred to as Kyushu grass, is indeed very abundant on the island of Kyushu. However, use this tip with caution, as they can be seen outside of this area.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Another notable region they can be found in is the prefectures of Niigata, Yamagata and Akita. Though, combining the rather large quantity found on Kyushu, its normally distinct vegetation, along with other information, there often will be a clear distinction.

metas.name: Japan - Vegetation - Giant Butterbur
metas.description: Giant butterbur (commonly referred to as cabbage) is abundant in Hokkaido and some northern prefectures. Plants found south of Hokkaido often have smaller leaves. It is often found growing along the roadside.

metas.name: Japan - Vegetation - Japanese White Birch
metas.description: Japanese White Birch grows dominantly in the Chubu and Hokkaido regions, and to a lesser extent in Tohoku. Small areas of white birch can be found throughout Japan, so use this information primarily to help assist your region guess.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Japanese Beech is another species of tree found in Japan. They, however, have more grey and spotted bark, as opposed to the mostly white Japanese White Birch.

metas.name: Landscape - 35
metas.description: Road 35 is surrounded by hills and mountains, and the ground is mostly covered in green shrubs. Curved lamp posts are posted at regular intervals on the northeastern side of the road.

metas.name: Landscape - 45 south of Mudayy
metas.description: Most of Road 45 south of Mudayy is unpaved and goes generally north to south, through some very rough hilly terrain. The soil is light and very rocky. Beware that the southernmost stretch is paved.

metas.name: Landscape - Adam Ridge
metas.description: Just north of Adam, youâll find a flat desert landscape with greyish soil and mountains in the distance, notably one long ridge to the south followed by two smaller and rounder hills to the east and southeast. Other mountains are also visible to the north and west.

metas.name: Landscape - Al Amarat
metas.description: If you are surrounded by mountains on all sides, and you are in a somewhat urban area, you are likely just southeast of Muscat, in Al Amarat.

metas.name: Landscape - Bidiyah Landscape - Dunes
metas.description: South of Bidiyah you can find a couple of dirt roads going through a slightly rolling landscape consisting of orange-pink sand and small yellow-ish shrubs. The roads mainly go between long and low sand dunes with a general south-south-west direction.

metas.name: Landscape - Bidiyah Landscape - Flat
metas.description: Sandy desert with light coloured green and yellow shrubs can be found in northeastern Oman, mainly south and west of Bidiyah.

metas.name: Landscape - Coastal 41
metas.description: Coastal Road 41 features one of the sandiest landscapes in Oman, with very light sand all around. The coast is sometimes visible in the distance.

metas.name: Landscape - Coastal 41 - Ridge
metas.description: Coastal Road 41 features one of the sandiest landscapes in Oman, with very light sand all around. The coast is sometimes visible in the distance. On the north-to-south stretch, you can see a distant ridge to the west.

metas.name: Landscape - Dry Mountains
metas.description: Northern Oman features a dry mountainous landscape similar to eastern UAE. The south coast of Oman also rarely features some similar mountains.

metas.name: Landscape - Masirah
metas.description: Masirah Island features a dry and slightly hilly landscape, typically with somewhat grey soil and with brown shrubs visible. The front camera on the island is slightly smudged.

metas.name: Landscape - Masirah - 51
metas.description: Masirah Island features a dry and slightly hilly landscape, typically with somewhat grey soil and with brown shrubs visible. Road 51, which circulates the island, usually only has a white centre road line, which can help in recognising it. The front camera on the island is slightly smudged.

metas.name: Landscape - Max South 45
metas.description: Most of Road 45 south of Mudayy is unpaved and goes generally north to south, through some very rough hilly terrain. The soil is light and very rocky. Beware that the southernmost stretch is paved.

metas.name: Landscape - Musandam
metas.description: Most of the coverage in the Musandam Governorate exclave is coastal, with rocky cliffs usually hugging the road. A majority, but not all, of this coverage will have the coast to the west, excluding any other roads in the country with a similar look.

metas.name: Landscape - Narrow 32
metas.description: Going further north, Road 32 travels through a hilly desert landscape, in a general northern direction.

metas.name: Landscape - Nizwa Mountains
metas.description: The mountains north of Nizwa have an amount of green bushes that are unusually large for the north. The mountains are very rocky and jagged, which differentiates them from the more rolling mountains in the south.

metas.name: Landscape - North of Al Awaya Road
metas.description: The road north of Al Awaya features a desert landscape with dark grey soil, which is not common in the south. The road itself still has the orange tint characteristic of southwest Oman.

metas.name: Landscape - North of Al Mazyunah Road
metas.description: The unpaved road north of Al Mazyunah, near the Yemen border, has a north-north-west bound angle, and the desert has sandy, red-tinted sand, which still has some shrubbery around. You can see some hills in the distance. The southwards driving direction and sunny weather can be used as confirmation.

metas.name: Landscape - Orange Sanddunes
metas.description: A road going through large orange-pink sand dunes can be found north of Fasad.
metas.comparison: NOTE: The same dunes can be seen in the distance close to the northern part of the Yemen border.

metas.name: Landscape - Orocue Road
metas.description: This road leading from the 65 to the town of Orocue is characterized by its unique angle and the orange/brown dirt.

metas.name: Landscape - Rolling Hills
metas.description: Close to the southern coast, especially around Salalah, you will find a rolling hills landscape. The area commonly features rocky ground, bushes and small trees as well as some fairly green valleys.

metas.name: Landscape - Sadah Coastal Road
metas.description: Road 42/49 east of Salalah is a scenic coastal road that features a lot of light-coloured tall rocky cliffs. The coast is also often visible.

metas.name: Landscape - Salalah Plains
metas.description: Salalah is located on a flat coastal plain with rolling mountains surrounding it to the north.

metas.name: Landscape - Ubar Fields
metas.description: Around the town of Ubar, you can find patches of green agricultural land surrounded by desert.

metas.name: Landscape - Western 41
metas.description: The western stretch of Road 41 has wide shoulders similar to Road 31, however, the more northwest-bound angle along with the reddish soil should tell them apart.

metas.name: Landscape - Wide 32
metas.description: Crossing into the Ash Sharqiyah North Governorate, the shoulders become wide, like those on Road 31. However, unlike Road 31, the desert here is darker and has more shrubs and greenery. A long portion of the road also has overcast coverage. The lighter red section is no longer road 32 but still features the wide shoulders. The landscape further north also gets hillier and more vegetated.

metas.name: Malta - Infrastructure - Blue Signs
metas.description: These blue signs are unique to Valletta.

metas.name: Malta - Infrastructure - Bus Route with 3
metas.description: Bus routes starting with 3 are only found on Gozo Island. These can be quite hard to see, meaning they are most useful in moving games.

metas.name: Malta - Infrastructure - Guardrail
metas.description: Regular metal guardrails are rare on Gozo Island. And thus mainly found on the main island lol

metas.name: Malta - Infrastructure - Low Stone Barrier
metas.description: Regular metal guardrails are rare on Gozo Island. Low stone barriers are more common instead.

metas.name: Malta - Trekker - Ship Trekker
metas.description: This trekker on a ship that is painted white and blue can be seen between the main island and Gozo Island.

metas.name: Mexico - Agriculture - Blue Agave
metas.description: Commonly known as the blue agave, A. tequilana is immediately recognisable by its blue, sharply protruding leaves. This is the agave from which tequila is extracted, and it mainly inhabits Jalisco, where it is almost always observed in magnificent fields which can even coalesce into vast shades of blue from a distance.
metas.comparison: Similar, but different: A. anguistifolia. While it is difficult to distinguish them, A. tequilana is noticeably bluer. One other difference is that A. angustifolia is more commonly spotted in isolated groupings than A. tequilana, but expansive fields still exist.

metas.name: Mexico - Agriculture - Campeche Fields
metas.description: These red agricultural fields surrounded by dense forests of tropical trees are most common in northern Campeche.

metas.name: Mexico - Agriculture - Citrus Tree Plantation
metas.description: The area around Poza Rica in Veracruz features a lot of citrus tree plantations. It is common to see large amounts of these trees grown right on top of the hills.

metas.name: Mexico - Agriculture - Oil Palm
metas.description: Oil palm plantations are most common in Chiapas, and occasionally on the outskirts of the state in Veracruz, Tabasco, and Campeche.

metas.name: Mexico - Agriculture - Prickly Pear Farm
metas.description:
In the northeast most area of State of Mexico, around the town Nopaltepec, they often farm Opuntia in vast plains.
Farms of prickly pear are otherwise most commonly found in north east Morelos, where they foreground striking, sculpturally eroded dry hills. These farms can be found randomly elsewhere in the country, but much less commonly; if there is a third most common location for them it would be Guanajuato.

metas.name: Mexico - Agriculture - Pulque Agave Field
metas.description: One will often notice scattered farms of A. salmiana, gatherings which stretch limitlessly in neat rows; these will almost always be found around the city of Pachuca in Hidalgo, and rarely more south-east.

metas.name: Mexico - Agriculture - Red Agricultural Fields
metas.description: Red agricultural fields are commonly seen in Zacatecas and occasionally southern Durango.

metas.name: Mexico - Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.description: Sugarcane can be found all over the country, but by far most common in Veracruz.

metas.name: Mexico - Agriculture - Very Dark Fields
metas.description: Extremely dark fields are common in Guanajuato.

metas.name: Mexico - Architecture - Mud Brick
