metas.name: United States - Architecture - New Orleans Architecture
metas.description: Neighbourhoods all around the city of New Orleans feature many colourful, historic, shotgun-style houses.
metas.comparison: Buildings in central areas of New Orleans often feature colourful facades with second story wrap-around balconies.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - North-Eastern House
metas.description: Houses in North-Eastern USA often have walls made up of horizontal, overlapping boards

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Red Metal Roof
metas.description: Buildings with red metal rooftops are most commonly found in the Mid-South and Southern Appalachia states of Virginia, West Virginia, Ohio, Kentucky, Tennessee, Arkansas, and North Carolina.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These types of rooftops can be found in other areas, so use other clues before guessing.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Shingle Walls
metas.description: Houses in coastal New England often feature shingle walls, which are layered wood panels overlapping each other.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Short Stilt House
metas.description: Houses with short stilts are common in the western and central Gulf Coast. These houses typically feature short stilts made of concrete or wood (30cm-90cm off the ground) and are primarily found in areas near the coast and any adjacent rivers.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Shotgun House
metas.description: Very narrow, one-storey houses made out of wood are called âshotgun houses.â They are most common in and around New Orleans (LA,) Houston (TX,) Louisville (KY,) and the state of Mississippi.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Spanish Colonial Architecture
metas.description: Spanish Colonial Revival Architecture can be categorised as buildings with lightly-coloured stucco walls and red clay-tile roofs. They can be found in the desert southwest states of California, Nevada, Arizona, and Texas. You can also find similar types of buildings in Florida and coastal Georgia.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: See the second picture for an in-depth explanation of this architecture (sorry for the skew, it's a photo I took myself)

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Stacked Triplex
metas.description: Older three story wooden houses, also called âstacked triplexes,â are very common in urban areas of the Northeast. They are most prevalent in New York, Connecticut, Rhode Island, and Massachusetts.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These types of houses are also somewhat common in cities in Atlantic Canada.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Trailer House
metas.description: Small, rectangular manufactured homes, also known as mobile or âtrailerâ homes, are popular in rural areas of the US. In general, mobile homes are more common in the Southeast but they can be seen anywhere in the country.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Victorian Architecture
metas.description: Row Houses and other buildings in San Francisco are often in the style of Victorian architecture, with many bay windows, turrets, and ornate exterior details. These homes are built close together and can be very colourful.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Wooden House
metas.description: Houses and commercial buildings in the interior Western US are often made of lots of dark wooden boards and timbers. Buildings at high elevations also commonly have metal roofs, to avoid snow build-up.

metas.name: United States - Car Meta - Daniel Boone Car
metas.description: This section of road in Daniel Boone National Forest near Beattyville, KY has a unique Google car.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: This coverage is overwritten afaik.

metas.name: United States - Car Meta - Ford Bronco
metas.description: As part of a promotional campaign, the TransAmerica Trail from Oregon to North Carolina was covered by a Ford Bronco. The car can recognised by its unblurred black roof and red hood, and is mostly found on unpaved rural roads.
metas.comparison: Looking backwards, you will see two other Ford SUVs escorting the camera car.

metas.name: United States - Car Meta - Golden Gate Car
metas.description: This car can be found to the north of the Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco.

metas.name: United States - Car Meta - Santa Catalina Car
metas.description: This island to the south of Los Angeles has a unique Google car.

metas.name: United States - Coverage Meta - Winter - Appalachians
metas.description: Within the Appalachians, Winter Coverage is most common in West Virginia.

metas.name: United States - Coverage Meta - Winter - New England
metas.description: Winter/fall coverage such as this is commonplace in New England, particularly in Massachusetts, Connecticut, and Rhode Island. Be aware that winter coverage also exists in the South and hence why you may get Arkansas or another state in that region mixed up with New England if youâre trying to go based only on the vibes.

metas.name: United States - Donner Park Trekker
metas.description: You can see this car all over the Donner Park in Columbus, IN.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - 6 bolt bollard
metas.description:
This bollard has a white rectangular plate, with 6 bolts: 2 at the top, 2 in the middle and 2 at the bottom.
There are different variants, with circular reflectors, rectangular reflectors, or no reflectors at all.
metas.comparison: They're all found in California

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Adopt-A-Highway Signs
metas.description: Most states have unique, distinct and learnable Adopt-a-Highway signs, which can be seen on the side of roads. A map of those can be seen here. Keep in mind, some states have slight variations in design.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Arrow Street Number
metas.description: North Carolina commonly uses a style of street signs showing street numbers and arrows in addition to the street name.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Other states occasionally feature street signs with similar designs, so use other clues before guessing.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - ATV Route
metas.description: These green ATV Route signs are unique to Wisconsin.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Billboards
metas.description: Billboards are banned in Maine, Vermont, Alaska and Hawaii. So if you see one, you can rule those out.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Black Tar
metas.description: A black stripe can sometimes be seen in between the two yellow, middle road lines in California.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Black/White Overpass Support
metas.description: These stripes on an overpass support are a dead giveaway that itâs South Carolina. Sometimes a sign with yellow and black stripes is used instead

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - California Bridge Marker
metas.description: California posts these bridge markers (with a lot of numbers) on bridges. The county abbreviations used on the bridge markers are different from those on the postal markers.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - California Stripes
metas.description: Utility poles in California usually have markings at the bottom of the pole that consist of 3 yellow stripes.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Chattanooga Font
metas.description: The city of Chattanooga in Tennessee has its own unique font that is used on some signs in the city.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Circular Fraction-Sign
metas.description: West Virginia sometimes features street signs with a symbol that resembles a fraction inside a circle.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Clearance on Overpass
metas.description: South Carolina is the only southeastern state to post the clearance on every overpass.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Concrete Pavement
metas.description: Concrete paving on main highways is much more common in Iowa than in other states.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Concrete paving on residential streets is commonly seen throughout the Midwest states and parts of the East Coast.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - County Road - Clark County
metas.description: Clark County is the county Las Vegas is situated in and it uses a unique county route shield.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Dark Wooden Fences
metas.description: Dark-coloured wooden fences with several horizontal wooden supports are common in farming areas of central and southern Appalachia, stretching from Pennsylvania to Georgia.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These types of fences can be found elsewhere to a lesser extent, so use other clues before guessing.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Diamond Bollard
metas.description: The most common type of roadside bollard in South Dakota and Montana features a dark metal post with a white diamond on each side of the top.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These bollards can be found to a lesser extent in other western states.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Double Signposts
metas.description: Signs attached to two signposts can be seen in Michigan. Not all signs are attached to two signposts.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Double signposts can also be seen in other states, but are not as common.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - E-2 Sign
metas.description: In New Hampshire there will often be a white metal sign with the characters âE-2â on it adjacent to the road, typically at either end of bridges.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Exit Ramp / No Parking
metas.description: Georgia likes to decorate its freeway offramps with no parking signs.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Exit with Speed Limit
metas.description: New Alabama coverage can have these combined exit/speed limit signs.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Florida Bollard
metas.description: This bollard is found in Florida.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Green Overpass Marker
metas.description: Overpass bridges in Mississippi have green plaques with white numbers on them.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Green US Route
metas.description: This green U.S. Route shield with the word business at the top is unique to Maryland.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Green-White Sign
metas.description: This sign is Illinois-specific.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Green/Red Bridge Marker
metas.description: Maine, New Hampshire, and Massachusetts use small green and red rectangular signs to mark the ends of bridges and guardrails.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Not all bridges and guardrails in these states will have these markers.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - H-Reflector
metas.description: Snowplowable raised pavement markers can only be found on highways in the eastern states shown in the image. They are built into the road and somewhat resemble the letter H.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Hanging Yellow Boxes
metas.description: Many large intersections in Michigan have stop lights and signs that hang from wires that stretch across the middle of the intersection. These markers are commonly in yellow boxes.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These are not completely unique to Michigan, but are most commonly seen there.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Highway Signs
metas.description: Maximum speed limits vary by state and territory. The maximum speed limits shown here will generally be seen on interstate highways. Some interstates and highways in their respective states or territories will have lower maximum speed limits than what is shown.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Horizontal Traffic Light
metas.description: Horizontal Traffic Lights are common in Nebraska, New Mexico, Texas and Louisiana. They also appear occasionally in Oklahoma, Louisiana and Georgia.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - ICE Warning
metas.description: Signs warning about ice (like this) are commonplace in Louisiana.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Indiana Blue Square
metas.description: This kind of blue square on a post is exclusive to Indiana.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Kansas Sign Reflectors
metas.description: These white reflectors on signposts are unique to Kansas. They are most commonly seen on âstopâ signs in rural areas.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Kentucky Rumble Strips
metas.description: Some roads and highways in the state of Kentucky use uniquely-shaped rumble strips that are thin, relatively long recessed lines on the very outside edges of the road.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Key West Poles
metas.description: Poles on Intersections in Key West have a white paint at the bottom which contains the name of the street its on.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Kilometer
metas.description: Interstate 19 in Arizona from Tucson to the Mexico border uses kilometres on the exit and distance signs. This is the only part of the country that uses kilometres instead of miles for highway signs.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Speed limit signs in this area still use MPH instead of KPH.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Large Center Line Gap
metas.description: Yellow lines with a noticeably larger gap in between them are most common in Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Oregon. They can also be found to a lesser extent in Washington, Alabama, and Michigan.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Wide middle lines can also rarely appear in other states, so consider other clues before guessing.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Letter Highway Sign (with County)
metas.description: Wisconsin and Missouri are the only two states that use a lettering system (A - ZZZ) for their county highways. Wisconsin signs typically have the word âcountyâ above the letter, while Missouri signs typically do not. The borders of the signs also vary slightly.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Letter Highway Sign (without County)
metas.description: Wisconsin and Missouri are the only two states that use a lettering system (A - ZZZ) for their county highways. Wisconsin signs typically have the word âcountyâ above the letter, while Missouri signs typically do not. The borders of the signs also vary slightly.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Lone Star
metas.description: Texasâs nickname is the Lone Star State. You can see the Texas star on the stateâs flag. Many Texans use the star as a decoration on gates, for example.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Maine Roadlines
metas.description:
Maine often uses a dashed single yellow line or a combination of dashed and solid instead of a solid double one in the middle of a road.
I feel like Maine does it a bit more often than other states in the region.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Maryland Overpass Code
metas.description: Some Interstate bridges in Maryland (but not the neighboring states or DC) seem to have this code painted on them. (Discovered by bagaboiebailey in the USA GeoGuessr Community server).

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Midwest Grainy Roads
metas.description: Some rural roads in the Upper Midwest use a similar road pavement to Texas. They will have a grainy, âsalt and pepperâ-like road surface, but will vary in colour. These roads are most common in the state of Illinois.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Mile Marker
metas.description: California doesnât use mile markers.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Minnesota Bridge Sign
metas.description: In Minnesota, these yellow signs with vertical, black triangles are placed before bridges at most major river crossings and at the beginnings and ends of guardrail sections on large highways.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Minnesota Stop Sign
metas.description: On most rural âstopâ signposts in Minnesota, a black-and-white marker is attached to the posts horizontally. The shape may vary slightly.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Nashville Bins
metas.description: Nashville has trash bins with the recognizable logo.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - National Parks
metas.description: Guardrails, signs, and signposts are commonly painted a medium brown colour in US National Parks, which are often located in the west. Guardrails that are painted brown can be made out of both wood and metal. Rock walls can also sometimes be seen in place of guardrails.
metas.comparison: NOTE: There are occasional exceptions to this rule, so consider other clues before guessing in a National Park.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Nevada Bollard
metas.description: This bollard is found in Nevada. It consists of a reflector on a thin stick. The reflector is a vertical rectangle that consists of a white field surrounded by a black outline.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Nevada Mile Marker
metas.description: Top part has the highway name. The middle part is an abbreviation of the county name. The lower part has the mile number.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - New Hampshire Interstate Sign
metas.description: These signs should only be found in NH (notice the dividing line between the two numbers).

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - New Hampshire US Route Sign
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - New Hampshire US Route Sign
metas.description: These are also specific to New Hampshire. Notice the dividing line on the sign.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - New Jersey - 500 Series County Routes
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - New Jersey - 500 Series County Routes
metas.description: These county routes are given unique three-digit numbers that begin with a 5. There is only one route per number. The same number cannot be duplicated in multiple counties. There is therefore only one County Route 525 in the entire state of New Jersey. Whatâs also interesting about the 500 Series routes is that they follow the same cardinal direction rule as Interstates: even-numbered routes run east-to-west and odd-numbered ones north-to-south. In common with the U.S. Routes, the numbers increase southward.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - New Orleans Circle
metas.description: This circular windshield sticker is found in New Orleans, Louisiana.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - No Middle Line
metas.description: Some small roads in California lack a middle yellow line; instead only feature solid white lines on each side of the road.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This can rarely be seen in other states.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - North Carolina - Circular Pay to Park
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - North Carolina - Circular Pay to Park
metas.description: Raleigh, NC uses circular pay to park signs to indicate parking meter locations. (unlike Charlotte, NC)

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - North Carolina / Blue Parking Sign
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - North Carolina / Blue Parking Sign
metas.description: Charlotte uses green parking signs, whereas Raleigh uses blue parking signs.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - North Carolina / Green Parking Sign
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - North Carolina / Green Parking Sign
metas.description: Charlotte uses green parking signs, whereas Raleigh uses blue parking signs.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - North Carolina / Streetcar
metas.description: Charlotte has a streetcar system unlike Raleigh.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - North Carolina Signpost
metas.description: White signs attached to signposts can commonly be seen in North Carolina.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Number + Direction Road
metas.description: Streets in Utah and Idaho, particularly in urban areas, are often named by using a combination of a number and cardinal direction (i.e. â600 South.â)
metas.comparison: NOTE: This style of street naming can be found rarely in other Western states.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Oak Streetsign
metas.description: Oakland has this tree on their street name signs.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Oil Pumpjack
metas.description: Oil pumpjacks are short, industrial-looking metal structures located at the surface of oil fields and are used to pump crude oil from the earth below. They are most common in western states, particularly in Texas, Eastern New Mexico, and North Dakota.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Oklahoma Stopsigns
metas.description: In Oklahoma, you can often find a green rectangular sign with 3 rows of numbers attached to the back of stop signs at rural intersections

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Overpass Milemarker
metas.description: In Alabama, overpasses have these mile markers hanging from them.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Parish
metas.description: Louisiana doesnât call its counties counties but uses the word parish instead. This is a relic of the French colonial past of the state. You might occasionally spot the word on an intersection sign, for example. The location is guaranteed to be in Louisiana because no other state uses the word parish in that way.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Pennsylvania Intersection Signs
metas.description: Rectangular white signs can sometimes be seen attached to signposts at intersections in Pennsylvania. On top, the number of the converging state route is written.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Pillar Stripes
metas.description: Alabama likes to glue these stripes to overpass support pillars.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Pittsburgh Bridges
metas.description: Many bridges are used to connect the various neighbourhoods of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. These expansive, steel bridges are commonly painted bright yellow. Additionally, Pittsburgh is easy to identify because of it being flanked by 3 rivers and steep bluffs on all sides.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Pittsburgh Reflectors
metas.description: These circular reflectors are found in Pittsburgh.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Postal Marker
metas.description: Instead of Mile Markers, California uses postal markers that are white instead of green and have a county abbreviation.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Property Markers
metas.description: A horizontal blue, red, or green sign can commonly be seen at the ends of driveways in Wisconsin and the Michigan peninsula. The house number is present, in addition to either the town name and or the road name (usually.)
metas.comparison: NOTE: Nearby states often use similar markers, but typically lack any town or street name information and only feature numbers.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Rectangular Reflector
metas.description: These rectangular raised pavement markers are found in the south and west of the US and also in Massachusetts.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Red Streetsign
metas.description: Mesa, a city next to Phoenix, sometimes uses these red street name signs in the western part of the city.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Roadname on Sidewalk
metas.description: In San Francisco, CA, almost every intersection has the road name written on the sidewalk.
metas.comparison: This is due to the many earthquakes in this city, making sure every road is still labeled in case the streetsigns fall off.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Rock Walls
metas.description: In rural areas of Connecticut, Rhode Island, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire, short rock walls are commonly visible adjacent to the road.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These rock walls can be found rarely in adjacent states.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Small Circle Bollard
metas.description: Roadside bollards in Wyoming often feature a dark metal pole with a white circular reflector at the top. The top of the metal pole is sometimes painted white or grey, which is unique to Wyoming.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Small Green Signs
metas.description: Vermont features small rectangular green signs on stop sign posts with three rows of horizontal numbers. The top row of numbers correlates to the highway or road number that the road with the stop sign intersects with.
metas.comparison: The State of New York uses similar style signs. However, these signs can be attached to different types of sign posts (town entry signs, highway signs, etc.)

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - South Carolina Intersection Signs
metas.description: Black street signs with white text can commonly be found at intersections in South Carolina.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - SPEED Sign
metas.description: Speed signs in Oregon often simply have the word âSpeedâ instead of the standard âSpeed Limitâ.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Square Guardrail
metas.description: Square guardrails are the most dominant (but not the only) type of guardrail in the states of New York and Wyoming. They have a long bar across the top, with several square legs supporting them.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These guardrails can be found, to a lesser extent, in some adjacent states.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - State Flag - Arizona
metas.description: Each of the 50 states has its own state flag. These appear frequently enough that they are worth learning.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - State Flag - California
metas.description: Each of the 50 states has its own state flag. These appear frequently enough that they are worth learning.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - State Flag - Nevada
metas.description: Each of the 50 states has its own state flag. These appear frequently enough that they are worth learning.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - State Flag - North Carolina
metas.description: Each of the 50 states has its own state flag. These appear frequently enough that they are worth learning.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Tennessee Mile Marker
metas.description: Tennessee state routes have these unique mile markers. The larger number is the mile (resets at county borders) and the smaller bottom one is the state route number.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Tennessee Stars
metas.description: This three-star symbol is found in many places in Tennessee, including but not limited to these historical place signs. Itâs the same symbol as on the state flag but it can also be black and white.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Texas - Fully Black Traffic Light
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Texas - Fully Black Traffic Light
metas.description: Within Texas, completely black traffic lights can be found in Dallas and Houston

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Texas - Fully Yellow Traffic Light
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Texas - Fully Yellow Traffic Light
metas.description: Within Texas, fully yellow traffic lights can be found in San Antonio, El Paso and Austin.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Texas Bands
metas.description: Yellow or red bands can commonly be seen around signposts in Texas.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Similar reflectors can sometimes be seen in other states, such as Hawaii.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Texas Grainy Roads
metas.description: Texan roads often have a grainy, âsalt and pepperâ-like road surface.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Similar pavement can sometimes be seen in adjacent states such as New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Colorado.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Thick Black / Thinner Yellow Sign
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Thick Black / Thinner Yellow Sign
metas.description: The black stripes on these signs are a bit thicker in Louisiana than in other states.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Thick Lines
metas.description: Some roads in West Virginia, Virginia, and Maryland use middle yellow lines that are thicker than traditional yellow road lines.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These are not present on all roads in these states, and can be found elsewhere, so use this tip in conjunction with other clues.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Trolley - Miami
metas.description:
The Greater Miami area has a so-called trolley system which is a free public transport system.
Different towns have different colors in their trolleys. The Miami Trolley is orange at the top and green at the bottom, with a small white stripe in between (the colors of the Miami-Dade flag, which are the same as the Indian flag).

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Trolley - Miami Beach
metas.description:
The Greater Miami area has a so-called trolley system which is a free public transport system.
Different towns have different colors in their trolleys. The Miami Beach Trolley is blue.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Vertical House Number
metas.description: Properties in rural and exurban Ohio, Lower Michigan, and Indiana commonly feature a vertically-oriented metal sign with white numbers, indicating the house number of the adjacent building. These signs are most commonly blue or green, and are commonly attached to mailboxes.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These may be rarely found in other states.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Virginia Intersection Signs
metas.description: Rectangular white signs can sometimes be seen at intersections in Virginia.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Washington Bollard
metas.description: The state of Washington uses bollards that consist of a white or brown post with a white rectangle on the front of the bollard, and two smaller white or silver squares on the back of the bollard.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Waymo
metas.description: Waymo is an autonomous driving company which offers taxi services in several cities. Its cars are very distinct, have a lidar on top and notably have no person sitting behind the wheel. As of Dec 18th, 2025, it operates in San Francisco (CA), Los Angeles (CA), Phoenix (AZ), Austin (TX) and Atlanta (GA). You can find the current operation here

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - White-Orange Pole Plate
metas.description: A rectangular white metal plate, with an orange rectangle and diamond, can be seen on most poles in Wisconsin and the Michigan peninsula.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Windshield Sticker - DC
metas.description: Cars registered in DC are legally required to have this sticker in their windshield.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Windshield Sticker - Louisiana
metas.description: This sticker can be seen on windshields in Louisiana. The sticker has four smaller squares in it, hence the name.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Windshield Sticker - Maine
metas.description: The Maine inspection stickers come in various colors but they all have one thing in common - all have one edge or a chunk from one side missing.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Windshield Sticker - Massachusetts
metas.description: Three white rectangles. Central one is horizontal, and has a number on it. Left and right one are vertical.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Windshield Sticker - New Hampshire
metas.description: Number in a white rectangle with a thick colorful border.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Windshield Sticker - New Hampshire (old)
metas.description: They look like colorful post-its with a black number on it.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Windshield Sticker - New Jersey
metas.description: Three rectangles. Each contains a number. The outer ones make a year (like 2023), and are filled in a given color. The central one has a white background and a single digit.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Windshield Sticker - New York
metas.description: One number on the left, one on the right with a long white gap in between.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Windshield Sticker - Orange T Circle
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Windshield Sticker - Orange T Circle
metas.description: This windshield sticker with an orange T is found exclusively in Dallas.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Windshield Sticker - Texas
metas.description: MMYY (for example 1022) in a white rectangle with a colorful border.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Wisconsin Bollard
metas.description: These simple white bollards with black reflectors are unique to Wisconsin.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Wooden Signpost
metas.description: Wooden Signposts are mainly found in the Northwestern 5 States, and in California

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Yellow Direction Box
metas.description: The yellow direction box is only found in Mississippi.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Yellow Traffic Light / Black Border
metas.meta_label: Infrastructure - Yellow Traffic Light / Black Border
metas.description: Within Texas, yellow traffic lights with black borders are found in Dallas, Fort Worth and San Antonio

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Zoox
metas.description: Zoox is a robotaxi service that as of Dec 18th, 2025, operates in San Francisco and Las Vegas. The cars have a very distinct shape and have no driver. You can find the current coverage area of Zoox here

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Appalachian/Southern Hybrid
metas.description: Tennessee and Kentucky look like a mix of Appalachian and Southern Landscape.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Appalachians
metas.description: The Appalachian mountain range is a low mountain range that runs through the eastern states. The general landscape consists of low, forested mountains, with beech and oak trees being a common sight.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Houses in the south generally have less storeys. New England architecture, commonly consisting of wood panelling, high roofs and a porch, is also more common toward the north, especially in New England.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Badlands
metas.description: Badlands National Park features these distinct, sand-brown, eroded rock formations. The formations may sometimes appear more rounded, and lighter in colour.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Big Bend National Park
metas.description: Big Bend National Park is located along the Mexico border in Southwest Texas. It can be identified by its dry, rocky peaks and shrubby foliage. This park is adjacent to the Chihauhan desert, so plants such as yucca and prickly pear cactus are common.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Black Hills
metas.description: The Black Hills, located in far Western South Dakota and far Eastern Wyoming, are a series of moderately tall mountains with large amounts of conifer trees and rocky outcroppings. The surrounding areas are typically much flatter with lesser tree cover.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This area has a similar appearance to many areas within the Rocky Mountains, which lie further to the West.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Canadian Landscape (Maine)
metas.description: Landscapes vary quite a bit in New England. Maine in particular can look a lot like Canada.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Central Appalachians
metas.description: In the Appalachian area stretching from southern New York to southern Virginia, there are a lot of forest-covered rolling hills, with flat valleys dividing them. A majority of the ridges are oriented Southwest to Northeast.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Central Florida
metas.description: The soil gets a little more sandy in Central Florida. There are also more pine trees than palms (theyâre occasionally seen too).

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Central Valley
metas.description: Central Valley, California can be recognized by its Mediterranean climate. This is reflected in its agriculture, seen in the vineyards and olive trees that can commonly be found here.
metas.comparison: In addition, rolling hills can be seen toward the edges of the valley.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Circular Lakes
metas.description: Small circular shallow lakes are especially common in Central Florida around Lakeland and Orlando.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Colorado Ridge
metas.description: Central Colorado is home to a large North-to-South oriented mountain ridge. This divides the Rocky Mountains to the west and the Great Plains to the east.These mountains are adjacent to the major metropolitan areas of Boulder, Denver, and Colorado Springs.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Death Valley
metas.description: Death Valley National Park can be easily recognized by the dry, sandy, treeless mountains that can be seen from the roads that go through the park. In Generation 3 coverage, the sky can look particularly dusty.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Many smaller roads in Death Valley only have Generation 1 coverage.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Devil's Tower
metas.description: In far Northeastern Wyoming lies Devilâs Tower, which is a very tall, standalone butte protruding from the surrounding land. This can sometimes be seen from many miles away because of the lack of nearby mountains.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Driftless Area
metas.description: The driftless area in Southwestern Wisconsin is quite unique. It has features of Midwestern States (for example agriculture), but is very hilly.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Everglades
metas.description: Deep South Florida, between the metropolitan areas of Ft. Myers and Miami, features dense, jungle-like forests that have few inhabitants. Roads through these areas are commonly very straight and long.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Florida Jungle
metas.description: Deep South Florida, between the metropolitan areas of Ft. Myers and Miami, features dense, jungle-like forests that have few inhabitants. Roads through these areas are commonly very straight and long.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Florida Keys
metas.description: The Florida Keys are an archipelago of tropical islands west of Miami. The highway connecting the islands can be recognized by green, tropical vegetation on the sides of the usually single lane road. The soil is also sandy white.
metas.comparison: Urban locations are also similar, but with many more planted palm trees and mowed grass being a common sight.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Glacier National Park
metas.description: Along the Canadian border in Montana lies Glacier National Park. It is easily recognizable by its extremely tall and steep mountain peaks. Most coverage is also hazy and taken during summer.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Other National Parks within the Rocky Mountain range of the US can have a similar appearance, so consider other clues before guessing.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Great Basin
metas.description: The Great Basin, centred around Nevada, can be recognized by the tall, sometimes snow-capped mountains in the background. There are dry, but grassy, and slightly shrubby plains leading up to the mountains.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Great Basin - Green
metas.description: Within the Great Basin, greener mountains can be seen in Idaho and central Utah.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Great Basin - Oregon
metas.description: Within the Great Basin, more gradual, rocky hills can be seen in Oregon.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Great Plains
metas.description: The Great Plains are in the middle of the United States and stretch from the Canadian border in the North, to central Texas in the South. This area is primarily flat with few trees. Some areas feature agriculture fields, while others feature dry and barren grassy fields.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Guadaloupe Foothills
metas.description: In adjacent areas of New Mexico and Texas, smaller foothills of the Guadaloupe Mountains can be seen with relatively flat tops and shrubby foliage.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Guadalupe Mountains
metas.description: Along the New Mexico and or Texas border there is a ridge of tall, dry peaks known as the Guadalupe Mountains. In adjacent areas of both states, smaller foothills of these mountains can be seen with relatively flat tops and shrubby foliage.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Louisiana
metas.description: Flat and marshy landscapes are a common sight in Louisiana.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Lush Spruce Forest
metas.description: Spruce and pine forests are a common sight in the western United States in New Mexico, Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, and to the west of those states. The lush spruce forest types shown become increasingly common near the Pacific coast in Washington, Oregon, and California.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Mid-Atlantic Agricultural
metas.description: Some locations in the Mid-Atlantic region can look deceivingly Midwestern but with more trees.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Mid-Atlantic Forest
metas.description: Upstate New York and Pennsylvania are quite forested. Rolling hills are also common.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Mississippi River Valley
metas.description: The Lower Mississippi River Valley is a very flat and open landscape with red soil in areas of Tennessee, Arkansas, Mississippi, and Northeast Louisiana. Corn and other crops are common in this area.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Nebraska Sandhills
metas.description: The Nebraska Sandhills are a recognizable region of rolling hills covered with prairie grass in the central-north part of the state.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - New England
metas.description: Landscapes vary quite a bit in New England. Maine in particular can look a lot like Canada if you know your countries in GeoGuessr. The topography of New England is mostly rolling hills. The forests are littered with fir trees and aspens.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Northern California
metas.description: One thing that sets NoCal apart from SoCal is the amount of palm trees. You generally see palms everywhere in the LA area but hardly any in the San Francisco Bay Area.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Northern Florida
metas.description: North Florida has sandier soil and rarely has any palm trees. Most forests are pine forests and the vibes feel more like Floridaâs neighbors to the north than Florida itself.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Oklahoma Peaks
metas.description: Southwestern Oklahoma features a small area of rocky, shrubby peaks. Some of the mountains are also covered in trees, and the rocks can have a pinkish red tint to them.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Ouachita Mountains
metas.description: The Ouachita Mountains stretch from Eastern Oklahoma into West-Central Arkansas. Unlike the nearby Ozark Mountains, these mountains are typically more steep in nature and easier to see from a distance.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Pacific Rainforest
metas.description: Temperate rainforests are found in coastal areas of Washington, Oregon, and Northern California. These rainforests feature many broadleaf trees, large conifers, and ferns.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These rainforests stretch north into coastal British Columbia and Southeast Alaska as well.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Pine Forest Hills
metas.description: Spruce and pine forests are a common sight in the western United States in New Mexico, Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, and to the west of those states. The landscape that you can see in the picture meanwhile can be found in the states of Colorado, Montana, Wyoming, Utah, New Mexico, Arizona, Idaho, some locations in Nevada, and the eastern portions of Oregon, Washington, and California.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Prairie Pothole
metas.description: The area spanning from the Montana Border with Saskatchewan to the Western Great Lakes features many âprairie potholes.â These are areas of low-lying wetlands that feature marshy grasses and small, shallow ponds.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Reddish Soil
metas.description: Youâll find red soil everywhere in the South. The area where red soil can be found stretches all the way from some parts of Louisiana and Arkansas all the way to southern Virginia through Mississippi, southern Tennessee, Alabama, Georgia, South Carolina, and North Carolina.
metas.comparison: The Oklahoma City region in Oklahoma is also notable for its red soil.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Rio Grande Valley
metas.description: The Rio Grande Valley in South Texas is extremely flat and features shrubby trees and agricultural fields. This area borders the Mexican state of Tamaulipas.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Rocky Mountains
metas.description: The area stretching from the Canadian border to Northern New Mexico is home to the Rocky Mountains. These jagged, rocky formations often feature many pine trees and visible snow all-year round at the highest peaks. Some areas of the Rocky Mountain Range are noticeably dry, with few trees.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Rolling Hills in Florida
metas.description: The area between the cities of Orlando and Lakeland in Florida sometimes feature low, rolling hills. Lakes and agricultural fields are also common in this area. This is the only main hilly area in central or southern Florida.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Roosevelt National Park
metas.description: Theodore Roosevelt National Park features similar, sand-brown, eroded rock formations to Badlands National Park. The rock formations in this park tend to have more trees on them. Additionally, almost all coverage has fall colours visible.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Similar formations can be seen in far eastern Montana as well.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Rural New Jersey
metas.description: Rural New Jersey looks strikingly southern.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Shiprock
metas.description: Shiprock is a rock formation and a municipality in northwestern New Mexico. This striking, isolated mountain is visible from distances of up to 40 km (roughly the red square) and is therefore a good clue for identifying the region within the Navajo Nation. Similar rock formations can be seen around Shiprock, but they do not have a long, low stone wall next to them.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - South Florida
metas.description: South Florida is marshy and tropical. Youâll see an abundance of palm trees here.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Southern California - Rural
metas.description: Southern California outside the major cities of Los Angeles and San Diego is a barren desert.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Southern California - Urban
metas.description: In general Los Angeles and San Diego feel more tropical and the houses are more spread out as opposed to the more compact and dense feel of San Francisco.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Spruce/Pine Forest
metas.description: Spruce and pine forests are a common sight in the western United States in New Mexico, Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, and to the west of those states.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Tablelands
metas.description: The Southwest, centred around the Four Corners region of Utah, Arizona, New Mexico, and Colorado, feature many mesas and tablelands. Often, these rock formations will be red in colour. Additionally, red soil is common in these areas.

metas.name: United States - Landscape - Texas Hills
metas.description: Just west of the metropolitan areas of Austin and San Antonio Texas lies a large area of dry, rocky hills featuring many yucca and prickly pear plants. Texas Live Oak trees are the predominant tree type in this area.

metas.name: United States - Language - Cherokee
metas.description: The Cherokee language is concentrated in the Cherokee Nation of Oklahoma and a few areas of North Carolina. It has a distinctive writing system called the Cherokee syllabary.

metas.name: United States - Language - Finnish Roadnames
metas.description: In the town of Hancock in the Upper Peninsula of Michigan, the street name signs are in Finnish as well as English.

metas.name: United States - Language - Navajo
metas.description: Navajo is spoken in the Navajo Nation in Arizona and New Mexico. Itâs the largest Native American language by the number of speakers. Navajo can be recognized from the double vowels and diacritics.

metas.name: United States - Language - Spanish
metas.description: Spanish is the most commonly spoken non-English language in the United States. Itâs the most prevalent near Mexico in Texas, New Mexico, Arizona, and California and in Florida where itâs the most spoken language in Miami-Dade County.

metas.name: United States - Language - Town Suffix: -kill
metas.description: The ending -kill is common in New York place names. Examples include Catskill and Cobleskill. The word is derived from the Middle Dutch word kille (modern Dutch kil). As New York used to be under Dutch rule in the 17th century, thatâs where youâll find them the most.

metas.name: United States - Misc - Aldi
metas.description:
Aldi is found in the eastern half, starting at ~Mid Texas. It is however not found in Maine.
In the West, it's only found in California and around Phoenix, Arizona.

metas.name: United States - Misc - BP
metas.description: BP is not found

metas.name: United States - Misc - Buc-ee's
metas.description: âBuc-eeâsâ is a small chain of oversized gas stations located primarily in the state of Texas. These stores feature multiple rows of gas pumps, and a very large convenience store building.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Some other nearby states have Buc-eeâs locations, but they are quite rare outside of Texas.

metas.name: United States - Misc - Carl's Jr.
metas.description: âCarlâs Jr.â and âHardeeâsâ are fast food restaurants that are operated by the same company and have a similar logo and colour scheme. However, Carlâs Jr. locations are all located on the West Coast and Southwest US, while Hardeeâs are found in the central and Eastern areas of the country. Two states, Wyoming and Oklahoma, have both kinds of restaurants present.

metas.name: United States - Misc - Casey's
metas.description: âCaseyâsâ is a popular gas station and convenience store chain that is found in the Midwest, Plains, and parts of the Mid-South. Illinois, Iowa, and Missouri have the highest number of locations.

metas.name: United States - Misc - Dunkin' Donuts
metas.description: Dunkin Donut's is not found in States Northwest of South Dakota.

metas.name: United States - Misc - Food Lion
metas.description: Food Lion is mostly found between Maryland and South Carolina. You can sometimes see locations in Tennessee, Georgia and West Virginia.

metas.name: United States - Misc - H-E-B
metas.description: âH-E-Bâ is a supermarket that is only located in the state of Texas. Most H-E-B stores are in large cities.

metas.name: United States - Misc - Hardee's
metas.description: âCarlâs Jr.â and âHardeeâsâ are fast food restaurants that are operated by the same company and have a similar logo and colour scheme. However, Carlâs Jr. locations are all located on the West Coast and Southwest US, while Hardeeâs are found in the central and Eastern areas of the country. Two states, Wyoming and Oklahoma, have both kinds of restaurants present.

metas.name: United States - Misc - Hy-Vee
metas.description: âHy-Veeâ is a supermarket that is common primarily in the Upper Midwest states of Iowa, Minnesota, Wisconsin, and Illinois.

metas.name: United States - Misc - In-N-Out Burger
metas.description: âIn-N-Out Burgerâ is a regional fast food chain located primarily in the Southwest US. California has the most locations.

metas.name: United States - Misc - Kroger
metas.description: Kroger is not found in

metas.name: United States - Misc - Kum & Go
metas.description: âKum & Goâ is a regional gas station chain based out of the state of Iowa. They also have pockets of locations in the Ozarks, Colorado, Wyoming, and North Dakota.

metas.name: United States - Misc - Kwik Star
metas.description: âKwik Star' is a chain of gas stations and convenience stores that are located in Iowa

metas.name: United States - Misc - Kwik Trip
metas.description: âKwik Tripâ is a chain of gas stations and convenience stores that are located in the Upper Midwest states of Wisconsin and Minnesota.

metas.name: United States - Misc - Piggly Wiggly
metas.description: The supermarket chain âPiggly Wigglyâ is found mostly in the Southeast, as well as the state of Wisconsin.

metas.name: United States - Misc - Pizza Ranch
metas.description: âPizza Ranchâ is a restaurant chain that is found in the middle of the country. Iowa and Minnesota have the highest number of locations.

metas.name: United States - Misc - Publix
metas.description: âPublixâ is a regional supermarket chain that has locations primarily in Florida and adjacent areas of the Deep South.

metas.name: United States - Misc - Sheetz
metas.description: Another regional gas station and convenience store chain in the Eastern US is called âSheetzâ. Most of their locations are in the Mid-Atlantic and Central Appalachian areas of the US. Pennsylvania has the highest number of locations.

metas.name: United States - Misc - Shoprite
metas.description: âShopriteâ is a regional supermarket chain that has locations in 6 states in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic region of the US; Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware, and Maryland.

metas.name: United States - Misc - Stop-N-Go
metas.description: âStop-N-Goâ is a chain of gas stations and convenience stores that are located in the Upper Midwest states of Iowa, Wisconsin and Minnesota.

metas.name: United States - Misc - Tim Horton's
metas.description: âTim Hortonsâ is known for being the most popular restaurant chain in Canada. However, there are also many locations in the United States. They are primarily located in states adjacent to the Canadian Provinces of Ontario and Quebec, with a few locations also in Texas and Georgia.

metas.name: United States - Misc - Waffle House
metas.description: The restaurant chain âWaffle Houseâ is a regional chain that is primarily found in the Southern and Southeast US. Some midwest and mid-atlantic states have some locations. Georgia, by far, is the state with the most Waffle House locations.

metas.name: United States - Misc - WaWa
metas.description: âWaWaâ is a regional gas station and convenience store chain with locations in the Mid-Atlantic states and Florida. New Jersey and the Philadelphia, Pennsylvania area have the highest density of locations.

metas.name: United States - Misc - Whataburger
metas.description: âWhataburgerâ is a hamburger restaurant with locations across the South Central US. The State that is home to the most locations, by far, is Texas.

metas.name: United States - Misc - Zaxby's
metas.description: âZaxbyâs,â a fast-food chicken chain, is another restaurant that is most common in the Southeast US. There are several pockets outside the Southeast that have locations, such as Utah and Montana. Like Waffle House, Georgia has the highest number of locations.

metas.name: United States - Trekker - Disney World Trekker
metas.description: GeoGuessrâs official maps have a bias for trekkers. Thus, if youâre playing the official US map or official state streaks, you should be aware of there being a lot of trekker coverage in Disney World in Orlando.

metas.name: United States - Trekker - Dry Tortugas
metas.description: The main island of Dry Tortugas National Park, west of Key West, can be identified by the hexagonal brick structure and the surrounding moat.
metas.comparison: The Loggerhead Lighthouse, situated on the Loggerhead Key, has a brown top-half and a white bottom. The path on which the trekker walks on is also made of bright concrete, and many palm trees can be seen around the lighthouse.

metas.name: United States - Vegetation - Balsam Fir
metas.description: The Balsam Fir is a very symmetric tree. It has pretty dark needles and often grows close to the ground.
metas.comparison: Within the US, you will find it in the Northeast, starting in Northern New York. You can also see it near the Great Lakes, on Latitudes similar to Vermont/Maine.

metas.name: United States - Vegetation - Buckeye
metas.description: You may already know Ohioâs nickname, the Buckeye State, but despite the name, buckeyes grow in other states too. Theyâre most commonly seen in the east from Ohio down through West Virginia, Virginia, and Kentucky to Tennessee and North Carolina. Some can be found in Missouri too.
metas.comparison: California is the only state in the west where you can see buckeyes.

metas.name: United States - Vegetation - Cabbage Palmetto
metas.description: Sabal palmetto is native to the subtropical coastal regions of the American states of Florida, Georgia, South Carolina, southeastern North Carolina, and extreme southern Texas.

metas.name: United States - Vegetation - California Fan Palm
metas.description: Washingtonia filifera is the only palm native to the Western United States and one of the country's largest native palms.

metas.name: United States - Vegetation - Dormant Grass
metas.description: Grass that is used in lawns in the southern US (colloquially known as Bermuda and St. Augustine grasses) go dormant in the winter months. This causes the lawns to turn beige or light brown in winter; whereas grasses used in more northern areas of the US stay much greener in winter.

metas.name: United States - Vegetation - Douglas Fir
metas.description: Extremely tall conifer trees (Douglas firs) with a dark brown bark, and dark green leaves, can most commonly be seen in Cascadia. Notably, they can also be found in northern California, Idaho and as far east as Montana.
metas.comparison: Beware that they are also commonly found in British Columbia.

metas.name: United States - Vegetation - Gumbo Limbo Tree
metas.description: The Gumbo Limbo tree can be recognized by its red bark and by its irregular, sometimes twisting trunks. Its leaves are green and oval shaved. You will only find it in Coastal Florida, south of Orlando and south of Tampa.

metas.name: United States - Vegetation - Palms
metas.description: Palm trees are common in coastal areas of the Southeastern states, as well as the Desert Southwest region. Shown here is the Mexican Fan Palm, which is most common in California and along the Gulf Coast, but other palm tree types have a similar range.

metas.name: United States - Vegetation - Quaking Aspen
metas.description: Aspen trees are thin trees with white barks that often grow in groups. In the contiguous states, you can find it in North-East USA, all states that border the great lakes (+NE-Iowa), in Northern Idaho and in random areas in the West.

metas.name: United States - Vegetation - Sagebrush
metas.description: Great Basin Sagebrush (Artemisia tridentata) is a short, shrubby blue-green bush that is common in the interior western United States.It is most common in arid areas.

metas.name: United States - Vegetation - Saguaro
metas.description: Saguaro cacti are most commonly shaped like tall, straight tubes with several branches extending from the main tube. They are most commonly found in southern Arizona, on the Sonoran border.

metas.name: United States - Vegetation - Saw Palmetto
metas.description: Saw Palmetto grows in clumps or dense thickets in sandy coastal areas, and as undergrowth in pine woods or hardwood hammocks. You can find it in coastal areas of Florida and Georgia.

metas.name: United States - Vegetation - Southern Live Oak
metas.description: This tree can commonly be found in Florida and along the southern coast as shown by the range map. A southern live oak will often have Spanish moss hanging from the branches, giving the tree a pendulous appearance.

metas.name: United States - Vegetation - Southern Magnolia
metas.description: This tree can only be found in the South. However, southern magnolias donât grow in southern Florida. The range stretches from Orlando and Tampa to North Carolina and Texas.

metas.name: United States - Vegetation - Southern Pines
metas.description: The loblolly pine (Pinus taeda), and longleaf pine (Pinus palustris), commonly referred to as southern pines in the community, are found throughout the southeastern US. They are a great way to recognize this region, as they are abundant, recognizable and mostly limited to this part of the country. They tend to be tall, with fluffy-looking clusters of pine needles.

metas.name: United States - Vegetation - Spanish Moss
metas.description: Spanish moss, appearing as greyish white drapes, can sometimes be seen on trees in the deep south.

metas.name: Vegetation - Acacia
metas.description: Acacia trees, recognisable by their relatively short height and umbrella-like flat crowns, are most abundant and common in northern Oman, but can also be found close to the rest of the coast.

metas.name: Vegetation - Coconut Palm
metas.description: Coconut palms are usually found near Salalah.

metas.name: Vegetation - Date Palm
metas.description: Date palm plantations are most common along the northern coast.

metas.name: Vehicle - License Plate Meta
metas.description: The US, as well as most of the Americas, uses short licence plates, in contrast to longer European ones. Each US state has their own unique licence plate design. Some of these are recognizable through the blur, and are thus worth learning. Around half of the states also do not require front plates, which can also be useful in determining the state.

metas.name: 120-Degree Angle
metas.description: These attachments with an approximately 120-degree angle can commonly be found on poles in Kansai.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Sometimes there is no angle, and instead just an angled downward attachment.

metas.name: 90-Degree Angle
metas.description: These smaller attachments with a 90-degree angle can commonly be found on poles in Shikoku.

metas.name: Aichi Road Diamond
metas.description: You can narrow down the prefecture you are in based on the style of road diamond.
metas.comparison: Aichi uses a regular but thin design

metas.name: Akita Bollard
metas.description: This bollard, much like Tohoku, will be a thick, white bollard with an octagonal reflector. However, this Akita prefecture variation will have two yellow stripes underneath the reflector.

metas.name: Aomori Bollard
metas.description: This bollard, found in the Aomori prefecture, has two yellow stripes, a single circular reflector, and is extendable. Sometimes, only one thicker stripe near the top may be present.

metas.name: Aomori Road Diamond
metas.description: You can narrow down the prefecture you are in based on the style of road diamond.
metas.comparison: This design can only be found in Aomori.

metas.name: Aomori Signpost Sticker
metas.description: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.

metas.name: Bamboo
metas.description: In general, bamboo grows more often in the south, and slowly decreases further north. Population size and areas where it grows can vary, so use this information primarily in helping assist your region guess.

metas.name: Birch-painted Pole
metas.description: These artistically painted poles, made to resemble birch trees, are unique to the city of Date in Hokkaido.

metas.name: Cabbage
metas.description: Cabbage is abundant in Hokkaido and some northern prefectures. Plants found south of Hokkaido often have smaller leaves. It is often found growing along the roadside.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Cabbage is also found on the island of Sakhalin, Russia. However, the Google car will not have low-cam there.

metas.name: Chevron-like/Orange Sticker
metas.description: You can find these chevron-like stickers, or more rarely orange ones, on guardrails in Hokkaido.
metas.comparison: On the end or side of a guardrail. Stuck to metal posts between wire fences, which are often found in Hokkaido. On railings, which are often found on bridges, underneath the inside of the railing.

metas.name: Chinese Silver Grass
metas.description: Chinese Silver Grass, referred to as Kyushu grass, is indeed very abundant on the island of Kyushu. However, use this tip with caution, as they can be seen outside of this area.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Another notable region they can be found in is the prefectures of Niigata, Yamagata and Akita. Though, combining the rather large quantity found on Kyushu, its normally distinct vegetation, along with other information, there often will be a clear distinction.

metas.name: Chubu Pole
metas.description: The transformers in Chubu, which often have painted yellow numbers and black âtapâ connectors, are either attached with large triangle and horizontal bars, or these thin metal brackets.

metas.name: Chubu Pole Plate
metas.description: Every region in Japan features a distinct plate on their utility poles.
metas.comparison: The Chubu pole plate is the only pole plate with rounded edges/rounded shape.

metas.name: Chubu Pole Reflector
metas.description: The pole reflector pads vary by region in Japan.

metas.name: Chubu Pole Top (1)
metas.description: This pole top, with four thicker bars and a circle piece at the top, is common in the Chubu region.

metas.name: Chubu Pole Top (2)
metas.description: This tuning fork pole top, with a short top bar and horizontal bar below, is found the majority of the time in the Chubu region.

metas.name: Chubu/Okinawa Guy Wire
metas.description: Most regions in Japan have unique guy wires.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Only the most consistent ones are on this map.

metas.name: Chugoku Guy Wire
metas.description: Most regions in Japan have unique guy wires.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Only the most consistent ones are on this map.

metas.name: Chugoku Pole
metas.description: The transformers in Chugoku, which have a cross-shaped bar attached in the middle of the pole, mounted by a full triangle, will have a long horizontal or short vertical insulator(s) at the end.
metas.comparison: A white sticker will often be stuck to the bottom of the transformer with red numbers. They may also be painted on the side.

metas.name: Chugoku Pole Plate
metas.description: Every region in Japan features a distinct plate on their utility poles.
metas.comparison: The pole plates in Chugoku have always "Energia" written in latin on them.

metas.name: Chugoku Pole Reflector
metas.description: The pole reflector pads vary by region in Japan.

metas.name: Chugoku Pole Top
metas.description: This pole top, with four thin, skinny bars, is common in the Chugoku region.

metas.name: Claymore
metas.description: Kerosine tanks, otherwise known as âClaymoresâ, can be found more commonly the further north you go. They are abundant in Hokkaido, but can be found in prefectures south of it, or in high elevation mountainous areas.

metas.name: Cycling Route
metas.description: Cycling routes in Ehime use an outside white, with an inside blue line. They are more commonly found along the coast but may be found further inland too.
metas.comparison: While exceptions do exist, and can be found in other prefectures, they are the extreme minority.

metas.name: Cyrillic Letters
metas.description: Cyrillic can be found on signs in the cities of Wakkanai and Nemuro, in northern Hokkaido.

metas.name: Ehime Signpost Sticker
metas.description: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.

metas.name: Fukuoka Signpost Sticker
metas.description: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.

metas.name: Gas Tank
metas.description: Hot water, gas and propane tanks can be found more frequently in northern prefectures or high elevation mountainous areas.

metas.name: Gifu Road Diamond
metas.description: You can narrow down the prefecture you are in based on the style of road diamond.
metas.comparison: This design can also be found in Gunma, Chiba and as a thinner version in Yamanashi.

metas.name: Gifu Signpost Sticker
metas.description: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.

metas.name: Green Band
metas.description: Green bands on guardrails are most commonly found in Oita and Miyazaki, but can be found on all of Kyushu.

metas.name: Green Tea
metas.description: Green tea plants are often grown in hedged rows. You will often see these fans mounted on poles, which serve the purpose of preventing frost from falling on the plants.
metas.comparison: The prefectures of Shizuoka (36%) and Kagoshima (34%) make up the majority of the production, with Mie (7%), Miyazaki (4%), and other prefectures (17%) making up the minority.

metas.name: Grey "Insulator-Esque" Blocks
metas.description: These grey âinsulator-esqueâ blocks, which wires are fed through, can be found in the regions of Chubu, Kansai, Chugoku, Shikoku, and very rarely in Hokkaido.

metas.name: Hokkaido Pole
metas.description: The electrical poles in Hokkaido either have this plus-shaped bar attached to the side of the pole, or one transformer mounted on two bars.
metas.comparison: However, if there is more than one transformer, they will often be mounted on the sides of a square. NOTE: While the Kanto transformer may also be mounted on two bars, Hokkaido will never have a wooden plate.

metas.name: Hokkaido Pole Plate
metas.description: Every region in Japan features a distinct plate on their utility poles.
metas.comparison: The Hokkaido pole plate is the plate with the highest amount of characters on one plate.

metas.name: Hokkaido Signpost Sticker
metas.description: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.

metas.name: Hokuriku Pole
metas.description: The transformers in Hokuriku, which are attached with thin metal bars, often have these small âlampâ shaped insulators. There will never be a bar present except for the attachment mentioned above.
metas.comparison: NOTE: The prefecture of Niigata will have the Tohoku transformer design, as opposed to Hokuriku one.

metas.name: Hokuriku Pole Plate
metas.description: Every region in Japan features a distinct plate on their utility poles.
metas.comparison: There are multiple horizontal plates attached to the poles in Hokuriku. They are including NTT

metas.name: Hokuriku Pole Top

metas.name: Ibaraki Signpost Sticker

metas.name: Infrastructural Arrow (Highway 275)
metas.description: This infrastructural arrow informs drivers of where the shoulder line is when under snow, and is located almost exclusively in Hokkaido.
metas.comparison: This alternate yellow and black design can often be found on the northern part of National Highway 275 in Hokkaido.

metas.name: Infrastructural Arrow (Long)
metas.description: This infrastructural arrow informs drivers of where the shoulder line is when under snow, and is located almost exclusively in Hokkaido.
metas.comparison: This variation, found in the Gifu prefecture, is long and thin.

metas.name: Infrastructural Arrow (normal)
metas.description: This infrastructural arrow informs drivers of where the shoulder line is when under snow, and is located almost exclusively in Hokkaido.

metas.name: Infrastructural Arrow (Silver Bolts)
metas.description: This infrastructural arrow informs drivers of where the shoulder line is when under snow, and is located almost exclusively in Hokkaido.
metas.comparison: This arrow, found in the Aomori prefecture (or more rarely Hokkaido), has distinct silver bolts around the border.

metas.name: Infrastructural Arrow (Yellow/Black)
metas.description: This infrastructural arrow informs drivers of where the shoulder line is when under snow, and is located almost exclusively in Hokkaido.
metas.comparison: This yellow and black arrow can be found on Hokkaido.

metas.name: Infrastructural Arrow (Yellow/Green)
metas.description: This infrastructural arrow informs drivers of where the shoulder line is when under snow, and is located almost exclusively in Hokkaido.
metas.comparison: This yellow and green arrow is found southwest of Sapporo.

metas.name: Japanese White Birch
metas.description: Japanese White Birch grows dominantly in the Chubu and Hokkaido regions, and to a lesser extent in Tohoku. Small areas of white birch can be found throughout Japan, so use this information primarily to help assist your region guess.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Japanese Beech is another species of tree found in Japan. They, however, have more grey and spotted bark, as opposed to the mostly white Japanese White Birch.

metas.name: Kagawa Road Diamond
metas.description: You can narrow down the prefecture you are in based on the style of road diamond.

metas.name: Kagawa Sign
metas.description: These specific black signs with two yellow circles are found in Kagawa. Other variations can be seen, including them stacked on top of each other, or with an arrow attached above.

metas.name: Kanagawa Signpost Sticker
metas.description: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.

metas.name: Kansai Pole
metas.description: The transformers in Kansai have either a straight or zigzag bar mounted on the bottom of a square. The transformer(s) will be mounted on the sides of that same square.
metas.comparison: While this is uncommon, the bar and transformer(s) may be mounted on a vertical bar, rather than a square. NOTE: While Tohoku may have a square attachment as well, the bar will be mounted on the top rather than the bottom.

metas.name: Kansai Pole Plate
metas.description: Every region in Japan features a distinct plate on their utility poles.
metas.comparison: This plate can be recognized by the Japanese written vertically in the middle/ on the right with other characters written in rows of two. In the bottom left and right corner are also other characters written.

metas.name: Kansai Pole Reflector
metas.description: The pole reflector pads vary by region in Japan.

metas.name: Kansai Pole Top
metas.description: This tuning fork pole top, with a thin wire and horizontal bar below, is common in the Kansai region.

metas.name: Kansai/Hokuriku/Shikoku Guy Wire
metas.description: Most regions in Japan have unique guy wires.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Only the most consistent ones are on this map.

metas.name: Kanto Pole
metas.description: The transformers in Kanto, which can have three or two insulators, are often mounted on a wooden plate and two bars, or a round plate and a T-shaped bar.
metas.comparison: NOTE: While the Hokkaido transformer may also be mounted on two bars, Tokyo will always have a wooden plate.

metas.name: Kanto Pole Plate
metas.description: Every region in Japan features a distinct plate on their utility poles.

metas.name: Kanto Pole Top
metas.description: This tuning fork pole top, with a long top bar that sticks out each end and horizontal bar(s) below, is found the majority of the time in the Kanto region.

metas.name: Kumamoto Signpost Sticker
metas.description: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.
metas.comparison: These sticker in the prefecture of Kumamoto can also be found in Kagoshima and Miyazaki (In Kagoshima and Miyazaki, they can have changed colors)

metas.name: Kyushu Pole
metas.description: The transformers in Kyushu, which have a straight bar attached on the side of the pole with three insulators at the end, will have transformers mounted 180-degrees from one another.

metas.name: Kyushu Pole Platew
metas.description: Every region in Japan features a distinct plate on their utility poles.
metas.comparison: The Kyushu plate has a small logo on top, under the logo there are 3 numbers written horizontally and then 4 characters written vertically on the right.

metas.name: Kyushu/Okinawa Guy Wire
metas.description: Most regions in Japan have unique guy wires.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Only the most consistent ones are on this map.

metas.name: Kyushu/Okinawa Pole Reflector
metas.description: The pole reflector pads vary by region in Japan.

metas.name: Kyushu/Yamaguchi Bollard
metas.description: This flat, white bollard, found on the island of Kyushu and in Yamaguchi Prefecture, will have a series of separated orange reflectors on one side, and the same white on the opposite.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Rarely, you may find similar bollards in Hokkaido. However, both sides will have orange reflectors.

metas.name: Manhole Design
metas.description: Tokyo City features a nice manhole design, with a 5 petal flower and many small circles on the outside.

metas.name: Mie Road Diamond
metas.description: You can narrow down the prefecture you are in based on the style of road diamond.
metas.comparison: This road diamond can also be found in the Kochi prefecture. In the Kumamoto and Ishikawa prefecture it is the same design, but in a thinner version.

metas.name: Miyagi Road Diamond
metas.description: You can narrow down the prefecture you are in based on the style of road diamond.
metas.comparison: This road diamond can also be found in the Kyoto, Hyogo and Okayama prefecture. In the Tokushima and Hiroshima prefecture it is the same design, but in a smaller version.

metas.name: Miyagi Signpost Sticker
metas.description: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.
