metas.name: Kazakhstan - Bollards
metas.description:
Kazakhstan uses a variety of post-Soviet style bollards, as well as ones that resemble Turkish bollards.
Notably, the bollards seemingly consisting of two thin bollards attached at a 90Â° angle are unique to Kazakhstan.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Car
metas.description: All of the coverage in Kazakhstan was taken with a white pickup truck, which can either be fully visible or mostly blurred.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Gas Pipes
metas.description: Gas pipes are extremely common in Kazakh cities.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Landscape
metas.description:
Kazakhstan is a big and diverse country, which features a plethora of distinct landscapes like deserts, grassy steppes, mountain passes, and birch forests.
Most strikingly, most of the rural coverage in Kazakhstan is in a very empty, open and mostly flat landscape.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Pedestrian Crossing
metas.description:
Like Russia, Kazakhstan uses yellow and white stripes on their pedestrian crossings.
However, unlike Russia the stripes often have white dashes on either side.
Sometimes, you can find the dashes without the stripes.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Russian Infrastructure
metas.description: A lot of Kazakh infrastructure, from pedestrian signs, poles, houses, to bollards, is very similar to what you see in Russia.

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - Bollards
metas.description: Kyrgyzstan uses these simple white bollards with a diagonal black stripe near the top.

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - Car
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - Landscape
metas.description: All of Kyrgyzstan was covered during the winter months, so many of the trees will lack leaves, the landscape will be quite drab, and you can see snow in many parts of Kyrgyzstan.

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - License Plates
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Mongolia - Bollards
metas.description: Mongolia uniquely features white bowling-pin shaped bollards with two red stripes around the top.

metas.name: Mongolia - Cars
metas.description:
Mongolia very often has a visible Street View car as all of Mongolian coverage was driven with a large pickup truck.
The truck can have several features such as a tent on top, red side-view mirrors, a snorkel, and roof-racks.
All of these can be of help in identifying Mongolia.

metas.name: Mongolia - Landscape
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Mongolia - Round Yurts
metas.description: White, round yurts are the traditional dwelling of nomadic families in Mongolia, and are often seen all around the country.

metas.name: Oman - Car
metas.description: All the coverage in Oman was taken with a white pickup truck, meaning you will either see most of the car or a large front blur.

metas.name: Oman - Chevrons
metas.description: Oman uses black-and-yellow chevrons that have an unusually large number of arrows.

metas.name: Oman - Curbs
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Oman - Garbage Bins
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Oman - High Voltage Pylons
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Oman - Landscape
metas.description:
Most of Oman features a desert landscape with little vegetation.
While the middle and southern half is mostly flat, the north coast features dry mountains similar to those found in the UAE.
The southern coast also has mountains, though less dry.

metas.name: Oman - License Plates
metas.description: Licence plates on private vehicles are generally yellow, while commercial vehicles have red plates.

metas.name: Oman - Roadlines
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Oman - Striped Signposts
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Qatar - Car
metas.description:
The Google car will usually be blurred, with only the antenna on the left and a sliver of the car visible.
Sometimes the entire white pickup truck can be visible.
Rusty clips can be seen on the crossbar.

metas.name: Qatar - Chevrons
metas.description: Qatar uses white on red and white on blue chevrons.

metas.name: Qatar - Landscape
metas.description:
Qatar's landscape is predominantly desert, with arid, and mostly flat expanses of sand as far as the eye can see.
You will often not see a lot of trees or other greenery.

metas.name: Qatar - License Plates
metas.description:
Regular cars in Qatar have long, white licence plates with a maroon strip on the left.
Trucks have square, black licence plates and police plates are blue.

metas.name: Qatar - Pedestrian Sign
metas.description: Qatari crossing signs feature a man in a thobe.

metas.name: Qatar - Poles
metas.description:
Qatar uses round poles with 3 insulators on the pole top, with the middle one being slightly higher.
The crossbar also has 2 diagonal bars connecting it to the pole.

metas.name: Qatar - Roadlines
metas.description:
Qatar typically uses solid outer white lines with either white or yellow in the middle.
More rarely, you can also find outer yellow lines too.

metas.name: Turkey - Apartment Blocks
metas.description: Tall and somewhat square apartment blocks are very common in Turkey.

metas.name: Turkey - Bollards
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Turkey - Chevrons
metas.description:
Turkish chevrons are typically red on white.
Beware that there are some other regional variants.
Usually, the tip of the arrow does not touch the edge of the chevron.
Some chevrons have a neon yellow border.

metas.name: Turkey - Gen 3 No Antenna
metas.description: In the Generation 3 coverage, the Google car never has an antenna.

metas.name: Turkey - Gen 4 Truck
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: Turkey - Gen 4 White Car
metas.description:
The Generation 4 coverage in Turkey typically features a white Google car.
Usually, only a tiny sliver of the back of the car is visible.
The car can have a short antenna, or no antenna at all.

metas.name: Turkey - Roadlines
metas.description:
The colour of Turkish road lines is somewhat inconsistent.
Most roads simply have white road lines.
However, it is not uncommon to see yellow road lines.
These roads can have fully yellow lines, or a combination of yellow and white lines.

metas.name: Turkey - Salt & Pepper Roads
metas.description: Many roads have pavement with a grainy âsalt and pepperâ texture.

metas.name: Turkey - Stop Sign
metas.description:
Stop signs have the word âDURâ written on them.
This is unique to Turkey.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Curbs
metas.description:
Similarly, almost all curbs are striped.
They can be either black-and-white, or black-and-yellow.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Gen 3 Car
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Gen 4 Black Car
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Gen 4 Truck
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Landscape
metas.description: The UAE typically features a flat desert landscape.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Poles
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Reddish Sidewalks
metas.description:
Houses in residential areas are typically made of light-coloured stone.
Reddish stones are often used for sidewalks.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Roadlines
metas.description: --- NOTE:

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Unpaved Roads
metas.description: Although the UAE is a wealthy country, it is not uncommon for residential roads to be unpaved.

metas.name: Agriculture - Corn
metas.description: Corn fields can be found in most of northern Argentina, however they are most common in CÃ³rdoba, Buenos Aires and Santiago del Estero.

metas.name: Agriculture - Mendoza Vineyards
metas.description: If you see vineyards with mountains in the west and flatness in the east, you are most likely in the outskirts of Mendoza.

metas.name: Agriculture - Sorghum
metas.description: Fields of sorghum can most commonly be seen in Santa Fe, CÃ³rdoba and Buenos Aires. It can be identified by its dark red flowerheads.

metas.name: Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.description: Sugarcane plantations are most common in TucumÃ¡n, with hotspots appearing in Salta and Jujuy.

metas.name: Agriculture - Sunflower
metas.description: Fields of sunflowers are mainly found in southern Chaco, and less commonly in Buenos Aires and southern CÃ³rdoba.

metas.name: Agriculture - Tree Plantations
metas.description: The majority of tree plantations in Argentina are located in the Entre Rios province.

metas.name: Architecture - Mar del Plata Architecture
metas.description: In Mar Del Plata and surrounding cities (such as Miramar and Necochea), a unique style of architecture can be found. Its main features include quartzite stoned facades, orange tiled roofs, attached garages, and vault shaped porches.

metas.name: Architecture - Red Brick Architecture
metas.description: Red bricks, similar to what is common in Bolivia, can be found in the northwest of the country, especially in western Jujuy.

metas.name: Car Meta - Sawdust Car Meta
metas.description: The âsawdustâ car is found in centre-south Argentina and has a unique sandy dust on its visible black back.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Low Quality Sunset Coverage
metas.description: Sunset coverage with degraded image quality is found on the RN40 just south of the Mendoza border with NeuquÃ©n.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Melted Snow Coverage
metas.description: Melting snow coverage is seen on the eastern RN293 close to the Chilean border in southwestern Santa Cruz.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Snow Coverage
metas.description: This snow coverage is found on the eastern RP25 in eastern Santa Cruz.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Sunrise Coverage with Blurs
metas.description: Sunrise coverage with bad image quality and multiple blurs is found on a short part of the RN251 and RN22, west of RÃ­o Colorado.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bariloche Taxi
metas.description: This taxi with the white body, blue roof and blue logo is unique to the city of Bariloche.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Buenos Aires Taxi
metas.description: This taxi with a black body and yellow roof is common in Buenos Aires. Note that taxis from Jujuy and RosarÃ­o have the same combination. However, Buenos Aires is the only city where the taxi has the middle bar (behind the driver) painted.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Comodoro Rivadavia Taxi
metas.description: This all white taxi with a black logo is unique to Comodoro Rivadavia.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Cordoba km-marker
metas.description: You can find these unique markers on provincial roads in Cordoba.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Cordoba Taxi
metas.description: These all green or all yellow taxis with an oval shape beneath the driver door are unique to Cordoba.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Jujuy Taxi
metas.description: Taxis in Jujuy have a black body and a yellow roof. Notably, only the top of the roof is yellow, making it distinct from Rosario or Buenos Aires taxis.

metas.name: Infrastructure - km-marker
metas.description: Argentinian kilometer markers are typically white with a black strip displaying the road number at the top. RN stands for ruta national (white on the map), RP stands for ruta provincial (green on the map).

metas.name: Infrastructure - La Pampa Junction Sign
metas.description: T-Junctions in La Pampa sometimes have these yellow rectangular signs, with a chevron pattern on the bottom, and the Road Number(s) above, with an arrow on both sides.

metas.name: Infrastructure - La Plata Taxi
metas.description: La Plata has white taxis with green elements.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Latvian-style Poles
metas.description: Within Argentina, these Latvian style wooden hook poles are unique to La Rioja and Mendoza.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Mendoza Taxi
metas.description: This black and yellow taxi is unique to Mendoza. Jujuy, Rosario and Buenos Aires also have black and yellow taxis, but on those taxis, the body is completely black.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Neuquen Taxi
metas.description: Taxis in Neuquen are all yellow. What distinguishes them from Cordoba taxis is that their doors have no logos or paintings on them.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Resistencia Taxi
metas.description: Taxis with a red-white-green stripe (hungarian flag) are unique to Resistencia.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Rosario Taxi
metas.description: Taxis in Rosario have a black body and a yellow roof. The outer bars are yellow, while the middle bar (behind the driver) is black. This makes them distinguishable from taxis in Jujuy and Buenos Aires.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Salta Taxi
metas.description: Red taxis with a black stripe are unique to Salta.

metas.name: Infrastructure - San Juan Taxi
metas.description: White taxis with a yellow roof are unique to San Juan.

metas.name: Infrastructure - San Luis Taxi
metas.description: White taxis with two light-blue stripes (resembling the Argentinian flag) are unique to San Luis.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Santiago del Estero Taxi
metas.description: White taxis with light-green roofs are unique to Santiago del Estero.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Single Hook Insulator
metas.description: In Mendoza, poles with a single insulator attached to the side of the pole can be found.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tucuman Pole ID
metas.description: White vertical pole stickers with several digits can be found in TucumÃ¡n.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tucuman Taxi
metas.description: These old-school, white taxis with a yellow-black checkerboard stripe are unique to Tucuman.

metas.name: Landscape - Bahia Blanca Hills
metas.description: Semi-coastal grass hills are seen in southern Buenos Aires, especially northeast of BahÃ­a Blanca.

metas.name: Landscape - Chaco & Formosa Landscape
metas.description: In the Chaco and Formosa provinces, you will often see sandy soil with an abundance of vegetation; mainly low trees and bushes.

metas.name: Landscape - Chenque Hill
metas.description: Comodoro Rivadavia is built on the slopes of Chenque hill, making the city recognisable.

metas.name: Landscape - Cordoba Mountains
metas.description: These mountains are typically found west of CÃ³rdoba.

metas.name: Landscape - Flat & Barren Landscape
metas.description: Flat and barren landscapes like this are typically found in central southern Argentina.

metas.name: Landscape - Grassland
metas.description: Grassland with a few separated tree plantations is generally found in this area.

metas.name: Landscape - Mars Coverage
metas.description: The RP1 in Neuquen has dark, cloudy coverage. It is a dark red dirt road and thus resembles Mars. There is some spill onto the RP7 in the North and the RP10 in the South.

metas.name: Landscape - Max South Landscape
metas.description: If you see this kind of vegetation with flat grass and a low number of bushes, you are almost certainly in the state of Tierra del Fuego or southeastern Santa Cruz.

metas.name: Landscape - Mountains
metas.description: Far western Argentina typically features a mountainous landscape.

metas.name: Landscape - Red Mountains
metas.description: These red mountains are unique to the RN68 valley in southern Salta.

metas.name: Landscape - Red Soil
metas.description: Red soil is typically found in the Misiones province.

metas.name: Landscape - Road of Death
metas.description: The western part of the RN65 in western TucumÃ¡n can easily be recognized by this bendy unpaved road up in the mountains.

metas.name: Landscape - Road of Death - Cloudy
metas.description: The western part of the RN65 in western TucumÃ¡n can easily be recognized by this bendy unpaved road up in the mountains with its western part up in the clouds.

metas.name: Landscape - Salt Pans
metas.description: Salt pans in Argentina are typically found in Jujuy.

metas.name: Landscape - San Luis Roads
metas.description: Roads with reddish pavement lined with long Argentine needle-grass are common in San Luis.

metas.name: Landscape - Small Lakes and Ponds
metas.description: Small lakes near the road are occasionally seen in the province of Buenos Aires.

metas.name: Landscape - Talampaya National Park
metas.description: Red soil with a barren landscape and mountain ranges, can often be seen on the RN76 in Parque Nacional Talampaya in western La Rioja.

metas.name: Landscape - Ushuaia
metas.description: These snowy mountains to the north can only be found in Ushuaia.

metas.name: Landscape - Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino
metas.description: Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino in northeastern Chubut is surrounded by these rock formations.

metas.name: Landscape - Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino Dam
metas.description: This unique dam with the rock formations typical for Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino can be found west of the town.

metas.name: Landscape - Volcanic Rocks
metas.description: These volcanic rocks in Generation 4 coverage can only be found on the RP43 south of Antofagasta de la Sierra in northwestern Catamarca.

metas.name: Trekker - Horse Trekker
metas.description: This horse trekker can be found in southwestern San Juan.

metas.name: Vegetation - Azorella Prolifera - Light Green
metas.description:
Azorella Prolifera is a plant that looks like "cushions". It is found throughout Patagonia.
It's appearence depends on season.
metas.comparison: You can see this plant in a distinctive light green color in these regions:

metas.name: Vegetation - Beech Forest
metas.description: Beech forests are commonly found in the state of Tierra del Fuego.

metas.name: Vegetation - Butia Yatay Palm
metas.description: The Butia yatay palm has arching, pinnate leaves and often grows at an incline with varying heights. It is most common in Corrientes and Parque Nacional El Palmar, Entre Rios.

metas.name: Vegetation - CaldÃ©n
metas.description: Prosopis caldenia, known as the caldÃ©n, is a decently large deciduous tree with small leaves and sinuous branches. It is mainly found in La Pampa.

metas.name: Vegetation - Caranday Palm
metas.description: Trithrinax Campestris, or the caranday palm, not to be confused with the Caranday Wax Palm, is a rustic palm native to the Sierras de CÃ³rdoba with a broader distribution in San Luis and northern mountainous Argentina. It can be identified by its compact fan-like leaves with a trunk hidden by a coat of dead-leaves.

metas.name: Vegetation - Caranday Wax Palm
metas.description: Coperinicia alba, also known as the Caranday Wax Palm, have short, fan-like leaves that tend to grow in low-density, single-species forests. Most common in Formosa, they can also be found in Chaco, Corrientes and northern Santa Fe.

metas.name: Vegetation - CardÃ³n
metas.description: Trichocereus atacamensis, or the cardÃ³n, is a cactus native to the high elevation mountain ranges of Catamarca, TucumÃ¡n, Salta and Jujuy. It can be identified by its candelabra-like appearance and fuzzy golden brown spines.

metas.name: Vegetation - Macaw Palm
metas.description: The Macaw Palm has small thin leaves with a visible spear shaped top. It can be found as a decorational plant all across Argentina, however in the wild it is most common in Formosa, Chaco and Misiones.

metas.name: Vegetation - Monkey Puzzle Tree
metas.description: The monkey puzzle tree can be found in western Neuquen. The most specimens are seen on provincial road 23 + offroads, between Caviahue and Atreuco.

metas.name: Vegetation - Pampas Grass
metas.description: Pampas grass (Cortaderia selloana) is one of the most defining flora of the Pampas region. It is recognizable by its long bunched reeds and white fluffy flowerheads.

metas.name: Vegetation - Pink Trumpet Tree
metas.description: The Pink Trumpet Tree (Handroanthus impetiginosus) can be found in cities in northern Salta such as OrÃ¡n, Tartagal and General Mosconi.

metas.name: Vegetation - Poplar Plantation - Mediterranean
metas.description: Poplar Trees are thin and tall decidiuous trees. They can be found all over Argentina.
metas.comparison: If you see them planted in single rows accompanied by hilly to mountainous, mediterranean landscape, as well as mediterranean agriculture (e.g. vineyards and olives) and vegetation (e.g. palm trees, platanus trees), you are likely in a town or city in the provinces of Mendoza and San Juan.

metas.name: Vegetation - Red Baron
metas.description: Red Baron is a grass species that has a very distinctive red hue. It's found in

metas.name: Vegetation - Red Baron - Dense
metas.description: Red Baron is a grass species that has a very distinctive red hue.
metas.comparison: In very dense assemblages, it can appear here:

metas.name: Vegetation - Single Row Poplar - Flat
metas.description: Poplar Trees are thin and tall decidiuous trees. They can be found all over Argentina.
metas.comparison: If you see them planted in a single row and accompanied by a very flat landscape, you are in one of these places:

metas.name: Vegetation - Toothpick Cactus
metas.description: Stetsonia coryne, or the toothpick cactus, is a large tree-like cactus with many branches and spines resembling toothpicks. Its habitat includes a hotspot between Catamarca and Cordoba as well as the border area between Chaco, Salta and Formosa.

metas.name: Vegetation - Wild Sunflower
metas.description: Wild sunflowers (Verbesina encelioides) are often found in Salta, Jujuy and TucumÃ¡n.

metas.name: Canada - 45Â° angle transformers
metas.description: Transformers on Prince Edward Island and Nova Scotia will be installed at a 45Â° angle relative to the road. On PEI, red numbers will usually be written on the side.

metas.name: Canada - Alberta bollards
metas.description: Alberta has a unique black and white bollard that is often found at intersections. It has a cylindrical shape and two black bands that wrap all the way around. It is one of the most useful Canadian bollards to learn because it appears so frequently.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Some Alberta bollards have a yellow band between the two black bands, instead of a white one. Blue bands can also rarely be seen, particularly in and around Calgary, while green bands are rarely seen in and around Edmonton.

metas.name: Canada - Alberta license plates
metas.description: Alberta license plates has red text on white background, it shows up as a red tint in the blur. It can be hard to see and it takes some time to get used to spotting it. Front plates are NOT required. Note: New Brunswick has similar license plates.

metas.name: Canada - British Columbian speed limit signs
metas.description: Some provinces have unique speed signs.
metas.comparison: British Columbian signs include the âkm/hâ but lack the black section in the Ontario sign.

metas.name: Canada - Concrete barriers
metas.description: British Columbia predominantly uses concrete barriers instead of guardrails.

metas.name: Canada - Exposed rocks
metas.description: The Canadian Shield extends through the eastern part of Canada. Therefore, you will commonly see exposed rocks on street view in the highlighted area.

metas.name: Canada - Green and white striped sticker
metas.description: You can sometimes find a green and white striped sticker on signposts in Manitoba.

metas.name: Canada - Manitoba bollards
metas.description: Manitoba uses black and grey painted bollards. Most of the time an orange stripe will be present below the grey one.
metas.comparison: Wooden, rectangular bollards of this form are typically found further north in Manitoba NOTE: Bollards in this format with just a black top are seen in Manitoba and Saskatchewan.

metas.name: Canada - Manitoba license plates
metas.description: Manitoba license plates has green on both sides. Front plates are required.

metas.name: Canada - Newfoundland bins
metas.description: Bins made of wood planks can be seen on Newfoundland driveways. These are most commonly octagonal, however they can have other shapes.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Although they are most common in Newfoundland, they can also sometimes be seen in other provinces, such as New Brunswick.

metas.name: Canada - Newfoundland fire hydrant markers
metas.description: Fire hydrants in Newfoundland often have a diamond-shaped marker next to them.

metas.name: Canada - Ontario diamond-shaped markers
metas.description: You can find these diamond-shaped markers on the sides of the roads in Ontario. The colours can vary.

metas.name: Canada - Ontario KM markers
metas.description: Ontario KM markers have a white square at the bottom, which is unique to the province.

metas.name: Canada - Ontario pole tops
metas.description: These distinctive pole tops are most commonly found in Ontario. They have two insulators to the side, and one on top. The side insulators are affixed to the pole with a distinct attachment. Sometimes, multiple of them can be stacked on top of each other.
metas.comparison: NOTE: They can occasionally appear in British Columbia, Nova Scotia, or other provinces more rarely.

metas.name: Canada - Ontario speed limit signs
metas.description: Some provinces have unique speed signs.
metas.comparison: Ontario speed limit signs may have a black section on the bottom with the words âkm/hâ or âbeginsâ written in white.

metas.name: Canada - Ontario traffic cones
metas.description: Ontario uses distinct orange and black striped traffic cones.

metas.name: Canada - Ontario wooden guardrail posts
metas.description: In Ontario, you will often see these types of guardrails. They consist of cylindrical wooden posts, held together by precisely three metal wires. Some posts are marked by a reflective white band.

metas.name: Canada - Prince Edward Island red soil
metas.description: Prince Edward Island soil has a distinct red tint to it. Potato farming is also very common on PEI.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This type of soil can occasionally be seen in certain areas of New Brunswick and Nova Scotia.

metas.name: Canada - QuÃ©bec bollards
metas.description: QuÃ©bec has unique bollards that are always attached to guardrails. They are long, thin white poles with a red or green reflector at the top.

metas.name: Canada - QuÃ©bec fire hydrant markers
metas.description: You will often find these yellow fire hydrant markers atop signposts in QuÃ©bec.
metas.comparison: In QuÃ©bec City these markers will usually have a blue rectangle and markers in Trois-RiviÃ¨res are distinctly small. NOTE: Sometimes the markers will have different colours. Beware that Edmundston, in New Brunswick, uses these too.

metas.name: Canada - QuÃ©bec French speed limit signs
metas.description: Some provinces have unique speed signs.
metas.comparison: QuÃ©bec can sometimes have French on their speed limit signs.

metas.name: Canada - QuÃ©bec poles
metas.description: Some QuÃ©bec poles have recognizable pole tops with insulator rods that are angled slightly upwards.

metas.name: Canada - QuÃ©bec traffic cones
metas.description: QuÃ©bec has unique orange and white striped traffic cones.

metas.name: Canada - Saskatchewan alternating insulators
metas.description: Pole top insulators in Saskatchewan alternate. While one pole will have one insulator on the left and two on the right, the next will have two on the left and one on the right.

metas.name: Canada - Saskatchewan license plates
metas.description: Saskatchewan license plates has green text on white background, it shows up as a green tint in the blur. It can be hard to see and it takes some time to get used to spotting it. Front plates are NOT required.

metas.name: Canada - Stop and ArrÃªt signs
metas.description: Stop signs with both âStopâ and âArrÃªtâ are most commonly found in New Brunswick.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Such stop signs can rarely be found in other provinces.

metas.name: Canada - Transformers facing the road
metas.description: The transformers on poles will face the road in British Columbia and New Brunswick, while in other provinces, it will be parallel with the wires.

metas.name: Canada - White triangles on signpost
metas.description: Signposts in Saskatchewan can feature these white triangles. The number can vary.

metas.name: Canada - Wooden post pyramid top
metas.description: In Newfoundland and Labrador, most wooden posts on guardrails have this pyramid shaped top. Occasionally, you can spot them on standalone posts and signposts as well.

metas.name: United States - Agricultural golden fields
metas.description: Agricultural golden fields can commonly be seen in eastern Washington.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Flat areas of northern and eastern Oregon can have a similar appearance.

metas.name: United States - Alabama license plates
metas.description: Front plates are NOT required.

metas.name: United States - Alaska license plates
metas.description: There are three variants of Alaska license plates.

metas.name: United States - Alaskan highway shield
metas.description: The Alaskan highway shield has an image of the Big Dipper constellation on the bottom left.

metas.name: United States - Arizona license plates
metas.description: Front plates are NOT required.

metas.name: United States - Black between middle lines
metas.description: A black stripe can sometimes be seen in between the two yellow, middle road lines in California.

metas.name: United States - California Central Valley
metas.description: Central Valley, California can be recognized by its Mediterranean climate. This is reflected in its agriculture, seen in the vineyards and olive trees that can commonly be found here.
metas.comparison: In addition, rolling hills can be seen toward the edges of the valley.

metas.name: United States - California utility poles
metas.description: Utility poles in California usually have markings at the bottom of the pole that consist of 3 yellow stripes.

metas.name: United States - Colorado license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: United States - Concrete highways
metas.description: Concrete paving on main highways is much more common in Iowa than in other states.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Concrete paving on residential streets is commonly seen throughout the Midwest states and parts of the East Coast.

metas.name: United States - Connecticut license plates
metas.description: Connecticut license plates are blue on top and fades into white on the bottom. Front plates are required.

metas.name: United States - Corn fields
metas.description: Corn fields can most commonly be found in these regions. For a detailed overview, see this map.

metas.name: United States - Cotton
metas.description: Cotton is a crop that produces large fields of fluffy white flowers. It is most commonly produced in coastal Southeast States, the Lower Mississippi River Valley, Western Texas, and parts of California and Arizona. You can click here for a more detailed map.
metas.comparison: NOTE: When cotton is not fully grown (earlier in the year) cotton fields often look like image number 2.

metas.name: United States - Delaware license plates
metas.description: Delaware license plates has gold text on dark blue background, it shows up as a dark blue blur with gold in the middle, and is easy to spot. Front plates are NOT required. Note: A similar plate can be found in Michigan.

metas.name: United States - Diamond bollards
metas.description: The most common type of roadside bollard in South Dakota and Montana features a dark metal post with a white diamond on each side of the top.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These bollards can be found to a lesser extent in other western states.

metas.name: United States - Double signpost
metas.description: Signs attached to two signposts can be seen in Michigan. Not all signs are attached to two signposts.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Double signposts can also be seen in other states, but are not as common.

metas.name: United States - Douglas firs
metas.description: Extremely tall conifer trees (Douglas firs) with a dark brown bark, and dark green leaves, can most commonly be seen in Cascadia. Notably, they can also be found in northern California, Idaho and as far east as Montana.
metas.comparison: Beware that they are also commonly found in British Columbia.

metas.name: United States - Eastern white pine
metas.description: The Eastern white pine (Pinus strobus) is a large pine native to eastern North America. It can be found in the Great Lakes region and in the Appalachian Mountains.
metas.comparison: Image source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/nrs/atlas/tree/v3/129

metas.name: United States - Florida license plates
metas.description: Florida license plates has green text on a white background, and it has oranges in the middle, which makes the plate unique. Front plates are NOT required.

metas.name: United States - Georgia license plates
metas.description: Front plates are NOT required.

metas.name: United States - Hanging traffic lights and signs
metas.description: Many large intersections in Michigan have stop lights and signs that hang from wires that stretch across the middle of the intersection. These markers are commonly in yellow boxes.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These are not completely unique to Michigan, but are most commonly seen there.

metas.name: United States - Hawaii license plates
metas.description: Hawaii license plates has black text on a white background. It also has a rainbow in the background that is somtimes more or less visible. Front plates are required.

metas.name: United States - Hawaiian language
metas.description: Hawaii is the only state to use its own language, though English is still predominantly used. Most place names are in Hawaiian, so you can spot it on street signs, and other road markers.
metas.comparison: Hawaiian is a vowel-oriented language that only uses eight consonants: H, K, L, M, N, P, W, and (Ê»), called an Ê»Okina. Every Hawaiian word ends in one of 5 vowels: A, E, I, O, or U. Each vowel can also have a macron over it: Ä, Ä, Äª, Å, and Åª. These vowels are often combined to make Diphthongs. I.e. UI, AI, AE, etc...

metas.name: United States - Hawaiian topography
metas.description: Topography on Hawaii is characterised by many sloping volcanoes, rugged cliffs, hills, valleys and craters. Such distinct topography combined with tropical vegetation is a good way to identify Hawaii.

metas.name: United States - Idaho license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: United States - Illinois license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: United States - Indiana license plates
metas.description: Front plates are NOT required.

metas.name: United States - Kansas white reflectors
metas.description: These white reflectors on signposts are unique to Kansas. They are most commonly seen on âstopâ signs in rural areas.

metas.name: United States - Maryland license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: United States - Massachusetts license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: United States - Minnesota black-and-white marker
metas.description: On most rural âstopâ signposts in Minnesota, a black-and-white marker is attached to the posts horizontally. The shape may vary slightly.

metas.name: United States - Minnesota yellow signs
metas.description: In Minnesota, these yellow signs with vertical, black triangles are placed before bridges at most major river crossings and at the beginnings and ends of guardrail sections on large highways.

metas.name: United States - Nebraska Sandhills
metas.description: The Nebraska Sandhills are a recognizable region of rolling hills covered with prairie grass in the central-north part of the state.

metas.name: United States - Nevada Bollards
metas.description: This bollard is found in Nevada. It consists of a reflector on a thin stick. The reflector is a vertical rectangle that consists of a white field surrounded by a black outline.

metas.name: United States - Nevada license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: United States - New Hampshire license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: United States - New Jersey license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: United States - New Mexico license plates
metas.description: New Mexico license plates has red text on yellow background or yellow text on green background, it shows up as a mostly yellow or green blur, and is easy to spot. Front plates are NOT required.

metas.name: United States - New York license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: United States - No middle line
metas.description: Some small roads in California lack a middle yellow line; instead only feature solid white lines on each side of the road.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This can rarely be seen in other states.

metas.name: United States - North Dakota license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: United States - Oil pumpjacks
metas.description: Oil pumpjacks are short, industrial-looking metal structures located at the surface of oil fields and are used to pump crude oil from the earth below. They are most common in western states, particularly in Texas, Eastern New Mexico, and North Dakota.

metas.name: United States - Oklahoma license plates
metas.description: Front plates are NOT required.

metas.name: United States - Oregon license plates
metas.description: Oregon license plates has blue text on white background with a green tree in the middle, it shows up as a green dot in the white/blue blur on the sides. Front plates are required.

metas.name: United States - Prairie potholes
metas.description: The area spanning from the Montana Border with Saskatchewan to the Western Great Lakes features many âprairie potholes.â These are areas of low-lying wetlands that feature marshy grasses and small, shallow ponds.

metas.name: United States - Red mesas and tablelands
metas.description: The Southwest, centred around the Four Corners region of Utah, Arizona, New Mexico, and Colorado, feature many mesas and tablelands. Often, these rock formations will be red in colour. Additionally, red soil is common in these areas.

metas.name: United States - Red soil
metas.description: Many parts of the Deep South, stretching from Oklahoma to South Carolina, have reddish soil. The exact tint of the soil can range from yellow to deep red.

metas.name: United States - Rice
metas.description: Rice production only occurs in a few areas of the US, so it is very useful for region guessing. It is typically grown in large, flat fields that resemble low prairies. It is only grown in north-central California and the Lower Mississippi River Valley in Arkansas, Louisiana, Texas, and Mississippi. You can click here for a more detailed map.
metas.comparison: NOTE: When rice is not fully grown, rice fields often look similar to image 2.

metas.name: United States - Sagebrush
metas.description: Great Basin Sagebrush (Artemisia tridentata) is a short, shrubby blue-green bush that is common in the interior western United States.It is most common in arid areas.

metas.name: United States - Saguaro cacti
metas.description: Saguaro cacti are most commonly shaped like tall, straight tubes with several branches extending from the main tube. They are most commonly found in southern Arizona, on the Sonoran border.

metas.name: United States - South Dakota license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: United States - Southern pines
metas.description: The loblolly pine (Pinus taeda), and longleaf pine (Pinus palustris), commonly referred to as southern pines in the community, are found throughout the southeastern US. They are a great way to recognize this region, as they are abundant, recognizable and mostly limited to this part of the country. They tend to be tall, with fluffy-looking clusters of pine needles.

metas.name: United States - Soybeans
metas.description: Soybeans are short, dark green crops organised in long rows and are found in similar regions where corn is grown. They are most common in the Eastern Plains, Midwest, Lower Mississippi Valley, and areas of the Mid Atlantic.

metas.name: United States - Spanish moss
metas.description: Spanish moss, appearing as greyish white drapes, can sometimes be seen on trees in the deep south.

metas.name: United States - Speed instead of Speed Limit
metas.description: Speed signs in Oregon often simply have the word âSpeedâ instead of the standard âSpeed Limitâ.

metas.name: United States - Temperate rainforests
metas.description: Temperate rainforests are found in coastal areas of Washington, Oregon, and Northern California. These rainforests feature many broadleaf trees, large conifers, and ferns.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These rainforests stretch north into coastal British Columbia and Southeast Alaska as well.

metas.name: United States - Texan roads
metas.description: Texan roads often have a grainy, âsalt and pepperâ-like road surface.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Similar pavement can sometimes be seen in adjacent states such as New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Colorado.

metas.name: United States - Texas license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: United States - The Great Basin
metas.description: The Great Basin, centred around Nevada, can be recognized by the tall, sometimes snow-capped mountains in the background. There are dry, but grassy, and slightly shrubby plains leading up to the mountains.
metas.comparison: The tallest mountains are in Nevada, Utah and California. More gradual, rocky hills can be seen in Oregon, and greener mountains can be seen in Idaho and central Utah. Keep in mind that there are exceptions, so make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

metas.name: United States - The Rocky Mountains
metas.description: The area stretching from the Canadian border to Northern New Mexico is home to the Rocky Mountains. These jagged, rocky formations often feature many pine trees and visible snow all-year round at the highest peaks. Some areas of the Rocky Mountain Range are noticeably dry, with few trees.

metas.name: United States - Thick road lines
metas.description: Some roads in West Virginia, Virginia, and Maryland use middle yellow lines that are thicker than traditional yellow road lines.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These are not present on all roads in these states, and can be found elsewhere, so use this tip in conjunction with other clues.

metas.name: United States - Utah license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: United States - Vermont license plates
metas.description: Vermont license plates has white text on green background, it shows up as a green blur with white on the sides, and is easy to spot. Front plates are required.

metas.name: United States - Washington bollards
metas.description: The state of Washington uses bollards that consist of a white or brown post with a white rectangle on the front of the bollard, and two smaller white or silver squares on the back of the bollard.

metas.name: United States - Washington license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: United States - Wide middle lines
metas.description: Yellow lines with a noticeably larger gap in between them are most common in Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Oregon. They can also be found to a lesser extent in Washington, Alabama, and Michigan.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Wide middle lines can also rarely appear in other states, so consider other clues before guessing.

metas.name: United States - Wisconsin ATV Route signs
metas.description: These green ATV Route signs are unique to Wisconsin.

metas.name: United States - Wisconsin bollard
metas.description: These simple white bollards with black reflectors are unique to Wisconsin.

metas.name: United States - Wisconsin pole plate
metas.description: A rectangular white metal plate, with an orange rectangle and diamond, can be seen on most poles in Wisconsin and the Michigan peninsula.

metas.name: United States - Wyoming license plates
metas.description: Front plates are required.

metas.name: United States - Yellow or red bands
metas.description: Yellow or red bands can commonly be seen around signposts in Texas.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Similar reflectors can sometimes be seen in other states, such as Hawaii.

metas.name: Architecture - Ankara
metas.description: Within Ankara you can find many large townhouses, often with triangular roofs and sharp painted and/or mosaic patterns.

metas.name: Architecture - Ankara Outskirts
metas.description: Meanwhile the outskirts of Ankara are infamous for their urban sprawl, with strange skyscraper cities in the middle of Central Anatolian nothingness.

metas.name: Architecture - Bartin
metas.description: In older parts of BartÄ±n you will find many old all-wooden houses.

metas.name: Architecture - Bilecik Mud Bricks
metas.description: In Bilecik and large parts of neighbouring provinces like Bursa, Bolu and Sakarya, you can commonly find the combination of timber-framed houses with mud bricks.

metas.name: Architecture - Bozcaada
metas.description: Houses on Bozcaada feature many brightly coloured houses with wooden shutters and often wooden second floor faÃ§ades.

metas.name: Architecture - Cow Dung
metas.description: In remote villages in far eastern Turkey you can find cow dung being used as a construction material, mostly for walls. Cow dung âbricksâ or âslabsâ are often kept in large, very recognisable piles.

metas.name: Architecture - DiyarbakÄ±r
metas.description: The city of DiyarbakÄ±r is one of the poorest cities in Turkey and the largest in the southeast, consequently, it has many slums. These differ heavily from those in Adana however, with equally narrow streets but far taller buildings creating lots of dark alleys. The pavement visible in the image is unique to these slums.

metas.name: Architecture - Diyarkakir Center
metas.description: The old center of DiyarbakÄ±r however is a very strange place. Much of it was destroyed during the Turkish-Kurdish conflict in 2016 and now much is being rebuilt in this unique, oddly clean, modern style, with a lot of dark grey clean-cut bricks.

metas.name: Architecture - DÃ¼zce
metas.description: In DÃ¼zce province, you can often find clean timber-framed houses with well-defined edges and colours.

metas.name: Architecture - Elmali
metas.description: One noteworthy cluster of wood-framed houses outside the northwest is in the ElmalÄ± valley in Antalya province. Here the frames are notably intricate with many small beams packed together and eight beams meeting at one point - rare in the NW.

metas.name: Architecture - Grass Roofs
metas.description: In the inland northeast of Turkey it is very common in villages to find low stone structures with grass roofs - these are mostly storehouses although rarely they constitute actual houses.

metas.name: Architecture - KahramanmaraÅ
metas.description: KahramanmaraÅ was the worst-affected city by the 2023 earthquake. As a result, even though a lot of the coverage was taken two years later, you will still find a lot of rubble, construction sites and empty lots here. (Similar scenes can be seen less frequently in neighbouring provinces)

metas.name: Architecture - Kars
metas.description: Older buildings in the city of Kars will usually be made of this unique black tuff.

metas.name: Architecture - Kastamonu
metas.description: Kastamonu timber-framed houses often feature a pattern of downward-pointing bricks.

metas.name: Architecture - Kayseri
metas.description: These larger blocks made of volcanic stone are very common in the architecture of Kayseri.

metas.name: Architecture - Kurdish Mountain Villages
metas.description: Villages in more remote and mountainous parts of the Southeast, particularly in provinces like Siirt and Bitlis, have a distinct architecture consisting of flat-topped, tightly-packed stone houses. These are also identifiable from afar as house clusters look like âstepsâ on the mountainside.

metas.name: Architecture - Mugla Chimney
metas.description: The city of MuÄla (and to a lesser extent other towns in MuÄla province) have these very unique chimneys which have openings on four sides and little flashings on top.

metas.name: Architecture - Ne Coast
metas.description: Whereas the northwest of Turkey features a lot of traditional architecture with wooden elements, the northeastern coastal hills (roughly from Ordu province eastwards) feature almost entirely concrete buildings even in remote villages, as the extreme humidity of this region makes more traditional materials less viable.

metas.name: Architecture - Ottoman
metas.description: Ottoman architecture is characterised by plain-white walls with wooden window frames and shutters, as well as wooden outlines on most (but not all) buildings and an overhanging second floor. It correlates well with the original homeland of the Ottomans in the Northwest (particularly around Bolu). Some historical towns (e.g. Safranbolu, TaraklÄ±) even have predominantly Ottoman architecture.

metas.name: Architecture - Prince Islands
metas.description: The Prince Islands off the coast of Istanbul are famous for their predominantly wood panel, all-white, elegant architecture. The islands are also car-free, so the only vehicles youâll see will be trikes and bikes.

metas.name: Architecture - Syriac Architecture
metas.description: Tur Abdin is a cultural region in Eastern Mardin centered around Midyat. It is the cultural center of Syriac Orthodox Christianity and many buildings here have a very unique design defined by blocky buildings made of âMalta stoneâ, rich decoration and frequent use of balustrades. There is also a rarer âdiamond stoneâ wall type that is found here. The architectural influences of this area extend beyond it too. Certain features such as the stone type and prominent arches, as well as twin semi-circle windows on faÃ§ades, extend into villages in southern Batman too.

metas.name: Architecture - Usak Stone
metas.description: Because of the volcanic nature of UÅak, stone houses are more common here than other parts of Western Turkey. These are either white-beige, with a mix of large and small stones, or made of darker brown-grey stone. Quoins are common too. (This looks similar to houses in some regions further east such as Konya, however UÅak is the only region where this type of stone is abundant outside of mountains).

metas.name: Chevrons - Single Yellow on Black
metas.description: Single type yellow on black chevrons are almost exclusive to BalÄ±kesir province.

metas.name: Chevrons - Yellow Edge
metas.description:
Chevrons with yellow edges are found mainly in four provinces; Ä°stanbul, Sakarya, Bursa in the northwest, and Adana in the south. They are rarely found in other provinces(see the map below)
NOTE: Ä°stanbul, Bursa and Adana mainly use double type chevrons. When you see single type chevrons with yellow edges and the landscape does not look Mediterranean, you are likely to be in Sakarya.

metas.name: Cultural - Alawites
metas.description: Alawites are a unique sect within Shiism who are pretty much only found in Hatay (especially southern Hatay). Their mosques look completely different, usually being small, lacking a minaret, and painted all white, often with green highlights.

metas.name: Cultural - Arabic Signs
metas.description: There is a substantial Arab population living in certain border provinces like ÅanlÄ±urfa, Kilis and Mardin, as well as large numbers of refugees in those regions. These are most common in the border towns of AkÃ§akale and Nusaybin, and to a lesser extent in ÅanlÄ±urfa and Kilis.

metas.name: Cultural - Bulgarian Signs
metas.description: In towns near the Bulgarian border you can sometimes find Bulgarian translations on signs.

metas.name: Cultural - Kurds
metas.description: Kurds are an Iranic ethnic group that populate much of Southeastern Turkey. In some of the most Kurdish provinces such as Mardin, ÅÄ±rnak, HakkÃ¢ri or DiyarbakÄ±r you can occasionally find signage in Kurdish. Kurdish bilingual road signs are particularly common in DiyarbakÄ±r and less so in Mardin. The Kurdish language is identified by the presence of circumflex accents (e.g. Ãª, Ã®) as well as letters that Turkish lacks such as âqâ, âwâ and âxâ.

metas.name: Cultural - Russian Signs
metas.description: In Antalya and nearby tourist resorts you will sometimes find Russian signs as the area is very popular with Russian tourists.

metas.name: Cultural - Shiism
metas.description: IÄdÄ±r is the only Shia-majority province of Turkey (not counting Alevis/Alawites). In Shiite areas you will often see black flags with Arabic slogans on them (even without sometimes), as well as pictures of Husseyn.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Akmercan
metas.description: Akmercan is another trans-provincial company that is worth learning for more advanced players. Plaques are either divided into 3 colours, or feature the logo quite prominently.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Aksa

metas.description: The province of Edirne has these unique town entry signs with a trapezoid welcome sign followed by the province name (Edirne), followed by the district, followed by the municipality.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Gallipoli Signs
metas.description: The Gallipoli peninsula (the European part of Ãanakkale province) is famous for the WWI battles fought between Anzac forces of the British Empire and the Ottoman Empire. You will often find unique yellow-on-brown road signs here indicating tourist sites. There is also ample trekker coverage of the military cemeteries here, so if you get a cemetery trekker, go Gallipoli.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Gazdas
metas.description: GazdaÅ has two main divisions - Trakya and Gaziantep. The first operates in the three Thracian provinces of Edirne, KÄ±rklareli and TekirdaÄ, whereas the second operates in Gaziantep and Kilis. Its plaques are yellow, red and white, similar to some Akmercan plaques.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Istanbul
metas.description: Istanbul trams will always have the âMetro Istanbulâ symbol on either end (also found at metro stations).

metas.name: Infrastructure - Oil Fields
metas.description: Oil fields are a good meta for Batman province, particularly just south of Batman city. They exist in other provinces too, but are far more common here than anywhere else. You will also rarely see oil fields in eastern AdÄ±yaman.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Wind Farms
metas.description: Wind turbines are mostly found in the far west of the country, particularly the northwest. Particularly strong hotspots include BalÄ±kesir province, western Istanbul and the Karabunar peninsula and YeniÅakran areas in Ä°zmir province.
