metas.name: Landscape - Adana Plain
metas.description: The Adana plain is one of the largest expanse of flat land in Turkey with a subtropical landscape.The southwest is deadflat with very mixed agriculture consisting of different fruit and vegetable fields as well as cotton and corn, with subtropical plants such as eucalyptus, palms and reeds being common in between. Mountains will normally be visible to the northwest.

metas.name: Landscape - Afyonkarahisar
metas.description: The city of Afyonkarahisar has numerous small but steep-sided hills in the middle of town that can appear very close even on very urban rounds.

metas.name: Landscape - Aladaglari
metas.description: In AladaÄlarÄ± Milli Park (National Park) you will find a huge steep wall of mountains to your east which is highly recognisable, even from some distance.

metas.name: Landscape - Amasya
metas.description: The city of Amasya is tightly bound within a valley surrounded by rocky hills. The city centre is overlooked by a hill with a castle on top and imposing Pontic tombs carved within it.

metas.name: Landscape - Antalya
metas.description: Much of Antalya province is very recognisable for its forests composed entirely of Turkish pines combined with a rocky karst landscape.

metas.name: Landscape - Ararat
metas.description: Mount Ararat is the tallest peak in Turkey and the tallest in the Middle East outside Iran. It is particularly recognisable as it also has a prominent secondary peak called Masis. It is situated near the Armenian border on the border between AÄrÄ± (its Turkish name) province and IÄdÄ±r province.

metas.name: Landscape - Balik GÃ¶lÃ¼
metas.description: BalÄ±k GÃ¶lÃ¼ is one of two lakes in far eastern Turkey (beside Lake Van) situated within a pristine, green steppe-like environment. The other is ÃÄ±ldÄ±r GÃ¶lÃ¼, the main distinction being that BalÄ±k GÃ¶lÃ¼ is smaller and surrounded by mountains.

metas.name: Landscape - Bitlis
metas.description: Bitlis is one of the smallest provincial capitals. It is a very green city surrounded by dry mountains. The city itself is also very historical, with a huge castle in the middle and lots of old stone mosques.

metas.name: Landscape - Burdur GÃ¶lÃ¼
metas.description: Burdur is a saline lake in the west of Turkey, and therefore contained within a valley surrounded by mountains (unlike the salt lakes of Central Anatolia). The only other such lake is AcÄ± GÃ¶lÃ¼ just north of it.

metas.name: Landscape - Cappadocia
metas.description: Cappadocia is a very unique and famous area in Central Turkey just east of NevÅehir which is highly distinct for its âfairy chimneysâ. In the absence of these you can still identify the region through itâs exposed hillsides made of pink and white rock and general âUtah-likeâ landscape.

metas.name: Landscape - Central Volcanic Hills
metas.description: Stretching from Southern NevÅehir to KarapÄ±nar in Konya province are a range of long-extinct volcanoes. In the flatter parts between these volcanoes, where you will find more coverage, you will find numerous isolated, smooth-sloped volcanic hills which are largely unique to this area. (You can find somewhat similar hills in Northern Konya).

metas.name: Landscape - Cildir GÃ¶lÃ¼
metas.description: ÃÄ±ldÄ±r GÃ¶lÃ¼ is the other far-eastern steppe lake, situated much further north near the Georgian border. It is larger, greener, and surrounded by gentler slopes.

metas.name: Landscape - Eastern Hatay Northern Half
metas.description: Meanwhile, the northern half going into Gaziantep forms a more narrow valley with mountains clearly visible on either side. Here you will also find rock walls made of large orange boulders, as well as a more rocky landscape more generally.

metas.name: Landscape - Eastern Hatay South
metas.description: Eastern Hatay has a superflat landscape, however unlike the Central Plateau, the soil here is quite red and you will always be able to see mountains to your east & west. It can be divided in two parts - the southern half is wider and more featureless, with mountains often quite distant.

metas.name: Landscape - Eastern Mardin
metas.description: Eastern Mardin has a very distinct landscape of low, craggy hills covered in stone walls and scattered vegetation.

metas.name: Landscape - Eastern Taurus
metas.description: The Eastern Taurus are the high mountains that form a chain roughly from BingÃ¶l to south of Lake Van. Like Tunceli, they also form islands of forests in the Southeast, although the soil is less red and the whole region is visibly drier. The valleys will also be full of black poplars

metas.name: Landscape - Erciyes
metas.description: Mount Erciyes is the second tallest volcano in Turkey after Mount Ararat. It is located south of the city of Kayseri where it can be seen for some distance, and is particularly identifiable for the numerous volcanic ridges and sub-peaks surrounding the main peak (which is usually not visible).

metas.name: Landscape - Erzincan Plain
metas.description: Erzincan is situated in a relatively narrow plain with particularly high mountains on both sides, with high peaks to the northeast and southeast. The valley also has a moderate amount of tree cover with black poplars and willows being common.

metas.name: Landscape - Hasandag
metas.description: Another important volcano is HasandaÄ southeast of the city of Aksaray. Unlike Erciyes it is a more clear cone volcano and due to the dryness of Aksaray province its peak is more likely to be visible.

metas.name: Landscape - Igdir
metas.description: Most of IÄdÄ±r province is covered by the Arax plain, shared with Armenia. Here youâll find a flat landscape covered in grassy fields and loads of black poplars. The best indication that you are here is Mount Ararat to the south, but it can sometimes be hard to see. Besides the landscape, villages in IÄdÄ±r usually consist of houses made of large, plain grey bricks and sheet metal roofs, and youâll also find a lot of tall haystacks here.

metas.name: Landscape - Karaburun Ppeninsula
metas.description: The Karaburun Peninsula is one of the most mountainous parts of the west coast, and has a unique landscape of either low spongy bushes or olive plantations, often with wind farms visible in the background. The southern part of the peninsula is less mountainous but has a lot of small rocks all over the ground.

metas.name: Landscape - Karacadag
metas.description: KaracadaÄ is a wide, gently-rising volcanic hill with a unique barren, red soil and bushy landscape. The hill itself can be recognised from afar as a gently rising hill with a black stone peak. The area around it is also covered in volcanic rocks. Fun fact, it is on the slopes of this hill that the first evidence of wheat domestication was discovered.

metas.name: Landscape - Kastamonu
metas.description: Kastamonu is essentially a small plateau within the northern mountains, which is drier and more piney than anywhere else in the north, with a landscape of agricultural, gently-rolling hills, often with slightly taller greener hills visible in the distance. The northern half of this plateau around Devrekani is particular distinct for its mixture of bare with lots of exposed rocks and dry all-pine forests.

metas.name: Landscape - Kilis Hills
metas.description: The only similar area to Eastern Mardin (see above) is the hills of Kilis and Gaziantep. The key difference is that these hills are volcanic, meaning the stones and soil are darker, and you will also find more agriculture and fewer scattered bushes in the shallow valleys.

metas.name: Landscape - Konya
metas.description: The Konya plain is the flattest part of Turkey and also very green and agricultural in relation to other parts of the Anatolian plateau. Note that the plain stretches east from Konya to the city KarapÄ±nar.

metas.name: Landscape - KÃ¶se Dagi
metas.description: KÃ¶se DaÄÄ± is the highest peak of the Aras range, located to the northwest of the AÄrÄ± valley. Being far more prominent than the surrounding peaks, and having a relatively smooth shape, it is a good way to identify the valley.

metas.name: Landscape - KÃ¼re Daglari
metas.description: Within the northern forested mountains of Turkey there is one area that is topographically very different from the rest, situated in BartÄ±n province very near the coast covered by the KÃ¼re Mountains National Park. Whatâs unique about these mountains is that they form a plateau with steep cliffs on most sides which are visible from numerous angles, very different from the interlocking peaks in the rest of the north.

metas.name: Landscape - Malatya
metas.description: North of the city of Malatya is a relatively large flat agricultural area which can look very uncharacteristic for the east. Most of Turkeyâs apricots are grown here, so recognising apricot trees can help, otherwise you may be able to see dry mountains from the area, which should indicate you are in Malatya rather than other fruit-producing regions.

metas.name: Landscape - Medetsiz Tepe
metas.description: Medetsiz Tepe is one of the highest massifs in the Taurus Mountains forming a fairly long, roughly east-west ridge, which is visible from a stretch of the D750 and some remote villages and mountain roads as a wall of snow-capped mountains to the south.

metas.name: Landscape - Menderes Massif
metas.description: The Menderes Massif is a unique geological area covering much of AydÄ±n province. Here youâll find a lot of grey boulders and exposed rock, leading to the construction of lots of stone walls. Stone pines are also exceedingly common in this region.

metas.name: Landscape - Mut Landscape
metas.description: Around the town of Mut in western Mersin province, you will find a unique karst landscape of white soil with a mix of conical and table mountains and generally crazy topography, all surrounded by fruit tree plantations.

metas.name: Landscape - Nur Mountains 1
metas.description: The Nur Mountains is the range that runs the length of Hatay Province. They are identifiable in various ways - certain types of infrastructure in a green mountainous setting are especially common in Hatay, metal mesh poles and âsoutheast housesâ with flat roofs. Another distinct feature of these mountains is how âhigh upâ many rounds seem. While the Hatay mountains are far from the highest, they rise extremely precipitously, giving the illusion of being incredibly tall when looking down at the coast.

metas.name: Landscape - Red Soil
metas.description: North of Gaziantep, leaking a bit into ÅanlÄ±urfa province, you can find extreme dark red soils, mostly covered in pistachio or olive plantations.

metas.name: Landscape - Salt Pans
metas.description: In the middle of the Anatolian plateau you can find a number of salt pans, the largest being Tuz GÃ¶lÃ¼ (lit. âsalt lakeâ) at the tripoint of Konya, Aksaray and Ankara provinces. Around these lakes you will find a deadflat, pale landscape with very minimal vegetation consisting mostly of thistles. Sometimes the salt lakes themselves will be visible.

metas.name: Landscape - Strandzha
metas.description: Strandzha is a hill range on the Bulgarian border in the northern part of European Turkey. It consists of low but very green hills, however it can be extremely difficult to tell apart from other parts of North Turkey. Besides a general âEuropean forest vibeâ, other clues for Strandzha are small, empty grassy clearings by the roadside, young cottonwood plantations, and yellow bollards which, whilst not exclusive to KÄ±rklareli, are common here while very rare in the rest of the country.

metas.name: Landscape - SÃ¼phan Dagi
metas.description: SÃ¼phan DaÄÄ± is an isolated, snow-capped volcano on the northern shore of Lake Van, which makes it an excellent reference point for pinpointing your position on the lake, but also for the remote dirt roads to the north of the mountain.

metas.name: Landscape - Tunceli
metas.description: Tunceli is unusually green for an eastern province. It is distinguishable from other forested parts of the country as its forests consist exclusively of oak trees, with slightly reddish soil and exposed dark grey mountain sides further confirming the province.

metas.name: Landscape - Uludag
metas.description: UludaÄ is the highest mountain in the northwest of Turkey. It is useful for identifying Bursa and the plain around it, as the mountain creates a huge, cloud-shrouded wall to the south.

metas.name: Landscape - Usak
metas.description: UÅak sits on an ancient volcanic basin (technically a northern extension of the Menderes Massif) meaning you will see a lot of scattered rocks on the ground, although these are much lighter coloured than in the Menderes Massif. (This is quite subtle but still useful in flatter, more agricultural areas).

metas.name: Landscape - White Bluffs
metas.description: There is a large area between the cities of Ankara and EskiÅehir that is full of these low hills with exposed white hillsides, with a generally green, agricultural, but mostly treeless landscape beside it.
metas.comparison: A smaller cluster of these exposed hillsides can be found in ÃankÄ±rÄ± province, where they are more pronounced and have marked striations.

metas.name: Recognisable Roads - D400
metas.description: The part of the D400 that runs along the Iraqi border is very recognisable. It runs through a narrow and very dry canyon with lots of poplars and a small stream (the border itself) at the bottom.

metas.name: Recognisable Roads - D885
metas.description: The D885 between Tunceli and PÃ¼lÃ¼mÃ¼r is quite recognisable. It goes through a typical Tunceli landscape (see above) however it consistently follows a stream with the road following the bottom of a valley. Furthermore, at many points along the road youâll find these mini tunnels, and there is frequent graffiti/political posters for Kurdish militant groups (PKK/HPG) and the left-wing HDP party (vastly more popular in Kurdish regions than other parts of the country - posters are always purple).

metas.name: Recognisable Roads - D915
metas.description: The D915, or âTurkeyâs death roadâ (not an official title, you heard it here first) is extremely recognisable. It crosses over the mountains between Bayburt and Of - the highest part consists only of a thin gravel road with a steep drop on one side.

metas.name: Recognisable Roads - E99
metas.description: The E99 leading into Azerbaijan is very identifiable. It is a very straight NW-SE road leading through a wetlands environment with dry mountains on either side. Mount Ararat is faintly visible to the northwest.

metas.name: Recognisable Roads - O-52
metas.description: Along the following stretches of the O-52 you will find a lane of fresh dark asphalt in the outer lane on both sides of the motorway.

metas.name: Recognisable Roads - SamandaÄ-kale
metas.description: The coastal road around Musa DaÄ (Hatay) is identifiable by the segregated cycle path that follows the length of the road between Kale and SamandaÄ.

metas.name: Vegetation - Alder
metas.description: Alder (Alnus glutinosa) can be recognized by its round leaves and pronounced leaf veins. It is very concentrated in the northeast of the country.

metas.name: Vegetation - Almonds
metas.description: Almonds are a decent meta for AdÄ±yaman province when found in isolated plantations. Another noteworthy hotspot in the southwest however is the DatÃ§a peninsula. where they grow abundantly.

metas.name: Vegetation - Apples
metas.description: The valleys around EÄirdir GÃ¶lÃ¼ in Isparta account for most of Turkeyâs apple production.

metas.name: Vegetation - Black Pine
metas.description: European black pine (Pinus nigra) is widely found in the northern and southwestern mountains, but it is very rare in the center of Anatolian plateau and eastern part of the country. This species features a lot of clusters of needles.

metas.name: Vegetation - Cabbage
metas.description: Samsun province produces the vast majority of Turkeyâs cabbages, and most of those are produced in the flat Bafra district that sticks out from the coast.

metas.name: Vegetation - Caucasian Spruce
metas.description: Caucasian spruce (Picea orientalis) is the only spruce species found in Turkey, and it is most common in the far northeastern part of the country.

metas.name: Vegetation - Cedar
metas.description: Lebanon cedar (Cedrus libani), which can be recognized by their big cones and fairly horizontal branches and leaves, is found in high mountains along the Mediterranean coast. NOTE: This species is often found planted in central-western plateau, in much shorter height. When the terrain is not mountainous, you should better ignore these trees.

metas.name: Vegetation - Cherries
metas.description: Cherries are mainly produced in three distinct areas - the KemalpaÅa valley just east of Ä°zmir, the SultandaÄÄ± valley stretching south to AkÅehir and the Bursa Valley just northeast of Bursa city, where it grows alongside many other fruit. Cherries can be recognised in spring by pink cherryblossoms and in summer by their short trunks and tall branches with long droopy leaves. And in summer by their short trunks and tall branches with long droopy leaves.

metas.name: Vegetation - Citrus
metas.description: Citrus plantations are found on much of the Mediterranean coast from AydÄ±n all the way to Hatay, being most common in the Adana plain.

metas.name: Vegetation - Cypress
metas.description: Mediterranean cypress (Cupressus sempervirens) is a conifer tree that features a very sharp crown resembling a spear and is mainly found along the south coast and the southern west coast, but also less commonly in the northwest of the country.

metas.name: Vegetation - Eucalyptus
metas.description: Eucalyptus is restricted to the southern and western coastal parts of the country, with particular concentrations in certain areas such as MuÄla. In an agricultural setting between fields, it is essentially unique to the Adana plain.

metas.name: Vegetation - Fan Palm
metas.description: Fan palms (Washingtonia robusta) are, as the name suggests, palms featuring fan-shaped leaves and are a good clue that you are somewhere along the south coast, especially around the cities of Antalya and Adana.

metas.name: Vegetation - Ferns
metas.description: Ferns in Turkey are mainly found along the north coast and less commonly in other coastal areas.

metas.name: Vegetation - Figs
metas.description: AydÄ±n province produces 70% of Turkeyâs figs, with most of the rest produced just across the border in Ä°zmir.

metas.name: Vegetation - Firs
metas.description: Firs (Abies spp.) are difficult to tell apart from other conifers, but the biggest clue lies in their branching structure, each branch coming off the trunk shaped like a flat fan. When viewed from the right angle you can often see the layers of flat branches stacked on top of one another. This contrasts with the branching structure of spruces, where secondary branches usually droop down from the primary branch. It is most common in the central northern mountains.

metas.name: Vegetation - Grapes
metas.description: Besides the dense vineyards of the AlaÅehir valley, there are a few other grape producing regions of Turkey. Just east of this valley, north of Denizli, is a unique red soil landscape with low, sporadic vineyards. There are also vineyards in the valley near the Gaziantep-Hatay border, particularly just south of Ä°slahiye, as well as small isolated vineyards spread around Thrace and Cappadoccia.

metas.name: Vegetation - Greenhouses
metas.description: Along the southern coast of Turkey you will find numerous dense clusters of plastic and glass greenhouses. The westernmost of these clusters is around KÄ±nÄ±k on the MuÄla-Antalya border and the easternmost lies just east of Mersin. Note that individual greenhouses can be found all over the country, it is best to use this meta if you find greenhouses on multiple sides.

metas.name: Vegetation - Hazelnuts
metas.description: Hazelnuts absolutely dominate the landscape of much of the forested northern parts of the country. It is cultivated throughout the coastal hills from Kocaeli province all the way to Artvin, however it is especially dominant in Ordu, Giresun and Sakarya (usually in the latter province they are found in a flatter landscape). Hazelnut trees can be identified by their multiple thin stems emanating from a single point and round leaves. Hazelnut-covered mountains are even distinct from afar as they have a seemingly fuzzy texture with a sort of green-purple colour.

metas.name: Vegetation - Hungarian Oak
metas.description: Hungarian oak (Quercus frainetto) is one of several oak species found in Turkey and can be recognized by the shape of its leaves. It has typical oak leaves, but they are larger and more deeply lobed than on other oak species.

metas.name: Vegetation - Inland Greenhouses
metas.description: Greenhouses in a drier, more inland landscape, often without roofs, are common in the ElmalÄ± valley and neighbouring inland regions of Western Antalya province.

metas.name: Vegetation - Mastic
metas.description: Mastic is a common Mediterranean shrub that can be used to identify the southwest coast, although it does exist less commonly up to halfway down the southern coast.

metas.name: Vegetation - Opium
metas.description: White opium poppies, yes you heard that right, are cultivated licitly in the valley around Afyonkarahisar, and they are very recognisable. A good mnemonic for this is that the name âAfyon-kara-hisarâ literally translates as âopium-black-fortressâ.

metas.name: Vegetation - Pears
metas.description: Pears are mostly produced in the aforementioned Bursa valley.

metas.name: Vegetation - Pickly Pear
metas.description: Prickly pear (Opuntia ficus-indica) is a type of cactus that consists of flat round pads and is found along the south coast and southern west coast.

metas.name: Vegetation - Pistachios
metas.description: Pistachios are mainly grown around Gaziantep.

metas.name: Vegetation - Poplar Plantations
metas.description: Also known as âDÃ¼zce treesâ - while poplar plantations can be found here and there in most temperate parts of Turkey, large orderly plantations are particularly common in the DÃ¼zce and Sakarya valleys.

metas.name: Vegetation - Rice
metas.description: Rice is most common along the Greek border, and in northern BalÄ±kesir, however it can be found in a few other distinct hotspots in the flat âdeltasâ of Samsun province, numerous river valleys in Ãorum, Sinop and ÃankÄ±rÄ±, and eastern Hatay.

metas.name: Vegetation - Scots Pine
metas.description: Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris) is recognized most easily by its red bark, but beware that the bottom section of the trunk is generally darker and not red. You can find it in inland regions along the north coast.

metas.name: Vegetation - Stone Pine
metas.description: Stone pine (Pinus pinea) can be recognized by its rounded crown, where all the branches and needles are concentrated towards the top of the tree. It is found predominantly along the west coast.

metas.name: Vegetation - Turkish Pine
metas.description: Turkish pine (Pinus brutia) is perhaps the most difficult pine species to identify in Turkey. It tends to have a less dense crown and brighter needles than other pines, the bark can be brown and can sometimes have a red tinge, but there is no stark contrast between the bottom and top sections of the trunk as there is with Scots pine. It is mainly found along the south and west coast.

metas.name: Vegetation - Van Mullein
metas.description: In northern Van there are numerous remote/dirt roads with âyellow flower spamâ. Known as mullein (Verbascum sp.), it is very distinct for its tall stem with yellow flowers all along it.

metas.name: Argentina Wild Sunflowers
metas.description: Wild sunflowers (Verbesina encelioides) are often found in Salta, Jujuy and TucumÃ¡n.

metas.name: Argentine Tree Plantations
metas.description: Along the border with Uruguay in Entre Rios and Corrientes is where you'll most commonly find tree plantations in Argentina. There may be others rarely in other parts of these provinces/Argentina.

metas.name: Bariloche
metas.description: Bariloche is a famous resort town in Nuequen. It can be recognized by the ski town vibes, the lake, and the mountains. While there are some other similar towns in Southern Argentina, Bariloche stands out and can be recognized with practice!

metas.name: Boat Coverage Entre Rios
metas.description: Just north of Buenos Aires City near Villa Paranacito there is boat coverage that is recognizable with the foliage and sometimes visible architecture.

metas.name: Buenos Aires Black and Yellow Taxi
metas.country: Buenos Aires Black and Yellow Taxi
metas.description: Black taxis with yellow rooftops can be seen commonly in the capital of Buenos Aires. While they should be unique to Buenos Aires Similar but distint taxis can be found in other cities.

metas.name: Buenos Aires Small Ponds
metas.description: Small ponds near the road are occasionally seen in the province of Buenos Aires.

metas.name: Cardon Cacti
metas.description: Trichocereus atacamensis, or the cardÃ³n, is a cactus native to the high elevation mountain ranges of Catamarca, TucumÃ¡n, Salta and Jujuy. It can be identified by its candelabra-like appearance and fuzzy golden brown spines.

metas.name: Chaco/Formosa - Sandy Soil and Vegetation
metas.description: In the Chaco and Formosa provinces, you will often see sandy soil with an abundance of vegetation; mainly low trees and bushes.

metas.name: Comodoro Rivadavia
metas.description: Comodoro Rivadavia is built on the slopes of Chenque hill, making the city recognisable.

metas.name: Cordoba Taxis
metas.description: Taxis in Cordoba are often all yellow or all green. May be seen uncommonly in other towns but if you're in a very large city with similar taxis it's likely Cordoba.

metas.name: Eastern Santa Cruz Snow Coverage
metas.description: Snow coverage is found on the eastern RP25 in eastern Santa Cruz.

metas.name: Green Hills of Buenos Aires
metas.description: Semi-coastal grass hills are seen in southern Buenos Aires, especially northeast of BahÃ­a Blanca.

metas.name: Jujuy Province
metas.description: The northern province of Jujuy has unique architecture similar to that of the brick buildings in Bolivia and Peru.

metas.name: La Pampa T-Intersection Sign
metas.description: T-Junctions in La Pampa sometimes have these usually yellow (rarely other colors) rectangular signs, with a chevron pattern on the bottom, usually the Road Number(s) above, with an arrow on both sides.

metas.name: Latvian Style Hook Poles
metas.description: Within Argentina, these Latvian style wooden hook poles are unique to La Rioja and Mendoza. (A bit more common in La Rioja, which also has a drier, more desert-like feel)

metas.name: Misiones Red Soil
metas.description: The soil in misiones is a distinct red color (similar to the Brazil across the border). This combined with the vegetation in the area can be a good clue for this region.

metas.name: Monkey Puzzle Tree
metas.description: The monkey puzzle tree can be found in western Neuquen. The most specimens are seen on state road 23.
metas.comparison: NOTE: They are seen on the other side in Chile as well.

metas.name: Pampas Grass
metas.description: Pampas grass (Cortaderia selloana) is one of the most defining flora of the Pampas region. It is recognizable by its long bunched reeds and white fluffy flowerheads.

metas.name: Pink Trumpet Tree
metas.description: The Pink Trumpet Tree (Handroanthus impetiginosus) can be found in cities in northern Salta such as OrÃ¡n, Tartagal, General Mosconi and Salvador Mazza.

metas.name: RN40 Low-Quality Sunset
metas.description: Sunset coverage with degraded image quality is found on the RN40 just south of the Mendoza border with NeuquÃ©n.

metas.name: RN68 Red Mountains
metas.description: These red mountains are unique to the RN68 valley in southern Salta.

metas.name: San Luis
metas.description: Roads with reddish pavement lined with long Argentine needle-grass are common in San Luis.

metas.name: South-Central Saw Dust Car
metas.description: The âsawdustâ car is found in centre-south Argentina (mostly west Rio Negro) and has a unique sandy dust on its visible black back.

metas.name: Southern Argentina
metas.description: If you see this kind of vegetation with flat grass and a low number of bushes, you are almost certainly in the state of Tierra del Fuego or southeastern Santa Cruz.

metas.name: Sugarcane
metas.description: Sugarcane plantations are most common in TucumÃ¡n, with hotspots appearing in Salta and Jujuy.

metas.name: The caldÃ©n
metas.description: Prosopis caldenia, known as the caldÃ©n, is a decently large deciduous tree with small leaves and sinuous branches. It is mainly found in La Pampa.

metas.name: Toothpick Cactus
metas.description: Stetsonia coryne, or the toothpick cactus, is a large tree-like cactus with many branches and spines resembling toothpicks. Its habitat includes a hotspot between Catamarca and Cordoba as well as the border area between Chaco, Salta and Formosa.

metas.name: Tucuman Pole Stickers
metas.description: White vertical pole stickers with several digits can be found in TucumÃ¡n.

metas.name: Ushuaia
metas.description: The southernmost city of Argentina, Ushuaia, is easily recognizable by the snowy mountains to the north, the archictecture, and the vegetation.

metas.name: Ushuaia Region - Tierra Del Fuego
metas.description: Well forested mountainous areas around Ushuaia in Southern Tierra Del Fuego are easily recognized.

metas.name: Valdes Peninsula Wide Dirt Roads
metas.description: Unusually wide dirt roads and flat geography make the Valdes peninsula of Eastern Chubut recognizable.

metas.name: Villa Dique Florentino
metas.description: Villa Dique Florentino Ameghino in northeastern Chubut is surrounded by these rock formations.
